### What Is ClickUp?
ClickUp is cloud-based project and work management software. It combines classic project management (tasks, dependencies, Gantt charts, milestones, sprints) with knowledge management (Docs and wikis), team communication (Chat) and an AI assistant, so that planning, documentation and discussion live next to the work.
Teams use it to manage:
- **Tasks and projects**, from personal to-dos to multi-team programmes
- **Sprints and backlogs** for software and product teams
- **Requests**, collected through Forms that create tasks automatically
- **Docs and wikis**, such as specs, SOPs and meeting notes linked to tasks
- **Goals, time tracking and workload**, to see progress and capacity
- **Dashboards and reports** across teams, clients and projects
ClickUp says it offers more than 15 views, so the same tasks can be shown as a list, board, table, calendar, Gantt chart, timeline, workload chart or mind map. It runs in the browser and as desktop and mobile apps. It is not a simple to-do list: its value, and its complexity, come from the number of building blocks it gives you and how much you can configure them.

### Who Owns ClickUp?
ClickUp was founded in 2017 by Zeb Evans (CEO) and Alex Yurkowski (CTO) and is headquartered in San Diego, California. It is privately held and venture-backed; its largest round was a $400 million Series C in October 2021 at an estimated $4 billion valuation. It acquired the search tool Slapdash in 2022 and the agentic AI coding company Codegen in December 2025, whose technology ClickUp says underpins its Super Agents. Like many software companies, it has also made layoffs, most recently a reported 22% reduction in May 2026.
For buyers, the practical point is that ClickUp is an established, fast-moving product: that pace brings frequent new features, but also interface changes some long-term users find disruptive.

### How Does ClickUp Work?
Everything in ClickUp sits inside a hierarchy, and understanding it is the key to a good setup:
- **Workspace** is the whole organisation. Paid plans apply to the entire Workspace.
- **Spaces** are the top-level areas, usually one per department, team or major client.
- **Folders** (optional) group related Lists, such as "Q4 campaigns" or "Client A". Subfolders are in beta.
- **Lists** hold tasks and usually represent a project, a sprint or a process.
- **Tasks and subtasks** are the individual pieces of work, each with **assignees**, **dates**, a **priority** and a **status**. Subtasks can be nested up to seven levels, and checklists break tasks into smaller steps.
- **Custom fields** add the data your team needs, such as budget, channel, client or sprint points.
Statuses and fields can be set at Space, Folder or List level, and **ClickApps** switch individual features on or off (for example time estimates, sprint points or nested subtasks). **Views** can be added at any level of the hierarchy, and **Dashboards** summarise work across it.
A typical workflow looks like this:
**Request arrives through a Form → task created in a List → work assigned → task moves through custom statuses → discussion in comments or Chat → progress shown on a Dashboard → task closed**
For example, a sales team submits a Form asking for a new case study. ClickUp creates a task in the Marketing Space's Content List, assigns it to a writer and sets the due date. The writer drafts the case study in a linked Doc, a reviewer leaves comments that become assigned actions, and the marketing lead sees the task move to Published on a Dashboard. Our [work breakdown structure](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/work-breakdown-structure/) guide is a good starting point for deciding how to split work into Spaces, Folders and Lists.

### ClickUp Key Features

#### Task Management
Tasks are where ClickUp is deepest. Each task can have subtasks, multiple assignees, start and due dates, priorities, custom statuses, custom task types (such as bug, lead or request), tags, custom fields, time estimates, checklists, attachments and comments. Task relationships handle [task dependencies](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/task-dependencies/), recurring tasks cover routine work, and task templates make repeatable work consistent.
This depth pays off once many people share the same work, but it also means there are many ways to model the same thing, so teams need agreed conventions.

#### Views
List, Board, Table and Calendar views are the everyday workhorses; Gantt, Timeline, Workload, Mind Map, Map and Activity views serve more specialised needs. Every view is a filtered window onto the same tasks, so a project manager can plan in Gantt while the team works from a board. Some views are limited on lower plans: Gantt is a trial on Free Forever, and Timeline, Activity and Mind Map are fully unlocked on Business.

#### Gantt Charts
ClickUp's [Gantt charts](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/gantt-chart/) support all four dependency types, automatic rescheduling of downstream tasks when a date moves, the [critical path](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/critical-path-method/), [slack time](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/float-and-slack/), milestones and baselines for planned-versus-actual comparison. The pricing page lists Gantt as a trial on Free Forever and unlimited from the Unlimited plan, and ClickUp says baselines are on paid plans.
For date-driven projects such as launches and events, this is a capable scheduler for the price; for simple task tracking it is more than most teams need.

#### Kanban Boards
Board view shows tasks as cards in columns by status, with drag-and-drop (including several cards at once), filters by assignee, priority, tag or field, and nested subtasks on cards. ClickUp supports [WIP limits](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/kanban/wip-limits/) per column and flags a column when it is full, which is unusual at this price. Board view is available on Free Forever. Our [Kanban boards](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/kanban/kanban-boards/) guide and free [Kanban board template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/kanban-board-template/) cover the practice behind it.

#### ClickUp Docs and Wikis
Docs are one of ClickUp's clearest advantages over task-first tools such as Asana and monday.com. They support nested pages, real-time co-editing with live cursors, inline comments that can be turned into tasks, embedded media, version history and granular permissions. Docs can be linked to tasks and sprints, and the Docs Hub lets you search and filter every Doc in the Workspace. Any Doc can be marked as a wiki; Free Forever includes one wiki.
For teams splitting work between a project tool and a separate wiki, this is a real consolidation opportunity, although teams with large, structured knowledge bases may still prefer a dedicated tool.

#### Whiteboards
Whiteboards provide a canvas for brainstorming and process mapping, and shapes or notes can be converted into tasks. They are capped at three on Free Forever and ten on Unlimited, with private whiteboards added on Business. They suit kick-offs and retrospectives rather than replacing a dedicated whiteboard app.

#### Forms
Forms turn requests into tasks. Each answer maps to a custom field, conditional logic shows follow-up questions only when relevant, and each submission lands in a chosen List with an assignee and priority already set. People outside ClickUp, such as clients and contractors, can submit without an account. Free Forever includes one Form; Unlimited removes the cap.
For example, a marketing team can use one Form to collect design requests with the deadline, channel, campaign, brief and attachments, so nothing arrives half-specified by email. Our free [work request template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/work-request-template/) follows the same idea if you are not ready for software.

#### Sprints and Agile Tools
ClickUp is one of the stronger general-purpose tools for Agile teams. Sprints are created as dated Lists, unfinished work spills over to the next sprint automatically, and sprint points (on Business) support [story point](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/scrum/scrum-story-points/) estimation. Sprint reporting includes burndown and burnup charts, [velocity](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/agile/agile-velocity-chart/) and [cumulative flow](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/kanban/cumulative-flow-diagram/), and GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket integrations link commits and pull requests to tasks.
It is less specialised than Jira for large engineering organisations, but a credible option for product teams that want Docs and stakeholder views in the same tool.

#### Time Tracking, Goals and Workload
Native time tracking, time estimates and timesheets with approvals are built in (a trial on Free Forever, included from Unlimited), which avoids a separate time-tracking subscription for many teams. Goals and Portfolios track progress across Lists and projects from the Unlimited plan. The Workload view shows each person's assigned effort over time, and portfolio-level workload management is on Business. These are practical for [capacity planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/capacity-planning/) in small and mid-sized teams, but less mature than the resource and financial planning in tools aimed at PMOs, such as [Wrike](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/).

#### ClickUp Automations
Automations follow a trigger-condition-action pattern: when a status changes, a date arrives or a Form is submitted, ClickUp can assign people, change statuses, post comments, move tasks, send emails or call a webhook. ClickUp advertises more than 100 templates and an AI builder that drafts rules from a plain-language description, which you can edit before publishing.
Automations are practical for removing routine coordination, but they are metered. The pricing page lists 100 automation executions on Free Forever, 1,000 on Unlimited, 5,000 per month on Business and 250,000 per month on Enterprise, so busy teams on lower plans can run out.

### ClickUp AI Features (ClickUp Brain)
AI is now central to how ClickUp sells itself (the Brain page currently uses the name Brain²), but the key buying point is that the most useful AI is **not included in the base plans**. Free Forever gives limited trial access, and the full capabilities are the paid **Brain AI** and **Everything AI** add-ons.

#### Brain Assistant and AI Writing
The Brain assistant answers questions about your tasks, Docs and Chat in plain language, drafts and rewrites text, summarises long threads and produces "catch me up" summaries. ClickUp says Brain only surfaces information the user already has permission to see. For project work, the most practical uses are status summaries, first drafts of briefs and quickly catching up on a busy task.

#### Enterprise Search and Model Choice
Enterprise search looks across the Workspace and connected apps such as Google Drive, GitHub and Salesforce from one place. The Brain AI add-on also includes AI chat with a choice of third-party models, which the pricing page lists as Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini. ClickUp states that it forbids third-party AI providers from training on customer data.

#### Super Agents
Super Agents are configurable AI teammates that can be @mentioned, messaged and assigned tasks. ClickUp says they can create and update tasks, draft documents, send emails and messages, schedule events and run multi-step workflows, and can be set up by describing the job in plain language. They work within the same permission model as human users and ClickUp says every action is recorded in an audit trail.
Treat them as workflow automation with a natural-language interface, not autonomous employees: they follow the instructions and access you give them, consume AI credits, and still need a human owner. ClickUp's claim that its AI "beats every benchmark" is vendor marketing; judge agents on a real workflow.

#### AI Notetaker, AI Fields and Ambient Answers
The higher Everything AI tier adds the AI Notetaker (meeting transcripts, summaries and action items), AI Fields that fill in summaries or categories on tasks automatically, AI-powered automations and dashboard cards, AI assignment and prioritisation, image generation, and Ambient Answers, which ClickUp says surface relevant answers and context automatically, before you ask.

#### How ClickUp AI Is Priced
| AI option | Listed price | What it adds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free Forever | $0 | Limited trial access to advanced AI features |
| Brain AI | $9/user/month | Unlimited Brain assistant and AI writing, AI chat with Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini, enterprise search, 1,500 AI Super Credits per user/month |
| Everything AI | $28/user/month | Everything in Brain AI plus AI Notetaker, AI Fields, AI automations and dashboards, AI assign and prioritise, more Super Agent usage, 5,000 AI Super Credits per user/month |
| AI Super Credits | $10 per 10,000 credits | Top-ups for Super Agents, AI Fields, AI automations and image generation |
The pricing page notes that yearly AI billing is discounted by up to 20%, so confirm which billing basis a quote uses. The add-ons change the value calculation considerably: a Business seat at $12 per month becomes $40 per month with Everything AI, more than many rivals' AI-inclusive plans. Many teams will get most of the value from Brain AI for a subset of users.

### ClickUp Collaboration Features
Collaboration happens both on tasks and in ClickUp Chat. On tasks, you get comments, @mentions, attachments and **assigned comments**, which turn a comment into an action item for a named person. **ClickUp Chat** adds channels, direct messages, posts for announcements, threads, FollowUps that turn messages into to-dos, and one-click voice and video calls with automatic summaries. ClickUp offers a Slack import for channels and history, and Chat is included from the Unlimited plan (Free Forever keeps 30 days of chat history).
Clips (screen and voice recordings), proofing on files, guests and a central Inbox round things out. Having discussion, documents and tasks in one place is a genuine advantage, but only if the team actually moves conversations out of Slack or Teams; otherwise Chat becomes one more place to check. Notification volume is a recurring complaint, so agree settings early.

### ClickUp Reporting and Dashboards
Dashboards combine cards for charts, tables, workload, time tracking, sprint metrics and calculations, filtered by owner, status, date or custom field. They are **actionable**, so you can change statuses or reassign tasks from the dashboard, and they can be shared with clients or executives without giving them access to the whole Workspace. Brain can answer questions about dashboard data in plain language.
Plan matters here: Dashboards are a trial on Free Forever and Unlimited, and unlimited Dashboards with advanced cards come with Business, which makes Business the realistic starting point for managers who rely on reporting. For deeper analysis, ClickUp connects to Tableau. Dashboards handle the weekly [project status report](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-status-report/) well, but they are not a full portfolio analytics suite.

### ClickUp Integrations
ClickUp claims more than 1,000 integrations, a figure that includes connections through automation platforms such as Zapier and Make. Native integrations include **Slack**, **Microsoft Teams**, **Zoom**, **GitHub**, **GitLab**, **Bitbucket**, **Google Drive**, **OneDrive**, **Dropbox**, **Outlook**, **Google Calendar**, **HubSpot**, **Zendesk**, **Figma**, **Tableau** and time-tracking tools such as Toggl and Harvest. Developers can use the public REST API, webhooks and the ClickUp MCP server for AI tools.
Importers bring in work from Asana, Trello, Jira, monday.com, Wrike, Basecamp, Confluence and Todoist, which makes migration easier. Integrations are unlimited from the Unlimited plan, while webhooks and automation integrations are listed under Business.

### ClickUp Ease of Use

#### Initial Setup
Setting ClickUp up well means designing the hierarchy, statuses, custom fields, ClickApps, views, permissions and automations. Templates help, but a poorly planned hierarchy is hard to reorganise later. A small team can be productive in a day; a company-wide rollout needs an owner and a plan.

#### Learning Curve
Basic task management is quick to pick up, and Capterra reviewers rate ease of use 4.3/5, the lowest of ClickUp's four sub-scores but still respectable. The difficulty is breadth: new users face many menus, views and options at once, and reviewers frequently describe the tool as overwhelming at first. ClickUp University, templates and the Help Center help, and it is worth hiding ClickApps and views your team does not need.

#### Interface and Performance
The interface is flexible and customisable, with themes, dark mode and personal views, but it is dense, and frequent product updates can move familiar controls. Performance is the most persistent criticism in third-party reviews. In Capterra's topic summaries, about 78% of the 290 reviews mentioning lag and slowdowns are negative, and about 56% of the 227 mentioning bugs and glitches are negative. Reports cluster around large boards and busy Workspaces. It is not universal, but it is common enough that larger teams should test performance with realistic data during evaluation.

### ClickUp Mobile App
ClickUp's iOS and Android apps let you check and update tasks, drag cards on boards, use Chat, receive notifications and make quick updates away from your desk. Brain is also available on mobile.
Mobile is a recurring concern in reviews. Capterra's topic summary on mobile functionality is mixed, with about 40% of the 273 reviews mentioning it negative, citing a less intuitive layout, bugs and occasional crashes. Treat the app as a companion for staying up to date, and do planning, configuration and reporting on desktop.

### ClickUp Pricing
ClickUp's published plans are below. Prices are per user per month; the lower figure applies when billed annually and the higher when billed monthly. ClickUp requires upgrades to apply to the entire Workspace rather than to individual users.
| Plan | Billed annually | Billed monthly | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free Forever | $0 | $0 | Personal use and trying ClickUp |
| Unlimited | $7/user/month | $10/user/month | Small teams |
| Business | $12/user/month | $19/user/month | Mid-sized teams that need reporting and advanced automation |
| Enterprise | Contact sales | Contact sales | Large organisations needing governance and security controls |
AI is extra: Brain AI is $9 and Everything AI is $28 per user/month, and extra AI Super Credits cost $10 per 10,000 (see the AI section above). ClickUp Assist, which provides two hours a month of one-to-one expert time, is also sold separately. Pricing checked on ClickUp's pricing page on 7 October 2026; always confirm before buying.

#### ClickUp Free Forever Plan
Free Forever costs $0 and includes unlimited members and tasks, 60MB of storage, Docs, Board, Calendar and Sprints, one Form, one wiki, three whiteboards, up to five Spaces and 100 automation executions. Gantt charts, Dashboards, time tracking and timesheets are available only as trials, activity history is kept for one day and chat history for 30 days. It is one of the more generous free plans for individuals and very small teams, but the 60MB storage limit and trial-only reporting mean most working teams will outgrow it quickly.

#### ClickUp Unlimited Plan
At $7 per user/month billed annually ($10 monthly), Unlimited removes the storage, Space and Form caps and adds unlimited Gantt charts, integrations and custom fields, native time tracking, Goals and Portfolios, resource management, guest permissions, ClickUp Chat and email in ClickUp. Limits include 1,000 automation executions and ten whiteboards, and Dashboards remain a trial. It suits small teams that want real project planning at a low price.

#### ClickUp Business Plan
At $12 per user/month billed annually ($19 monthly), Business adds unlimited Dashboards with advanced cards, unlimited Timeline and Activity views, mind maps, 5,000 automations per month, webhooks and automation integrations, sprint points and sprint reporting, portfolio workload management, private whiteboards, unlimited proofing, custom exporting and Google SSO. This is the plan most teams that rely on reporting or run sprints should evaluate first.

#### ClickUp Enterprise Plan
Enterprise is quote-based and adds enterprise permissions and governance, unlimited custom roles, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, audit logs, session management, an enterprise API, 250,000 automations per month, custom branding, data residency, HIPAA availability, live onboarding training and a Customer Success Manager. It is designed for large organisations with security, compliance and administration requirements.

#### ClickUp Free Trial and Money-Back Guarantee
ClickUp does not advertise a fixed-length trial of the whole product. Instead, Free Forever gives trial access to paid features such as Gantt charts, Dashboards, time tracking and AI, and the pricing page advertises a "100% Money-back Guarantee" without stating its conditions on the page, so check the refund terms before paying. Use the free plan to rebuild one real workflow with the people who will use it, and test it with a realistic volume of tasks so you can judge performance, not just features.

### ClickUp Pros and Cons

##### Pros
- Very strong value for money on paid plans
- Huge feature set in one Workspace
- Flexible hierarchy, statuses, fields and 15+ views
- Docs, wikis, Whiteboards and Chat built in
- Strong sprint and Agile support
- Generous Free Forever plan
- Large automation library with an AI builder
- Wide integrations, API and importers
- Native time tracking and Goals from Unlimited

##### Cons
- Setup takes deliberate design to do well
- Interface can feel overwhelming to new users
- Lag and bugs are the most common user complaints
- Best AI features cost $9 to $28 per user/month extra
- Dashboards and sprint points need Business
- Free plan storage (60MB) and automation limits are tight
- Mobile app less complete than desktop
- Frequent updates can change familiar workflows
- Less mature portfolio and financial controls than PMO-focused tools
This balance matches what users report: people value ClickUp's breadth, flexibility and price, while complexity and performance are its most consistent drawbacks.

Ratings and review themes as published on G2 and Capterra on 5 October 2026; summarised in our own words. Visit the links above for full, verified user reviews.
On **Capterra**, ClickUp is rated **4.6/5 from 4,634 reviews**, with sub-scores of **4.3 for ease of use**, **4.6 for features**, **4.6 for value for money** and **4.5 for customer service** (checked 7 October 2026). On **G2**, it is rated **4.6/5 from 14,714 reviews** (checked 5 October 2026). The themes below summarise these third-party reviews in our own words, not ClickUp's testimonials.
**Positive themes.** Reviewers most often praise having everything in one place, collaboration and visibility, flexible and customisable workflows, productivity gains, and the value of the free and low-cost plans. In Capterra's topic summaries, collaboration (about 97% positive across 466 mentions), productivity (about 95% positive) and adaptable project management (about 98% positive) stand out.
**Negative themes.** The most common complaints are lag and slowdowns, especially in large boards and busy Workspaces, recurring bugs and glitches, a learning curve caused by the number of features, a less capable mobile app, notification settings that are hard to tune, and costs rising as users are added. Some reviewers also find frequent interface changes disruptive.
When reading reviews yourself, check whether a review was invited or incentivised by the vendor. Both Capterra and G2 label these, and filtering for non-incentivised reviews gives a more cautious picture. Read the critical reviews from companies similar in size to yours, not just the five-star ones.

### ClickUp Customer Support
ClickUp's pricing page lists 24/7 support, including on Free Forever. Self-service resources include the Help Center, ClickUp University courses, templates and a user community. Enterprise adds live onboarding training and a dedicated Customer Success Manager, and ClickUp Assist is a paid add-on for one-to-one expert help, including setting up AI agents.
Third-party views are mostly positive, with a 4.5/5 customer service sub-score on Capterra, but individual experiences vary. For larger rollouts, ask during the sales process exactly what onboarding is included and who will help design your hierarchy.

### ClickUp Security
ClickUp's security page states that it holds SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2 and SOC 3 reports, ISO 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701 certifications and ISO 42001 for AI management, maintains PCI compliance, and is GDPR and HIPAA compliant (HIPAA agreements are listed as available on Enterprise). Data is hosted on Amazon Web Services, encrypted at rest with AES-256 and in transit with TLS 1.2, and Enterprise customers can choose data residency in the US, Europe or Asia Pacific.
Access controls scale by plan: two-factor authentication on every plan, Google SSO and SMS 2FA on Business, and SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, audit logs, session management and custom roles on Enterprise. Guest permissions let you share specific work with clients without exposing the Workspace. Confirm current certifications and their scope in ClickUp's trust documentation as part of procurement, and review how AI features handle your data.

### ClickUp for Different Types of Teams

#### ClickUp for Software and Product Teams
Sprints, sprint points, burndown and velocity reporting, Git integrations, bug task types and Docs for specs make ClickUp a strong fit for small and mid-sized product teams that want planning and documentation together. Large engineering organisations with complex release and issue workflows may still prefer Jira.

#### ClickUp for Marketing and Creative Teams
Forms for requests, content calendars, proofing for creative feedback, Docs for briefs and Whiteboards for campaign planning cover most marketing needs. The flexibility suits teams with varied work types, provided someone keeps the setup tidy.

#### ClickUp for Agencies and Client Services
Agencies can run each client in its own Space or Folder, track time against tasks, share Dashboards or Lists with clients as guests, and collect client requests through Forms. The low per-user price helps agencies with many staff.

#### ClickUp for Project Managers and PMOs
Gantt charts with critical path and baselines, Portfolios, Goals, workload views and Dashboards give project managers most of what they need for [managing multiple projects](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/managing-multiple-projects/). For a formal [PMO](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-management-office-pmo/) needing advanced resource, budget and financial control across a large portfolio, ClickUp is less mature than tools built for that purpose.

#### ClickUp for Small Businesses and Start-ups
This is one of ClickUp's best fits: a usable free plan, low paid prices, and enough breadth to replace a task manager, a wiki and a time tracker. The risk is over-building; start with a simple hierarchy and add features only when you need them.

### Is ClickUp Worth It?
ClickUp is likely worth it if you:
- Want to replace separate task, docs, whiteboard and time-tracking tools with one platform.
- Need many views over the same work, from boards to Gantt charts.
- Run sprints or Agile workflows alongside non-technical teams.
- Are price-sensitive but need more than a basic task list.
- Have someone willing to design and maintain the setup.
It may not be worth it if:
- You want a tool that works well with almost no setup.
- Your Workspace will be very large and performance is critical.
- You need mature portfolio, resource and financial management.
- You would need Everything AI for every user, which removes much of the price advantage.
- Your team is unlikely to adopt a feature-dense platform.
Our verdict: ClickUp's breadth is both its biggest advantage and its biggest drawback. For teams that will use its Docs, sprints, automations and dashboards, it delivers more for the money than most competitors, which is why it ranks fourth in our [project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/) review. For teams with simple needs, or those that cannot tolerate occasional lag, the same breadth adds complexity they do not need. If you are still deciding, our guide on [how to choose project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/how-to-choose-project-management-software/) sets out the questions to ask, and the Free Forever plan is the place to test them.

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: Is ClickUp good project management software?**
Yes, for the right team. ClickUp offers an unusually broad feature set, including tasks, Gantt charts, sprints, Docs, Chat and Dashboards, at low prices, and it rates 4.6/5 on Capterra. The trade-offs are a learning curve, a dense interface and recurring complaints about lag, so it suits teams willing to invest in setup.

**Q: Is ClickUp free?**
Yes. ClickUp's Free Forever plan costs $0 and includes unlimited members and tasks, Docs, Board view and Sprints, but only 60MB of storage, one Form, three whiteboards and 100 automation executions. Gantt charts, Dashboards and time tracking are trial-only on the free plan.

**Q: How much does ClickUp cost?**
ClickUp costs $0 on Free Forever, $7 per user/month on Unlimited and $12 per user/month on Business when billed annually ($10 and $19 billed monthly), with Enterprise priced on request. AI is extra: Brain AI is $9 and Everything AI $28 per user/month (checked 7 October 2026).

**Q: Does ClickUp have a free trial?**
ClickUp does not advertise a fixed-length trial of the whole product. Instead, the Free Forever plan includes trial access to paid features such as Gantt charts, Dashboards, time tracking and AI, and the pricing page advertises a money-back guarantee. Check the refund terms before paying.

**Q: Is ClickUp easy to use?**
Partly. Creating and updating tasks is quick to learn, but ClickUp's breadth of views, settings and features makes it overwhelming for many new users, and a good setup needs planning. Capterra users rate ease of use 4.3/5, lower than its scores for features and value.

**Q: What is ClickUp best used for?**
ClickUp is best for teams that want tasks, projects, sprints, Docs, request Forms, time tracking and Dashboards in one place, particularly start-ups, small and mid-sized businesses, product and software teams, marketing teams and agencies.

**Q: Is ClickUp better than Asana?**
Neither is universally better. ClickUp offers more features for the money, including Docs, Chat and native time tracking; Asana is cleaner, more focused and usually easier to adopt. See our [ClickUp vs Asana comparison](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/asana-vs-clickup/).

**Q: Is ClickUp better than monday.com?**
It depends on the use case. ClickUp is cheaper and has stronger Docs and Agile tools; monday.com is generally easier to learn and more visually polished. See our [ClickUp vs monday.com comparison](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/monday-vs-clickup/).

**Q: Does ClickUp have Gantt charts?**
Yes. ClickUp's Gantt view supports all four dependency types, automatic rescheduling, the critical path, slack time, milestones and baselines. It is a trial on Free Forever and unlimited from the Unlimited plan.

**Q: What is ClickUp Brain and is ClickUp AI free?**
ClickUp Brain is ClickUp's AI assistant for answering questions about your work, writing, summarising, searching connected apps and running Super Agents. Free Forever includes only limited trial use; full AI requires the Brain AI ($9) or Everything AI ($28) add-on per user per month.

**Q: What are the main disadvantages of ClickUp?**
The main disadvantages are the setup effort, an interface that can feel overwhelming, reported lag and bugs in large Workspaces, AI that costs extra, a less capable mobile app, and frequent interface changes.

**Q: Why is ClickUp slow?**
Lag is the most common complaint in ClickUp reviews, usually in large boards, busy Workspaces or views loading many tasks. Keeping Lists focused, archiving finished work, limiting heavy views and testing with realistic data during evaluation all help.

**Q: Does ClickUp integrate with Slack and Microsoft Teams?**
Yes. ClickUp has native integrations with both Slack and Microsoft Teams, alongside GitHub, GitLab, Google Drive, HubSpot, Zoom, Figma and Tableau. It claims more than 1,000 integrations in total, including those through Zapier and Make.

**Q: Is ClickUp suitable for small businesses?**
Yes, it is one of ClickUp's best fits. The free plan and low paid prices suit small budgets, and one tool can replace a task manager, wiki and time tracker. Start with a simple setup to avoid overwhelming the team.

**Q: Is ClickUp secure?**
ClickUp says it holds SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2 and SOC 3 reports and several ISO certifications, encrypts data with AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2 in transit, and hosts on AWS. SAML SSO, SCIM and audit logs require Enterprise.
How we review.

### What every comparison covers
Each of the 45 pages follows the same structure, so you can compare like with like:
- **At a glance:** score, rank, starting price, free plan and best-for summary for both tools.
- **Pricing:** each plan side by side, with what you get at each tier.
- **Features:** a checklist covering Gantt and timeline views, Kanban boards, time tracking, resource management, portfolios, docs, automation, Agile tools, proofing, built-in AI and guest access.
- **Category winners:** the seven category scores and who wins each one.
- **User ratings:** published G2 and Capterra ratings and review counts.
- **Choose A if, choose B if:** a plain verdict on which type of team each tool suits.
Around those tables, each comparison explains the differences in ease of use, planning views, collaboration, automation and AI, reporting, integrations, security and pricing, and how to switch between the two.

### How to compare project management tools yourself
A comparison narrows the field; a short, structured evaluation makes the decision. This is the process we recommend:
1. **Write down the work the tool must support.** List your project types, team size, methods (Scrum, Kanban, Waterfall or hybrid) and who outside the team needs access.
2. **Separate must-haves from nice-to-haves.** For example: Gantt charts with dependencies, resource planning, sprints, proofing, client guest access or Microsoft 365 integration. Our guide to [project management software features](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-management-software-features/) explains what each one does.
3. **Shortlist two or three tools** using the tables above, then read their head-to-head comparisons.
4. **Trial them on a real project**, not a demo board. Ask the people who will use it every day to do their normal work in it for a week or two.
5. **Check integrations, security and administration** with IT: single sign-on, permissions, data residency and the apps you already use.
6. **Work out the total cost** for your team size over a year, including the plan you will need in 12 months and any paid add-ons such as AI.
7. **Plan adoption**: templates, training and a clear owner matter more to success than the last few features.
For a fuller walkthrough, read [how to choose project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/how-to-choose-project-management-software/).

### Free plans and trials
Most tools in our review offer a free plan or free trial, but the limits differ a great deal. At our last check, Jira's free plan covered up to 10 users, Trello's free plan suited small teams, and monday.com's free plan was limited to two seats. Smartsheet discontinued its free plan in 2025 and now offers a 30-day free trial instead. Basic Microsoft Planner is included with many Microsoft 365 business subscriptions.
Free plans are best for testing a tool or running small projects. Features such as Gantt charts, automation, resource management and admin controls usually sit on paid plans, so check the pricing table in each comparison against your must-have list.

# Jira Review 2026: Is It Worth It?

URL: https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/jira/
Section: Project management software reviews
Summary: Our Jira review covers Scrum and Kanban boards, JQL, Rovo AI, pricing, the free plan, pros and cons, integrations and whether Jira is worth it in 2026.


## Jira Review 2026: Is It Worth It?
Jira is Atlassian's work management and issue-tracking platform, and for many software organisations it is simply where development work lives: backlogs, sprints, boards, bugs, releases and the links between code and tasks. It now also includes business templates for non-technical teams. Its biggest strength is the depth of its Agile tooling, workflows and query language; the same depth means it needs an administrator, takes time to learn and can feel heavy to casual users. This review covers features, Scrum and Kanban support, JQL, Rovo AI, integrations, pricing, ease of use, reporting and overall value.
- Published 7 September 2026
- Last updated 7 October 2026
- Pricing and Capterra rating checked 7 October 2026

### Jira review: quick verdict
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Best for | Software development, IT and product teams running Scrum or Kanban, especially those already using Confluence, Bitbucket or GitHub |
| Less suitable for | Marketing, creative or business teams that want a simple, visual tool with little setup, and teams with nobody to administer it |
| Our overall score | **8.6/10**, ranked #6 in our [top 10 project management tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/) |

Jira is the most complete Agile tool for software teams that we review: backlogs, sprints, boards, configurable workflows, JQL and deep developer integrations are all mature, and the free plan is genuinely usable for up to 10 people. The trade-offs are just as clear: it needs someone to design and maintain its configuration, the learning curve is steep, users regularly complain about clutter and slowness on large sites, and advanced planning, the stronger AI allowances and some security controls sit on higher plans or paid add-ons. For company-wide work management beyond engineering, easier tools often get better adoption.

### What Is Jira?
Jira is cloud-based software for planning, tracking and releasing work. It started in 2002 as a bug and issue tracker and grew into the default [Agile](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/agile/agile-methodology/) tool for many software organisations. In 2024 Atlassian folded Jira Work Management into Jira, so the same product now offers templates and views for business teams as well as software teams.
Teams use Jira to manage:
- **Backlogs and sprints** for Scrum teams, and continuous-flow boards for Kanban teams
- **Bugs and technical work**, with a full history of who changed what
- **Feature delivery and releases**, linked to branches, commits, pull requests and deployments
- **IT and platform work**, such as infrastructure changes and internal requests
- **Business requests**, collected through forms and tracked in list, calendar or board views
- **Cross-team planning**, using timelines and, on higher plans, multi-team plans with dependencies
The same work can be viewed as a board, backlog, list, timeline, calendar or summary page. Jira Cloud is Atlassian's main product; the self-managed Data Center edition is being retired, with Atlassian giving an end-of-life date of 28 March 2029. Jira Service Management (for service desks), Jira Product Discovery (for product ideas) and Confluence (for documentation) are separate products that work closely with Jira.

### Who Owns Jira?
Jira is made by Atlassian, which Mike Cannon-Brookes and Scott Farquhar founded in Sydney in 2002, the same year Jira launched. Atlassian is listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange, and Cannon-Brookes has been sole CEO since Farquhar stepped down as co-CEO in 2024. Its other products include Confluence, Trello, Bitbucket, Loom and Jira Service Management.
For buyers, the practical point is that Jira is a mature product backed by a large public company with a big partner network and app marketplace, so long-term availability is not a realistic concern. The more relevant question is how Atlassian's cloud-first strategy and plan packaging affect your costs.

### How Does Jira Work?
Jira's structure looks complicated at first, but the core building blocks are consistent:
- A **site** is your organisation's Jira instance (for example yourcompany.atlassian.net).
- **Spaces** (until 2025 called projects) hold the work for a team or product. They are either **team-managed**, which a team can configure for itself, or **company-managed**, which administrators configure and share across teams.
- **Work items** (previously called issues) are the units of work: **epics**, **stories**, **tasks**, **bugs** and **subtasks**, each with an assignee, status, priority and fields.
- **Workflows** define the statuses a work item moves through and the transitions between them.
- **Boards and views** show work as a Scrum or Kanban board, backlog, list, timeline or calendar.
- **Filters** written in JQL (Jira Query Language) select work items, and they feed boards, dashboards and reports.
A typical software workflow looks like this:
**Idea or bug logged → backlog refined and estimated → sprint planned → work moves across the board → code linked → release shipped → sprint reviewed and reported**
For example, a product team keeps its [product backlog](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/scrum/product-backlog/) in Jira, refines and estimates the top items, then drags them into a two-week sprint. Developers move work items from To do to In progress to Done, branches and pull requests appear on each item, and at the end of the sprint the burndown and velocity reports feed the [sprint retrospective](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/scrum/sprint-retrospective/).

### Jira Key Features

#### Scrum Boards and Backlogs
Scrum is where Jira is strongest. The backlog lets product owners rank work items, group them into epics and estimate them with [story points](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/scrum/scrum-story-points/). [Sprint planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/scrum/sprint-planning/) happens by dragging work into a sprint, setting a goal and starting it; at the end, unfinished work can roll into the next sprint or back to the backlog. The [Scrum board](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/scrum/scrum-boards/) then shows the sprint's progress column by column.
These features are on every plan, including Free. For a team that runs Scrum by the book, Jira's model maps closely to the Scrum Guide's events and artefacts, which is one reason it remains the default choice for software teams.

#### Kanban Boards
Kanban boards show continuous flow rather than time-boxed sprints. Columns map to workflow statuses, and teams can add [WIP limits](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/kanban/wip-limits/), [swimlanes](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/kanban/kanban-swimlanes/) by assignee, epic or priority, and quick filters. Many support, platform and operations teams prefer Kanban in Jira because work arrives unpredictably.

#### Work Items, Issue Types and Custom Fields
Jira's work item hierarchy runs from epics down to stories, tasks, bugs and subtasks, and administrators can add further levels above epics, such as initiatives. Each type can have its own fields, screens and workflow, and administrators can add custom fields such as customer, component, severity or environment. This flexibility is what lets one Jira site serve very different teams, but it is also where configurations become messy over time. Our guide to [epics vs stories vs tasks](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/agile/epics-vs-stories-vs-tasks/) explains how to use the levels sensibly.

#### Custom Workflows
Workflows define statuses (for example To do, In progress, In review, Testing, Done) and the transitions between them. In company-managed spaces administrators can add conditions, validators and post-functions, such as requiring a resolution before closing a bug or limiting who can approve a release. Team-managed spaces offer a simpler editor that teams can change themselves.
This is one of Jira's major strengths and one of its main costs. Well-designed workflows enforce your process; overgrown ones, with dozens of statuses and schemes, are a common reason teams find Jira frustrating. Our [Agile workflow](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/agile/agile-workflow/) guide covers principles that keep them lean.

#### JQL and Filters
JQL (Jira Query Language) is Jira's search language, for example finding all open bugs in a space assigned to your team that were created in the last 14 days. Saved JQL filters drive boards, dashboards, reports, automation rules and subscriptions, so anyone fluent in JQL can answer almost any question about the work.
JQL is powerful but technical, which is why Atlassian now offers natural-language search through Rovo: you describe what you want in plain English and Rovo converts it into a JQL query, and a JQL error fixer corrects typos and syntax errors. Non-technical users still tend to rely on saved filters built by someone else.

#### Timeline and Plans
Every plan includes a timeline view that shows epics and their child work on a calendar, with basic dependencies, which is useful for an [Agile roadmap](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/agile/agile-roadmap/) of one team. Premium and Enterprise add advanced planning, called Plans (previously Advanced Roadmaps), which spans multiple spaces and teams, maps cross-team dependencies, compares capacity with scheduled work and lets you model scenarios before committing changes.
This matters for organisations running [release planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/agile/agile-release-planning/) or [PI planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/agile/pi-planning/) across several teams. Jira does not offer a classic Gantt chart with critical path and baselines, so plan-driven projects with fixed dates are better served by tools built around [Gantt charts](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/gantt-chart/).

#### Release Management
Versions group the work items that ship together. The releases view shows progress for each version, which items are still open, and, when connected to development tools, related commits, builds and deployments. For teams practising [continuous delivery](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/kanban/continuous-delivery/), the deployment tracking is more useful than the version list itself.

#### Forms and Business Templates
Forms let anyone submit a request that becomes a work item with the right fields filled in, which helps business teams such as marketing, HR or legal take in work without email threads. Business spaces add list and calendar views and templates for campaigns, approvals and similar processes. These are capable, but they sit inside a product still shaped around software terminology, which is why business users often find Jira less natural than tools designed for them. Our free [work request template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/work-request-template/) covers the same idea without software.

#### Jira Automation
Jira Automation uses no-code rules made of a trigger, conditions and actions: when a pull request is merged, move the work item to Done; when a bug is marked critical, assign it and alert a channel; when all subtasks are done, close the parent. Atlassian provides a library of rule templates, and with Rovo you can describe a rule in plain language and have it drafted for you.
Automation is included on every plan, but usage allowances differ: Free has a small allowance, and paid plans scale with the number of users, rising on Premium and Enterprise. Teams with many cross-space rules should check the allowance in Atlassian's plan comparison before choosing a tier.

### Jira AI Features
Atlassian's AI is branded **Rovo**. According to Atlassian, Rovo is available and switched on automatically for Standard, Premium and Enterprise Cloud plans; it is not listed for the Free plan. Usage is measured in AI credits: Atlassian's Rovo pricing page lists 25 credits per user per month on Standard, 70 on Premium and 150 on Enterprise, shared across Jira and Confluence. Administrators can switch AI features off.

#### Natural-Language Search and JQL Help
Rovo can turn a plain-language request, such as "bugs assigned to my team that are overdue", into a JQL query, and it can fix broken JQL. It can also write formulas for custom fields (in beta). For teams where only a few people know JQL, this lowers the barrier to self-service reporting.

#### Writing, Summaries and Work Breakdown
Atlassian's documentation lists AI features for drafting and improving work item descriptions, summarising long comment threads, producing a summary card of a work item's status and next steps, suggesting child work items from a parent epic, predicting field values as you type, detecting likely duplicates and linking similar work items. It can also create work items from Slack or Microsoft Teams conversations and suggest related Confluence pages. These are practical time-savers in day-to-day backlog work rather than headline features.

#### Rovo Chat, Search and Agents
Rovo Chat and Search answer questions across Jira, Confluence and connected tools. Atlassian also offers Rovo agents and supports third-party agents that can be assigned work like a teammate. Examples it describes include a Work Readiness Checker that reviews whether work is clear and complete before planning, project management skills that create and update work items and draft status updates from chat, and Rovo Dev, which aims to turn Jira work items into code.
Treat these as assistance that still needs review, not as autonomous team members. Their usefulness depends on clean data in Jira and Confluence, credit allowances limit heavy use, and some capabilities are still labelled beta.

### Jira Collaboration Features
Collaboration in Jira happens on the work item: comments with @mentions, watchers, attachments, links between related items, and a full change history. Linking work items to Confluence pages keeps specifications and decisions close to the work, and integrations with Slack and Microsoft Teams let people create and update work items from chat.
Jira is strongest for collaboration within delivery teams, where the work item is the natural unit of conversation. It is weaker as a general collaboration space: it has no built-in documents (that is Confluence's job), and stakeholders outside engineering often prefer a summary or dashboard to reading work items. Notifications can also become noisy on busy spaces, so agree notification schemes and watch habits early.

### Jira Reporting and Dashboards
Jira includes the standard Agile reports: sprint reports, burndown and burnup charts, velocity charts, [cumulative flow diagrams](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/kanban/cumulative-flow-diagram/) and control charts for [cycle time](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/kanban/cycle-time/). Dashboards combine gadgets such as filter results, pie charts, created-versus-resolved trends and sprint health, and every space has a summary page showing work by status, priority and type.
For team-level metrics such as [velocity](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/scrum/scrum-velocity/) this is more than enough. Cross-portfolio, executive or financial reporting is weaker out of the box, and many organisations add Marketplace apps or export to a BI tool. On Capterra's topic summaries, around 96% of reviews that discuss progress visualisation are positive, so most users are satisfied with what is there. Our guide to [Agile metrics and KPIs](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/agile/agile-metrics-and-kpis/) explains which reports are worth watching.

### Jira Integrations
Integrations are a major reason teams choose Jira. Atlassian says the Atlassian Marketplace offers more than 3,000 apps and integrations. Commonly used connections include:
- **Confluence** for specifications, meeting notes and documentation linked to work items
- **Bitbucket**, plus GitHub and GitLab through Marketplace apps, to show branches, commits, pull requests, builds and deployments on each work item
- **Slack** and **Microsoft Teams** for notifications and creating work items from chat
- **Google** and **Zoom** integrations, and **Trello** for teams moving between the two
- **Tempo Timesheets** for time tracking and **Zephyr** for test management
Developers can also use Jira's REST APIs and webhooks. One practical caution: most Marketplace apps are priced per user on the same tier as your Jira site, so adding several apps to a large site can increase the total cost noticeably. Budget for the apps you actually need before committing.

### Jira Ease of Use

#### Initial Setup
A small team can create a team-managed space from a Scrum or Kanban template and start working within an hour. A proper rollout is different: designing issue types, fields, workflows, permission schemes, notification schemes, boards and dashboards in company-managed spaces is real administrative work, and most organisations of any size have a dedicated Jira administrator or use an Atlassian Solution Partner.

#### Learning Curve
Day-to-day use, such as updating a work item or moving a card, is straightforward. Planning, JQL, workflows and administration take much longer to learn, and Jira's terminology (schemes, screens, resolutions, components) is unfamiliar to non-developers. Capterra's ease-of-use sub-score of 4.1 is Jira's lowest, and on G2 a steep learning curve and challenging setup are among the most cited drawbacks. Training resources help, but budget time for onboarding.

#### Interface and Performance
Atlassian has redesigned Jira's navigation several times, and the current interface is cleaner than older versions. Users still report clutter: on Capterra, about 64% of reviews that discuss navigation describe it as cluttered or hard to learn. Performance on large sites is the most negative theme, with around 84% of reviews mentioning slowness at scale being negative. Neither is a reason to avoid Jira on its own, but large organisations should test performance with realistic data during the trial.

### Jira Mobile App
Jira's iOS and Android apps let you view boards and backlogs, update and transition work items, comment and review notifications while away from your desk. They are well suited to checking on a sprint, triaging a bug or replying to an @mention.
Planning, JQL-heavy work, reporting and administration are better done on desktop. Treat the mobile app as a companion for staying up to date rather than a full replacement for the web app.

### Jira Pricing
Jira Cloud has four plans. Atlassian prices Standard and Premium progressively: the per-user rate falls as your user count rises, so its pricing page works as a calculator rather than a fixed list. The figures below are the commonly quoted list prices for small teams on monthly billing; Capterra lists Standard from $7.91 per user/month. Annual subscriptions are priced in user tiers and can work out cheaper.
| Plan | Published price | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0, up to 10 users | Small teams and startups trying Scrum or Kanban |
| Standard | About $7.91/user/month (monthly, small teams) | Growing teams needing permissions, more storage and support |
| Premium | About $14.54/user/month (monthly, small teams) | Multi-team organisations needing advanced planning and 24/7 support |
| Enterprise | Contact sales (annual only) | Large organisations with multiple sites and strict governance |
Atlassian offers discounts of 75% for eligible community (non-profit) organisations and 50% for eligible academic institutions. Monthly plans are billed on the highest number of users during the billing period. Pricing checked on Atlassian's Jira pricing page and licensing pages on 7 October 2026; always use Atlassian's calculator for your exact team size before buying.

#### Jira Free Plan
The Free plan supports up to 10 users, includes Scrum and Kanban boards, backlogs, the timeline, reports and basic automation, and comes with 2 GB of storage and community support only. It is one of the most generous free plans for software teams: a small startup can run real sprints on it. The limits are the 10-user cap, limited permissions and roles, the small automation allowance and no Rovo AI. Once you pass 10 users, every user must be on a paid plan.

#### Jira Standard Plan
Standard (about $7.91 per user/month on monthly billing for small teams) raises the limit to up to 100,000 users and adds advanced permissions and roles, work-level security, 250 GB of storage, data residency, audit logs, anonymous access, a larger automation allowance, business-hours support and Rovo with 25 AI credits per user per month. It is the plan most single teams and small engineering departments should start with.

#### Jira Premium Plan
Premium (about $14.54 per user/month on monthly billing for small teams) adds Plans for cross-team planning and capacity, unlimited storage, a larger automation allowance, a 99.9% uptime SLA, 24/7 support with one-hour response times for critical issues, sandboxes, release tracks for controlling when changes reach users, admin insights, IP allowlisting and 70 AI credits per user per month. It suits organisations coordinating several teams or running scaled Agile.

#### Jira Enterprise Plan
Enterprise is quote-based and billed annually only. It adds a 99.95% uptime SLA, 24/7 Enterprise support, up to 150 sites, the highest automation allowance and 150 AI credits per user per month, and includes Atlassian Guard features such as single sign-on, SCIM provisioning and Active Directory sync, which lower plans need to buy separately. It is designed for large, regulated or multi-business-unit organisations.

#### Jira Free Trial
Atlassian offers free trials of Standard and Premium. Its licensing FAQ says Standard can be trialled for 14 days and Premium or Enterprise for 30 days, although some product pages mention a 7-day trial for new customers, so check the length at sign-up. No credit card is needed to start; if you do not add one when the Standard trial ends, the site falls back to the Free plan. Use the trial to run a real sprint with your real team rather than clicking through sample data.

#### Hidden Costs to Budget For
- **Marketplace apps**, usually priced per user across your whole site
- **Confluence**, if you want documentation linked to Jira (a separate subscription)
- **Atlassian Guard**, for SSO and user provisioning on Free, Standard and Premium
- **Administration time**, or a Solution Partner, for larger rollouts

### Jira Pros and Cons

##### Pros
- Best-in-class Scrum and Kanban tooling
- Highly configurable work types, fields and workflows
- JQL makes almost any question about the work answerable
- Deep integrations with Bitbucket, GitHub, GitLab and CI/CD
- Free plan genuinely usable for up to 10 users
- Marketplace with more than 3,000 apps
- Scales from startups to very large enterprises
- Rovo AI included on all paid plans
- Mature automation with natural-language rule creation
- Strong Atlassian ecosystem and partner network

##### Cons
- Steep learning curve, especially for administration and JQL
- Needs a dedicated administrator as usage grows
- Interface can feel cluttered, particularly for business users
- Users report slow performance on large sites
- Documentation needs Confluence, a separate product
- Marketplace apps add per-user cost
- Advanced planning and higher AI allowances need Premium or Enterprise
- SSO and provisioning need Atlassian Guard below Enterprise
- Less natural for creative, marketing or operations teams
This matches what users report: Jira's depth for Agile and developer work is widely valued, while complexity, administration and interface clutter are its most consistent drawbacks.

On **Capterra**, Jira is rated **4.4/5 from 15,493 reviews**, with sub-scores of **4.4 for features**, **4.1 for ease of use**, **4.3 for value for money** and **4.2 for customer service** (checked 7 October 2026). On **G2**, it is rated **4.3/5 from 7,988 reviews** (checked 5 October 2026). The themes below summarise these third-party reviews in our own words, not Atlassian's testimonials.
**Positive themes.** Reviewers most often praise Agile workflow support, oversight of projects and progress visualisation; in Capterra's topic summaries these are about 97%, 97% and 96% positive respectively. G2 reviewers highlight ease of use for Agile workflows, flexibility and powerful task tracking. Integration with developer tools and Confluence, and the ability to tailor workflows, come up repeatedly.
**Negative themes.** The most common complaints are bugs and glitches (about 57% of reviews on the topic are negative), slow performance at scale (about 84% negative) and cluttered, hard-to-learn navigation (about 64% negative). G2 reviewers cite the steep learning curve, complex interface and processes, and challenging initial setup.
When reading reviews yourself, check whether a review was invited or incentivised by the vendor; both Capterra and G2 label these. Reviews from organisations of your size, and from roles like yours, are more informative than the overall average, because a developer and a marketing manager often have very different experiences of Jira.

### Jira Customer Support
Support depends on your plan: the Free plan relies on the Atlassian Community and documentation; Standard includes support during local business hours; Premium adds 24/7 support with one-hour response times for critical issues; and Enterprise includes 24/7 Enterprise support. Atlassian also provides extensive documentation, Atlassian University training courses and a very large community forum, and a global network of Solution Partners offers implementation and administration services.
Capterra's customer service sub-score of 4.2/5 suggests a generally reasonable experience, though individual reviews vary. In practice, many Jira questions are answered faster in the Community or by an internal administrator than through a support ticket.

### Jira Security
Jira provides space permissions, user roles, work-level security to restrict who can see individual work items, audit logs, data residency options, and encryption in transit and at rest on paid plans. Administrators can manage password policies, session duration and mobile device management. Premium adds IP allowlisting and admin insights.
Single sign-on, SCIM user provisioning and Active Directory sync are included on Enterprise and require an Atlassian Guard subscription on other plans. Atlassian's Trust Center displays AICPA SOC, ISO 27001, PCI DSS and FedRAMP compliance marks; confirm the current certifications and their scope for Jira Cloud as part of procurement. Atlassian also runs a separate Government Cloud offering, where Rovo is not available.

### Jira for Different Types of Teams

#### Jira for Software Development Teams
This is Jira's core use case: backlogs, sprints, story points, bug tracking, releases and code integration in one place. Teams following [agile software development](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/agile/agile-software-development/) will find almost every practice supported.

#### Jira for IT and DevOps Teams
IT and platform teams use Kanban boards, automation and deployment tracking to manage infrastructure work and changes. Service desks are better handled in Jira Service Management, which shares the same platform.

#### Jira for Product Managers
Product managers use Jira for backlog management, roadmaps and release planning, often alongside Jira Product Discovery for ideas and Confluence for specifications. Writing good [user stories](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/agile/user-stories/) and keeping epics tidy is what makes Jira roadmaps trustworthy.

#### Jira for Business and Marketing Teams
Business teams can work in Jira with list, calendar and board views, forms and business templates, which is especially useful when they work closely with engineering. However, they usually find the interface and terminology heavier than tools built for them; marketing teams that rarely interact with developers will often adopt a more visual tool faster.

#### Jira for Small Businesses and Startups
For a startup engineering team of up to 10 people, the Free plan is hard to beat, and Standard stays affordable as you grow. For a small business whose work is mainly non-technical, Jira is usually more tool than it needs.

#### Jira for Enterprises
Large organisations use Jira at scale for portfolios of software teams, scaled frameworks such as [SAFe](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/agile/scaled-agile-framework-safe/), and strict governance. Premium or Enterprise is normally needed for cross-team planning, uptime commitments and identity controls.

### Who Should Use Jira?

- Organisations already using Atlassian tools

##### Look elsewhere if
- Marketing, creative or business teams needing a simple tool
- Teams without someone to administer it

Jira fits teams of almost any size, from small software teams running their first sprints to large organisations coordinating many teams and releases. Beginners can start with a ready-made Scrum or Kanban template and simple board, then add backlogs, timelines, automation and dashboards as their work grows. ### Is Jira Worth It?
Jira is likely worth it if you:
- Run software, IT or product work using Scrum or Kanban.
- Want work items linked to code, builds and deployments.
- Need configurable workflows and precise, query-based reporting.
- Already use Confluence, Bitbucket or other Atlassian products.
- Have, or can appoint, someone to administer Jira properly.
- Expect to scale to many teams and want a tool that will grow with you.
It may not be worth it if:
- Your teams are mainly marketing, creative or operations staff.
- You want a simple, visual tool with almost no setup.
- Nobody will own the configuration and keep it tidy.
- You need Gantt charts with critical path and baselines for plan-driven projects.
- You would need many paid Marketplace apps to fill gaps.
Our verdict: Jira is the strongest Agile tool for software teams in our review, which is why it scores 10/10 for Agile in our methodology, and its free plan makes it easy to start. Its overall score of 8.6/10 and #6 ranking in our [project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/) review reflect the cost of that depth: a steep learning curve, real administration effort and a less comfortable fit for non-technical teams. Run a real sprint on the free plan or a trial before committing your whole organisation.

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: Is Jira good project management software?**
Yes, especially for software and IT teams. Jira offers mature Scrum and Kanban boards, configurable workflows, JQL and deep developer integrations, and it is rated 4.4/5 on Capterra. It is less suited to non-technical teams that want a simple, visual tool, and it needs someone to administer it.

**Q: Is Jira free?**
Yes. Jira's Free plan supports up to 10 users and includes Scrum and Kanban boards, backlogs, the timeline, reports and basic automation, with 2 GB of storage and community support. Rovo AI, advanced permissions and higher limits require a paid plan.

**Q: How much does Jira cost?**
Jira is free for up to 10 users. For small teams on monthly billing, Standard is about $7.91 and Premium about $14.54 per user/month, with the per-user rate falling as team size grows; Enterprise is quote-based and annual only (checked 7 October 2026). Use Atlassian's calculator for your exact team size.

**Q: Does Jira have a free trial?**
Yes. Atlassian offers free trials of Standard and Premium. Its licensing FAQ gives 14 days for Standard and 30 days for Premium, though some pages mention shorter trials for new customers. No credit card is needed to start, and an expired Standard trial falls back to the Free plan.

**Q: Is Jira easy to use?**
Basic use is straightforward, but Jira has a steep learning curve for planning, JQL, workflows and administration. Ease of use is its lowest Capterra sub-score at 4.1/5, and many reviewers mention cluttered navigation. Most organisations benefit from a trained administrator.

**Q: What is Jira used for?**
Jira is mainly used for Agile software development: backlogs, sprints, bug tracking, release management and linking work to code. IT, DevOps and product teams also use it, and business teams can manage requests and projects with forms, list and calendar views.

**Q: What is JQL in Jira?**
JQL (Jira Query Language) is Jira's search language for finding work items by any field, such as status, assignee, dates or labels. Saved JQL filters power boards, dashboards and automation. On paid plans, Rovo can convert plain-language questions into JQL and fix query errors.

**Q: Is Jira better than Asana?**
For software teams running Scrum or Kanban, Jira is usually stronger; for cross-functional business teams that want simpler, faster adoption, Asana is often a better fit. See our [Jira vs Asana comparison](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/asana-vs-jira/).

**Q: Is Jira better than monday.com?**
Jira offers deeper Agile tooling, JQL and developer integrations; monday.com is more visual and usually easier for non-technical teams. See our [Jira vs monday.com comparison](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/monday-vs-jira/).

**Q: Does Jira have Gantt charts?**
Not in the classic sense. Every plan has a timeline view for epics and work with basic dependencies, and Premium adds Plans for cross-team roadmaps and capacity. There is no built-in critical path or baseline tracking; Marketplace apps can add full Gantt charts.

**Q: Does Jira have AI?**
Yes. Atlassian's Rovo AI is included on Standard, Premium and Enterprise plans, with 25, 70 and 150 AI credits per user per month respectively. It offers natural-language search, writing help, summaries, work breakdown, natural-language automation and agents. It is not listed for the Free plan.

**Q: Can non-software teams use Jira?**
Yes. Jira includes business templates, forms, list and calendar views, and Jira Work Management has been merged into Jira. Business teams that collaborate closely with engineering benefit most; teams that rarely work with developers often find more visual tools easier.

**Q: What are the main disadvantages of Jira?**
The main disadvantages are the steep learning curve, the administration it needs, a cluttered interface for casual users, reported slowness on large sites, the extra cost of Marketplace apps and Confluence, and advanced planning and SSO sitting on higher plans or add-ons.

**Q: Does Jira integrate with Slack, Microsoft Teams and GitHub?**
Yes. Jira integrates with Slack and Microsoft Teams for notifications and creating work items, and with GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket to show branches, commits and pull requests on work items. The Atlassian Marketplace lists more than 3,000 apps and integrations.

**Q: Is Jira suitable for small businesses?**
It is a strong choice for small software teams, since the Free plan covers up to 10 users. For small businesses whose work is mainly non-technical, Jira is often more complex than needed, and a simpler tool may be adopted faster.
How we review.
Rankings and scores are the editorial opinion of the Neural Project Institute, based on features, pricing, ease of use, scalability and published user ratings. Prices were checked on vendors' pricing pages and ratings on G2 and Capterra on 5 October 2026; both change often, so confirm on the vendor's site before buying. We are independent and do not receive payment for rankings.

# Microsoft Planner Review 2026: Is It Worth It?

URL: https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/microsoft-planner/
Section: Project management software reviews
Summary: Our Microsoft Planner review covers basic vs premium plans, pricing, Copilot, Teams integration, pros and cons, and whether Planner is worth it in 2026.


## Microsoft Planner Review 2026: Is It Worth It?
Microsoft Planner is Microsoft's task and project management app for Microsoft 365. Since Microsoft folded Project for the web into it in 2025, Planner covers everything from simple team task boards to scheduled projects with Gantt charts, dependencies, sprints and goals. Its biggest strengths are that basic Planner comes with most Microsoft 365 business subscriptions and that it lives inside Teams and Outlook, where many organisations already work; the main trade-offs are a lighter feature set than specialist platforms and licensing that is genuinely confusing. This review covers basic and premium plans, pricing, scheduling, Copilot, collaboration, integrations, ease of use, reporting, security and overall value.

Microsoft Planner is the convenient default for organisations that already run on Microsoft 365. Basic plans cover everyday team task management at no extra cost, and the premium plans now offer real project scheduling, including timelines, dependencies, sprints and, on Plan 3, baselines and critical path. The trade-offs: reporting and customisation are basic without Power BI, AI needs a separate Copilot licence, basic and premium plans behave differently, and Microsoft's frequent product changes make it hard to know exactly what you are buying.
