### What Is Microsoft Planner?
Microsoft Planner is a cloud-based task and work management app that is part of Microsoft 365. Microsoft describes it as a way to "manage your tasks, to-do lists, plans, and projects across Microsoft 365 apps in one place". The same app runs in a web browser, as the Planner app in Microsoft Teams, and on iOS and Android.
Planner now contains two kinds of plan, and understanding the difference is the key to this review:
- **Basic plans** are the original Planner: Kanban-style boards of tasks grouped into buckets, with assignees, due dates, labels and checklists. They are included with Microsoft 365 business, enterprise and education subscriptions.
- **Premium plans** are what used to be Microsoft Project for the web: scheduled projects with a timeline (Gantt) view, task dependencies, milestones, sprints, goals and custom fields. They require a Planner Plan 1 or Planner and Project Plan 3 licence.
Organisations typically use Planner for:
- **Team task boards**, such as a marketing team's weekly work or an office move
- **Meeting follow-ups**, turning actions from Teams meetings into assigned tasks
- **IT and operations work**, such as rollouts, onboarding checklists and maintenance tasks
- **Scheduled projects** with dependencies and milestones, on premium plans
- **Agile work** using backlogs and sprints, on premium plans
- **Personal task management**, through the My Day and My Tasks views that pull together tasks from across Microsoft 365
Planner is not a standalone product that you would normally buy on its own. Its value comes from the fact that it sits inside the Microsoft 365 environment: the same identities, groups, Teams channels, Outlook mailboxes and security policies.

### Who Owns Microsoft Planner?
Planner is made by Microsoft Corporation, the Redmond-based software company. It was released to Microsoft 365 (then Office 365) subscribers in June 2016.
Microsoft has since consolidated its cloud project tools into Planner. In a 2025 Microsoft 365 message centre notice, Microsoft said it would "retire Project for the web and will redirect its users to Planner for the web", starting in August 2025, with premium plans "automatically" available in Planner. Microsoft's pricing pages also state that Project Online was being retired on 30 September 2026. For buyers, the practical point is that Planner is now Microsoft's main cloud project management tool, and the desktop Project application remains for heavy-duty scheduling.

### How Does Microsoft Planner Work?
Planner organises work in a simple structure:
- **Plans** hold the work for a team or project. Each basic plan is connected to a **Microsoft 365 group**, which also gives the team a shared mailbox, files and, optionally, a Teams channel.
- **Buckets** are the columns of a plan, such as To do, In progress and Done, or one bucket per workstream.
- **Tasks** carry an assignee (or several), start and due dates, priority, labels, notes, attachments and a checklist.
- **Premium plans** add summary tasks and subtasks, dependencies, milestones, custom fields, sprints and goals. Microsoft documents that premium plans, formerly projects in Project for the web, are backed by **Dataverse**, the Power Platform data store.
- **My Day, My Tasks and My Plans** give each person a cross-plan view of their own work, including tasks from Microsoft To Do and flagged emails from Outlook.
A basic plan can be converted to a premium plan when a team needs scheduling; admins can switch this conversion off with a PowerShell setting.
A typical workflow looks like this:
**Actions agreed in a Teams meeting → tasks added to the team's plan → owners assigned and dates set → work moved across the board → progress checked in the Charts view or, on premium, the timeline**
For example, an IT team planning a laptop refresh creates a basic plan in its Teams channel, adds buckets for each office, and assigns tasks to technicians. If the project grows to include supplier deliveries and dependencies, the plan can be upgraded to a premium plan so the project lead can schedule work on a timeline and see which delays affect the go-live date.

### Microsoft Planner Key Features

#### Board, Grid, Schedule and Charts Views
Every plan includes the core views. **Board** shows tasks as cards in buckets, the familiar [Kanban board](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/kanban/kanban-boards/) layout; **Grid** shows tasks as a sortable list; **Schedule** (basic plans) shows tasks on a calendar; and **Charts** summarises tasks by status, bucket, priority and assignee. Filtering and grouping, copying plans and exporting to Excel are available in both basic and premium plans.
Basic plans have a few features that premium plans do not, according to Microsoft's comparison: the Schedule view, recurring tasks, Outlook calendar and SharePoint integration, and the Tasks app in Teams mobile. This is a common source of confusion when teams upgrade. If you just need a simple board, our [Kanban board template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/kanban-board-template/) follows the same idea.

#### My Day, My Tasks and To Do
My Day is a personal list of what you plan to work on today, and My Tasks gathers tasks assigned to you from every plan, together with personal tasks from Microsoft To Do and flagged emails from Outlook. For people who work across several teams, this is one of Planner's most useful features, because it removes the need to check each plan separately. It works like a built-in [to-do list](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/to-do-list-template/) connected to team work.

#### Timeline (Gantt), Dependencies and Milestones
Planner Plan 1 adds the **Timeline (Gantt) view**, **task dependencies**, **milestones**, summary tasks and subtasks, and **custom calendars** that set which days count as working days. Microsoft's support documentation describes finish-to-start, start-to-start, start-to-finish and finish-to-finish links, with a scheduler that "will automatically update execution dates for your plan" when something changes.
This turns Planner from a task board into a genuine [Gantt chart](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/gantt-chart/) tool for moderately complex projects. Understanding how [task dependencies](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/task-dependencies/) and [project milestones](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-milestones/) work will help you get more from it.

#### Baselines, Critical Path and Lead and Lag
Microsoft's pricing page lists **baselines and critical path** and **advanced dependencies with lead and lag** among the features of Planner and Project Plan 3, alongside task history, the Assignments view and the right to create portfolios. A [project baseline](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-baseline/) lets you compare the current schedule with the original plan, and the [critical path](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/critical-path-method/) highlights the tasks that determine the end date. [Leads and lags](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/leads-and-lags/) allow overlaps and waiting time between linked tasks.
Plan 3 also includes the Project desktop application, so project managers who need full scheduling, resource levelling and cost tracking can still use it. In our assessment this is Planner's strongest card for organisations moving off Project Online: scheduling depth that most work management tools at the same price do not offer.

#### Backlogs and Sprints
Premium plans support Agile planning with a prioritised **backlog** and time-boxed **sprints** that tasks can be moved into. It covers the basics of [sprints](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/agile/what-is-a-sprint/) and a [product backlog](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/scrum/product-backlog/), which is enough for teams that run light Agile processes alongside other work. Microsoft's pages do not describe story points, velocity or burndown reporting, so software teams that rely on Scrum metrics should test it carefully. Our [sprint planning template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/sprint-planning-template/) shows what a sprint plan should capture.

#### Goals
Plan 1 includes **project goals**: you set goals for a plan and link tasks to them so progress can be tracked against what the project is meant to achieve. Microsoft's product page says goals can be defined "at the organizational, team, or project level". This is lighter than a dedicated OKR system, but it is useful for keeping a project focused. Our [OKR template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/okr-template/) can help you define good goals first.

#### Custom Fields, Conditional Colouring and Templates
Premium plans let you create up to ten custom fields per plan (text, date, number, yes/no and choice), and conditional colouring rules highlight tasks that match a condition, such as overdue or high priority. Planner includes basic plan templates for every user and premium templates on Plan 1; Microsoft lists ready-made templates for marketing, sales, software development, IT, HR, project management and operations.
Ten custom fields is enough for most teams, but much less than the configurable data models in tools such as monday.com or Wrike.

#### Portfolios
Microsoft's pricing page lists **view portfolios** on Plan 1 and **create portfolios** on Plan 3. Portfolios group premium plans so managers can see several projects together; Microsoft told Project for the web users to migrate their old Roadmaps into Portfolios, because Planner does not support roadmaps. This helps with [managing multiple projects](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/managing-multiple-projects/), but it is not a full portfolio management system.

#### People and Assignments Views
The **People view** (premium) shows how work is distributed across the team, helping managers spot people who are over- or under-allocated. The **Assignments view** (Plan 3) lets project managers set effort per person by day, week or month for more precise resource and cost estimates. These support basic [resource allocation](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/resource-allocation/), but they are not a substitute for dedicated resource management.

#### Plan Size Limits
Microsoft's comparison lists a limit of **9,000 tasks** for basic plans and **3,000 tasks** for premium plans. Most team plans never approach these limits, but large programmes should be split into several plans. Capterra reviewers also note that Planner becomes harder to manage on very large projects.

### Microsoft Planner AI Features
Planner's AI features come from **Microsoft 365 Copilot**, which is sold separately. Microsoft's Planner pages are explicit: "Access to AI capabilities in Planner and Planner in Teams requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot license."

#### Copilot in Planner
According to Microsoft, Copilot in Planner can create buckets and tasks from your planning goals, help you "set clear, measurable goals", generate status reports and keep you up to date on high-priority tasks, potential risks and team availability. AI-assisted templates and plan creation are also listed on the pricing page.

#### Planner Agent
The **Planner agent**, previously called the Project Manager agent, is an AI agent you can assign tasks to. According to Microsoft 365 message centre notice MC1250279, as reported by Office 365 for IT Pros, it was renamed in March 2026 and extended to basic as well as premium plans, with general availability expected by early May 2026. When a task is assigned to it, the agent works in the background and produces a written outline of how to complete the task in an editable Loop component, which plan members can review, regenerate and discuss.
The agent needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, and the agent activity tab was reported as available in the browser and Teams but not in the Planner mobile app.

#### Our Assessment of Planner AI
The AI features are useful for drafting plans, goals and status updates, but they come at a meaningful extra cost: Copilot is $30 per user/month, paid yearly, which can triple the cost of a Plan 1 seat. Copilot also works across Word, Excel, Outlook and Teams, so organisations already buying it for other reasons get Planner's AI features as part of that. Treat AI output as a first draft that a person checks.

### Microsoft Planner Collaboration Features
Collaboration in Planner leans on the rest of Microsoft 365. Plans can be added as tabs in Teams channels, tasks can be created from Teams messages and meetings, notifications arrive in Teams and Outlook, and plans can be embedded in Loop. Premium plans add **task chat**, which Microsoft describes as "real-time, threaded conversations directly in tasks" with @mentions, and **task history**, which shows recent edits and schedule changes.
This is convenient for internal teams: there are no extra accounts to manage, and work stays next to the conversations that created it. It is less suited to working with clients or freelancers, who need to be set up as guests in your Microsoft 365 tenant rather than simply invited to a project, and there is no built-in proofing or approval of creative assets. Our guide to [project communication management](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-communication-management/) covers how to set up good habits whatever tool you use.

### Microsoft Planner Reporting and Dashboards
Reporting in Planner is simple. The **Charts view** shows how many tasks are not started, in progress, late or complete, broken down by bucket, priority and person. Premium plans add the timeline, People view, goals and, on Plan 3, baselines for schedule comparison. Plans can be exported to Excel.
For anything more, Microsoft points customers to **Power BI**, which can report on Planner data across many plans; because premium plans are stored in Dataverse, that data is available to the Power Platform. This works well for organisations with Power BI skills, but it means building reports rather than using them out of the box. "Reporting capabilities are somewhat basic" is one of the cons Capterra highlights from reviews, and in our assessment this is Planner's clearest gap against tools like Wrike, Smartsheet or monday.com. A regular written [project status report](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-status-report/) still fills the gap for many teams.

### Microsoft Planner Integrations
Planner's integrations are mainly within Microsoft's own ecosystem:
- **Microsoft Teams**: the Planner app, plan tabs in channels and tasks created from messages
- **Outlook**: flagged emails appear in My Tasks, and basic plans can be shown in Outlook calendars
- **Microsoft To Do**: personal and Planner tasks appear in one list
- **Microsoft Loop**: plans and tasks can be added to Loop pages
- **SharePoint**: Planner web part and full-page app (basic plans)
- **Power Automate, Power Apps and Power BI**: automation, custom apps and reporting
- **Microsoft Graph API**: programmatic access to Planner data
- **Project desktop**: included with Plan 3
Planner does not have its own rules engine of the kind found in Asana or monday.com. Automation is built in **Power Automate**, which can connect Planner with hundreds of third-party services but adds a layer of complexity and, for some connectors, separate licensing. Microsoft's pricing page notes that some of the Microsoft app integrations require a separate licence. Organisations that use Slack, Google Workspace, Jira or Salesforce as their main tools will find Planner much less connected than tools built to sit between many vendors.

### Microsoft Planner Ease of Use

#### Initial Setup
For a team already on Microsoft 365, setup takes minutes: open Planner in Teams or on the web, create a plan, add buckets and assign tasks. There is nothing to install and no new accounts to provision. Premium plans need licences assigned by an administrator, and organisations should decide early which teams get basic plans and which need premium ones.

#### Learning Curve
Basic Planner is one of the easiest project tools to learn. Capterra reviewers give it **4.5/5 for ease of use**, and "simple and easy-to-use task management" is one of the pros Capterra highlights. Premium plans are more demanding, as scheduling with dependencies, baselines and critical path requires some project management knowledge.

#### Interface and Licensing Confusion
The interface is clean and familiar to anyone who uses Microsoft 365. The confusion comes from elsewhere: basic and premium plans look similar but support different features (recurring tasks and the Schedule view are basic-only; timelines and custom fields are premium-only), Microsoft's support pages note that apps and workflows built for basic plans "will require modification to work on premium plans", and AI requires yet another licence. Microsoft's licensing documentation says that Planner "includes full editing on basic plans and basic editing capabilities on premium plans", while premium features need a premium subscription, so check exactly who needs a premium licence before rolling out.

### Microsoft Planner Mobile Apps
Planner has iOS and Android apps for viewing plans, updating tasks, adding comments and attachments, and receiving notifications. Planner tasks are also available in the Teams mobile app and in Microsoft To Do on mobile.
The mobile apps are fine for updates on the move. Scheduling premium plans, reviewing the timeline and working with the Planner agent's output are better done in the browser or Teams on a larger screen.

### Microsoft Planner Pricing
Microsoft's published Planner options are below. Prices are per user per month in US dollars and are shown as "paid yearly" with an annual subscription that auto-renews; Microsoft's Planner pricing page does not show monthly billing prices.
| Plan | Price | Main additions | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Microsoft Planner (basic) | Included in Microsoft 365 | Grid, Board, Schedule and Charts views; basic templates | Teams that need simple task boards |
| Planner Plan 1 | $10/user/month, paid yearly | Timeline (Gantt), dependencies, milestones, sprints, goals, custom fields, view portfolios | Teams running scheduled projects |
| Planner and Project Plan 3 | $30/user/month, paid yearly | Baselines and critical path, lead and lag, Assignments view, create portfolios, task history, Project desktop | Project managers and PMOs |
| Microsoft 365 Copilot (add-on) | $30/user/month, paid yearly | Copilot in Planner, Planner agent, AI status reports | Organisations using AI across Microsoft 365 |
Microsoft says that once a paid subscription begins, you have a seven-day cancellation window for a prorated refund. Pricing checked on Microsoft's Planner pricing page on 7 October 2026; prices vary by region and by agreement type, so confirm before buying.

#### Is Microsoft Planner Free?
Basic Planner has no separate price: Microsoft's licensing documentation says Planner "is part of the M365 and Office 365 suite subscriptions", and Planner in Teams requires a subscription that includes Teams. There is no free stand-alone Planner plan for people without Microsoft 365. Basic plans include up to 9,000 tasks per plan, the Board, Grid, Schedule and Charts views, and integration with Teams, Outlook and To Do.

#### Planner Plan 1
At $10 per user/month, paid yearly, Plan 1 unlocks premium plans: subtasks, premium templates, backlogs and sprints, task dependencies, the Calendar, Timeline (Gantt) and People views, project goals, milestones, custom task fields and the ability to view portfolios. For most teams that need scheduling, this is the right level.

#### Planner and Project Plan 3
At $30 per user/month, paid yearly, Plan 3 adds task history, the Assignments view, the ability to create portfolios, baselines and critical path, advanced dependencies with lead and lag, and the Project desktop app, which Microsoft says can be installed on up to five PCs per user. It is aimed at project managers and PMOs; usually only the people who build and manage schedules need it.

#### Microsoft 365 Copilot
Copilot costs $30 per user/month, paid yearly, and requires an eligible Microsoft 365 subscription. It covers Copilot across Microsoft 365, not only in Planner. Microsoft also promotes a Microsoft 365 Copilot Business offer for organisations with up to 300 users; check the current price, as the discount shown on the pricing page was a time-limited offer.

#### Microsoft Planner Free Trial
Microsoft offers a one-month free trial of Planner Plan 1 and Planner and Project Plan 3. Its terms state that "a credit card is required to begin a one-month trial" and that the trial converts to a paid subscription unless cancelled. Microsoft's support pages also describe starting a free 30-day premium trial from within Planner, or requesting a licence from your administrator. Note that Capterra currently lists the free trial as "not available" and still shows a Planner and Project Plan 5 at $55, which does not appear on Microsoft's Planner pricing page.

### Microsoft Planner Pros and Cons

##### Pros
- Basic Planner included with most Microsoft 365 subscriptions
- Works inside Teams, Outlook, To Do and Loop
- Very easy to learn for simple task boards
- Low-cost Plan 1 adds Gantt, dependencies, sprints and goals
- Plan 3 adds baselines, critical path and Project desktop
- Uses existing Microsoft 365 identity, security and admin
- My Day and My Tasks unify tasks across Microsoft 365
- Available in government clouds

##### Cons

- Basic and premium plans support different features
- Reporting is basic without Power BI
- Only ten custom fields per premium plan
- No built-in rules engine; automation needs Power Automate
- AI requires a separate $30 Copilot licence
- Weak for client collaboration, proofing and approvals
- Frequent product changes and retirements confuse buyers
This matches what users report: people value Planner's simplicity and its integration with Microsoft 365, while basic reporting, limited depth for large projects and licensing confusion are the most common drawbacks.

### Microsoft Planner Customer Support
Support is provided through Microsoft 365's normal channels: administrators raise service requests in the Microsoft 365 admin centre, and users have Microsoft's support articles, Microsoft Learn documentation, training videos and the Microsoft Tech Community forum. Capterra lists email/help desk, knowledge base, forum, phone and chat support, and training through documentation, videos, webinars and live sessions. Large organisations often get help through their Microsoft partner or enterprise support agreement.
Capterra's customer service sub-score is 4.2/5. In practice, the quality of support depends on your Microsoft agreement and partner, so ask about Planner-specific help, especially for premium plan migrations, before buying.

### Microsoft Planner Security
Planner runs within Microsoft 365, so it uses the same Microsoft Entra ID identities, sign-in policies and admin controls as the rest of the suite, which is one of its main advantages for IT teams. Basic plans are tied to Microsoft 365 groups, and premium plans are stored in Dataverse; administrators can control whether users may convert basic plans into premium ones. Microsoft's service description shows Planner available in commercial, education, GCC, GCC High and DoD environments, although some features (such as To Do integration and the Tasks app in Teams) are not available in every government cloud.
Microsoft refers customers to its Trust Center for security and compliance information. Microsoft 365 publishes extensive audit reports, but confirm in the Service Trust Portal which certifications cover Planner and Dataverse in your region as part of procurement.

### Microsoft Planner for Different Types of Teams

#### Microsoft Planner for IT and Operations Teams
IT and operations teams are a natural fit: rollouts, onboarding checklists and maintenance tasks can be run in basic plans inside Teams, with Power Automate for repeatable steps.

Project managers get Gantt scheduling and dependencies on Plan 1, and baselines, critical path and Project desktop on Plan 3. A [PMO](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-management-office-pmo/) can use portfolios and Power BI for oversight, though portfolio and [capacity planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/capacity-planning/) features are lighter than in dedicated PPM tools.

#### Microsoft Planner for Small Businesses
Small businesses on Microsoft 365 Business plans already have basic Planner, so it is the obvious place to start. Plan 1 at $10 is reasonable for the people who need scheduling. Small businesses not on Microsoft 365 have no reason to choose Planner.

#### Microsoft Planner for Enterprises and the Public Sector
Large organisations benefit from central licensing, Entra ID security and availability in government clouds, which simplifies procurement considerably.

#### Microsoft Planner for Software Teams
Backlogs and sprints cover light Agile work, but software teams that need story points, velocity, releases and developer integrations will usually prefer a dedicated tool; see our guide to [Scrum software tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/scrum/scrum-software-tools/).

#### Microsoft Planner for Marketing Teams
Marketing teams can plan campaigns on boards and timelines and work in Teams, but Planner has no proofing, approvals or request forms of its own.

### Is Microsoft Planner Worth It?
Microsoft Planner is likely worth it if you:
- Already use Microsoft 365 and Teams across the organisation.
- Want simple, shared task boards without buying another tool.
- Need affordable Gantt scheduling, dependencies and sprints (Plan 1).
- Are moving off Project for the web or Project Online and want to stay with Microsoft.
- Value central identity, security and licensing over specialist features.
- Already pay for Microsoft 365 Copilot.
It may not be worth it if:
- Your organisation does not use Microsoft 365.
- You need rich dashboards and reporting without building them in Power BI.
- You work heavily with clients and freelancers outside your organisation.
- You need built-in automation rules, request forms, proofing or approvals.
- You need detailed time tracking, budgets or resource management.
Our verdict: Planner's strength is convenience. It is already there for most Microsoft 365 organisations, it works inside the tools people use all day, and the premium plans add real scheduling at a fair price. Its limitations are lighter reporting, customisation and automation than specialist platforms, and licensing that takes effort to understand. That balance is why it ranks seventh in our [project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/) review.

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: Is Microsoft Planner good project management software?**
Yes, for Microsoft 365 organisations. Planner offers easy task boards in every plan and, with a premium licence, timelines, dependencies, sprints and goals, and it is rated 4.3/5 on Capterra. Its reporting, customisation and automation are lighter than specialist tools, so complex projects may need more.

**Q: Is Microsoft Planner free?**
Basic Planner has no separate price because it is included with Microsoft 365 business, enterprise and education subscriptions. There is no free stand-alone Planner plan for people without Microsoft 365. Premium features require Planner Plan 1 or Planner and Project Plan 3.

**Q: How much does Microsoft Planner cost?**
Basic Planner is included in Microsoft 365. Planner Plan 1 costs $10 per user/month and Planner and Project Plan 3 costs $30 per user/month, both paid yearly. Microsoft 365 Copilot, needed for AI features, is a $30 per user/month add-on (checked 7 October 2026).

**Q: Does Microsoft Planner have a free trial?**
Yes. Microsoft offers a one-month free trial of Planner Plan 1 and Planner and Project Plan 3. Its terms say a credit card is required and that the trial converts to a paid subscription unless you cancel. Users can also start a 30-day premium trial from within Planner.

**Q: What is the difference between basic and premium plans in Planner?**
Basic plans are simple task boards included in Microsoft 365. Premium plans, which need Plan 1 or Plan 3, add timeline (Gantt) views, dependencies, milestones, sprints, goals, custom fields and, on Plan 3, baselines and critical path. A few features, such as recurring tasks and the Schedule view, are basic-only.

**Q: Is Microsoft Planner easy to use?**
Yes. Basic Planner is one of the easiest project tools to learn and scores 4.5/5 for ease of use on Capterra. Premium scheduling features need some project management knowledge, and the difference between basic and premium plans can confuse new users.

**Q: Does Microsoft Planner have Gantt charts?**
Yes, on premium plans. Planner Plan 1 includes a Timeline (Gantt) view with task dependencies and milestones, and Planner and Project Plan 3 adds baselines, critical path and dependencies with lead and lag.

**Q: Does Microsoft Planner have Kanban boards?**
Yes. The Board view shows tasks as cards in buckets that you drag between columns. It is available in both basic and premium plans, including the basic Planner included with Microsoft 365.

**Q: Does Microsoft Planner have AI?**
Yes, with a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence. Copilot in Planner can create buckets and tasks from goals, help set goals and produce status reports, and the Planner agent can work on tasks assigned to it. Copilot costs $30 per user/month, paid yearly.

**Q: Has Microsoft Planner replaced Microsoft Project?**
Partly. Microsoft retired Project for the web from August 2025 and moved its features into Planner premium plans, and it announced Project Online's retirement for 30 September 2026. The Project desktop app remains and is included with Planner and Project Plan 3.

**Q: Is Microsoft Planner better than Trello?**
It depends on your setup. Planner suits Microsoft 365 organisations that want boards inside Teams and Outlook plus premium scheduling; Trello suits teams wanting flexible, visual boards that work with many tools. See our [Microsoft Planner vs Trello comparison](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/microsoft-planner/microsoft-planner-vs-trello/).

**Q: Is Microsoft Planner better than Asana?**
Neither is universally better. Planner is cheaper and more convenient for Microsoft 365 organisations; Asana offers richer cross-team features such as rules, forms, portfolios and goals reporting. See our [Asana vs Microsoft Planner comparison](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/asana-vs-microsoft-planner/).

**Q: Can I use Microsoft Planner without Teams?**
Yes. Planner runs in a web browser and on iOS and Android, as well as inside Teams. Microsoft notes that Planner in Teams requires a subscription that includes Teams.

**Q: What are the main disadvantages of Microsoft Planner?**
The main disadvantages are basic reporting without Power BI, limited customisation, no built-in rules engine, weak support for external collaborators, AI that needs a separate Copilot licence, and confusing differences between basic and premium plans.

**Q: Is Microsoft Planner suitable for small businesses?**
Yes, if the business already uses Microsoft 365, because basic Planner is included and Plan 1 adds scheduling for $10 per user/month. Small businesses not on Microsoft 365 will usually find other tools easier to adopt.

# monday.com Review 2026: Is It Worth It?

URL: https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/
Section: Project management software reviews
Summary: Our monday.com review covers features, pricing, seat minimums, AI, integrations, pros and cons, and whether monday.com is worth it in 2026.


## monday.com Review 2026: Is It Worth It?
monday.com is a board-based work management platform that teams use to plan, track and automate projects, campaigns, requests and everyday processes. Its biggest strengths are how quickly people pick it up, its colourful and flexible boards, and its dashboards and automations. The trade-offs are a pricing model built on seat buckets with a three-seat minimum, monthly limits on automation actions and AI credits, and several important project management features reserved for the Pro and Enterprise plans. This review covers pricing, project management, collaboration, automation, AI, integrations, ease of use, reporting and overall value.
- Published 5 September 2026
- Last updated 7 October 2026
- Pricing and Capterra rating checked 7 October 2026

### monday.com review: quick verdict
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Best for | Teams that want an intuitive, visual platform they can shape into almost any workflow, with fast adoption across non-technical departments |
| Less suitable for | Very small or cost-sensitive teams (seats are sold in buckets), and teams that need advanced scheduling or resource control on a tight budget |
| Our overall score | **9.1/10**, ranked #2 in our [top 10 project management tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/) |
| Price | Free plan for up to 2 seats; Basic $9, Standard $12 and Pro $19 per seat/month (billed annually, minimum 3 seats); Enterprise on quote |
| Free trial | 14-day trial of the Pro plan; monday.com says no credit card is needed |
| Capterra rating | 4.6/5 from 6,120 reviews (checked 7 October 2026) |
| G2 rating | 4.7/5 from 17,248 reviews (checked 5 October 2026) |
monday.com is one of the easiest capable work management platforms to roll out, and it is at its best when many different teams need to build their own workflows without help from IT. The trade-offs are real: the seat buckets and three-seat minimum make it poor value for very small teams, automation actions and AI credits are capped by plan, and time tracking, workload, portfolio and resource management only arrive on Pro or Enterprise. Teams that need deep scheduling and resource control may find more depth elsewhere.

### What Is monday.com?
monday.com is cloud-based work management software. Everything is built on **boards**: flexible, spreadsheet-like tables where each row is a piece of work and each column holds information about it, such as an owner, a status, a date or a budget. The same board can be displayed as a table, a Kanban board, a timeline, a Gantt chart or a calendar, and dashboards pull data from several boards into one view.
Organisations use it to manage:
- **Projects**, from simple trackers to multi-phase plans with dependencies
- **Campaigns and content calendars**, with approvals and deadlines
- **Requests**, collected through WorkForms instead of email
- **Operational processes**, such as onboarding, procurement or IT requests
- **Portfolios and resources**, on the Enterprise plan
- **Automated workflows**, using rules, integrations and AI agents
monday.com sells several products on the same platform: work management, CRM, service and monday dev for software teams. This review focuses on work management, which the vendor now markets as its "AI work platform". It runs in the browser, as desktop apps and on iOS and Android. It is more structured than a to-do list and more connected than a spreadsheet, which is why it suits both plan-driven [waterfall projects](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/waterfall-project-management/) and looser operational work.

### Who Owns monday.com?
monday.com Ltd. was founded in Tel Aviv in 2012 by Roy Mann and Eran Zinman, originally under the name dapulse, and renamed monday.com in 2017. It has been listed on Nasdaq (ticker MNDY) since June 2021, and the two co-founders run it as co-CEOs. The company says its platform is used by around a quarter of a million customers.
For buyers, the practical point is that monday.com is a large, publicly listed vendor with published financial results and a long product track record, not an early-stage start-up.

### How Does monday.com Work?
monday.com organises work in a few simple layers:
- **Workspaces** hold the boards for a team, department or client.
- **Boards** are the core unit: one board per project, process or tracker.
- **Groups** split a board into sections, such as phases, sprints or months.
- **Items** are the rows (tasks, requests, deals or deliverables), and **subitems** break them down further.
- **Columns** add structure: status, people, date, timeline, numbers, dependency, files, formula and many more.
- **Views** show a board as a table, Kanban, timeline, Gantt, calendar or chart, and **dashboards** combine several boards.
A typical workflow looks like this:
**Form submitted → item created on a board → owner assigned automatically → status updated as work progresses → dashboard shows progress → item marked done**
For example, a sales team fills in a WorkForm asking for a new case study. The submission creates an item on the content team's board, an automation assigns it to a writer and sets a due date, and the item moves through statuses such as Drafting, In review and Published. Comments and files stay on the item, and the content lead sees everything on a dashboard without sending a chasing email.

### monday.com Key Features

#### Boards, Items and Columns
Boards are monday.com's main strength. Adding a column takes seconds, and the colour-coded status labels make a board readable at a glance, which is a big part of why non-technical teams adopt it so quickly. Each item has a clear owner, a status and a date, so accountability is visible to everyone on the board.
The flexibility has a cost: because anyone can build a board, large accounts can end up with dozens of slightly different boards for the same process. Agree a few standard boards and column sets early, or cross-team reporting becomes hard later. Our free [project tracker template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/project-tracker-template/) shows the core columns most project boards need.

#### Board Views and Kanban
The same data can be shown in several views. The table is the default; the Kanban view groups items into columns by status so you can drag them along; the calendar shows dated work; and the timeline and Gantt views (from Standard) show work over time. Filters, sorting and grouping work across views, and each person can save the views they use most.
Kanban works well for content, creative and support-style work where the flow matters more than the dates.

#### Timeline and Gantt Charts
Timeline and [Gantt chart](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/gantt-chart/) views start on the Standard plan. You can set [task dependencies](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/task-dependencies/) with a dependency column, drag bars to reschedule, and add a Gantt widget to a dashboard. According to monday.com's plan documentation, Pro adds milestones and the [critical path](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/critical-path-method/), and its Gantt feature page also lists baselines.
For most marketing, operations and client projects this is enough. Teams running large, tightly sequenced schedules with many dependencies, such as construction or engineering programmes, may find dedicated scheduling tools or Wrike's Gantt charts more thorough.

#### Dashboards
Dashboards turn board data into charts, numbers, battery (progress) widgets, Gantt widgets and workload views, so managers can see status across projects without opening each board. monday.com also offers scheduled reports and AI-written summaries on dashboards.
The key limit is how many boards one dashboard can combine: 1 board on Free and Basic, 5 on Standard, 20 on Pro and 50 on Enterprise, according to monday.com's plan documentation. A team running a dozen projects on separate boards will therefore need Pro for a single cross-project dashboard.

#### WorkForms and Request Intake
WorkForms collect requests from colleagues or external people and turn each submission into an item on a board, which can then trigger automations and integrations. Forms support conditional questions, branding (colours, fonts, logo, welcome and thank-you pages) and editable responses, and monday.com offers an AI form builder that drafts a form from a prompt.
For example, a marketing team can use one form to collect design requests, including the deadline, channel, campaign, brief and attachments. Every request then arrives complete and in the right place, rather than half-specified in a chat message. If you are not ready for software, our free [work request template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/work-request-template/) follows the same idea.

#### Automations and Workflows
Automations follow a "when this happens, do that" pattern: when a status changes, notify the owner; when a date arrives, send a reminder; when an item is created, assign it and add subitems. There are ready-made automation recipes and a custom builder, and integrations use the same approach to sync with tools such as Gmail or Google Calendar.
Automations and integrations are metered. Standard includes 250 automation actions and 250 integration actions a month, Pro 25,000 of each, and Enterprise up to 250,000 combined actions a month. 250 actions disappears quickly in a busy team, so in practice serious automation starts on Pro. The newer AI-powered workflows are capped separately at 3 active workflows on Standard, 20 on Pro and 250 on Enterprise.

#### Docs, Templates and Time Tracking
monday docs are collaborative documents that can embed and update board items, useful for briefs, meeting notes and plans. The template centre offers more than 200 templates, which is a quick way to start a board for a campaign, event or [content calendar](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/content-calendar-template/).
Time tracking and formula columns are Pro features. Teams that bill by the hour or need to compare estimates with actual effort should budget for Pro from the start.

### monday.com AI Features
AI is now central to how monday.com describes its product. For accounts that joined from May 2026, AI use draws on a monthly pool of **AI credits** shared across the account: at least 1,000 a month on Basic, 2,000 on Standard and 3,000 on Pro, with larger buckets available to buy and custom amounts on Enterprise. Different actions use different amounts: monday.com's documentation says a sidekick message uses roughly 10 to 150 or more credits, an agent run roughly 10 to 250 or more, an AI block action 8 credits, and the Notetaker 120 credits per meeting hour. Admins are alerted at 80% and 100% of usage.
That means AI costs are usage-based in practice. A team that leans heavily on agents and meeting notes will need a bigger credit bucket, so test real usage during the trial.

#### monday sidekick
monday sidekick is the built-in AI assistant. The vendor says it uses context from your boards, docs and connected apps such as Slack, Gmail and Google Calendar to summarise updates, draft content and project plans, update tasks and timelines, analyse data, and create automations, dashboards and forms. It follows existing permissions and asks for approval before acting, and scheduled "Routines" can run regular AI tasks. It is available on paid plans and uses AI credits.

#### AI Agents
monday.com offers prebuilt agents for departments such as marketing, IT, HR and the PMO, including project intake, project planning, status reporting, risk analysis and portfolio health, plus a builder for custom agents where you define the goal, rules and expected results. The vendor lists governance controls including agent permissions, activity logs, a simulation mode for human review and an AI cost centre that tracks usage by team.
Treat agents as configurable automation, not as autonomous staff. They act within the permissions you give them, every run uses credits, and someone still needs to own and review the process. The Basic plan's agent access is marked "limited" on the pricing page.

#### AI Blocks, Notetaker and AI Workflows
AI blocks add AI steps to boards, such as categorising requests, extracting information or summarising long text. The Notetaker (from Standard) records meetings and produces summaries and action items, and Pro adds an AI workflow builder. monday.com states that customer data is not used to train AI models; check the AI security documentation if that matters for your organisation.

### monday.com Collaboration Features
Each item has an updates thread for comments, @mentions, files and replies, so the conversation stays with the work. Docs can be edited together, boards can be shared with guests (external users who only see the boards they are invited to) from the Standard plan, and all paid plans include unlimited free viewers with read-only access, which is useful for executives and clients who only need to look.
Collaboration is strongest when monday.com becomes the single place where work is discussed. The downside, echoed in Capterra reviews, is notification overload: in an active account, updates, mentions and automation notifications pile up quickly. Agree notification habits early, and use automations to notify the right person rather than everyone.

### monday.com Reporting and Analytics
Reporting works at two levels. **Board-level reporting** uses the chart view and dashboard widgets to show status, workload, totals and progress, and is what most teams use daily. **Cross-board and portfolio reporting** depends on your plan, because the number of boards a dashboard can combine rises from 1 on Basic to 50 on Enterprise, and full portfolio management is an Enterprise feature.
Capterra reviewers rate monday.com's project tracking highly, but some mention needing workarounds for reporting across many boards. If cross-project reporting is a priority, model your board structure and dashboard needs during the trial, and see our guide to [project status reports](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-status-report/) for what to include.

### Portfolio and Resource Management
On Pro, the workload view shows how much work is assigned to each person, so managers can spot who is overloaded and rebalance. Time tracking is also on Pro. monday.com's pricing page lists **portfolio management** and **resource management** as Enterprise features, along with multi-level permissions.
For small and mid-sized teams, the Pro workload view is often enough for basic [capacity planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/capacity-planning/). PMOs that need formal [resource allocation](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/resource-allocation/), portfolio roll-ups and standardised project templates across the organisation will be looking at Enterprise pricing, so ask for a quote early rather than assuming Pro will cover it.

### monday.com Integrations
monday.com's integrations page advertises more than 850 integrations and apps, counting its marketplace. Named examples include **Slack**, **Microsoft Teams**, **Gmail**, **Outlook**, **Google Calendar**, **Zoom**, **Jira**, **GitHub**, **GitLab**, **Salesforce**, **HubSpot**, **Zendesk**, **Mailchimp**, **Dropbox**, **OneDrive**, **Zapier** and **Make**. Developers can use the API and SDKs, and the **monday MCP** server lets AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT and Copilot work with monday.com data.
Two practical points. First, integration actions are metered in the same way as automations (250 a month on Standard, 25,000 on Pro), so a busy two-way sync can hit the Standard limit fast. Second, some marketplace apps are sold separately by third parties, so check whether an app you need carries its own cost.

### monday.com Ease of Use

#### Getting Started
Ease of adoption is monday.com's best-known advantage. A new user can understand a board in minutes, templates give a working starting point, and the visual design makes status obvious without training. Small teams can be running real work on the first day.

#### Learning Curve
Basic use is simple; advanced use is not. Building good automations, connecting boards, designing dashboards that span many boards and setting permissions all take thought. G2 reviewers list a learning curve for advanced setups among monday.com's cons, and organisations rolling out across many departments benefit from an administrator who owns board standards. Compared with tools such as Wrike or Jira, though, the curve starts lower.

#### Performance at Scale
One recurring theme in Capterra's review summaries is slower performance with very large boards and accounts, which about two-thirds of reviewers who mention it describe negatively. Bugs and glitches are another mixed theme. These are not universal experiences, but if you plan to run boards with thousands of items, test a realistic volume during the trial.

### monday.com Mobile App
The iOS and Android apps let you view and update items, reply to updates and @mentions, receive notifications, check dashboards and use forms on the move. monday sidekick also has a mobile experience, including voice input, according to the vendor.
Some Capterra reviewers describe the mobile app as weaker than the desktop experience. Treat it as a companion for keeping up with work and making quick updates, and do board design, automation and reporting on desktop.

### monday.com Pricing
monday.com's published work management plans are below. Prices are per seat per month, billed annually, and every paid plan has a **minimum of 3 seats**. monday.com says yearly billing includes an 18% discount compared with monthly billing, and it asks teams of more than 40 users to request a quote.
| Plan | Published price | Key inclusions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 | Up to 2 seats, 3 boards, 3 docs, 200+ templates, 8 column types |
| Basic | $9/seat/month | Unlimited items and free viewers, 1,000 AI credits/month |
| Standard | $12/seat/month | Timeline, Gantt and calendar views, guest access, 250 automation and 250 integration actions/month, 2,000 AI credits |
| Pro | $19/seat/month | Private boards and docs, time tracking, advanced columns, 25,000 automation and 25,000 integration actions/month, 3,000 AI credits |
| Enterprise | Contact sales | Portfolio and resource management, enterprise security and governance, up to 250,000 combined actions/month, custom AI credits |
Pricing checked on monday.com's pricing page on 7 October 2026. monday.com also offers discounted pricing for qualifying nonprofits. Always confirm the current price for your seat count before buying.

#### Seat Minimums and Buckets
This is the part of monday.com's pricing that most often surprises buyers. According to monday.com's support documentation, paid plans are sold in groups of seats, starting at 3 and then rising in multiples of 5. A team of 4 pays for 5 seats, and a team of 6 pays for 10. On Pro billed annually, that means a six-person team pays for ten seats, or $190 a month instead of $114. Free viewers do not use a seat, but anyone who edits does.

#### monday.com Free Plan
The Free plan costs $0 for up to 2 seats, with up to 3 boards and 3 docs, 200+ templates and 8 column types, plus the mobile apps. It is fine for an individual or a pair trying the product, but it has no timeline or Gantt view, no automations and only single-board dashboards, so it is not a realistic long-term option for a team.

#### monday.com Basic Plan
At $9 per seat/month billed annually, Basic removes the item and board limits, adds unlimited free viewers and includes 1,000 AI credits a month. It works for simple task tracking, but without timeline, Gantt, guests or automations it is light for project management.

#### monday.com Standard Plan
At $12 per seat/month billed annually, Standard adds timeline, Gantt and calendar views, guest access, automations and integrations (250 actions a month each), dashboards that combine up to 5 boards and 2,000 AI credits. It is the entry point for real project work, but the action limits are tight for busy teams.

#### monday.com Pro Plan
At $19 per seat/month billed annually, Pro adds private boards and docs, time tracking, formula and other advanced columns, the workload and chart views, 25,000 automation and integration actions a month, dashboards combining up to 20 boards and 3,000 AI credits. monday.com labels it the most popular plan, and for most teams managing several projects it is the plan to evaluate.

#### monday.com Enterprise Plan
Enterprise is quote-based and adds portfolio and resource management, enterprise-grade security and governance (such as SAML single sign-on, SCIM, audit logs and IP restrictions, per monday.com's plan documentation), multi-level permissions, dashboards combining up to 50 boards, custom AI credits, 24/7 enterprise support and a 99.9% uptime SLA. It is aimed at large organisations and PMOs, and requires at least a 12-month term.

#### monday.com Free Trial
New sign-ups get a 14-day trial of the Pro plan, and monday.com says no credit card is needed. Its support documentation states that trials cannot be extended; at the end you choose a paid plan or drop to Free. Use the two weeks to rebuild one real workflow, including the automations and dashboards you would rely on, with the people who will use it.

### monday.com Pros and Cons

##### Pros
- Very easy to learn and adopt, even for non-technical teams
- Flexible boards that fit almost any workflow
- Clear, colourful interface that makes status obvious
- Strong dashboards, with cross-board views on higher plans
- Useful automation recipes and WorkForms intake
- Large integration library, API and MCP access
- Unlimited free viewers on paid plans
- Over 200 templates for a fast start

##### Cons
- Seats sold in buckets with a 3-seat minimum
- Automation and integration actions capped by plan
- Time tracking, workload and private boards need Pro
- Portfolio and resource management only on Enterprise
- AI usage metered through monthly credits
- Can slow down with very large boards
- Mobile app less capable than desktop
- Boards can sprawl without governance
This balance matches what users report: people value monday.com's ease of use, flexibility and visibility, while pricing structure, plan limits and performance at scale are the most common complaints.

### monday.com Customer Support
monday.com provides a help centre with detailed articles and tutorials, a community forum, and support that the vendor describes as available 24/7. Enterprise accounts get 24/7 enterprise support and, depending on account size, tailored onboarding, implementation help and account management.
Capterra's customer service sub-score of 4.4/5 suggests most reviewers are satisfied, although individual experiences vary. For large deployments, confirm during the sales process exactly which onboarding and support your plan includes.

### monday.com Security
monday.com's trust centre lists SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II and SOC 3 reports, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018, 27032 and 27701 certifications, CSA STAR and TX-RAMP. It also describes GDPR and UK GDPR, CCPA and other privacy programmes, and a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement (an agreement rather than a certification, available on Enterprise).
Access controls grow with the plan. Pro adds private boards and docs, board and column permissions and Google sign-in; Enterprise adds SAML single sign-on (Okta, OneLogin or custom SAML), SCIM provisioning, an audit log, IP restrictions, closed workspaces and granular permissions. Confirm current certifications, their scope and data residency options in monday.com's trust documentation as part of procurement. If you use AI agents, review the permissions each agent is given, as you would for a new team member. Permissions and governance on your side matter as much as the vendor's certificates.

### monday.com for Different Types of Teams

#### monday.com for Marketing and Creative Teams
Marketing is one of monday.com's strongest fits: campaign boards, content calendars, WorkForms for creative requests, approvals through statuses and automations, and dashboards for campaign progress. Its visual style suits teams that do not want a heavy project management tool.

#### monday.com for Agencies
Agencies can run a workspace per client, share boards with clients as guests or viewers, and track deliverables and deadlines on dashboards. Time tracking on Pro supports billing, but resource management across clients is an Enterprise feature.

#### monday.com for Operations and HR Teams
Operations and HR teams use boards for repeatable processes such as onboarding, procurement and facilities requests, combining forms, automations and checklists. This is where monday.com's flexibility shines.

#### monday.com for PMOs and Project Managers
Project managers get Gantt charts, dependencies, milestones, workload views and dashboards on Pro, while full portfolio and resource management needs Enterprise. A [PMO](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-management-office-pmo/) that wants standardised templates and portfolio roll-ups can do it in monday.com, but should compare Enterprise pricing and depth with dedicated portfolio tools. Our guide to [managing multiple projects](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/managing-multiple-projects/) covers the practices behind it.

#### monday.com for Software Teams
Software teams can use work management boards for simple sprints, but monday.com sells a separate product, monday dev, for sprints, roadmaps and bug tracking. Teams that need deep Scrum tooling should compare monday dev with [Jira](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/jira/).

#### monday.com for Small Businesses
monday.com is easy enough for any small business to adopt, but the economics need checking. With a 3-seat minimum and seat buckets, a team of 4 or 6 pays for unused seats, and useful features such as automations and Gantt start on Standard. Small teams with simple needs may get better value from cheaper or flat-priced tools.

### Is monday.com Worth It?
monday.com is likely worth it if you:
- Need a tool that non-technical colleagues will actually use.
- Run varied workflows across several departments.
- Want visual boards and dashboards that make status obvious.
- Need structured request intake and automated handoffs.
- Have a team size that fits the seat buckets well (3, 5, 10, 15 and so on).
- Are prepared to pay for Pro to get time tracking, workload and serious automation.
It may not be worth it if:
- You are a team of one or two who has outgrown the Free plan.
- Your headcount falls awkwardly between seat buckets and budget is tight.
- You need advanced scheduling, resource levelling or portfolio control without Enterprise pricing.
- Your software team needs deep Scrum tooling in the core product.
- You expect heavy AI use but do not want usage-based costs.
Our verdict: monday.com's ease of use and flexibility are its biggest advantages, and they are why it ranks second in our [project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/) review. Its pricing structure and plan limits are its biggest drawbacks, so the real question is not whether monday.com is good but whether the plan you need is good value for your team size. Use the Pro trial on a real workflow, and read our guide on [how to choose project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/how-to-choose-project-management-software/) before you commit.

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: Is monday.com good for project management?**
Yes, for most teams. monday.com offers boards, Kanban, timeline and Gantt views, dependencies, dashboards, automations and request forms, and it is rated 4.6/5 on Capterra. It is easier to adopt than most rivals. The limits are that time tracking and workload need Pro, and portfolio and resource management need Enterprise.

**Q: Is monday.com free?**
Yes. monday.com has a Free plan at $0 for up to 2 seats, with up to 3 boards and 3 docs, 200+ templates and the mobile apps. It has no timeline or Gantt view and no automations, so it suits individuals or pairs trying the product rather than growing teams.

**Q: How much does monday.com cost?**
monday.com costs $0 on Free, $9 per seat/month on Basic, $12 on Standard and $19 on Pro, billed annually, with Enterprise priced on request. Paid plans start at 3 seats, and monthly billing costs more than annual, according to monday.com (checked 7 October 2026).

**Q: Why does monday.com have a 3-seat minimum?**
monday.com sells paid plans in seat groups that start at 3 seats and then rise in multiples of 5. That means a team of 4 pays for 5 seats and a team of 6 pays for 10. Free viewers do not count as seats, but everyone who edits does.

**Q: Does monday.com have a free trial?**
Yes. New sign-ups get a 14-day trial of the Pro plan, and monday.com says no credit card is needed. Trials cannot be extended; afterwards you choose a paid plan or move to the Free plan.

**Q: Is monday.com easy to use?**
Yes, for everyday work it is one of the easiest work management tools to learn, with a clear visual interface and many templates. Advanced setups, such as connected boards, cross-board dashboards, complex automations and permissions, take more planning and benefit from an administrator.

**Q: Does monday.com have Gantt charts?**
Yes. Timeline and Gantt views are included from the Standard plan, with dependencies and drag-and-drop rescheduling. According to monday.com's plan documentation, milestones and the critical path are added on Pro.

**Q: Does monday.com have time tracking?**
Yes, but only on the Pro and Enterprise plans. The time tracking column records time against items and can feed dashboards, which is useful for agencies and teams comparing estimates with actual effort.

**Q: Does monday.com have AI?**
Yes. Paid plans include monday sidekick (an AI assistant), AI agents, AI blocks and, from Standard, the Notetaker. AI use draws on a shared monthly credit pool: at least 1,000 credits on Basic, 2,000 on Standard and 3,000 on Pro, with custom amounts on Enterprise and extra credits available to buy.

**Q: Is monday.com better than Asana?**
Neither is universally better. monday.com is more visual and flexible for building custom workflows; Asana is more task-focused, with strong goals and cross-team coordination. See our [monday.com vs Asana comparison](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/monday-vs-asana/).

**Q: Is monday.com better than Wrike?**
It depends on the use case. monday.com is usually easier to adopt and more visual; Wrike offers more project management depth, resource control and reporting for complex, multi-project work. See our [Wrike vs monday.com comparison](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/wrike-vs-monday/).

**Q: Does monday.com integrate with Slack and Microsoft Teams?**
Yes. monday.com integrates with Slack and Microsoft Teams, along with Gmail, Outlook, Zoom, Jira, GitHub, Salesforce, HubSpot, Zapier and many others. Integration actions are counted against a monthly limit that depends on your plan.

**Q: Is monday.com secure?**
monday.com's trust centre lists SOC 1, SOC 2 and SOC 3 reports and several ISO/IEC certifications, including 27001 and 27701, plus GDPR and HIPAA BAA programmes. Advanced controls such as SAML single sign-on, SCIM, audit logs and IP restrictions are on the Enterprise plan.

**Q: Is monday.com good for small businesses?**
It can be. It is easy to adopt and very flexible, but the 3-seat minimum and seat buckets mean small teams often pay for unused seats, and automations and Gantt charts start on Standard. Compare the real cost for your exact headcount with simpler or flat-priced tools.

**Q: What are the main disadvantages of monday.com?**
The main disadvantages are seat-bucket pricing with a 3-seat minimum, monthly caps on automation and integration actions, metered AI credits, key features such as time tracking and workload on Pro, portfolio and resource management on Enterprise, and slower performance reported on very large boards.

# Notion Review 2026: Is It Worth It?

URL: https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/notion/
Section: Project management software reviews
Summary: Our Notion review covers docs, databases, project tracking, Notion AI and agents, pricing, pros and cons, and whether Notion is worth it in 2026.


## Notion Review 2026: Is It Worth It?
Notion is a connected workspace that combines documents, wikis and databases, and lets teams build project trackers, roadmaps and sprint boards on top of those databases. Its biggest strength is flexibility: specs, meeting notes and the tasks that come out of them can live in the same place. For project management, that same flexibility means you design much of the system yourself, and Notion has no native time tracking, resource management or advanced scheduling. This review covers docs, databases, project features, AI, collaboration, integrations, ease of use, pricing and overall value.
- Published 8 September 2026
- Last updated 7 October 2026
- Pricing and Capterra rating checked 7 October 2026

### Notion review: quick verdict
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Best for | Teams that want documents, wikis and lightweight-to-moderate project tracking in one flexible workspace |
| Less suitable for | PMOs and teams that need resource, budget, time-tracking and portfolio controls out of the box |
| Our overall score | **8.0/10**, ranked #8 in our [top 10 project management tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/) |
| Price | Free plan; Plus $10 and Business $20 per member/month (yearly rate); Enterprise on quote |
| Free trial | Free plan instead of a published trial; Notion AI is a limited trial below Business |
| Capterra rating | 4.7/5 from 2,834 reviews (checked 7 October 2026) |
| G2 rating | 4.6/5 from 13,862 reviews (checked 5 October 2026) |
Notion is an excellent workspace for documentation and knowledge, and a capable, very flexible tool for lightweight to moderately complex project tracking. It is at its best when a team wants specs, wikis, meeting notes and tasks connected in one place. The trade-offs for project work are real: you build and maintain the structure yourself, there is no native time tracking, workload view or portfolio reporting, large databases can feel slow, and the most useful AI features now sit on the Business plan and, for agents, on paid credits.
