### What Is Notion?
Notion is a cloud-based workspace made of pages and databases. Every page is built from blocks (text, headings, to-do lists, tables, images, embeds), and any page can contain a database: a structured collection of items with properties such as status, owner, date and priority. Project management in Notion is built on those databases.
Teams use it for:
- **Docs and wikis**, from company handbooks to product specs and meeting notes
- **Projects and tasks**, tracked in databases shown as boards, timelines, calendars or tables
- **Roadmaps and sprints**, especially in product and engineering teams
- **Forms and intake**, collecting requests straight into a database
- **Lightweight dashboards**, using charts and filtered database views
- **AI assistance**, through Notion AI, Notion Agent and Custom Agents
Notion runs in the browser and as apps for Windows, macOS, iOS and Android, and the company also offers Notion Calendar and Notion Mail as companion apps. It is neither a simple to-do app nor a classic project management suite. It is a set of building blocks that can become a project system, which is why it sits in our [project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/) rankings as the docs-first option rather than a dedicated PM platform.

### Who Owns Notion?
Notion is made by Notion Labs, Inc., a privately held, venture-backed company based in San Francisco. It was founded in 2013 by Ivan Zhao and colleagues, launched Notion 1.0 in 2016, and has since acquired the calendar app Cron (now Notion Calendar) and the email company Skiff, whose technology underpins Notion Mail.
For buyers, the practical point is that Notion is an established, independent product with a large user base, not a side project of a bigger suite vendor.

### How Does Notion Work?
Notion's structure is simple at the top and flexible underneath:
- **Workspace** is your organisation's account.
- **Teamspaces** group pages by team or department, with their own members and permissions (private teamspaces need Business).
- **Pages** hold documents and can be nested inside each other without limit.
- **Databases** are pages that hold items. Each item is itself a page, so a task can contain its full brief, files and discussion.
- **Properties** add structure: status, assignee, dates, priority, select fields, formulas, and **relations** and **rollups** that link databases together (for example, tasks to projects).
- **Views** show the same database as a table, board, timeline, calendar, list, gallery or chart, each with its own filters and sorting.
A typical project workflow looks like this:
**Request submitted through a form → item lands in a database → owner, status and dates set → brief written inside the item → progress tracked on a board or timeline → automation notifies the team → charts summarise status**
For example, a product team relates a Projects database to a Tasks database. Each project page holds the spec, decisions and a linked view of its tasks; engineers work from a filtered board, while the product lead watches a timeline of all projects. You design all of this yourself or start from a template, such as our [meeting notes template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/meeting-notes-template/) for the notes that feed it.

### Notion Key Features

#### Docs and Wikis
Documentation is Notion's core strength. Pages are fast to write in, easy to nest, and can embed databases, files, Figma frames, code and much more. Wikis gather pages into a searchable knowledge base, and the Business plan adds verified pages so readers know which documents are current.
For project teams, this matters because the reasoning behind work, such as the [project brief](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/project-brief-template/), requirements and decisions, stays next to the tasks themselves. In most dedicated PM tools, that context lives in a separate document system.

#### Databases and Properties
Databases are the engine behind every project feature in Notion. Properties hold structured data, formulas calculate values, and relations and rollups connect databases, so a project can show how many of its tasks are done, or a client page can list every project for that client.
This is powerful and genuinely flexible, but it is also where the work is. Someone has to design the databases, decide which properties matter and keep them consistent. Done badly, you end up with several half-used databases that nobody trusts.

#### Projects and Tasks
Notion's projects and tasks setup gives you linked Projects and Tasks databases with assignees, statuses, due dates, subtasks, a progress bar and a personal "My tasks" view. Notion says you can mark when one task is blocking another to avoid bottlenecks, and dependencies are visible on the timeline.
It covers what most small and medium teams need for day-to-day [task dependencies](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/task-dependencies/) and ownership. It does not include the controls found in dedicated tools, such as workload balancing, time budgets or project-level financials. If you prefer to start simpler, our free [project tracker template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/project-tracker-template/) shows the minimum fields a tracker needs.

#### Board (Kanban) View
Board view shows database items as cards grouped by status or any select property, and you drag cards between columns to update them. Filters and sub-groups let one database serve several boards, such as one per team. Board view is available on every plan, including Free.

#### Timeline View
Timeline view plots database items with a date range on a Gantt-style chart. You can drag items to change dates or stretch them to change duration, and the vendor highlights dependencies on the timeline to help teams spot blocked work. It is well suited to roadmaps and high-level project plans.
It is not a full scheduling engine. Notion's documentation does not describe baselines, [critical path](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/critical-path-method/) analysis or lead and lag times, which teams running complex, date-driven projects expect from a dedicated [Gantt chart](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/gantt-chart/) tool. For a [product roadmap](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-roadmap/), Notion's timeline is often enough; for a construction-style schedule, it usually is not.

#### Sprints
For product and engineering teams, Notion can add sprints to a task database. Turning them on creates a Sprints database and a sprint board with Current sprint, Sprint planning and Backlog views. Sprints can last one to eight weeks, and you choose whether unfinished tasks roll into the next sprint, return to the backlog or stay put. With automated sprints, each sprint closes and the next one starts on schedule.
This covers the basics of [sprint planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/scrum/sprint-planning/) well, but lacks Jira's depth, such as velocity and burndown reports, so larger engineering organisations often keep Notion for specs and a dedicated tracker for issues.

#### Forms
Notion forms send each response straight into a database, so requests become trackable items without copying them from email. The Free plan has basic forms, Plus removes Notion branding and adds customisation, and conditional logic needs Business. Combined with automations, a form can be the front door for design requests, bug reports or content ideas, similar to our [work request template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/work-request-template/).

#### Database Automations
Database automations run when a page is added, a property changes or a recurring schedule fires. Actions include editing properties, adding or editing pages, sending notifications, sending email through Gmail, posting to Slack and sending webhooks. Automations require a paid plan; Free users are limited to Slack notification automations and can use, but not edit, automations included in templates.
They handle routine coordination well, but they are simpler than the rule engines in dedicated work management tools; multi-step logic usually needs webhooks, an external automation tool or Custom Agents.

#### Charts and Dashboards
Notion can turn any database into a bar, line or donut chart, and you can place several charts and filtered views on one page as a dashboard. Free includes one chart; Plus and above include unlimited charts. This gives managers a reasonable status overview, but it is assembled by hand rather than provided as ready-made project reports.

### Notion AI Features
AI is now central to Notion, and its plan structure has changed. According to Notion's pricing and AI pages, **Notion AI is included with the Business and Enterprise plans**; Free and Plus workspaces get only a limited trial. Since **4 May 2026**, Custom Agents run on **Notion credits**, an add-on for Business and Enterprise priced at $10 per 1,000 credits monthly or $13 per 1,000 on annual terms. Credits are shared across the workspace, and unused credits do not roll over.

#### Notion Agent
Notion Agent is the built-in assistant. Notion says it can complete multi-step tasks using context from your workspace, connected apps and the web, creating or editing pages and databases from a chat, such as drafting a project plan from meeting notes or building a task database from a brief.

#### AI Meeting Notes
AI Meeting Notes transcribes meetings and summarises key points and action items without adding a bot to the call. For teams whose projects are driven by meetings, this links decisions directly to the pages where work is tracked.

#### Enterprise Search
Enterprise Search, still labelled beta, searches across Notion and connected apps such as Slack, Google Drive and GitHub, which helps when you need to find where a decision was made.

#### Custom Agents
Custom Agents are team-wide automations that run on triggers or schedules, whether or not anyone is online. Notion lists triggers such as Slack mentions and emoji reactions, incoming email, calendar events and recurring schedules, and examples such as Q&A agents, task-routing agents and agents that compile recurring status reports. Admins can control who builds agents, see what each one can access, pause any agent, and track credit usage with alerts at 80% and 100%; every run is logged.
These are best understood as configurable workflow automation, not autonomous team members. They follow the instructions and access you give them, consume credits on every run, and need an owner. A weekly [project status report](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-status-report/) agent can save real time, but budget for credits before rolling agents out widely.

#### Writing, Autofill and Research Mode
Notion AI can draft and improve text inside pages, and Autofill can populate database properties automatically, for example summarising each project or extracting key results. Research Mode generates longer reports from your workspace and the web. Notion states that it does not train AI models on customer content, and Enterprise customers get zero data retention with its AI providers.

### Notion Collaboration Features
Collaboration is where Notion users are happiest. Several people can edit a page at once, comment on any block, @mention colleagues and pages, and follow updates through the inbox. Guests can be invited to specific pages: Free allows 10 external guests and Plus and above allow unlimited guests. Page history runs from 7 days on Free to 30 days on Plus, 90 days on Business and unlimited on Enterprise.
On Capterra, the real-time collaborative workspace is one of the most positively reviewed themes, at around 97% positive among reviews that mention it. The downside is structure: because anyone can create pages and databases, workspaces can sprawl. Agree a teamspace structure, naming conventions and owners for key databases early, especially for [remote teams](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/industries/remote-project-management/) that rely on written documentation.

### Notion Reporting and Dashboards
Reporting in Notion is built from the same pieces as everything else: database views, filters, formulas, rollups and charts. A well-built dashboard page can show projects by status, overdue tasks per owner and progress across a quarter, and Business adds page analytics showing who viewed and edited pages.
What Notion does not offer is packaged project reporting: no built-in portfolio reports, workload charts or burndown charts. If leadership needs consistent reporting across many projects, someone has to build and maintain it. Our guide to [managing multiple projects](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/managing-multiple-projects/) explains what that reporting usually needs to show.

### Resource Management and Time Tracking
This is Notion's clearest gap for project managers. It has no native time tracking, no workload or capacity view and no resource scheduling. Teams can approximate these with number properties (estimated hours, effort points), rollups and third-party time-tracking integrations, but there is nothing equivalent to the workload views in Wrike, monday.com or ClickUp.
For small teams, this rarely matters. For agencies billing hours, professional services firms or PMOs doing [capacity planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/capacity-planning/) and [resource allocation](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/resource-allocation/), it is usually a deciding factor against using Notion as the main project system.

### Notion Integrations
Notion's integrations gallery covers engineering, design, sales, marketing, analytics, automation, security and identity tools. Plan matters here: **Plus** includes basic connections such as Slack and Google Drive, while **Business** adds premium connections such as GitHub and Asana. Notion's projects page highlights bringing GitHub pull requests and issues, Jira bug updates, Figma designs and Slack messages into Notion pages.
Other listed integrations include an AI connector for Microsoft Teams, Linear, Loom, Canva, Tableau and Calendly, plus identity and security tools such as Microsoft Entra ID, OneLogin and Splunk, and a public API supports custom integrations. In practice, integrations are good at pulling context into Notion; deep two-way project syncing is more limited than in some dedicated PM tools.

### Notion Ease of Use

#### Initial Setup
A new workspace starts close to empty, which is liberating for some teams and paralysing for others. Templates help, but a team-wide project system still means designing databases, relations, views, permissions and automations. A small team can be productive in an afternoon; a department-wide setup is a project in its own right.

#### Learning Curve
Writing pages and ticking off tasks is easy, and most people pick it up within minutes. Databases, relations, rollups and formulas take longer, and this is where Notion's reputation for a learning curve comes from. G2 users list a steep learning curve for advanced setups and limited features for complex project management among the main drawbacks, while still rating Notion highly overall. Capterra's ease-of-use sub-score of 4.4 is good, but lower than its features and value scores.

#### Performance and Interface
The interface is clean and minimal, which most users like. The most consistent complaint on Capterra is performance: around 85% of reviews that discuss large amounts of content describe Notion as sluggish. Very large databases, heavy relations and long pages are where this shows, so plan to archive old work and keep databases focused.

### Notion Mobile App and Offline Access
Notion's iOS and Android apps let you read and edit pages, update tasks, comment and check notifications. Capterra feedback on mobile is mixed, with about half of reviews on mobile usability negative, so treat the apps as companions for updates and reading rather than for building or reorganising databases.
Offline access now exists on the desktop and mobile apps for all plans, with limits: you mark pages for offline use on each device, only the first 50 rows of a database download automatically, and embeds, forms and buttons do not work offline. Capterra reviewers still list offline functionality as a weakness, so test it if your team often works without a connection.

### Notion Pricing
Notion's published plans are below. Prices are per member per month at the yearly rate; Notion says paying yearly saves up to 20%, and listings such as Capterra show the monthly-billed rates as $12 for Plus and $24 for Business. Guests are free but limited to the pages they are invited to.
| Plan | Published price | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 | Individuals and very small trials |
| Plus | $10/member/month | Small teams that need unlimited collaborative use |
| Business | $20/member/month | Growing teams that want Notion AI, SSO and private teamspaces |
| Enterprise | Contact sales | Large organisations with advanced security and admin needs |
Add-ons include Notion credits for Custom Agents and extra AI usage ($10 per 1,000 credits monthly, $13 per 1,000 annually, Business and Enterprise only) and custom domains for Notion Sites ($8 per month per domain billed yearly, or $10 monthly). Pricing checked on Notion's pricing page on 7 October 2026; always confirm before buying.

#### Notion Free Plan
The Free plan is aimed at individuals. It includes pages and databases with subtasks, dependencies and custom properties, basic forms and sites, Notion Calendar and a trial of Notion AI. The limits matter for teams: blocks are unlimited for one person but limited once a workspace has two or more members, uploads are capped at 5 MB per file, page history lasts 7 days, and you get 10 guests and one chart. It is a good way to evaluate Notion, but not a long-term home for a team.

#### Notion Plus Plan
At $10 per member/month on yearly billing, Plus removes the block limit for teams and adds unlimited file uploads (a per-file size limit may apply), unlimited charts and guests, custom forms and sites, 30-day page history and basic connections such as Slack and Google Drive. It suits small teams that want collaborative docs and project tracking, but note that Notion AI is only a trial on Plus. Students and educators can get a one-member Plus plan free with a school email.

#### Notion Business Plan
At $20 per member/month on yearly billing, Business is the plan Notion recommends. It adds Notion AI (Notion Agent, AI Meeting Notes and Enterprise Search), SAML SSO, private teamspaces, granular database permissions, verified pages, conditional logic in forms, premium connections such as GitHub and Asana, 90-day page history and page analytics. For most teams using Notion as their main workspace, and anyone who wants AI included, this is the plan to evaluate.

#### Notion Enterprise Plan
Enterprise is quote-based and adds SCIM provisioning, advanced security controls, the audit log, SIEM and DLP connections, custom data retention, unlimited page history, zero data retention with LLM providers, premium support and a customer success manager. It is designed for large organisations with formal IT and compliance requirements.

#### Notion Free Trial
Notion's pricing page does not advertise a standard free trial of its paid plans; the Free plan is the main way to try the product, and Notion AI is available as a limited trial below Business. Notion's agents page refers to Business trials, so ask sales if you want to test Business features. Notion's pricing page also states a refund window: three days for monthly plans and 30 days for annual plans. Whichever way you test it, rebuild one real project, with its brief, tasks and views, using the people who will use it.

### Notion Pros and Cons

##### Pros
- Excellent docs, wikis and knowledge management
- Very flexible databases, relations and views
- Specs, notes and tasks connected in one place
- Strong real-time collaboration
- Board, timeline, calendar and sprint views
- Strong value on Plus and Business
- Capable AI: Agent, meeting notes, Custom Agents
- Large template gallery and community
- Mature security certifications

##### Cons
- No native time tracking or resource management
- Project systems take design effort to build and maintain
- Timeline lacks baselines and critical path
- Can feel sluggish with large databases or pages
- Reporting must be assembled by hand
- Notion AI requires Business; agents need paid credits
- Workspaces can sprawl without clear ownership
- Offline and mobile still weaker than desktop
- Less suited to large, structured portfolios
This balance matches what users report: people love Notion's flexibility and collaboration, while performance with large content, offline access and the effort of building advanced setups are the recurring drawbacks.

### Notion Customer Support
Notion provides a detailed help centre, guides, video tutorials, a template gallery and a large user community. Enterprise customers get premium support and a dedicated customer success manager; on other plans, support is mainly self-service and through in-app messaging.
Capterra's customer service sub-score of 4.4/5 is solid, though experiences vary between reviewers. For a large rollout, ask during the sales process exactly which onboarding and support are included.

### Notion Security
Notion's security page states that it holds a SOC 2 Type 2 attestation and certifications for ISO 27001, ISO 27017, ISO 27018 and ISO 27701. Healthcare organisations can process protected health information after signing Notion's Business Associate Agreement under HIPAA, and Notion says its privacy programme is mapped to GDPR and other global privacy regulations. It hosts on AWS and Cloudflare infrastructure.
Plan matters for controls: SAML SSO, private teamspaces and granular database permissions start on Business, while SCIM provisioning, the audit log, advanced security controls, SIEM and DLP connections and zero data retention with LLM providers are Enterprise features. For AI, Notion states that it does not train models on customer content. As with any vendor, confirm current certifications and their scope in Notion's trust documentation during procurement.

### Notion for Different Types of Teams

#### Notion for Product and Engineering Teams
This is one of Notion's strongest fits: specs, PRDs, roadmaps, decision logs and sprint boards in one connected space, with GitHub and Jira context pulled in. Many teams use Notion for planning and documentation and keep a dedicated issue tracker for engineering execution.

#### Notion for Marketing and Content Teams
Editorial calendars, campaign briefs, content databases with status and owner, and request forms all work well in Notion, and the docs-first approach suits teams that write for a living. Approval workflows and proofing are basic compared with dedicated creative tools.

#### Notion for Start-ups and Small Businesses
For start-ups, Notion can be the wiki, roadmap and project board at once, which is excellent value on Plus or Business. The risk is building elaborate systems before the team needs them.

#### Notion for Project Managers and PMOs
Be realistic here. Notion can track projects and give a readable overview, but it lacks the resource management, time tracking, baselines, portfolio reporting and standardised controls that a [PMO](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-management-office-pmo/) typically relies on. Many PMOs use Notion for documentation alongside a dedicated platform such as [Wrike](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/).

#### Notion for Enterprises
Large organisations often adopt Notion as a knowledge and collaboration layer, helped by Enterprise security and admin controls. As the main system for complex, cross-department delivery it is less common; see our guide to [enterprise project management](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/industries/enterprise-project-management/) for the capabilities that usually matter at that scale.

### Is Notion Worth It?
Notion is likely worth it if you:
- Want docs, wikis and project tracking in one workspace.
- Are a small or medium team, or a product, engineering or content team.
- Value flexibility and are willing to design your own databases and views.
- Want built-in AI for writing, meeting notes and search (on Business).
- Need strong real-time collaboration on written work.
It may not be worth it as your main project tool if you:
- Need time tracking, workload or resource management.
- Want project management features ready to use without building them.
- Run complex schedules that need baselines and critical path.
- Need standardised reporting across a large portfolio.
- Work with very large databases or often without a connection.
Our verdict: Notion's flexibility is both its biggest advantage and its main limitation. As a workspace for knowledge and lightweight-to-moderate project tracking, it is excellent value, which is why it earns 8.0/10 and a place in our [top 10 project management tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/). As a replacement for a dedicated project management platform in a PMO or resource-heavy organisation, it falls short. Before committing, read our guide on [how to choose project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/how-to-choose-project-management-software/) and build one real project in the Free plan.

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: Is Notion good for project management?**
Yes, for lightweight to moderately complex projects. Notion offers task databases, boards, timelines, sprints, forms and automations, all connected to your docs. It lacks native time tracking, resource management, baselines and packaged portfolio reporting, so PMOs and resource-heavy teams usually need a dedicated project management tool.

**Q: Is Notion free?**
Yes. Notion's Free plan costs $0 and is aimed at individuals. It includes pages, databases, basic forms and sites, and a trial of Notion AI, but blocks are limited for workspaces with two or more members, uploads are capped at 5 MB and page history lasts 7 days.

**Q: How much does Notion cost?**
Notion costs $0 on Free, $10 per member/month on Plus and $20 per member/month on Business at the yearly rate, with Enterprise priced on request. Monthly billing costs more; Notion says yearly saves up to 20%. Notion credits for Custom Agents are extra (checked 7 October 2026).

**Q: Does Notion have a free trial?**
Notion's pricing page does not advertise a standard free trial of paid plans. The Free plan is the main way to try it, and Notion AI comes as a limited trial on Free and Plus. Notion refers to Business trials for agents, so ask sales if you need one.

**Q: Is Notion easy to use?**
Partly. Writing pages and managing simple task lists is easy. Building project systems with relational databases, rollups, formulas and automations takes more learning, and G2 users cite a steep learning curve for advanced setups. Capterra rates its ease of use 4.4/5.

**Q: What is Notion best used for?**
Notion is best for documentation, wikis, meeting notes, product specs and roadmaps, combined with lightweight to moderate project and task tracking. It suits start-ups, product and engineering teams, content teams and any team that wants knowledge and work in one place.

**Q: Is Notion better than ClickUp?**
It depends on your priorities. Notion is stronger for documents and flexible knowledge management; ClickUp offers more built-in project management, including time tracking and workload views. See our [Notion vs ClickUp comparison](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/clickup/clickup-vs-notion/).

**Q: Is Notion better than Asana?**
Neither is universally better. Notion suits docs-heavy teams that want to build their own systems, while Asana offers dedicated task, goal and portfolio management with less setup. See our [Notion vs Asana comparison](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/asana-vs-notion/).

**Q: Does Notion have Gantt charts?**
Notion has a timeline view that works like a simple Gantt chart, showing items with date ranges and dependencies. It does not offer baselines or critical path analysis, so complex schedules are better handled in a dedicated Gantt tool.

**Q: Does Notion have Kanban boards?**
Yes. Board view turns any database into a Kanban board grouped by status or another property, with filters and sub-groups. It is available on every plan, including Free.

**Q: Does Notion have AI, and how much does it cost?**
Yes. Notion AI, including Notion Agent, AI Meeting Notes and Enterprise Search, is included on Business and Enterprise; Free and Plus get a limited trial. Custom Agents run on Notion credits, sold to Business and Enterprise customers at $10 per 1,000 credits monthly or $13 per 1,000 annually.

**Q: Does Notion have time tracking?**
No. Notion has no native time tracking or resource management. Teams use number properties, formulas or third-party time-tracking integrations as workarounds, which is one reason agencies and PMOs often choose a dedicated tool instead.

**Q: Does Notion work offline?**
Yes, on the desktop and mobile apps for all plans. You mark pages for offline use on each device, only the first 50 rows of a database download automatically, and embeds, forms and buttons do not work offline.

**Q: Does Notion integrate with Slack and Jira?**
Yes. Slack and Google Drive connections are included from Plus, premium connections such as GitHub and Asana need Business, and Notion can bring Jira issues, Figma designs and GitHub pull requests into pages. A public API supports custom integrations.

# Smartsheet Review 2026: Is It Worth It?

URL: https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/smartsheet/
Section: Project management software reviews
Summary: Our Smartsheet review covers features, pricing, AI, Gantt charts, Control Center, pros and cons, integrations and whether Smartsheet is worth it in 2026.


## Smartsheet Review 2026: Is It Worth It?
Smartsheet is a spreadsheet-style work and project management platform: its sheets look like Excel, but behave like project plans, with dependencies, Gantt charts, forms, automation, reports and dashboards built in. Its biggest strength is that familiar grid combined with serious scheduling, roll-up reporting and enterprise governance; its main trade-offs are a less visual interface than board-first tools, no free plan, and quote-based pricing for its most powerful portfolio features. This review covers pricing, planning, collaboration, automation, AI, integrations, ease of use, reporting, security and overall value.
- Published 6 September 2026
- Last updated 7 October 2026
- Pricing and Capterra rating checked 7 October 2026

### Smartsheet review: quick verdict
|  |  |

Smartsheet is a strong choice for spreadsheet-minded organisations that want to turn scattered Excel trackers into connected, governed project plans, and it scales further than most rivals into enterprise portfolio management. The trade-offs are real: there is no free plan, per-member pricing and premium add-ons push costs up, the interface is less visual than board-first tools, and advanced formulas and cross-sheet designs take time to learn. Users also report performance concerns on very large solutions.

### What Is Smartsheet?
Smartsheet is cloud-based work and project management software built around the **sheet**: a grid of rows and columns that feels like a spreadsheet, but where each row can be a task with an owner, dates, dependencies, a status and a discussion thread. On top of sheets, Smartsheet adds the things a spreadsheet cannot do well on its own: Gantt charts, forms, automated workflows, cross-sheet reports and dashboards.
Organisations use it to manage:
- **Project plans and schedules**, with phases, dependencies and milestones
- **Trackers and registers**, such as issue logs, risk registers and asset lists
- **Intake and requests**, collected through forms
- **Approvals and process workflows**, driven by automation
- **Resource and workload planning**, on higher plans and add-ons
- **Portfolio reporting**, rolling up many projects into reports and dashboards
The same sheet can be shown as a grid, Gantt chart, board, calendar, timeline or table, and Smartsheet runs in the browser and on iOS and Android. It is not simply an online spreadsheet: its value comes from structured columns, automation and roll-up reporting across many sheets.

### Who Owns Smartsheet?
Smartsheet was developed in 2005 and launched publicly in 2006; it is based in Bellevue, Washington. After several years as a listed company, it was taken private by Blackstone and Vista Equity Partners in a deal worth about $8.4 billion that completed on 22 January 2025, and its shares were delisted from the New York Stock Exchange. Smartsheet says its platform is used by over 85% of the 2024 Fortune 500.
For buyers, the practical point is that Smartsheet is a mature, enterprise-focused product with a long track record. Private-equity ownership is common in this market (Wrike is in a similar position), but it is worth watching pricing and packaging changes at renewal.

### How Does Smartsheet Work?
Smartsheet organises work in a straightforward structure:
- **Workspaces** hold everything for a team, department or programme, and control who has access.
- **Folders** group related sheets, reports and dashboards inside a workspace.
- **Sheets** are the core item: each **row** is a task or record and each **column** is a field with a type, such as text, date, dropdown, checkbox, contact or duration.
- **Row hierarchy** (indenting rows under a parent) turns a flat list into phases and subtasks, and parent rows can roll up dates and progress.
- **Reports** pull matching rows from many sheets into one view, such as "all overdue tasks across every project".
- **Dashboards** visualise sheets and reports with charts, metrics and widgets for stakeholders.
A typical workflow looks like this:
**Request submitted via form → row created in an intake sheet → automation assigns an owner and notifies them → owner updates status and dates → report rolls up work across sheets → dashboard shows progress to stakeholders**
For example, an operations team uses a form to collect facilities requests. Each submission becomes a row; an automated workflow routes it to the right coordinator based on location; the coordinator updates the status column; and a weekly report of open requests feeds a dashboard that the operations director checks without opening any individual sheet.

### Smartsheet Key Features

#### Grid View and Formulas
The grid is where most Smartsheet users spend their time. It supports sorting, filtering and grouping, typed columns, conditional formatting, formulas and links between cells in different sheets. For anyone moving from Excel, this is the main attraction: the layout is instantly familiar, but the data is shared, permissioned and live.
Formulas and cross-sheet references are powerful, and they are how experienced users build trackers, scoring models and roll-ups. They also have limits: on Capterra, limited advanced formula capabilities is one of the recurring criticisms, particularly from heavy Excel users who expect the full spreadsheet function library.

#### Gantt Charts and Dependencies
Smartsheet's [Gantt view](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/gantt-chart/) is available on all plans. Task bars reflect start date, end date and duration; you can set [task dependencies](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/task-dependencies/) between rows, drag bars to change dates, highlight milestones and identify the [critical path](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/critical-path-method/). Because the Gantt chart sits on the same rows as the grid, editing a date in either place updates both.
For date-driven projects, such as construction programmes, system implementations, events or product launches, this is one of Smartsheet's strongest areas and a key reason PMOs choose it. For simple task tracking it is more than you need, and a board or list will be quicker. Our free [Gantt chart template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/gantt-chart-template/) shows the same structure if you want to sketch a plan first.

#### Board, Calendar, Timeline and Table Views
**Board view** shows rows as cards in lanes that can represent a stage, team or sprint, with drag-and-drop and up to 14 fields per card. It works well as a simple [Kanban board](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/kanban/kanban-boards/), though it is a view on a sheet rather than a board-first experience. **Calendar view** lays out dated rows by day, week or month. **Timeline view**, available from the Business plan, groups date-based work into lanes such as team or region. The newer **table view** modernises the grid with live co-editing, a formula editor with column-name autocomplete and an editing side panel.

#### Forms
Forms let anyone submit structured information straight into a sheet. They can be branded, use conditional logic to show follow-up questions, and be shared by link or embedded on a website; Smartsheet says they also work on mobile in low-connectivity areas. For intake processes this removes much of the email back-and-forth. Our [work request template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/work-request-template/) follows the same idea if you are not ready for software.

#### Automation
Smartsheet's no-code automated workflows combine triggers, conditions and actions: send reminders and notifications (including via Slack and Microsoft Teams), request approvals, update or move rows, create recurring tasks, and generate documents such as PDFs and contracts, with DocuSign signing for customers that hold an enterprise DocuSign licence.
Automation is practical and widely used, but plan limits matter. The Pro plan includes **250 automations per month**, which a busy team can exhaust; Business and above have unlimited automations.

#### Proofing and Approvals
Proofing, on the Business plan and above, lets reviewers pin comments to specific areas of images and documents, with version control and an audit history. Combined with approval workflows, it covers straightforward marketing and document review. It is serviceable rather than specialist: creative teams with heavy review cycles may prefer tools built around proofing.

#### Reports
Reports combine and filter rows from many sheets into a single view, such as every at-risk task owned by one person across ten projects. They can be shared, exported or added to dashboards, and they are what turns a collection of individual sheets into a manageable portfolio. Pro includes unlimited sheets, forms and reports.

### Smartsheet AI Features
Smartsheet has expanded its AI substantially, and its pricing page lists the core AI tools on all four plans. According to Smartsheet's AI feature page, the main capabilities are:

#### Smart Assist
Smart Assist is a built-in assistant that can summarise a sheet or workspace, run a project health check that flags risks and dependency problems, and take actions such as creating sheets, workspaces and folders, bulk-updating rows, managing columns and reassigning tasks. It can also draft stakeholder emails, Slack updates and stand-up preparation from project data. The vendor describes it as new; treat the action features as something to test carefully on a copy of a real sheet before trusting it with bulk changes.

#### Smart Columns
Smart Columns add an AI-powered column that processes every row as data changes, for example summarising long text, translating content or analysing sentiment, with custom instructions for tone, length and format. This is a genuinely useful idea for intake sheets and feedback logs, where it can condense long free-text answers into something a manager can scan.

#### Dashboards, Formulas and Data Analysis
The **AI dashboard builder** creates a dashboard from a description and selected data sources, which you then edit. **Generate formulas** converts plain-language requests into working formulas, which directly addresses one of Smartsheet's learning-curve problems. **Analyse data** produces charts and metrics from typed questions, **intelligent form fill** maps spoken answers to form fields, and new trial users get **AI-guided project setup**.

#### MCP and External AI Assistants
Smartsheet also offers an MCP server that connects sheets to Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini and other MCP-compatible assistants, so they can read live project data and take actions such as checking overdue tasks or updating statuses. The pricing page lists connecting external AI tools through MCP from the Business plan upwards.
Our assessment: Smartsheet's AI is most valuable for summarising and querying structured data, which is exactly what sheets hold. It does not remove the need for a well-designed sheet, and its quality depends on clean, consistent columns.

### Smartsheet Collaboration Features
Collaboration in Smartsheet happens on rows and sheets: conversations and comments, @mentions, attachments (Smartsheet says up to 100 files at once), a file library, proofing, and notifications in-app, on mobile and by email. Sheets can be shared with internal colleagues and external partners, and everything is private by default until shared.
The user model is worth understanding because it affects both collaboration and cost. **Members** are paid users who create and manage items. **Contributors** are free users who can view shared work and, with commenter permissions, comment and add attachments. **Guests** are free external users, available on Business and above, who can view or edit items shared with them. Internal users who start editing may become **Provisional Members**, with full access for a limited period before an administrator decides whether to assign a paid seat.
Collaboration is strongest when sheets become the single source of truth. The downside is governance: as sheets multiply, sharing, permissions and seat assignments need active management, or administrators lose track of who can see and edit what. Compared with board-first tools, collaboration also feels more like editing a shared document than working in a social, card-based workspace.

### Smartsheet Reporting and Dashboards
Reporting works at three levels. **Reports** roll up rows across sheets. **Dashboards** present charts, metrics, reports and links to stakeholders; Pro limits each dashboard to 10 widgets, while higher plans allow more. **Portfolio-level reporting** comes through Portfolios on Enterprise and Control Center on Advanced Work Management, and data can be pushed into Power BI or Tableau for deeper analysis.
This roll-up model is one of Smartsheet's real strengths: well-designed sheets feed consistent [project status reports](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-status-report/) without anyone copying data by hand. It depends on discipline, though: if every project manager builds sheets differently, reports become hard to maintain. On Capterra, project tracking is one of the most consistently praised areas.

### Resource Management and Workload
Resource features are split across plans and products:
- **Workload tracking** (Business and above) shows each person's capacity and task load and flags over-allocation so work can be rebalanced.
- **Scenario Planning** (Enterprise) lets you view timelines alongside capacity and test what-if changes without affecting live plans.
- **Resource Management** (a premium add-on) covers capacity planning, time tracking, demand management, role- and skill-based assignments and project budgets.
Basic workload visibility is enough for many teams. Firms that bill for time or plan staff across many projects, such as professional services and PMOs, will need the Resource Management add-on, which adds cost and a separate set-up exercise. Our guides to [capacity planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/capacity-planning/) and [resource allocation](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/resource-allocation/) explain the underlying techniques.

### Portfolio Management: Portfolios and Control Center
This is where Smartsheet separates itself from most rivals. **Portfolios**, included in Enterprise plans with no extra licence, gives a standardised, central view of related projects with out-of-the-box set-up. **Control Center**, included in Advanced Work Management or sold as a premium add-on, goes further: project "blueprints" define a standard set of sheets, reports and dashboards, new projects are provisioned automatically from intake, changes can be pushed across every existing project at once, and portfolio reporting rolls everything up.
Related premium apps extend this: **Dynamic View** shares only the rows and columns a person needs (useful for secure request management), **Data Shuttle** automates imports and exports between external systems and Smartsheet, and **DataMesh** and the **Pivot App** handle data mapping and summary tables.
For a [PMO](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-management-office-pmo/) that wants every project built the same way, Control Center is a strong reason to choose Smartsheet. It is not plug-and-play, though: designing good blueprints takes time, and many organisations use Smartsheet's professional services or a partner to set it up. Our guide to [program vs project vs portfolio management](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/program-vs-project-vs-portfolio-management/) explains when portfolio tooling becomes worthwhile.

### Smartsheet Integrations
Smartsheet says it has over 175 integrations. Examples include **Microsoft Teams** (alerts and Smartsheet content in channel tabs), **Outlook**, **Slack**, **Google Drive, Calendar and Gmail**, **Salesforce**, **Jira**, **DocuSign**, **Power BI** and **Tableau**, plus MCP-based connections for **Claude**, **ChatGPT** and **Microsoft Copilot**. Some integrations are included in Business and Enterprise plans, while others are paid add-ons, so check the specific connector you need.

#### Bridge by Smartsheet
Bridge is Smartsheet's low-code tool for building workflows that span other systems, using pre-built connections, APIs and JavaScript. It suits organisations with technical administrators who want to automate cross-system processes without a separate integration platform.

#### API and Data Connectors
The Smartsheet API is free for licensed users on Business plans or higher, and Data Shuttle and Connectors (on Advanced Work Management or as add-ons) handle scheduled data movement. Smartsheet's integration strength is in the enterprise stack, Microsoft, Salesforce, BI tools and Jira, rather than in a long tail of small-business apps.

### Smartsheet Ease of Use

#### Initial Setup
A single sheet can be running in minutes, especially if you import an Excel file or start from Smartsheet's template gallery. A well-designed solution takes longer: column types, row hierarchy, dependencies, cross-sheet formulas, automations, reports, dashboards and sharing all need thought. For enterprise rollouts with Control Center, set-up is a project in its own right.

#### Learning Curve
For anyone comfortable with spreadsheets, basic Smartsheet use is quick to pick up, and this is one of its main advantages over tools with an unfamiliar model. Advanced use is harder: cross-sheet references, complex formulas, report logic and permission design all require training. G2 reviewers summarise this well, citing ease of use for spreadsheet users alongside a steep learning curve for advanced use. AI formula generation helps, but does not remove the need for someone who understands the design.

#### Interface
The interface is functional, dense and familiar. Its strengths are information density and precision: you can see and edit a lot of data quickly. Its weaknesses are that it is less visual and less inviting than board-first tools, which can slow adoption among non-spreadsheet users, and that large, formula-heavy sheets can feel slow. On Capterra, performance and reliability concerns are among the recurring criticisms. The newer table view is a step towards a more modern experience.

### Smartsheet Mobile App
Smartsheet's iOS and Android apps let you view and update sheets, submit forms, respond to conversations and notifications, and check dashboards while away from a desk. Forms are designed to work in low-connectivity areas, which matters for field teams in construction, facilities and inspections, and enterprises can manage the app through Microsoft Intune.
Our assessment: a wide grid is inherently awkward on a phone, so the mobile app works best as a companion for updates, approvals and data capture. Do planning, sheet design and reporting on desktop.

### Smartsheet Pricing
Smartsheet's published plans are below. Prices are per member per month; paid Members are charged, while Contributors (and Guests on Business and above) are free. Pricing checked on Smartsheet's pricing page on 7 October 2026; always confirm before buying.
| Plan | Published price | Members | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pro | $9/member/month billed yearly ($12 billed monthly) | 1–10 | Small teams needing Gantt, forms and basic automation |
| Business | $19/member/month billed yearly ($24 billed monthly) | 3 or more | Teams needing timeline, workload, unlimited automation and guests |
| Enterprise | Contact sales | 10 or more | Organisations needing Portfolios, Scenario Planning and SAML SSO |
| Advanced Work Management | Contact sales | Custom | Enterprises scaling portfolios with Control Center and premium apps |

#### Is There a Smartsheet Free Plan?
No. Smartsheet's pricing page does not list a free plan; the cheapest option is Pro. Free Contributors can view and comment on shared work, which helps keep costs down for stakeholders, but anyone who needs to create and manage work needs a paid seat. If a free tier is essential, look at the options in our [Smartsheet alternatives](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/smartsheet/smartsheet-alternatives/) guide.

#### Smartsheet Pro Plan
At $9 per member/month billed yearly ($12 monthly), Pro supports 1 to 10 members with unlimited free Contributors. It includes Gantt, table, board and calendar views, formulas, unlimited sheets, forms and reports, 250 automations per month, 20 GB of storage and dashboards of up to 10 widgets. It does not include timeline view, workload tracking, proofing, Guests or Portfolios. It suits a small team moving off spreadsheets, but the 10-member cap and automation limit mean growing teams will move to Business.

#### Smartsheet Business Plan
At $19 per member/month billed yearly ($24 monthly), with a minimum of 3 members, Business adds timeline view, workload tracking, unlimited automations, unlimited free Guests, proofing, publishing, admin capabilities, API access, 1 TB of attachment storage and MCP connections to external AI tools. This is the plan most departments should evaluate first, and it is the plan used for the free trial.

#### Smartsheet Enterprise Plan
Enterprise is quote-based, for 10 or more members, and adds Portfolios, Scenario Planning, SAML-based single sign-on, Enterprise Plan Manager, directory integrations and unlimited attachment storage. It suits organisations that need governance across many teams.

#### Advanced Work Management
Advanced Work Management is also quote-based. It adds Control Center, Dynamic View, Data Shuttle, Connectors, DataMesh, Calendar App, Pivot App and Premium Support on top of Enterprise. It is designed for PMOs and enterprises running standardised portfolios at scale, not for small teams.

#### Smartsheet Add-ons
Several capabilities are sold separately. The pricing page lists **Resource Management** (Business and Enterprise), **Brandfolder** digital asset management (all plans), **Dynamic View** from about $125 per month and **Data Shuttle** from about $100 per month (Business and Enterprise), and a **Premium Support** package. Budget for these early, as they can change the total cost noticeably.

#### Smartsheet Free Trial
Smartsheet offers a 30-day free trial with no credit card required, and its help centre says the trial gives access to a Business plan. After the trial, sheets become read-only and are later deleted unless you subscribe, so export anything you want to keep. Use the trial to rebuild one real project plan or tracker, including the report and dashboard your stakeholders would actually use.

### Smartsheet Pros and Cons

##### Pros
- Familiar spreadsheet grid that Excel users pick up quickly
- Strong Gantt charts with dependencies and critical path
- Powerful cross-sheet reports and roll-up dashboards
- Enterprise-grade governance, security and compliance
- Portfolios and Control Center for standardised PMOs
- Forms and no-code automation built in
- Free Contributors, and free Guests from Business
- Broad enterprise integrations, including MCP for AI assistants
- Growing AI tools for summaries, risks and formulas

##### Cons
- No free plan; the cheapest option is paid
- Per-member pricing and premium add-ons raise total cost
- Portfolio and premium apps are quote-based
- Less visual than board-first tools
- Learning curve for advanced formulas and cross-sheet design
- Performance concerns reported on large, complex sheets
- Pro is capped at 10 members and 250 automations per month
- Limited Agile and sprint tooling compared with Jira
This balance matches what users report: people value Smartsheet's familiarity, tracking and collaboration, while cost, licensing and performance are its most common drawbacks.

Ratings and review themes as published on G2 and Capterra on 5 October 2026; summarised in our own words. Visit the links above for full, verified user reviews.
On **Capterra**, Smartsheet is rated **4.5/5 from 3,559 reviews**, with sub-scores of **4.4 for features**, **4.4 for value for money** and **4.3 for customer service** (checked 7 October 2026). On **G2**, it is rated **4.4/5 from 22,766 reviews** (checked 5 October 2026). The themes below summarise these third-party reviews in our own words, not Smartsheet's testimonials.
**Positive themes.** Reviewers most often praise real-time team collaboration (about 98% positive in Capterra's topic summary), versatile project tracking (about 96% positive) and comprehensive task and data tracking (about 95% positive). The familiar spreadsheet layout, Gantt charts, forms and dashboards come up repeatedly as reasons teams adopted it.
**Negative themes.** The most common complaints are cost and licensing (about 46% of reviews discussing it are negative), performance and reliability (about 61% negative), and limited advanced formula capabilities (about 60% negative). Others mention the learning curve for advanced features and a less modern, less visual interface than newer tools.
When reading reviews yourself, check whether a review was invited or incentivised by the vendor. Capterra and G2 both label these, and filtering for non-incentivised reviews from organisations of your size gives a more reliable picture than the headline score.

### Smartsheet Customer Support
Smartsheet provides a searchable help centre, structured learning tracks from beginner to advanced, recorded and live webinars, instructor-led training, Pro Desk coaching, a user Community and Smartsheet University, which leads to official certification. Support requests are made through the help centre.
A **Premium Support** package, included in Advanced Work Management and available as an add-on for Business and Enterprise, adds 24x7 live chat and one-to-one coaching sessions. Professional services are available for complex rollouts such as Control Center. Capterra's customer service sub-score is a solid 4.3/5, but individual experiences vary, so confirm what support is included in your plan during the sales process.

### Smartsheet Security
Smartsheet's Trust Center lists SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, FedRAMP and HIPAA (with a Business Associate Agreement), and says ISO 42001 certification for AI management is in progress. Data is encrypted with AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2 and 1.3 in transit. Identity controls include SSO through SAML or OAuth 2.0 (SAML on Enterprise and above), admin-enforced multi-factor authentication and SCIM directory sync with Okta, Entra ID, Google Workspace and Apple.
Enterprise customers can add customer-managed encryption keys, choose data regions, apply granular data egress and retention policies through Smartsheet Safeguard, and use activity logs and event reporting covering more than 100 event types. These are strong controls for regulated industries and government, but certifications and their scope change over time, so confirm current status and plan availability in Smartsheet's trust documentation as part of procurement. Good permission design and [project governance](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-governance/) still matter.

### Smartsheet for Different Types of Teams

#### Smartsheet for PMOs and Enterprise Portfolios
This is Smartsheet's strongest use case: standardised project templates, Gantt charts with critical path, cross-sheet reporting, Portfolios and Control Center for provisioning and governing hundreds of projects.

#### Smartsheet for Operations and Finance Teams
Teams that already run processes in spreadsheets, such as budgets, trackers, registers and approvals, often find Smartsheet the most natural step up, because their data model barely changes while gaining automation, forms and dashboards. Our [project tracker template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/project-tracker-template/) shows a typical starting structure.

#### Smartsheet for IT Teams
IT teams use Smartsheet for implementation plans, infrastructure projects, intake and portfolio reporting, often with the Jira integration so developers stay in Jira while the PMO tracks milestones in Smartsheet.

#### Smartsheet for Construction and Engineering
Date-driven schedules with dependencies, mobile forms for field data capture and roll-up reporting make Smartsheet a common choice in construction and engineering.

#### Smartsheet for Marketing Teams
Marketing teams can manage campaign calendars, content plans, intake forms and proofing, and Brandfolder adds digital asset management. Teams that prefer visual, board-first workflows may find other tools more natural.

#### Smartsheet for Small Businesses
Smartsheet can work for small businesses that think in spreadsheets and need proper scheduling, but the absence of a free plan, the 10-member Pro cap and the 250-automation limit make it less economical than some rivals for very small teams.

- Small teams wanting a free plan
- Creative teams wanting a visual, board-first tool

### Is Smartsheet Worth It?
Smartsheet is likely worth it if you:
- Already run projects and processes in spreadsheets and want them connected, shared and governed.
- Manage date-driven schedules with dependencies and milestones.
- Need reports and dashboards that roll up many projects automatically.
- Want a PMO to standardise how projects are set up and reported.
- Need enterprise security, compliance and administration.
- Are willing to invest time in sheet design and training.
It may not be worth it if:
- You need a free plan or have a very tight budget.
- Your team prefers visual, card-based boards over grids.
- You run Agile software teams that need sprints and backlogs.
- You only need a shared to-do list.
- You need advanced resource management but cannot budget for add-ons.
Our verdict: Smartsheet's spreadsheet DNA is both its biggest advantage and its main limitation. For organisations that think in rows and columns and need structured plans, roll-up reporting and governance at scale, it is one of the most capable options available, which is why it ranks in the top five of our [project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/) review. For small or highly visual teams, the lack of a free plan, the add-on costs and the grid-first interface are harder to justify. Use the 30-day trial on a real project before committing, and read our guide on [how to choose project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/how-to-choose-project-management-software/).

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: Is Smartsheet good project management software?**
Yes, for the right team. Smartsheet combines a familiar spreadsheet grid with Gantt charts, dependencies, automation, cross-sheet reports and enterprise portfolio tools, and it rates 4.5/5 on Capterra. The trade-offs are no free plan, add-on costs and a learning curve for advanced design, so it suits structured, spreadsheet-minded organisations more than small visual teams.

**Q: Is Smartsheet free?**
No. Smartsheet does not list a free plan on its pricing page; the cheapest plan is Pro at $9 per member/month billed yearly. Free Contributors can view and comment on shared work, and Guests are free on Business and above, but anyone creating and managing work needs a paid seat.

**Q: How much does Smartsheet cost?**
Smartsheet Pro costs $9 per member/month billed yearly ($12 monthly) and Business costs $19 per member/month billed yearly ($24 monthly). Enterprise and Advanced Work Management are priced on request, and Resource Management, Dynamic View, Data Shuttle and Premium Support are add-ons (checked 7 October 2026).

**Q: Does Smartsheet have a free trial?**
Yes. Smartsheet offers a 30-day free trial with no credit card required, and the trial gives access to the Business plan. Sheets become read-only after the trial ends unless you subscribe, so test a real project and export anything you need.

**Q: Is Smartsheet easy to use?**
Partly. Anyone comfortable with Excel can pick up the basics quickly, which is one of Smartsheet's main advantages. Advanced use, such as cross-sheet formulas, report logic, automation and permission design, takes training, and the grid-based interface is less visual than board-first tools.

**Q: What is Smartsheet best used for?**
Smartsheet is best for date-driven project plans, trackers and registers, intake and approval workflows, roll-up reporting across many projects, and PMO portfolio management, especially in organisations that already work in spreadsheets.

**Q: Is Smartsheet better than Wrike?**
Neither is universally better. Smartsheet suits spreadsheet-minded teams that want grid-based plans and strong roll-up reporting; Wrike offers a broader all-in-one platform with stronger collaboration, proofing and resource management. See our [Smartsheet vs Wrike comparison](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/wrike-vs-smartsheet/).

**Q: Is Smartsheet better than monday.com?**
It depends on the use case. Smartsheet is stronger for spreadsheet-style scheduling and enterprise portfolio governance; monday.com is more visual and usually easier for non-technical teams to adopt. See our [Smartsheet vs monday.com comparison](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/monday-vs-smartsheet/).

**Q: Is Smartsheet better than Excel for project management?**
For shared project work, usually yes. Smartsheet keeps the familiar grid but adds real-time collaboration, permissions, Gantt charts with dependencies, forms, automation and cross-sheet reports. Excel remains more powerful for complex calculations and modelling, and many teams use both.

**Q: Does Smartsheet have Gantt charts?**
Yes. Gantt view is available on every plan, with task dependencies, drag-and-drop rescheduling, milestones and critical path highlighting. Timeline view, a separate lane-based view, starts on the Business plan.

**Q: Does Smartsheet have Kanban boards?**
Yes. Board view displays sheet rows as cards in lanes that can represent stages, teams or sprints, with drag-and-drop and up to 14 fields per card. It is available on all plans, though Smartsheet remains grid-first rather than board-first.

**Q: Does Smartsheet have AI?**
Yes. Smartsheet lists Smart Assist (summaries, risk checks and actions), Smart Columns, an AI dashboard builder, formula generation, data analysis and intelligent form fill on all plans. From Business, it can also connect to Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot and other assistants through its MCP server.

**Q: What is Smartsheet Control Center?**
Control Center is a premium Smartsheet app for portfolio management. It uses blueprints to provision standardised project sheets, reports and dashboards automatically, pushes changes across existing projects and rolls up portfolio reporting. It is included in Advanced Work Management or sold as an add-on.

**Q: What are the main disadvantages of Smartsheet?**
The main disadvantages are the lack of a free plan, the cost of per-member pricing and premium add-ons, a less visual interface than board-first tools, a learning curve for advanced formulas and design, and performance concerns on large, complex sheets.

**Q: Does Smartsheet integrate with Microsoft Teams and Slack?**
Yes. Smartsheet integrates with Microsoft Teams, Outlook and Slack, and lists over 175 integrations in total, including Salesforce, Jira, DocuSign, Google Workspace apps, Power BI and Tableau.
How we review.
Rankings and scores are the editorial opinion of the Neural Project Institute, based on features, pricing, ease of use, scalability and published user ratings. Prices were checked on vendors' pricing pages and ratings on G2 and Capterra on 5 October 2026; both change often, so confirm on the vendor's site before buying. We are independent and do not receive payment for rankings.

# Trello Review 2026: Is It Worth It?

URL: https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/trello/
Section: Project management software reviews
Summary: Our Trello review covers boards, Power-Ups, automation, AI, pricing, the free plan, pros and cons, and whether Trello is worth it in 2026.


## Trello Review 2026: Is It Worth It?
Trello is a visual work management tool built around boards, lists and cards, and it is owned by Atlassian, the company behind Jira and Confluence. Its biggest strength is how quickly anyone can understand it and start using it; its biggest limitation is how little it offers, out of the box, for complex projects with dependencies, shared resources and many moving parts. This review covers boards and views, automation, Power-Ups, AI, Inbox and Planner, integrations, ease of use, pricing and overall value.
- Published 8 September 2026
- Last updated 7 October 2026
- Pricing and Capterra rating checked 7 October 2026

### Trello review: quick verdict
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Best for | Individuals and small teams that want simple, visual Kanban boards with almost no setup |
| Less suitable for | Teams managing complex schedules, dependencies, resources, budgets or many projects at once |

| Capterra rating | 4.5/5 from 23,628 reviews (checked 7 October 2026) |
| G2 rating | 4.4/5 from 14,063 reviews (checked 5 October 2026) |
Trello is one of the easiest project management tools to adopt, and for simple, card-based workflows it is fast, flexible and inexpensive. The trade-offs are clear: the Free plan is now capped at 10 collaborators per Workspace, timeline, table, calendar and dashboard views need Premium, there is no native dependency scheduling, resource management or portfolio reporting, and stretching Trello with Power-Ups adds cost and complexity. It is a strong choice for teams whose work fits on a board, and a weak one for teams whose work does not.
