### Collaboration and guests
Asana scores 9/10 for collaboration in our review and ClickUp 8/10. Asana keeps conversation on tasks with comments, collaborators, project messages and status updates, and includes **unlimited free guests** on paid plans, which suits agencies and partner work. ClickUp adds assigned comments (a comment that becomes an action for a named person), Chat channels, Clips (screen recordings) and guest permissions from Unlimited.
Notification volume is a common complaint for both: "excessive notifications" is one of the most discussed topics in Asana's Capterra reviews, and ClickUp reviewers raise the same issue. Agree notification settings early in either tool.

### Integrations
Asana says even its free plan includes more than 100 free integrations, including Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Workspace, Zoom, Jira, GitHub, Figma, Canva and Zapier, with Salesforce, Tableau and Power BI on Advanced.
ClickUp claims more than 1,000 integrations, a figure that includes connections through Zapier and Make. Native integrations include Slack, Microsoft Teams, Zoom, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Google Drive, HubSpot, Figma and Tableau. Integrations are unlimited from Unlimited, and webhooks and automation integrations are on Business. Both tools offer a public API and MCP connectivity for AI assistants.

### Security, administration and support
Asana's trust centre lists SOC 2 Type 2 and SOC 3 reports, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701, CSA STAR Level 1 and HIPAA support, with data residency in Europe, Australia and Japan. ClickUp's security page lists SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2 and SOC 3 reports, ISO 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701, ISO 42001 for AI management and PCI compliance, with HIPAA agreements and data residency (US, Europe or Asia Pacific) on Enterprise.
On both, SAML single sign-on, SCIM provisioning and audit logs are Enterprise features; ClickUp adds Google SSO on Business. Asana scores 9/10 for enterprise readiness against ClickUp's 8/10, reflecting Asana's longer record in large rollouts and its governance features on Enterprise+.
For support, ClickUp's pricing page lists 24/7 support on every plan, including Free Forever, and Capterra users rate its customer service 4.5/5. Asana offers a help centre, Asana Academy and a community forum, with a 4.3/5 customer service score on Capterra.

### Which is better for your team?

#### Start-ups and small businesses
ClickUp usually wins. Its free plan supports unlimited members, and $7 per user buys Gantt charts, time tracking, goals and docs. Asana Starter is a good choice for small teams that value simplicity over breadth.

#### Cross-functional teams and larger organisations
Asana usually wins. Its consistent structure, single-owner tasks, unlimited guests, portfolios and goals make it easier to roll out across many departments and keep reporting reliable.

#### Product and software teams
ClickUp has the edge with native sprints, sprint points, burndown and velocity reporting, and Docs for specs.

#### Marketing and creative teams
Both work well. Asana suits marketing functions that coordinate many campaigns with other departments and need approvals and proofing on Advanced. ClickUp suits teams that want briefs, calendars, whiteboards and proofing in one place at a lower price.

#### Agencies and freelancers
ClickUp's low price, native time tracking and client-shareable dashboards suit agencies; Asana's unlimited free guests make client collaboration simple. Solo freelancers will find ClickUp's free plan more capable than Asana Personal.

##### Choose ClickUp if…
- Start-ups and SMBs wanting maximum features per dollar
- Software and product teams wanting sprints and docs together
- Teams consolidating several tools

Asana review
ClickUp review

### How to switch between Asana and ClickUp
Moving from **Asana to ClickUp** is the better-supported direction. ClickUp has a built-in Asana importer that maps projects to Spaces, Folders or Lists, and lets you turn Asana sections into statuses, Lists or label fields. According to ClickUp's help centre, some items are not imported automatically, including nested subtasks, tasks shared between several projects, recurring tasks, private tasks and @mentions, and on the free plan you should check the 60MB storage limit before importing attachments. Imports take from about a minute to a few hours depending on volume.
Moving from **ClickUp to Asana** uses Asana's CSV importer: export a ClickUp view to CSV, then map the columns to Asana fields, creating matching custom fields first.
1. Rebuild one live project in the new tool during the trial, including automations, forms and the dashboard you rely on.
2. Agree the structure first: Spaces, Folders and Lists in ClickUp, or teams, projects and sections in Asana.
3. Import active work only and export completed projects as an archive.
4. Fix the items importers miss, such as recurring tasks and multi-project tasks, by hand.
5. Run both tools in parallel for a week or two, then switch off the old one.
Our guide on [how to choose project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/how-to-choose-project-management-software/) includes a checklist for running a fair trial.

### Alternatives worth comparing
If neither is quite right, [Wrike](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/) adds deeper resource planning, portfolio management and proofing for organisations that want one system of record, and [monday.com](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/) offers a more visual, board-based alternative that is very easy to adopt.
Compare [monday.com vs Asana](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/monday-vs-asana/) and [monday.com vs ClickUp](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/monday-vs-clickup/), browse [Asana alternatives](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/asana-alternatives/) and [ClickUp alternatives](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/clickup/clickup-alternatives/), or see every pairing on our [compare page](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/compare/).

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: Is ClickUp better than Asana?**
It depends on what you value. In our review Asana scores 9.0/10 and ClickUp 8.9/10. ClickUp wins on feature depth, Agile support and value for money; Asana wins on ease of use, collaboration and enterprise readiness. Choose ClickUp for breadth at a low price, Asana for easy adoption across many teams.

**Q: Is ClickUp cheaper than Asana?**
Yes, before AI. ClickUp costs $7 (Unlimited) or $12 (Business) per user/month billed annually, against $10.99 for Asana Starter and $24.99 for Advanced (checked 7 October 2026). ClickUp's full AI costs an extra $9 or $28 per user/month, while Asana's AI is included on paid plans with monthly allowances.

**Q: Which is easier to use, Asana or ClickUp?**
Asana. It scores 9/10 for ease of use in our review against ClickUp's 7/10. Asana's fixed structure and clean interface make it quick to adopt; ClickUp's many views and settings take longer to learn and benefit from a planned setup.

**Q: Which has the better free plan, Asana or ClickUp?**
ClickUp. Free Forever allows unlimited members and includes Docs, boards, calendars and sprints, though storage is limited to 60MB and Gantt and Dashboards are trial-only. Asana Personal is limited to 2 seats per project and team and has no timelines, dashboards, forms or automation.

**Q: Is ClickUp AI free?**
Only partly. ClickUp's free plan includes limited trial use of AI; full ClickUp Brain capabilities require the Brain AI add-on ($9 per user/month) or Everything AI ($28). Asana includes AI Teammates, Dash and AI Studio on its paid plans, within monthly usage allowances.

**Q: Which is better for Agile and software teams?**
ClickUp. It has native sprints, automatic spillover of unfinished work, sprint points on Business, and burndown, burnup and velocity reporting, plus GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket integrations. Asana suits product managers coordinating launches but is not a dedicated Agile tool.

**Q: Do Asana and ClickUp have Gantt charts?**
Yes. ClickUp's Gantt view (from the $7 Unlimited plan) supports all four dependency types, the critical path, slack time and baselines. Asana's timeline and Gantt views (from Starter) show dependencies and let you compare progress against a target schedule.

**Q: Which has better automation, Asana or ClickUp?**
Asana is more generous on limits, with unlimited rules on all paid plans. ClickUp has a larger automation library and an AI builder, but caps executions at 1,000 on Unlimited and 5,000 a month on Business.

**Q: Can Asana replace docs and chat like ClickUp?**
Not fully. Asana has project overviews, messages, comments and status updates, but no full docs-and-wiki workspace, whiteboard or chat. ClickUp includes Docs, wikis, Whiteboards and Chat, which helps teams consolidate tools.

**Q: Which is better for freelancers and small businesses?**
ClickUp is usually better value: its free plan allows unlimited members and its $7 plan includes Gantt charts, time tracking and goals. Asana Starter suits small teams that prefer a simpler tool and are happy to pay a little more per user.

**Q: Can I import Asana into ClickUp?**
Yes. ClickUp has a built-in Asana importer that maps projects to Spaces, Folders or Lists. Some items, such as nested subtasks, recurring tasks, private tasks and tasks shared between projects, are not imported automatically and need moving by hand.

**Q: Why do teams switch from Asana to ClickUp, or back?**
Teams move to ClickUp mainly for lower prices, built-in docs and sprints, and consolidating tools. Teams move to Asana mainly for a simpler, more consistent experience that is easier to roll out across many departments, and for its goals and portfolios.

**Q: What are good alternatives to Asana and ClickUp?**
Wrike is our top-rated tool and goes further on resource management, portfolios and approvals. monday.com offers a highly visual, easy-to-adopt alternative. See our Asana alternatives and ClickUp alternatives pages, or our top 10 project management tools.

## Asana vs Jira (2026): Which Is Better?
Asana is best for cross-team task and goal management; Jira is best for software and agile teams. We compare pricing, features, ease of use and G2 and Capterra ratings to help you choose.
- Published 22 September 2026

### Key takeaways
- **Overall winner:** Asana (9.0/10 vs 8.6/10), winning 3 of 7 categories.

- **Choose Jira** for software development and IT teams running Scrum or Kanban.
- **Price:** Asana Free (Personal); paid from $10.99/user/month; Jira Free for up to 10 users; Standard roughly $7.91/user/month.

### Quick verdict
Asana is a superb, easy choice for coordinating work across teams. For deeper resource, budget and approval management in one platform, Wrike goes further.

# Asana vs Microsoft Planner (2026): Which Is Better?

## Asana vs Microsoft Planner (2026): Which Is Better?
Asana is best for cross-team task and goal management; Microsoft Planner is best for microsoft 365 organisations. We compare pricing, features, ease of use and G2 and Capterra ratings to help you choose.
- Published 23 September 2026

### Key takeaways
- **Overall winner:** Asana (9.0/10 vs 8.1/10), winning 6 of 7 categories.
- **Choose Asana** for organisations that want clean, reliable task management connected to goals and portfolios.
- **Choose Microsoft Planner** for organisations standardised on Microsoft 365 and Teams.
- **Price:** Asana Free (Personal); paid from $10.99/user/month; Microsoft Planner Basic Planner included in Microsoft 365; Plan 1 from $10/user/month.

### Quick verdict
Asana is a superb, easy choice for coordinating work across teams. For deeper resource, budget and approval management in one platform, Wrike goes further.
Planner is the convenient default for Microsoft 365 shops. For richer collaboration, resource and portfolio management, Wrike integrates with Microsoft tools while offering far more depth.

### Asana vs Microsoft Planner at a glance
|  | [Asana](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/) | [Microsoft Planner](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/microsoft-planner/) |

# Asana vs Notion: Which Should Your Team Use in 2026?

URL: https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/asana-vs-notion/
Section: Tool comparisons
Summary: Asana vs Notion compared: pricing, project views, docs, goals, AI, workload and ratings, plus clear advice on which tool fits your team in 2026.

vs

## Asana vs Notion: Which Should Your Team Use in 2026?
Asana vs Notion comes down to one question: do you want a dedicated work management tool, or a flexible workspace where you build your own project system next to your documents? Asana is the stronger choice for structured, cross-team project work with goals, portfolios and workload views; Notion is the better fit for docs-first teams that want wikis, specs and lightweight project tracking in one place. This comparison covers ease of use, planning, docs, AI, pricing, ratings and how to choose.
- Published 23 September 2026
- Last updated 9 October 2026
- Prices and ratings checked 5 October 2026

### Key takeaways
- Asana scores 9.0/10 and Notion 8.0/10 in our review; Asana wins four of seven categories, Notion wins value for money, and two are tied.
- Asana is built for managing work across teams, with goals, portfolios, workload and approvals on its Advanced plan.
- Notion is a docs-and-databases workspace: unbeatable for wikis and specs, but you design the project system yourself and there is no native time tracking or workload view.
- Paid plans start at $10.99 per user/month for Asana Starter and $10 per member/month for Notion Plus (annual billing, checked 7 October 2026).
- Notion AI is included only from the Business plan ($20); Asana includes AI Teammates, Dash and AI Studio on every paid plan, with metered usage.
- Many teams use both: Notion for knowledge and planning documents, Asana for day-to-day execution.

### Quick verdict
**Choose Asana** if you need a ready-made system for assigning, scheduling and tracking work across several teams, and want to connect that work to goals and portfolio reporting. **Choose Notion** if your team lives in documents and wants specs, meeting notes, wikis and simple project boards in one flexible workspace, and you are happy to design how it works.
In our scoring, Asana (9.0/10, ranked #3 in our [top 10 project management tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/)) wins on ease of use, planning and resource management, Agile and software teams, and enterprise readiness. Notion (8.0/10, #8) wins on value for money, and the two tie on feature depth and collaboration. The scores reflect our focus on project management: as a knowledge base, Notion is the stronger product.
If neither fits because you need detailed resource planning, budgets, critical path scheduling and portfolio control in one platform, our top-ranked tool, [Wrike](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/), goes further than both.

### Asana vs Notion at a glance
|  | [Asana](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/) | [Notion](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/notion/) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Our score | **9.0/10** | **8.0/10** |

| Free plan | Yes (Personal plan, up to 2 users) | Yes |
| Free trial | Advanced plan trial, no credit card | Free plan available |

### The core difference: work manager vs connected workspace
On the surface, Asana and Notion look alike. Both have boards, timelines, calendars, forms, automations and AI. The difference is in how they are built, and that shapes almost every other comparison on this page.
**Asana** is purpose-built work management. Tasks, projects, portfolios and goals are fixed building blocks that Asana connects in what it calls the Work Graph, so finishing a task can update a project, a portfolio and a goal. Every team gets the same structure on day one, which makes Asana fast to adopt and easy to report across.
**Notion** is a set of building blocks. Pages hold documents; databases hold items with properties; views show those items as tables, boards, timelines or calendars. A project tracker in Notion is a database you (or a template) design. That flexibility lets Notion become a wiki, a CRM, a roadmap and a task board in the same workspace, but someone has to design and maintain it.
|  | Asana | Notion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it is | Dedicated work and project management | Docs, wikis and databases in one workspace |
| Unit of work | Task, with one assignee | Database item, which is also a full page |
| Structure | Provided: teams, projects, portfolios, goals | Designed by you: pages, databases, relations |
| Strongest at | Cross-team coordination and visibility | Documentation and connected knowledge |
| Main trade-off | Key features on the Advanced plan | No native workload, time tracking or portfolios |
A useful rule of thumb: if your main problem is **knowing who is doing what by when across teams**, start with Asana. If it is **keeping knowledge, decisions and work in one place**, start with Notion.

### What are Asana and Notion?

#### Asana
Asana, Inc. was founded in 2008 by Dustin Moskovitz and Justin Rosenstein and is listed on the New York Stock Exchange. It is used for cross-team projects, campaign planning, request intake, goals and OKRs, and portfolio reporting. Each task has one owner, a due date and optional dependencies, and a task can sit in several projects at once.

#### Notion
Notion is made by Notion Labs, Inc., a privately held company based in San Francisco that launched Notion 1.0 in 2016. Teams use it for wikis, product specs, meeting notes, roadmaps and project trackers, with companion apps for calendar and mail. Project management features (projects and tasks databases, sprints, timelines, forms and automations) are built on its databases.

### Ease of use and setup
**Asana** gives you a working structure immediately: create a project from a template, add tasks, invite colleagues and switch between list, board and calendar views. Reviewers consistently describe the interface as clean and intuitive, and its Capterra ease-of-use sub-score is 4.4/5 (checked 7 October 2026). The harder part is organisational, not technical: agreeing custom fields, templates, rules and portfolio structures so every team works the same way.
**Notion** is easy to start and harder to master. Writing pages and ticking off to-dos takes minutes. Building a reliable project system with related databases, rollups, formulas, filtered views and automations takes real design effort, and G2 users list a steep learning curve for advanced setups among its main drawbacks. Capterra reviewers also report that Notion can feel sluggish with very large databases and long pages. Its Capterra ease-of-use sub-score is also 4.4/5, but that reflects its many users who mainly write documents.
In our scoring, Asana takes ease of use 9/10 to Notion's 7/10 because a non-technical team can manage projects in Asana without anyone building the system first.
Tip
If you choose Notion for projects, start from Notion's projects and tasks template rather than a blank page, and appoint one owner for the core databases. Most Notion sprawl comes from several people building slightly different trackers.

### Project planning: views, timelines and dependencies
Both tools let you see the same work in several ways. The difference is depth and which plan you need.
| View or feature | Asana | Notion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List / table | Yes, every plan | Yes, every plan |
| Board (Kanban) | Yes, every plan | Yes, every plan |
| Calendar | Yes, every plan | Yes, every plan |
| Timeline / Gantt | Timeline and Gantt from Starter | Timeline view on database items |
| Dependencies | Yes, shown as chains on timeline and Gantt | Blocking relationships, visible on the timeline |
| Target schedule / baseline | Compare progress against a target schedule in Gantt | Not described in Notion's documentation |
| Critical path | Not described on Asana's product pages | Not described in Notion's documentation |
| Sprints | Boards and sprint-style projects | Built-in sprints with backlog and rollover options |
Asana's [Gantt chart](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/gantt-chart/) view, from the Starter plan, shows dependency chains, lets you drag tasks to reschedule and compares progress against a target schedule. That covers most campaign plans, launches and cross-team projects. Notion's timeline plots database items on a Gantt-style chart with draggable dates and visible dependencies, which is well suited to roadmaps and high-level plans.
Neither vendor describes [critical path](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/critical-path-method/) analysis, so teams running tightly sequenced, date-driven schedules should test carefully or consider a scheduling-focused tool. Both offer [Kanban boards](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/kanban/kanban-boards/) on every plan, including free.
For product teams, Notion's built-in sprints are a genuine plus: switching them on creates a sprint board with current sprint, planning and backlog views, and lets you choose what happens to unfinished tasks. It covers the basics of sprint planning, though neither tool matches Jira for velocity and burndown reporting.

### Docs, wikis and knowledge management
This is Notion's clearest win. Pages are fast to write, nest without limit, embed databases, files, code and design frames, and can be organised into a searchable team wiki. On Business, verified pages tell readers which documents are current. For project teams, the big benefit is that the brief, requirements, decisions and meeting notes live next to the tasks they produce. Our [meeting notes template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/meeting-notes-template/) shows the kind of page that works well as a Notion database item.
Asana is not a wiki. It has task descriptions, project overviews and briefs, project messages and status updates, which are enough to give context to the work. But company handbooks, long-form specs and knowledge bases usually live in another tool alongside Asana, and Notion is a common choice for that role.

### Goals, portfolios and multi-project reporting
This is Asana's clearest win. On the Advanced plan, **goals** let you set company, team and individual objectives, break them into sub-goals, and update progress automatically from connected projects. **Portfolios** group projects so leaders see status, progress and owners on one screen and publish written status updates. **Dashboards**, from Starter, chart tasks by status, overdue work and custom-field totals. If you manage by OKRs, our [OKR template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/okr-template/) is a good way to draft goals before building them in Asana.
Notion has no packaged goals, portfolio or status-reporting features. You can build them: a Projects database with status and owner, a Goals database related to it, rollups for progress, and a dashboard page of charts and filtered views. Free includes one chart and paid plans include unlimited charts. It works, but someone has to build and maintain it. If leaders need consistent reporting across many projects, see our guide to [managing multiple projects](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/managing-multiple-projects/) for what that reporting should cover.

### Workload, resources and time tracking
Asana's **workload** view (Advanced) shows each person's effort across projects in a portfolio against a capacity you set, and lets managers drag work to rebalance. Advanced also adds time tracking with estimated versus actual effort, and Enterprise adds organisation-wide resource management and capacity planning.
Notion has no native time tracking, workload view or resource scheduling. Teams approximate them with number properties for estimated hours, rollups and third-party time-tracking integrations. For a small team that rarely matters; for agencies billing hours or PMOs doing [capacity planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/capacity-planning/), it is usually decisive.
This gap explains most of the difference in our planning and resource score (Asana 8/10, Notion 5/10). Organisations that need deeper resource, budget and financial control than Asana offers usually look at Wrike; see [Wrike vs Asana](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/wrike-vs-asana/).

### Automation and AI

#### Automation
Asana's **rules** pair a trigger (a form submission, a task moved, a due date approaching) with actions such as assigning, moving, requesting approval or posting to Slack, and every paid plan includes unlimited automations. Notion's **database automations** run when a page is added, a property changes or a schedule fires, and can edit properties, add pages, notify people, post to Slack or send webhooks. They require a paid plan, and multi-step logic is simpler in Asana.

#### AI
Both vendors now put AI at the centre of their products, but they package it differently (checked 7 October 2026):
- **Asana:** AI Teammates (prebuilt and custom AI agents), Asana Dash (AI briefs and next steps) and AI Studio (a no-code builder for AI workflows) are included on paid plans, with usage metered by requests and credits and paid top-ups available.
- **Notion:** Notion AI (Notion Agent, AI Meeting Notes and Enterprise Search) is included on Business and Enterprise; Free and Plus get only a limited trial. Custom Agents, which run on triggers or schedules, use Notion credits sold to Business and Enterprise customers at $10 per 1,000 credits a month.
In practice, Asana's AI is aimed at moving project work along (triage, routing, status reports, capacity checks), while Notion's is strongest at writing, summarising meetings and finding information across your workspace and connected apps. On data, Asana states that its AI partners do not use customer data to train their models, and Notion states that it does not train AI models on customer content.

### Collaboration, guests and notifications
Both tools score 9/10 for collaboration in our review, for different reasons. Asana keeps conversation on the task: comments, @mentions, collaborators who follow a task, approvals (on Advanced) and status updates, with unlimited free guests on paid plans for clients and freelancers. Notion excels at real-time co-editing: several people can write on the same page, comment on any block and @mention colleagues, and Plus and above allow unlimited guests.
Each has a familiar downside. Asana users frequently mention notification overload, so agree notification settings and @mention habits early. Notion users more often mention workspace sprawl, so agree a teamspace structure and database owners. For intake, both offer forms that create work automatically; our [work request template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/work-request-template/) lists the fields worth collecting in either tool.

### Integrations and using Asana and Notion together
Asana says even its free plan includes more than 100 integrations, including Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Workspace, Zoom, Jira, GitHub, Figma and Zapier; Salesforce, Tableau and Power BI are listed on Advanced. Notion's Plus plan includes basic connections such as Slack and Google Drive, and Business adds premium connections, including GitHub and Asana. Both have public APIs.
That Asana connection points to a common pattern: **use both**. Many teams keep their wiki, specs and meeting notes in Notion and run day-to-day execution in Asana, linking the two so context and tasks stay connected. It costs more than one tool, but it plays to each product's strengths. If you would rather have docs and project management in a single tool, ClickUp combines both; see [ClickUp vs Notion](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/clickup/clickup-vs-notion/).

### Security and administration
Both vendors publish strong security credentials. Asana's trust centre lists SOC 2 Type 2 and SOC 3 reports, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701, CSA STAR Level 1, and HIPAA (opt-in) and GDPR support, with data residency options and customer-managed encryption keys. Notion's security page lists a SOC 2 Type 2 attestation and ISO 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701 certifications, and Notion signs a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement for healthcare customers.
Admin controls scale by plan in both. Asana reserves SAML single sign-on and SCIM for Enterprise; Notion offers SAML SSO from Business and SCIM, audit logs and advanced controls on Enterprise. Confirm current certifications and their scope in each vendor's trust documentation during procurement.

### Asana vs Notion pricing
|  | Asana | Notion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plans | **Personal:** $0 **Starter:** $10.99/user/month annual ($13.49 monthly) **Advanced:** $24.99/user/month annual ($30.49 monthly) **Enterprise:** Contact sales | **Free:** $0 **Plus:** From $10/member/month **Business:** From $20/member/month **Enterprise:** Contact sales |
Checked on vendors' pricing pages on 5 October 2026. Read the full [Asana pricing](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/#pricing) and [Notion pricing](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/notion/#pricing) breakdowns.
Here is what each plan means in practice, based on the vendors' pricing pages (checked 7 October 2026). Prices are per user (Asana) or member (Notion) per month in US dollars.
- **Asana Personal ($0)** includes unlimited tasks and projects with list, board and calendar views, but is limited to 2 seats per project and team, so it suits individuals and pairs.
- **Asana Starter ($10.99 annual, $13.49 monthly)** adds timeline and Gantt, dashboards, forms, custom fields, unlimited automations, unlimited free guests and AI.
- **Asana Advanced ($24.99 annual, $30.49 monthly)** adds goals, portfolios, workload, approvals and proofing, time tracking and Salesforce, Tableau and Power BI integrations.
- **Notion Free ($0)** is aimed at individuals: blocks are limited once a workspace has two or more members, uploads are capped at 5 MB and page history lasts 7 days.
- **Notion Plus ($10 yearly; about $12 monthly)** removes the block limit for teams and adds unlimited uploads, charts and guests and custom forms. Notion AI is only a trial on Plus.
- **Notion Business ($20 yearly; about $24 monthly)** adds Notion AI, SAML SSO, private teamspaces, granular database permissions and premium connections.
Enterprise plans for both are priced on request. Here is the monthly cost for a team on annual billing, before add-ons:
| Team size | Asana Starter | Asana Advanced | Notion Plus | Notion Business |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 people | $54.95 | $124.95 | $50 | $100 |
| 10 people | $109.90 | $249.90 | $100 | $200 |
| 25 people | $274.75 | $624.75 | $250 | $500 |
At entry level, the two are close. The real comparison is usually **Asana Advanced vs Notion Business**, because those are the plans that unlock the features each tool is known for (goals and portfolios in Asana; AI and advanced permissions in Notion). Remember to add Notion credits if you plan to run Custom Agents, and extra AI usage in Asana if you lean heavily on AI Teammates or AI Studio.

Asana's wins come from structure: it is quicker for non-technical teams to adopt (ease of use), it has native workload, goals and portfolios (planning and resource management), and it has the admin and security controls large organisations expect (scalability). Notion wins value for money because Plus and Business include unlimited docs, wikis and databases at a lower price than Asana's equivalent tiers. Feature depth is tied because each tool is deep in a different area.

Notion's ratings are slightly higher, but read them in context: many Notion reviewers use it mainly for notes and knowledge, not as a project system. In Capterra's topic summaries (checked 7 October 2026), Asana users most often praise real-time project tracking, versatile work organisation and deadline management, and most often criticise excessive notifications and occasional performance problems. Notion users most often praise the flexible all-in-one hub and real-time collaboration, and most often criticise sluggish performance with large content, limited offline use and the mobile app.
Both review sites label vendor-invited and incentivised reviews. Filtering for non-incentivised reviews from companies of your size gives a more cautious and more useful picture than the headline score.

##### Choose Asana if…

- Companies that manage by goals and OKRs

##### Choose Notion if…
- Start-ups and small teams wanting docs and tasks together
- Product teams managing specs and roadmaps

Whatever you pick, read [how to choose project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/how-to-choose-project-management-software/) and test one real project before you commit.

### How to switch between Asana and Notion
Moving in either direction is manageable if you migrate active work, not your entire history.
1. **Decide what moves.** List active projects, templates and the documents people still use. Archive the rest in the old tool or export it.
2. **Design the target structure first.** In Asana, agree teams, projects, sections and custom fields. In Notion, design your Projects and Tasks databases, their properties and relations before importing anything.
3. **Export and import.** Asana exports projects to CSV, and Notion databases export to CSV and pages to Markdown or HTML. Notion's importer lists Asana among its supported sources, and Asana can import CSV files into a new project. Check field mapping (assignees, dates, statuses) on a small sample first.
4. **Rebuild automation.** Rules, automations and forms do not transfer. Recreate the few that matter most and add others as people ask for them.
5. **Pilot with one team** for two to four weeks, then fix structure problems before the wider rollout.
6. **Set a cut-over date** after which new work only goes into the new tool, and keep the old one read-only for reference.
Tip
If you are moving from Notion to Asana, you may not need to move your docs at all. Keeping the wiki in Notion and linking it to Asana projects is often less disruptive than recreating long documents as task descriptions.

### Alternatives to Asana and Notion
If neither tool feels right, three others are worth a look:
- **[Wrike](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/)**, our #1 tool (9.4/10), for organisations that need critical path scheduling, resource planning, budgets, proofing and portfolio reporting in one platform.
- **[ClickUp](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/clickup/)**, for teams that want docs and richer project management in one tool at a lower price.
- **[monday.com](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/)**, for highly visual, customisable boards that non-technical teams adopt quickly; see [monday.com vs Notion](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/monday-vs-notion/) and [monday.com vs Asana](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/monday-vs-asana/).
For more options, read our [Asana alternatives](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/asana-alternatives/) and [Notion alternatives](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/notion/notion-alternatives/) guides, or browse all [head-to-head comparisons](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/compare/).

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: Is Notion better than Asana?**
Not overall for project management, but it is better for documentation. Notion is the stronger choice for wikis, specs and meeting notes connected to lightweight project tracking. Asana is stronger for structured cross-team work, with goals, portfolios, workload and approvals. In our review Asana scores 9.0/10 and Notion 8.0/10.

**Q: Can Notion replace Asana for project management?**
For small teams and lightweight-to-moderate projects, yes: Notion has task databases, boards, timelines, sprints, forms and automations. It cannot replace Asana's native goals, portfolios, workload view or time tracking, so teams that rely on those usually keep a dedicated tool.

**Q: Is Asana or Notion cheaper?**
Notion is slightly cheaper at each level: Plus costs $10 per member/month and Business $20, against $10.99 for Asana Starter and $24.99 for Asana Advanced on annual billing (checked 7 October 2026). Add Notion credits for Custom Agents or extra Asana AI usage if you need them.

**Q: Are Asana and Notion free?**
Both have free plans. Asana Personal is free but limited to 2 seats per project and team. Notion Free is aimed at individuals, with limited blocks once two or more members join, 5 MB uploads and 7-day page history. Growing teams will need a paid plan on either.

**Q: Which is easier to use, Asana or Notion?**
Asana is easier for project management because the structure is ready-made: projects, tasks, owners and dates work out of the box. Notion is easy for writing and simple lists, but building a full project system with relations, rollups and automations takes more learning. We score ease of use 9/10 for Asana and 7/10 for Notion.

**Q: Does Notion have Gantt charts like Asana?**
Notion has a timeline view that works like a simple Gantt chart, with draggable dates and visible dependencies. Asana has both timeline and Gantt views from the Starter plan, including comparison against a target schedule. Neither vendor describes critical path analysis.

**Q: Which has better AI, Asana or Notion?**
They are strong in different areas. Asana's AI Teammates, Dash and AI Studio focus on moving project work along, such as triage, routing and status reports, and are on all paid plans with metered usage. Notion AI excels at writing, meeting notes and search, but is included only from the Business plan.

**Q: Does Notion have time tracking or workload management?**
No. Notion has no native time tracking, workload view or resource scheduling; teams use number properties, rollups or third-party integrations instead. Asana includes workload and time tracking on Advanced, and capacity planning on Enterprise.

**Q: Can you use Asana and Notion together?**
Yes, and many teams do. A common set-up keeps the wiki, specs and meeting notes in Notion and runs execution in Asana. Notion's Business plan includes a premium connection with Asana, and both tools have APIs and connect through automation tools such as Zapier.

**Q: Which is better for small teams or start-ups?**
Notion often suits start-ups that want one affordable workspace for docs and tasks. Asana suits small teams that mainly need clear ownership, deadlines and timelines, and Starter is reasonably priced. Note that Asana's free plan is limited to two seats, so most teams will pay from the start.

**Q: Which is better for product and engineering teams?**
Notion is popular for specs, PRDs, roadmaps and sprints, while Asana is popular for cross-functional launches. Both integrate with GitHub and Jira, and many engineering teams keep a dedicated issue tracker for execution alongside either tool.

**Q: Which is better for large organisations?**
Asana, in most cases. It offers goals, portfolios, enterprise identity controls, data residency and capacity planning for coordinating many teams. Large organisations often adopt Notion as a knowledge and collaboration layer rather than as their main delivery system.

**Q: How do I move from Notion to Asana, or from Asana to Notion?**
Export active projects to CSV, design the target structure first, import a small sample to check field mapping, then rebuild your most important automations and pilot with one team. Notion's importer supports Asana, and Asana imports CSV files into new projects.

**Q: What are good alternatives to Asana and Notion?**
Wrike suits organisations needing resource, budget and portfolio control; ClickUp combines docs and project management at a lower price; monday.com offers very visual, customisable boards. See our [Asana alternatives](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/asana-alternatives/) and [Notion alternatives](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/notion/notion-alternatives/).

# monday.com vs Asana (2026): Which Is Better for Your Team?

URL: https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/monday-vs-asana/
Section: Tool comparisons
Summary: monday.com vs Asana compared: pricing, seat minimums, automation limits, AI, Gantt, goals and portfolios, ratings and which to choose in 2026.

vs

## monday.com vs Asana (2026): Which Is Better for Your Team?
monday.com vs Asana is one of the closest contests in work management: monday.com scores 9.1/10 in our review and Asana 9.0/10. Choose monday.com if you want colourful, flexible boards that any team can shape into its own workflow; choose Asana if you want structured cross-team task management with clear ownership, linked to goals and portfolios. Below we compare current pricing (including monday.com's seat buckets), automation limits, AI, reporting, resource management and user ratings so you can decide for your own team.
- Published 19 September 2026
- Last updated 9 October 2026
- Prices and ratings checked 5 October 2026

### Key takeaways
- Overall: monday.com 9.1/10 vs Asana 9.0/10. monday.com wins on feature depth; the other six categories are tied in our scoring.
- Price: monday.com is cheaper per seat ($9, $12 and $19 billed annually) but sells seats in buckets with a 3-seat minimum; Asana Starter is $10.99 and Advanced $24.99 per user/month billed annually (checked 7 October 2026).
- Automation: Asana includes unlimited rules on every paid plan; monday.com caps actions at 250 a month on Standard and 25,000 on Pro.
- Strategy and reporting: Asana's goals and portfolios (Advanced) are its standout; monday.com's dashboards and visual boards are its standout.
- If resource, portfolio and approval depth decides it, also look at Wrike, our #1-ranked tool.

### Quick verdict
Both tools are excellent, easy-to-adopt work management platforms, and most teams would be well served by either. The difference is in their philosophy. **monday.com** gives you a flexible board, a large library of column types and colourful dashboards, and lets each team build the workflow it wants. **Asana** gives you a clear structure of teams, projects and tasks with exactly one owner per task, and connects that work to portfolios and company goals.
- **Pick monday.com** if adoption across non-technical teams, visual dashboards and custom workflows (requests, campaigns, operations) matter most.
- **Pick Asana** if you coordinate work across many teams, manage by goals or OKRs, or want unlimited automation rules without counting actions.
- **Consider Wrike** if you need deeper resource planning, portfolio control and creative approvals in one platform; it is our highest-rated tool overall.
Read the [Wrike vs monday.com](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/wrike-vs-monday/) and [Wrike vs Asana](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/wrike-vs-asana/) comparisons if resource management is on your list.

### monday.com vs Asana at a glance
|  | [monday.com](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/) | [Asana](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Our score | **9.1/10** | **9.0/10** |
| Best for | Teams that want a colourful, intuitive platform they can shape into almost any workflow | Organisations that want clean, reliable task management connected to goals and portfolios |
| Starting price | Free for up to 2 seats; paid from $9/seat/month | Free (Personal); paid from $10.99/user/month |
| Free plan | Yes (up to 2 seats) | Yes (Personal plan, up to 2 users) |
| Free trial | 14-day Pro trial, no credit card | Advanced plan trial, no credit card |
| Vendor | monday.com Ltd. | Asana, Inc. |
Scores are our editorial ratings; prices and ratings in the tables on this page come from vendor pricing pages, G2 and Capterra, and change often.

### Key differences in one table
The overall scores are almost identical, so the decision usually comes down to a handful of practical differences. These are based on each vendor's published plan information, checked on 7 October 2026.
|  | monday.com | Asana |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How work is structured | Boards of items (rows) and columns, grouped into workspaces | Teams, projects, sections and tasks; one task can sit in several projects |
| Free plan | Up to 2 seats, 3 boards and 3 docs | Personal: up to 2 seats per project and team, unlimited tasks and projects |
| Cheapest plan with Gantt / timeline | Standard, $12/seat/month | Starter, $10.99/user/month |
| Seat rules | 3-seat minimum, then buckets in multiples of 5 | Per user; no seat minimum listed on paid plans |
| Automation | 250 automation and 250 integration actions a month on Standard; 25,000 each on Pro | Unlimited rules on all paid plans |
| Time tracking | Pro and Enterprise | Advanced (or via integrations on lower plans) |
| Workload view | Pro | Advanced |
| Portfolios and goals | Portfolio and resource management on Enterprise | Portfolios and goals on Advanced |
| External users | Unlimited free viewers on paid plans; guests from Standard | Unlimited free guests on paid plans |
| Free trial | 14-day Pro trial, no credit card | Advanced trial, no credit card |

### What is monday.com?
monday.com is a board-based work management platform launched in 2012 and listed on Nasdaq since 2021. Every piece of work is an item on a board, and columns hold its owner, status, dates, budget or any other data you need. The same board can be shown as a table, Kanban board, calendar, timeline or Gantt chart, and dashboards pull numbers from several boards into one view. monday.com also sells separate CRM, service and software development (monday dev) products on the same platform.
Its biggest strength is how quickly people pick it up. Colour-coded status columns make a board readable at a glance, more than 200 templates give a working start, and WorkForms and automations turn requests into assigned, tracked work. The trade-offs are a seat-bucket pricing model, metered automation actions and AI credits, and several project management features (time tracking, workload, portfolio and resource management) reserved for higher plans.

### What is Asana?
Asana is a work management platform founded in 2008 and listed on the New York Stock Exchange since 2020. Work is organised into teams, projects (split into sections) and tasks, and each task has exactly one assignee. Above projects sit **portfolios**, which group related projects for status reporting, and **goals**, which show what the work is for. A completed task can update the progress of a portfolio or goal, which Asana calls its Work Graph.
Asana's strengths are a clean interface, dependable cross-team coordination and the way goals and portfolios connect daily tasks to strategy. The trade-offs are that those distinctive features start on the Advanced plan, AI use is metered, and its resource and financial controls are lighter than those of PMO-focused platforms.

### Pricing compared
|  | monday.com | Asana |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plans | **Free:** $0 **Basic:** $9/seat/month (annual) **Standard:** $12/seat/month (annual) **Pro:** $19/seat/month (annual) **Enterprise:** Contact sales | **Personal:** $0 **Starter:** $10.99/user/month annual ($13.49 monthly) **Advanced:** $24.99/user/month annual ($30.49 monthly) **Enterprise:** Contact sales |
Checked on vendors' pricing pages on 5 October 2026. Read the full [monday.com pricing](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/#pricing) and [Asana pricing](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/#pricing) breakdowns.
On paper, monday.com looks cheaper: $9, $12 and $19 per seat/month billed annually against Asana's $10.99 (Starter) and $24.99 (Advanced) per user/month billed annually, or $13.49 and $30.49 billed monthly. In practice, the comparison depends on which plan you need and how many people you have.

#### Plan for plan: which tiers match?
The plans do not line up neatly. Asana Starter is roughly equivalent to monday.com Standard: both add timeline and Gantt views, dashboards, forms, guests and automation. Asana Advanced sits somewhere between monday.com Pro and Enterprise: it adds time tracking and workload (Pro on monday.com) but also portfolios, goals, approvals and proofing, which monday.com either reserves for Enterprise or handles through boards and statuses. monday.com Basic ($9) has no Asana equivalent; it removes Free plan limits but has no timeline, Gantt, guests or automations, so most project teams skip it.

#### Seat minimums and buckets
monday.com's support documentation says paid plans start at 3 seats and then rise in groups of 5 (5, 10, 15 and so on). A team of 6 therefore pays for 10 seats. Free viewers do not use a seat, but everyone who edits does. monday.com asks organisations with more than 40 users to request a quote. Asana's pricing page lists no seat minimum on paid plans and says you can add unlimited members.

#### What a team actually pays
Here is the monthly cost at three team sizes, using annual prices checked on 7 October 2026. We have applied monday.com's published seat buckets; Asana is calculated per user. Taxes, add-ons and negotiated discounts are excluded, so treat these as indicative.
| Team size | monday.com Standard | Asana Starter | monday.com Pro | Asana Advanced |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5 users | $60 (5 seats) | $54.95 | $95 (5 seats) | $124.95 |
| 6 users | $120 (10 seats) | $65.94 | $190 (10 seats) | $149.94 |
| 12 users | $180 (15 seats) | $131.88 | $285 (15 seats) | $299.88 |
The pattern is clear. At the entry level, Asana Starter is cheaper than monday.com Standard and much cheaper when your headcount falls just above a monday.com bucket. At the higher tier, monday.com Pro is usually cheaper than Asana Advanced, but Asana Advanced includes portfolios, goals and approvals that monday.com keeps for Enterprise. Price the plan you will really need, not the headline starting price.

#### Free plans and trials
Both free plans are now aimed at individuals and pairs. monday.com Free allows up to 2 seats, 3 boards and 3 docs, with no timeline, Gantt or automations. Asana Personal allows up to 2 seats per project and team with unlimited tasks and projects, and list, board and calendar views, but no timelines, dashboards, forms, rules or AI. For trials, monday.com offers 14 days of Pro with no credit card, and Asana offers a self-serve Advanced trial with no credit card; Asana's pricing page does not state the length.

### Ease of use
Both tools score 9/10 for ease of use in our review, and both are among the easiest capable platforms to roll out. They are easy in different ways.
monday.com is easy to **start**. A new user understands a colourful board within minutes, and adding a column or status takes seconds. The learning curve arrives later, when you connect boards, design dashboards across many boards, set permissions and build automations within the action limits. Without agreed standards, large accounts can end up with many slightly different boards for the same process.
Asana is easy to **stay organised in**. Its structure (team, project, section, task, one owner) is opinionated, which means less design work up front and more consistency across teams. My Tasks and Inbox give each person a clear daily view. The harder parts are portfolios, goals, workload and AI Studio, which depend on teams keeping projects up to date.
Tip
Whichever you choose, appoint one owner for templates, fields and naming conventions before you invite the wider organisation. It is the single biggest factor in whether reporting works six months later.

### Views, planning and Gantt charts
Both tools offer list or table, Kanban board, calendar, timeline and Gantt views. Asana includes list, board and calendar views on its free plan; on monday.com, the timeline, Gantt and calendar views start on Standard.
For scheduling, monday.com's Standard plan adds timeline and Gantt views with a dependency column and drag-to-reschedule. According to monday.com's plan documentation, Pro adds milestones and the critical path, and its Gantt feature page also lists baselines. Asana's timeline and Gantt views start on Starter, show dependency chains, and let you set a target schedule and compare progress against it. Asana's product pages do not describe critical path analysis, so if your projects are tightly sequenced, test both on a real plan.
For most marketing, operations and client projects, either tool is enough. For large, date-driven programmes with many dependencies, look at a scheduling-focused tool such as [Wrike](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/) or read our guides to [Gantt charts](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/gantt-chart/) and the [critical path method](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/critical-path-method/). If your work is flow-based rather than date-based, our guide to [Kanban boards](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/kanban/kanban-boards/) explains how to set up columns in either tool.

### Automation and request intake
This is one of the clearest practical differences. **Asana includes unlimited automation rules on every paid plan**, from Starter upwards, with a library of ready-made rules such as reassigning work when a section changes or posting to Slack when a task is complete.
**monday.com meters automation.** Standard includes 250 automation actions and 250 integration actions a month; Pro includes 25,000 of each; Enterprise up to 250,000 combined. 250 actions disappears quickly in a busy team, so in practice serious automation on monday.com starts on Pro. In return, monday.com's recipe-style builder is very approachable, and its AI-powered workflows add more capability (capped at 3 active workflows on Standard and 20 on Pro).
For intake, both tools turn form submissions into tracked work. monday.com WorkForms support conditional questions, branding and an AI form builder. Asana forms (from Starter) support required attachments and website embedding, and Advanced adds branching. If your team handles many requests, our free [work request template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/work-request-template/) shows the fields worth collecting before you build the form.

### AI features
Both vendors now put AI at the centre of their products, and both meter it.
**monday.com** includes monday sidekick (an AI assistant that summarises, drafts, updates tasks and builds automations, dashboards and forms), prebuilt and custom AI agents, AI blocks on boards, and a meeting Notetaker from Standard. For accounts that joined from May 2026, AI draws on a shared monthly pool of credits: at least 1,000 on Basic, 2,000 on Standard and 3,000 on Pro, with extra credits available to buy.
**Asana** includes AI Teammates (more than 30 prebuilt agents, plus custom ones), Asana Dash (AI briefs and next steps) and AI Studio (a no-code builder for AI workflows) on paid plans. According to Asana's pricing comparison, AI Teammates and Dash include 5 requests per user per month, capped at 50 per account on Starter and Advanced, and AI Studio includes a monthly credit allowance that rises by plan. Extra usage costs $0.50 per request in prepaid packs or $0.60 pay-as-you-go.
Neither tool's AI is a reason to choose it on its own. Both work within existing permissions, both need a human owner for every agent, and heavy users on either side will pay for extra usage. Test AI on a real workflow during the trial.

### Collaboration and external users
Both tools keep discussion attached to the work: monday.com through an updates thread on each item, Asana through comments, collaborators and @mentions on each task, plus project messages and status updates.
For external people, Asana includes **unlimited free guests** on paid plans, which suits agencies and teams working with freelancers. monday.com includes **unlimited free viewers** (read-only) on paid plans, and guests who can edit from the Standard plan. Both tools score 9/10 for collaboration in our review.
Users of both report the same downside: notification volume. Capterra reviewers mention notification overload for monday.com, and "excessive notifications" is one of the most discussed topics in Asana's Capterra reviews. Agree notification and @mention habits early, and use automations to notify the right person rather than everyone.

### Reporting, goals and portfolios
**monday.com** reporting is built on dashboards: charts, numbers, progress batteries, Gantt and workload widgets that read live board data. The key limit is how many boards one dashboard can combine: 1 on Free and Basic, 5 on Standard, 20 on Pro and 50 on Enterprise. Full portfolio management is an Enterprise feature.
**Asana** offers project and team dashboards from Starter. Its standout is on Advanced: **portfolios** that show the health of many projects on one screen, a status update builder, and **goals** that can be broken into sub-goals and updated automatically from connected projects. Advanced also adds Tableau and Power BI integrations.
If you manage by OKRs, Asana's goals are a genuine advantage; our free [OKR template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/okr-template/) helps you define them first. If your leaders want a visual, at-a-glance dashboard per department, monday.com is excellent, provided you budget for the plan that combines enough boards. For what a good status report contains, see our guide to [project status reports](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-status-report/).

### Resource management and time tracking
Both tools score 8/10 for planning and resource management in our review, and both reserve the deeper features for higher tiers.
- **monday.com:** time tracking and the workload view are on Pro. Portfolio and resource management are on Enterprise.
- **Asana:** time tracking (estimated vs actual) and workload within a portfolio are on Advanced. Capacity planning and universal resource management are on Enterprise, and a Timesheets & Budgets add-on is available from Starter.
For small and mid-sized teams, either tool's workload view is enough for basic [capacity planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/capacity-planning/). PMOs and professional services firms that need formal resource allocation, budgets and financial tracking across many projects often find both lighter than they need. That is the main reason Wrike ranks first in our review.

| Free plan | ✓ Yes | ✓ Yes |
| Gantt / timeline | ✓ Yes | ✓ Yes |
| Kanban boards | ✓ Yes | ✓ Yes |

### Integrations
monday.com's integrations page advertises more than 850 integrations and apps, counting its marketplace, including Slack, Microsoft Teams, Gmail, Outlook, Zoom, Jira, GitHub, Salesforce, HubSpot, Zapier and Make. Integration actions are metered like automations (250 a month on Standard), and some marketplace apps carry their own cost.
Asana says even its free plan includes more than 100 free integrations, including Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Workspace, Zoom, Jira, GitHub, Figma and Zapier. Salesforce, Tableau and Power BI integrations are listed on Advanced.
Both offer a public API and MCP connectivity, so AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT and Copilot can work with your data. For most teams the integration you need exists on both; check the plan it requires and, for monday.com, whether the monthly action limit is enough for a two-way sync.

### Security and administration
Both vendors publish extensive trust documentation. monday.com lists SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II and SOC 3 reports, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018, 27032 and 27701, CSA STAR and TX-RAMP, with a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement on Enterprise. Asana lists SOC 2 Type 2 and SOC 3 reports, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701, CSA STAR Level 1 and HIPAA support, with data residency in Europe, Australia and Japan and customer-managed encryption keys.
On both, SAML single sign-on and SCIM provisioning are Enterprise features. Both score 9/10 for scalability and enterprise readiness in our review. Confirm current certifications and their scope in each vendor's trust centre during procurement.

### Category winners
| Category | monday.com | Asana | Winner |

### Which is better for your team?

#### Marketing and creative teams
Both are strong. monday.com's visual campaign boards, content calendars and WorkForms suit teams that want a lightweight, colourful tool. Asana's timelines, forms and approvals and proofing on Advanced suit teams that run many campaigns across departments.

#### Operations and HR teams
monday.com has the edge for repeatable processes such as onboarding, procurement and facilities requests, where flexible boards and automations shine, as long as the action limits fit your volume.

#### PMOs and cross-functional programmes
Asana has the edge: portfolios, goals and status updates on Advanced give leaders a structured view across many projects at a lower tier than monday.com's Enterprise portfolio features. For deep resource and financial control, compare [Wrike](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/) as well.

#### Agencies
Asana's unlimited free guests make client collaboration simple; monday.com's free viewers and client-facing dashboards suit agencies that mainly share progress. Both need Pro or Advanced for time tracking.

#### Software teams
Neither is a dedicated Agile tool (both score 7/10 here). monday.com sells monday dev for sprints and bugs; Asana connects to Jira and GitHub.

#### Small businesses
Check the maths. monday.com's 3-seat minimum and buckets can make a team of 4 or 6 pay for unused seats, while Asana Starter is priced per user. If budget is the main driver, also compare [ClickUp](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/clickup/).

### Choose monday.com or Asana

- Marketing, operations and agencies with varied workflows
- Teams that value visual dashboards
- Very easy to learn and adopt matters to you

##### Choose Asana if…
- Cross-functional teams in mid-size and large organisations
- Companies that manage by goals and OKRs
- Marketing and operations teams
- Clean, intuitive interface matters to you
monday.com review
Asana review

### How to switch between monday.com and Asana
Moving from **Asana to monday.com** is the easier direction. monday.com has a built-in Asana importer: you connect your Asana account, choose a workspace and projects, and each project becomes a board. According to monday.com's help centre, it imports the task name, assignee, completion status, notes, due date and parent name, and creates an automation that keeps new Asana tasks syncing to the board. Comments and attachments are not listed, so plan to move important files separately.
Moving from **monday.com to Asana** uses Asana's CSV importer: export each board to Excel, save the main sheet as a CSV and map the columns to Asana fields. Specific information needs matching custom fields in Asana before you import.
1. Pick one live project and rebuild it in the new tool during the trial, including automations and the dashboard you rely on.
2. Agree the structure first: boards and columns in monday.com, or teams, projects, sections and custom fields in Asana.
3. Import or recreate active work only; archive completed projects as exports.
4. Rebuild automations and forms, then test them with real requests.
5. Run both tools in parallel for one or two weeks, then switch off the old one.
Our guide on [how to choose project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/how-to-choose-project-management-software/) includes a checklist for running a fair trial.

### Alternatives worth comparing
If neither tool is quite right, three comparisons are worth reading. [Wrike](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/) adds deeper resource planning, portfolio management and proofing for organisations that need one system of record. [ClickUp](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/clickup/) packs docs, sprints and time tracking into lower-priced plans. Smartsheet suits teams that think in spreadsheets.
Compare [monday.com vs ClickUp](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/monday-vs-clickup/) and [Asana vs ClickUp](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/asana-vs-clickup/), browse [monday.com alternatives](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/monday-alternatives/) and [Asana alternatives](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/asana-alternatives/), or see every pairing on our [compare page](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/compare/).

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: Is monday.com better than Asana?**
Neither is better for every team. In our review monday.com scores 9.1/10 and Asana 9.0/10, with monday.com winning only on feature depth. monday.com suits teams that want flexible, visual boards and dashboards; Asana suits teams that want structured cross-team task management linked to goals and portfolios.

**Q: Is monday.com cheaper than Asana?**
Per seat, usually yes: monday.com costs $9, $12 or $19 per seat/month billed annually, against $10.99 for Asana Starter and $24.99 for Advanced (checked 7 October 2026). But monday.com has a 3-seat minimum and sells seats in buckets, so a team of 6 pays for 10 seats and can end up paying more than on Asana Starter.

**Q: Which is easier to use, monday.com or Asana?**
Both score 9/10 for ease of use in our review. monday.com is quicker to start with thanks to its visual boards; Asana's fixed structure of projects, sections and single-owner tasks makes it easier to stay consistent across many teams.

**Q: Do monday.com and Asana have free plans?**
Yes. monday.com Free allows up to 2 seats, 3 boards and 3 docs. Asana Personal allows up to 2 seats per project and team with unlimited tasks and projects. Neither free plan includes timeline or Gantt views or automation, so both suit individuals and pairs rather than teams.

**Q: Why does monday.com have a 3-seat minimum?**
monday.com sells paid plans in seat groups that start at 3 and then rise in multiples of 5, according to its support documentation. A team of 4 pays for 5 seats and a team of 6 for 10. Free viewers do not count as seats.

**Q: Which has better automation, monday.com or Asana?**
Asana is more generous: all paid plans include unlimited automation rules. monday.com caps automation actions at 250 a month on Standard and 25,000 on Pro, though its recipe builder is very approachable and Pro's allowance is enough for most teams.

**Q: Do monday.com and Asana have Gantt charts?**
Yes. monday.com includes timeline and Gantt views from Standard, with milestones and critical path added on Pro according to its plan documentation. Asana includes timeline and Gantt views from Starter, with dependencies and a target schedule to compare progress against.

**Q: Which is better for marketing teams?**
Both are strong for marketing. monday.com suits teams that want visual campaign boards, content calendars and WorkForms. Asana suits larger marketing functions that run many campaigns across departments and want approvals, proofing and portfolios on Advanced.

**Q: Which has better AI, monday.com or Asana?**
Both offer AI assistants and AI agents on paid plans, and both meter usage. monday.com uses a monthly pool of AI credits (from 1,000 on Basic); Asana includes AI Teammates, Dash and AI Studio with monthly allowances and paid top-ups. Test each on a real workflow rather than choosing on AI alone.

**Q: Can I import Asana projects into monday.com?**
Yes. monday.com has a built-in Asana importer that turns each Asana project into a board, bringing across task names, assignees, completion status, notes, due dates and parent names. Going the other way, Asana imports monday.com boards through its CSV importer.

**Q: Is Asana or monday.com better for small businesses?**
It depends on headcount. Asana Starter is priced per user, which suits teams whose size falls between monday.com's seat buckets. monday.com can be better value for teams of exactly 3, 5 or 10 that want Pro features such as time tracking at a lower per-seat price than Asana Advanced.

**Q: What is a good alternative to monday.com and Asana?**
Wrike is our top-rated tool and goes further on resource management, portfolios and approvals. ClickUp offers more features at lower prices. See our monday.com alternatives and Asana alternatives pages, or our top 10 project management tools.
