# Smartsheet vs Basecamp: Which Should You Choose in 2026?

URL: https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/smartsheet/smartsheet-vs-basecamp/
Section: Tool comparisons
Summary: Smartsheet vs Basecamp compared: pricing, Gantt charts, client access, AI, reporting and ease of use, with a clear verdict for your team.

vs

## Smartsheet vs Basecamp: Which Should You Choose in 2026?
Smartsheet vs Basecamp is a choice between two very different ideas of project management. Smartsheet turns spreadsheets into connected project plans with Gantt charts, dependencies, automation and roll-up reporting, priced per member; Basecamp keeps each project's messages, to-dos, files and chat on one calm page, with flat pricing and no per-user fees. Choose Smartsheet if you need structured, date-driven planning and reporting; choose Basecamp if your main problem is scattered communication, especially with clients.
- Published 27 September 2026
- Last updated 9 October 2026
- Prices and ratings checked 5 October 2026

### Key takeaways
- Overall, Smartsheet scores 8.6/10 and Basecamp 7.6/10 in our review; Smartsheet wins 4 of 7 categories and Basecamp 3.
- Smartsheet is stronger for scheduling, dependencies, reporting, resource and portfolio management, automation, AI and enterprise security.
- Basecamp is easier to adopt, better for asynchronous communication and client collaboration, and better value for larger teams.
- Pricing models differ: Smartsheet starts at $9 per member/month with no free plan; Basecamp has a free one-project plan and paid plans from $25/month flat (checked 7 October 2026).
- Basecamp has no Gantt dependencies or critical path; Smartsheet has no message-board-style communication hub. Decide which gap matters more to you.

### Smartsheet vs Basecamp: Quick Verdict
**Smartsheet is the better choice for structured, date-driven work** that has to be planned, tracked and reported across many projects: PMOs, operations and finance teams, IT implementations and construction programmes. Its spreadsheet-style grid feels familiar to Excel users, and it scales into enterprise portfolio management with Portfolios and Control Center.
**Basecamp is the better choice for communication-centred work**: agencies, consultancies, small businesses and remote teams who want discussions, decisions, to-dos and files in one place, and who want to bring clients in without paying for their seats. It is one of the easiest tools to adopt, but it deliberately leaves out dependencies, resource planning and detailed reporting.
In our scoring, Smartsheet wins on feature depth, planning and resource management, Agile and software teams, and scalability; Basecamp wins on ease of use, collaboration and value for money.
|  | [Smartsheet](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/smartsheet/) | [Basecamp](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/basecamp/) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Our score | **8.6/10** | **7.6/10** |
| Best for | Organisations comfortable with spreadsheets that need enterprise-grade planning and reporting | Agencies and small businesses that want calm, communication-centred projects with flat pricing |
| Starting price | From $9/member/month (no free plan) | Free (1 project, up to 5 users); paid from $25/month flat |
| Free plan | No (30-day free trial) | Yes (1 project, up to 5 users) |
| Free trial | 30-day Business plan trial, no credit card | 30-day trial (45 days on Unlimited), no credit card |
| Vendor | Smartsheet Inc. | 37signals |

### What Is Smartsheet?
Smartsheet is a cloud-based work and project management platform built around the **sheet**: a grid of rows and columns that looks like a spreadsheet, but where each row can be a task with an owner, dates, dependencies, a status and its own discussion. The same sheet can be shown as a grid, Gantt chart, board, calendar or (from the Business plan) timeline, and forms, automated workflows, cross-sheet reports and dashboards are built on top.
It was launched in 2006 and is based in Bellevue, Washington. Blackstone and Vista Equity Partners took the company private in January 2025. Smartsheet's strength is turning scattered Excel trackers into shared, governed plans, and its higher plans add portfolio tools that few rivals match.

### What Is Basecamp?
Basecamp is project management and team communication software from 37signals, launched in 2004. Instead of organising work around tasks and views, it organises everything around **projects**: each project has one page holding a Message Board, To-dos, a Kanban-style Card Table, a Schedule, Campfire group chat, Automatic Check-ins and Docs & Files. You switch on only the tools a project needs.
The current version, which 37signals calls Basecamp 5, added a new home screen, faster search, My Bar, subtasks, account-wide Everything pages and an improved editor. Basecamp's premise is that most teams need clearer communication more than more project controls, and its flat pricing reflects that.

### Key Differences Between Smartsheet and Basecamp
|  | Smartsheet | Basecamp |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core idea | Spreadsheet-style plans that roll up into reports | One calm page per project for communication and tasks |
| Structure | Workspaces, folders, sheets, rows and columns | Account HQ, teams and projects with built-in tools |
| Scheduling | Gantt with dependencies, milestones and critical path | Schedules, calendars and a Lineup timeline; no dependencies |
| Progress tracking | Status columns, % complete, reports and dashboards | Hill Charts, check-ins and activity feeds |
| Pricing model | Per paid member; free Contributors and (Business+) Guests | Flat monthly price per account; plans capped by active projects |
| Free plan | No (30-day trial of Business) | Yes: 1 project, up to 5 users, 1 GB |
| Automation | No-code workflows: 250/month on Pro, unlimited on Business+ | No workflow automation engine |
| Built-in AI | Smart Assist, Smart Columns, AI dashboards and formulas | None built in; access for your own AI agents via API and CLI |
| Enterprise controls | SAML SSO, SCIM, SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP | Two-factor authentication; no SAML SSO advertised |
| Best for | PMOs, operations, finance, IT and construction | Agencies, consultancies, small businesses and remote teams |
The rest of this comparison looks at each difference in turn. Feature and price details come from our long reviews, checked on the vendors' sites on 7 October 2026.

### Ease of Use and Setup

#### Basecamp: Ready in Minutes
Basecamp is one of the easiest project tools to set up and learn. You create a project, choose its tools, invite people and start posting. There are no custom fields to design and no workflow rules to build, so non-technical staff and clients usually need little or no training. Every project looks the same, which keeps the interface calm and predictable.
The trade-off is structure. Teams that want custom fields, priorities or dependencies will find to-do lists limiting, and in accounts with many projects, reviewers say finding older items can be cumbersome. Basecamp 5's improved search, My Bar and Everything pages help here.

#### Smartsheet: Familiar for Spreadsheet Users
For anyone comfortable with Excel, basic Smartsheet use is quick to pick up: a sheet can be running in minutes, especially if you import a spreadsheet or start from a template. Well-designed solutions take longer, because column types, row hierarchy, cross-sheet formulas, automations, reports, dashboards and sharing all need thought. G2 reviewers sum it up as easy for spreadsheet users, with a steep learning curve for advanced use.
Smartsheet's interface is dense and precise rather than visual. That suits people who like to see a lot of data at once, but it can slow adoption among teams who prefer cards and boards. AI formula generation helps, though you still need someone who understands sheet design.
Tip
Our verdict on ease of use: Basecamp (9/10 vs 7/10). If the people doing the work are not spreadsheet users, or you are inviting clients, Basecamp will be adopted faster.

### Planning, Scheduling and Views

#### Smartsheet Planning Features
Planning is Smartsheet's home ground. Its [Gantt chart](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/gantt-chart/) view, available on every plan, shows task bars on the same rows as the grid, so editing a date in either place updates both. You can set [task dependencies](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/task-dependencies/), drag bars to reschedule, mark milestones and highlight the [critical path](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/critical-path-method/). Row hierarchy turns a list into phases and subtasks, with parent rows rolling up dates and progress.
Board view shows rows as cards in lanes, calendar view lays out dated work, timeline view (Business and above) groups work into lanes such as team or region, and the newer table view adds live co-editing and an easier formula editor. Forms collect requests straight into a sheet.

#### Basecamp Planning Features
Basecamp plans work with to-do lists, which can have assignees, due dates, notes, files and, since Basecamp 5, subtasks. The Card Table is a [Kanban board](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/kanban/kanban-boards/) for reactive work, with a Triage area for new requests, custom columns, Not Now and On Hold sections, and a Done column. Project schedules and calendars hold deadlines and events, and the **Lineup** shows every project as a bar on one timeline.
Basecamp's most distinctive feature is the **Hill Chart**. Each to-do list is a dot on a hill: uphill while the team is still working out the approach, downhill once it is executing. Dots are moved by hand, each update is saved, and stuck work becomes easy to spot. It is a useful way to show real progress on creative or software work, but it does not replace a schedule.
What Basecamp does not have is a real Gantt chart: no dependencies, critical path, baselines or automatic rescheduling. Third-party integrations such as Ganttify and Le Gantt can add Gantt views. If your projects depend on sequencing, this is the single biggest reason to choose Smartsheet. You can sketch a schedule first with our free [Gantt chart template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/gantt-chart-template/).
| Feature | Smartsheet | Basecamp |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free plan | ✕ No | ✓ Yes |
| Gantt / timeline | ✓ Yes | ◐ Partial |
| Kanban boards | ✓ Yes | ✓ Yes |
| Time tracking | ◐ Partial | ✓ Yes |
| Resource & workload management | ✓ Yes | ✕ No |
| Portfolio management | ✓ Yes | ◐ Partial |
| Docs & wiki | ✕ No | ✓ Yes |
| Automations | ✓ Yes | ✕ No |

Two cells in the feature table need context. Basecamp's "partial" for Gantt reflects its schedules and Lineup timeline without dependencies; its "no" for built-in AI means there are no AI features inside the app, although your own AI agents can work with Basecamp through its API and connectors (see the automation and AI section below).

### Collaboration and Client Access

#### How Basecamp Handles Collaboration
Collaboration is Basecamp's core purpose. Message Boards hold announcements and longer discussions, Campfire handles quick chat, Pings are private messages, and Automatic Check-ins ask a recurring question such as "What did you work on this week?" so routine status meetings become unnecessary. Every message, to-do, file and event has its own comment thread, so decisions stay on the project.
Client work is where Basecamp stands out. You can invite clients into a project and choose which messages, to-dos, files and events they see, keeping internal discussion separate. Because paid plans have no per-user fees (Freelancer allows up to 20 users; Studio and above are unlimited), adding clients does not raise the bill. The most common complaint from users is notification volume, so agree notification settings early. Our guide to [agency project management](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/industries/agency-project-management/) covers client communication in more depth.

#### How Smartsheet Handles Collaboration
In Smartsheet, collaboration happens on rows and sheets: comments and conversations, @mentions, attachments, proofing on images and documents (Business and above), and notifications in-app, by email, on mobile and through Slack or Microsoft Teams. Smartsheet has three kinds of user. **Members** are paid users who create and manage work. **Contributors** are free and can view, and with commenter permission comment on, shared work. **Guests**, free on Business and above, are external users who can view or edit what is shared with them.
This works well when a sheet is the single source of truth for a plan, and free Contributors and Guests keep stakeholder costs down. It feels more like editing a shared document than having a conversation, though, and there is no project message board or check-in tool. As sheets multiply, sharing and seat assignments need active management.
Tip
Our verdict on collaboration: Basecamp (9/10 vs 8/10), especially for asynchronous teams and client projects. Smartsheet is stronger for structured approvals and proofing.

### Automation and AI

#### Smartsheet Automation and AI
Smartsheet's no-code automated workflows combine triggers, conditions and actions to send reminders, request approvals, update or move rows, create recurring tasks and generate documents. Pro includes 250 automations per month; Business and above are unlimited.
Smartsheet lists its core AI tools on all plans. **Smart Assist** can summarise sheets, run a project health check that flags risks and dependency problems, and take actions such as bulk-updating rows. **Smart Columns** apply AI instructions to every row, for example to summarise or translate free text. There is also an AI dashboard builder, plain-language formula generation and data analysis. From the Business plan, Smartsheet's MCP server connects sheets to assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot and Gemini (checked 7 October 2026).

#### Basecamp Automation and AI
Basecamp has no workflow automation engine; recurring check-ins and Card Table column watching are the closest built-in equivalents, and Zapier, Zoho Flow and Unito can connect it to other apps. As of October 2026 it has **no built-in AI features** such as summaries or writing help. 37signals has said it is still working on native AI.
Instead, Basecamp is open to AI agents you run yourself: a revamped API, a command-line interface, SDKs and agent skills let tools such as Claude, Codex and Cursor work in Basecamp, and its pricing page lists ChatGPT and Claude connectors, with full MCP support marked as coming soon. This suits technical teams; non-technical buyers who want AI inside the interface will find Smartsheet far ahead.

### Reporting, Resources and Portfolios

#### Smartsheet Reporting and Portfolio Tools
Smartsheet reports pull matching rows from many sheets into one view, such as every overdue task across ten projects, and dashboards present charts, metrics and reports to stakeholders (Pro allows up to 10 widgets per dashboard). Well-designed sheets can feed consistent [project status reports](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-status-report/) without anyone copying data by hand. Data can also flow into Power BI or Tableau.
For resources, Business adds workload tracking that flags over-allocation, Enterprise adds Scenario Planning, and the Resource Management add-on covers capacity planning, time tracking and budgets. **Portfolios** (Enterprise) and **Control Center** (Advanced Work Management or add-on) let a [PMO](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-management-office-pmo/) create every project from a standard blueprint and roll them up into portfolio reports.

#### Basecamp Reporting and Visibility
Basecamp's Reports show what is overdue, who is assigned to what and what is coming up across projects. With the Activity feed, Hill Chart history, Lineup and Everything pages, a manager can usually see what is happening without asking. This is operational visibility rather than analytics: there are no custom dashboards, charts, budgets, utilisation reports or portfolio rollups, and no capacity planning. Teams that need to manage [resource allocation](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/resource-allocation/) across many projects will outgrow it.
Tip
Our verdict on planning and resource management: Smartsheet (9/10 vs 4/10), and Smartsheet also leads on scalability and enterprise readiness (10/10 vs 6/10).

### Integrations Compared
**Smartsheet** says it has over 175 integrations, concentrated on the enterprise stack: Microsoft Teams, Outlook, Slack, Google Workspace, Salesforce, Jira, DocuSign, Power BI and Tableau, plus MCP connections for AI assistants. Bridge, its low-code integration builder, and the API (free for licensed users on Business and above) handle custom workflows. Some connectors are paid add-ons, so check the one you need.
**Basecamp's** integrations directory lists 93 third-party integrations (checked 7 October 2026), including Harvest, Toggl, Clockify and Everhour for time tracking, Ganttify and Le Gantt for Gantt views, Bridge24 for reporting and Zapier for automation. These are built by third parties. Basecamp has no native Slack or Microsoft Teams integration, positioning Campfire and Pings as the alternative, though third-party connectors exist.
If your organisation runs on Microsoft 365, Salesforce or Jira, Smartsheet fits more naturally. If you mainly need time tracking and invoicing alongside projects, Basecamp's partner apps cover that.

### Security and Administration
**Smartsheet** is built for enterprise procurement. Its Trust Center lists SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, FedRAMP and HIPAA (with a Business Associate Agreement); data is encrypted with AES-256 at rest and TLS in transit; and it supports SAML single sign-on (Enterprise and above), admin-enforced multi-factor authentication and SCIM directory sync. Enterprise customers can add customer-managed encryption keys and choose data regions.
**Basecamp's** security policy covers HTTPS encryption in transit, encryption at rest for uploaded files and encrypted daily backups, and Basecamp supports two-factor authentication. 37signals publishes a CAIQ self-assessment and a HECVAT for education buyers. We could not find SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning or a SOC 2 report for 37signals itself advertised, so organisations with formal identity or compliance requirements should check these directly before buying.
For regulated industries and government, Smartsheet is the safer choice. For most agencies and small businesses, Basecamp's controls are adequate. Good permission design matters in either tool.

### Smartsheet vs Basecamp Pricing in Detail
|  | Smartsheet | Basecamp |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plans | **Pro:** $9/member/month annual ($12 monthly) **Business:** $19/member/month annual ($24 monthly) **Enterprise:** Contact sales **Advanced Work Management:** Contact sales | **Free:** $0 **Freelancer:** $25/month **Studio:** $59/month **Pro:** $99/month **Unlimited:** $299/month (annual) |
Checked on vendors' pricing pages on 5 October 2026. Read the full [Smartsheet pricing](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/smartsheet/#pricing) and [Basecamp pricing](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/basecamp/#pricing) breakdowns.
The two tools charge in completely different ways. **Smartsheet charges per paid member**: Pro is $9 per member/month billed yearly ($12 monthly) for 1 to 10 members, Business is $19 per member/month billed yearly ($24 monthly) with a minimum of 3 members, and Enterprise and Advanced Work Management are quote-based. Contributors are free on every plan and Guests are free from Business. Add-ons such as Resource Management, Dynamic View and Data Shuttle cost extra. There is no free plan, but there is a 30-day free trial of Business with no credit card.
**Basecamp charges one flat price per account**: Free ($0, 1 project, up to 5 users, 1 GB), Freelancer ($25/month, 3 active projects, 20 users), Studio ($59/month, 10 active projects, unlimited users), Pro ($99/month, 25 active projects, unlimited users) and Unlimited ($299/month billed annually, unlimited projects). Archived projects do not count towards the limit. Basecamp offers a 30-day free trial on Freelancer, Studio and Pro and 45 days on Unlimited, with no credit card (all prices checked 7 October 2026).

#### What You Would Pay: Three Examples
These examples use published prices with annual billing where offered. Your own bill depends on how many people need to edit rather than view, and on how many projects you run at once.
| Scenario | Smartsheet | Basecamp |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5-person team, 4 active projects, all editing | Pro: 5 × $9 = $45/month | Studio (Freelancer allows only 3 projects): $59/month |
| 15 staff editing, 8 projects, clients invited | Business (Pro caps at 10 members): 15 × $19 = $285/month; clients as free Guests | Studio: $59/month; clients included |
| 40 staff editing, 30 active projects | Business: 40 × $19 = $760/month, or an Enterprise quote | Unlimited (Pro caps at 25 projects): $299/month billed annually |
The pattern is clear: Basecamp gets cheaper per person the bigger your team, while Smartsheet can be cheaper for a very small team with a handful of projects. Smartsheet's cost also falls if many people only need to view or comment, because Contributors are free. Count your editors and your active projects before comparing.

### Who Should Choose Smartsheet or Basecamp?

##### Choose Smartsheet if…
- Enterprises and PMOs standardising project portfolios
- Operations and finance teams who think in spreadsheets
- Familiar spreadsheet interface for Excel users matters to you

##### Choose Basecamp if…
- Agencies and consultancies working with clients
- Small businesses wanting simple project communication
- Very simple and calm to use matters to you
Smartsheet review
Basecamp review

#### Choose Smartsheet If
- Your projects depend on dates, dependencies and milestones.
- You are replacing Excel trackers and want them shared, automated and governed.
- Leadership expects dashboards and reports that roll up many projects.
- You run a PMO, or need resource, portfolio or scenario planning.
- You need SAML SSO, formal compliance certifications or Microsoft 365 and Salesforce integrations.
- You want built-in AI to summarise, check and query project data.

#### Choose Basecamp If
- Your main problem is scattered email, chat and files rather than scheduling.
- You work with clients and want to control what they see without paying for their seats.
- You want a tool that non-technical staff will adopt in a day.
- Your team works asynchronously or remotely and wants fewer status meetings.
- You want a predictable monthly bill as the team grows.
- You run a moderate number of projects at the same time.
If you need Smartsheet-level planning, resource management and reporting but also want richer collaboration, request forms and proofing in a more visual workspace, Wrike, our top-ranked tool, is worth trialling alongside both.
Small businesses should also read our guide to [project management for small businesses](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/industries/small-business-project-management/).

### Using Smartsheet and Basecamp Together
Some organisations use both: Smartsheet for the master schedule, budget tracking and portfolio reporting that a PMO or operations lead owns, and Basecamp for day-to-day communication with the delivery team and clients. This can work, but there is no native integration between them, so you would rely on Zapier or a similar tool, or on someone copying key dates across.
Before running two systems, decide which one is the source of truth for dates and status, and keep the other for conversation only. If you find yourself duplicating tasks in both, that is a sign you need a single platform. A [communication plan](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/communication-plan-template/) helps agree which updates go where.

### How to Switch Between Smartsheet and Basecamp
Moving in either direction is mostly a matter of structure, because the two tools model work differently. A practical approach:
1. **Map the structure.** A Basecamp project usually becomes a Smartsheet sheet (or a workspace for larger projects), and to-do lists become parent rows with tasks underneath. Going the other way, each sheet becomes a project and row groups become to-do lists.
2. **Export what matters.** Smartsheet sheets can be exported to spreadsheets. From Basecamp, gather active to-dos, key dates and important files; technical teams can use Basecamp's API or CLI to extract them.
3. **Decide what not to move.** Archive old discussions in the source tool rather than recreating them. Move active work, open decisions and current files.
4. **Rebuild one project first.** Use Smartsheet's 30-day trial or a Basecamp trial to pilot one real project, including its report or client access.
5. **Set conventions.** In Smartsheet, agree column types and a template so reports work; in Basecamp, agree notification settings and when to use messages, chat and pings.
6. **Run both briefly, then switch off.** Give the team a clear cut-over date so updates do not split across two tools.
If you are moving to Smartsheet from spreadsheets as well as Basecamp, our [project tracker template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/project-tracker-template/) is a useful starting structure. For choosing criteria, see [how to choose project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/how-to-choose-project-management-software/).

### Alternatives to Smartsheet and Basecamp
If neither tool fits, the most common alternatives sit between them: monday.com and Asana are more visual than Smartsheet and more structured than Basecamp, and ClickUp offers a lot of features per dollar. Wrike suits teams that need enterprise planning and resource management with stronger collaboration.

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: Which is better, Smartsheet or Basecamp?**
It depends on your work. Smartsheet (8.6/10 in our review) is better for date-driven projects that need Gantt charts, dependencies, reporting and enterprise controls. Basecamp (7.6/10) is better for communication-centred projects, client work and teams that want a simple tool with flat pricing.

**Q: Is Basecamp cheaper than Smartsheet?**
Usually, for teams of more than a few people. Basecamp charges a flat $25 to $299 per month regardless of users, while Smartsheet charges $9 or $19 per paid member per month on its published plans. A very small team running only a few projects can pay less on Smartsheet Pro (checked 7 October 2026).

**Q: Does Smartsheet have a free plan?**
No. Smartsheet's cheapest plan is Pro at $9 per member/month billed yearly. It offers a 30-day free trial of the Business plan with no credit card, and free Contributors can view and comment on shared work.

**Q: Does Basecamp have a free plan?**
Yes. Basecamp Free costs $0 and includes one project, up to five users and 1 GB of storage, with no time limit. Paid plans start at $25 per month for Freelancer.

**Q: Does Basecamp have Gantt charts?**
No. Basecamp has project schedules, calendars, Hill Charts and the Lineup timeline of all projects, but no Gantt chart with dependencies or critical path. Third-party integrations such as Ganttify and Le Gantt can add one. Smartsheet includes a Gantt view with dependencies on every plan.

**Q: Which is easier to use, Smartsheet or Basecamp?**
Basecamp. It takes minutes to set up and needs little training, which is why it scores 9/10 for ease of use in our review against Smartsheet's 7/10. Smartsheet is easy for spreadsheet users at a basic level, but advanced formulas, reports and automation take training.

**Q: Which is better for agencies and client work?**
Basecamp, for most agencies. You can invite clients into a project, choose exactly what they see and add them without extra cost. Smartsheet also offers free Guests on Business and above, and suits agencies that need detailed schedules, proofing and resource planning.

**Q: Which is better for small businesses?**
Basecamp suits most small businesses because of its free plan, fast setup and predictable flat price. Smartsheet suits small businesses that already run on spreadsheets and need proper scheduling, though Pro is capped at 10 members and 250 automations per month.

**Q: Do Smartsheet and Basecamp have AI?**
Smartsheet does: Smart Assist, Smart Columns, AI dashboards, formula generation and an MCP server for external assistants from the Business plan. Basecamp has no built-in AI features as of October 2026, but lets your own AI agents work in it through its API, CLI and ChatGPT and Claude connectors.

**Q: Do Smartsheet and Basecamp integrate with Slack and Microsoft Teams?**
Smartsheet integrates natively with both Slack and Microsoft Teams. Basecamp has no native integration with either and positions its Campfire chat and Pings as the alternative, though third-party connectors and Zapier can link them.

**Q: Which is better for Agile teams?**
Smartsheet, though neither is a dedicated Agile tool. Smartsheet's board view can represent sprints and its sheets can hold backlogs, while Basecamp has no backlogs, sprints or velocity reports. Software teams running Scrum usually prefer Jira; see our [Smartsheet vs Jira comparison](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/smartsheet/smartsheet-vs-jira/).

**Q: Can I use Smartsheet and Basecamp together?**
Yes, but there is no native integration, so you would connect them through Zapier or a similar tool. Some organisations keep the master schedule and reporting in Smartsheet and day-to-day team and client communication in Basecamp. Decide which tool owns dates and status to avoid duplication.

**Q: How do I move from Basecamp to Smartsheet?**
Map each Basecamp project to a sheet and each to-do list to a group of rows, export active to-dos, dates and files, and rebuild one pilot project during Smartsheet's 30-day trial. Archive old discussions in Basecamp rather than moving them, then set a clear cut-over date.
How we review.
Rankings and scores are the editorial opinion of the Neural Project Institute, based on features, pricing, ease of use, scalability and published user ratings. Prices were checked on vendors' pricing pages and ratings on G2 and Capterra on 5 October 2026; both change often, so confirm on the vendor's site before buying. ## Smartsheet vs Jira (2026): Which Is Better?
Smartsheet is best for spreadsheet-style enterprise planning; Jira is best for software and agile teams. We compare pricing, features, ease of use and G2 and Capterra ratings to help you choose.
- Published 26 September 2026
- Prices and ratings checked 5 October 2026

### Key takeaways
- **Overall winner:** Smartsheet (8.6/10 vs 8.6/10), winning 4 of 7 categories.
- **Choose Smartsheet** for organisations comfortable with spreadsheets that need enterprise-grade planning and reporting.
- **Choose Jira** for software development and IT teams running Scrum or Kanban.
- **Price:** Smartsheet From $9/member/month (no free plan); Jira Free for up to 10 users; Standard roughly $7.91/user/month.

### Quick verdict
Smartsheet is excellent for spreadsheet-minded enterprises. Wrike offers a broader all-in-one experience with stronger collaboration and proofing.
Jira is the strongest choice for software teams. For organisations that need one platform across engineering, marketing and operations, Wrike or monday.com are easier to roll out widely.

# Wrike vs ClickUp: Which Is Better in 2026?

URL: https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/wrike-vs-clickup/
Section: Tool comparisons
Summary: Wrike vs ClickUp compared: pricing (including AI add-ons), features, resource management, sprints, ease of use and ratings, plus which tool to choose.

vs

## Wrike vs ClickUp: Which Is Better in 2026?
Wrike vs ClickUp is a choice between two feature-rich, all-in-one platforms with different priorities. Wrike is a structured work management platform with strong resource planning, request intake, proofing and portfolio reporting, and it is our #1 tool overall (9.4/10). ClickUp packs tasks, Docs, Chat, sprints and dashboards into very low-priced plans (8.9/10). Below we compare them on features, pricing, AI, ease of use and user ratings so you can choose with confidence.
- Published 15 September 2026
- Last updated 9 October 2026
- Prices and ratings checked 5 October 2026

### Key takeaways
- **Overall:** Wrike scores 9.4/10 and ClickUp 8.9/10 in our review. Wrike wins planning and resource management, collaboration and scalability; ClickUp wins Agile support and value for money.
- **Choose Wrike** for structured cross-team workflows, request intake and approvals, resource and capacity planning, and enterprise-scale portfolios.
- **Choose ClickUp** for the most features per dollar, built-in Docs and Chat, and strong sprint tools for product and software teams.
- **Price:** ClickUp starts at $7 and Wrike at $10 per user/month (billed annually), but ClickUp's full AI costs $9 to $28 per user/month extra, while Wrike includes AI Essentials from its Team plan.
- **Ease of use is a tie (7/10 each):** both take deliberate set-up; Wrike's challenge is depth, ClickUp's is breadth, and ClickUp reviewers report more lag on large Workspaces.

### Wrike vs ClickUp: Quick Verdict
**Wrike is the better choice for growing teams and enterprises** that need structured workflows across departments, dependable resource and capacity planning, request intake and approvals, and portfolio reporting at scale. It leads in planning and resource management (10 vs 8), collaboration (9 vs 8) and scalability (10 vs 8) in our scoring.
**ClickUp is the better choice for budget-conscious teams** that want to replace several apps with one: tasks, Docs, Chat, Whiteboards, Goals, time tracking and sprints, all at low per-user prices. It leads on value for money (9 vs 7) and Agile and software teams (9 vs 8).
Both tools tie on ease of use and feature depth. If your organisation is scaling and needs governance, Wrike is the safer long-term platform; if you are a start-up or small team that values breadth and price, ClickUp is hard to beat.
| If your top priority is… | Our pick | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resource and capacity planning | Wrike | Workload views on paid plans and advanced resource planning and budgeting on Pinnacle |
| Lowest price for lots of features | ClickUp | Unlimited is $7 and Business $12 per user/month billed annually |
| Structured request intake and approvals | Wrike | Request forms with routing, custom workflows and built-in proofing |
| Docs, wikis and chat in the same tool | ClickUp | Docs, wikis and ClickUp Chat are built in |
| Sprints and Agile reporting | ClickUp | Sprint points, burndown, burnup and velocity on Business |
| Enterprise scale and governance | Wrike | Pinnacle and Apex add BI, advanced resource planning, Integrate and Sync |
| AI included in the plan price | Wrike | AI Essentials from Team; ClickUp's full AI is a paid add-on |

### Wrike vs ClickUp at a Glance
|  | [Wrike](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/) | [ClickUp](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/clickup/) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Our score | **9.4/10** | **8.9/10** |
| Best for | Growing teams and enterprises that want one platform for projects, resources, portfolios, approvals and reporting | Budget-conscious teams that want tasks, docs, goals, sprints and dashboards in one tool |
| Starting price | Free; paid from $10/user/month | Free; paid from $7/user/month |
| Free plan | Yes | Yes |
| Free trial | 14-day free trial, no credit card | Free plan available |
| Vendor | Wrike, Inc. | ClickUp |
Scores are our editorial ratings using the same methodology for every tool. Prices and plan details in the prose below were checked on each vendor's pricing page on 7 October 2026; always confirm before buying.

### What Is Wrike?
Wrike is a cloud-based work and project management platform founded in 2006 and owned by Symphony Technology Group since 2023. Work is organised into spaces, folders, projects and tasks, with custom item types, fields and statuses, and the same work can be viewed as a list, board, table, Gantt chart, calendar or dashboard.
Wrike's strength is structured breadth: interactive Gantt charts with the critical path and baselines, request forms with conditional logic, custom workflows, proofing and approvals, workload and resource planning, cross-project dashboards and, on higher tiers, budgeting, advanced reporting and BI. Wrike AI adds summaries, writing help, Copilot and configurable AI agents.

### What Is ClickUp?
ClickUp is an all-in-one work platform founded in 2017 and headquartered in San Diego. Its hierarchy runs from Workspace to Spaces, Folders, Lists and tasks, and ClickUp says it offers more than 15 views, from List and Board to Gantt, Workload and Mind Map.
Alongside project management, ClickUp includes Docs and wikis, Whiteboards, ClickUp Chat, Forms, Goals, native time tracking and sprint tools. Its AI layer, ClickUp Brain, is sold mainly as paid add-ons. The result is one of the broadest feature sets available at a low price, with the trade-off that a good set-up takes deliberate design.

### Key Differences Between Wrike and ClickUp
|  | Wrike | ClickUp |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Philosophy | Structured work management for teams and enterprises | An everything-app that replaces several tools |
| Free plan | Yes: basic task management, board and table views | Yes: Free Forever with Docs, boards and sprints, 60MB storage |
| Free trial | 14 days, no credit card | Trial access to paid features on Free Forever |
| Entry paid plan | Team: $10/user/month, 2–15 users | Unlimited: $7/user/month ($10 monthly) |
| Main team plan | Business: $25/user/month, 5–200 users | Business: $12/user/month ($19 monthly) |
| AI | AI Essentials from Team; Copilot and agents from Business | Brain AI ($9) or Everything AI ($28) add-on per user/month |
| Resource planning | Workload views; advanced planning and budgeting on Pinnacle | Workload view; portfolio workload on Business |
| Docs and chat | Comments and approvals on tasks; Whiteboard add-on | Docs, wikis, Whiteboards and Chat built in |
| Sprints | Supported through workflows, templates and AI agents | Native sprints, sprint points and sprint reporting |
| Integrations | About 60 listed, plus Wrike Integrate and Wrike Sync | Claims 1,000+ including Zapier and Make |
Prices are per user per month billed annually unless stated, checked 7 October 2026.

### Ease of Use, Setup and Performance
Both tools score 7/10 for ease of use in our review, and both reward teams that plan their set-up before inviting everyone.
**Wrike** is quick for everyday tasks, and its learning curve comes from depth: spaces, workflows, custom item types, request forms, dashboards and permissions. Reviewers praise its visibility and flexibility while mentioning onboarding effort, a dense interface and notification volume. Once an administrator has configured workflows, most people work in a small number of familiar views.
**ClickUp's** learning curve comes from breadth. New users meet many menus, views and ClickApps at once, and Capterra reviewers rate its ease of use 4.3/5, the lowest of its four sub-scores. Performance is the most persistent criticism: in Capterra's topic summaries, about 78% of the 290 reviews mentioning lag and slowdowns are negative, mostly in large boards and busy Workspaces. Frequent product updates also move familiar controls.
Tip
Test both tools with a realistic volume of tasks, not an empty demo workspace. That shows you ClickUp's performance and Wrike's configuration effort before you commit.

### Views, Planning and Gantt Charts
Both tools offer interactive [Gantt charts](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/gantt-chart/) with all four dependency types, automatic rescheduling, milestones, the critical path and baselines.
- **Wrike:** Gantt charts are included from the Team plan, with lead and lag, float and drag-and-drop rescheduling. Board and table views are available on every plan, including Free, and dashboards span projects.
- **ClickUp:** Gantt is a trial on Free Forever and unlimited from Unlimited, with slack time and baselines on paid plans. Timeline, Activity and Mind Map views are fully unlocked on Business. Board view includes WIP limits per column, which is unusual at this price.
**Verdict:** a draw for scheduling. ClickUp offers more view types; Wrike's Gantt is part of a more structured planning and reporting model that suits multi-project, date-driven work.

### Resource Management and Portfolios
This is Wrike's clearest advantage, and it scores 10/10 against ClickUp's 8/10 for planning and resource management in our review.
**Wrike** shows workload and capacity across the team, accounting for working hours, non-working days and holidays, with time tracking and approved timesheets. Pinnacle adds advanced resource and capacity planning, role-based planning, budgeting and financial tracking, and advanced reporting and BI. That makes Wrike a natural fit for PMOs, agencies and professional services firms that plan people across many projects.
**ClickUp** includes native time tracking, Goals and Portfolios from the Unlimited plan, a Workload view showing each person's assigned effort, and portfolio-level workload management on Business. These are practical for small and mid-sized teams, but less mature than Wrike's resource and financial planning.

### Agile and Sprint Support
ClickUp scores 9/10 and Wrike 8/10 for Agile and software teams in our review.
**ClickUp** treats sprints as dated Lists, rolls unfinished work into the next sprint automatically, supports sprint points on Business, and reports burndown, burnup, velocity and cumulative flow. GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket integrations link code to tasks, and Docs hold specs next to the backlog.
**Wrike** supports Agile teams through boards, custom workflows and templates, and its AI agents can handle sprint operations such as rolling over work, updating statuses and writing summaries. Wrike Sync keeps items aligned with Jira or GitHub, so developers can stay in their tools while business teams track the same work in Wrike.
Our free [sprint planning template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/sprint-planning-template/) and guide to [Scrum software tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/scrum/scrum-software-tools/) cover what to look for.

### Docs, Chat and Collaboration
Wrike scores 9/10 and ClickUp 8/10 for collaboration in our review, but they collaborate in different ways.
**ClickUp** brings documents and conversation into the tool. Docs support nested pages, real-time co-editing and comments that become tasks, and any Doc can be a wiki. ClickUp Chat adds channels, direct messages, threads and calls, and assigned comments turn feedback into action items. This is a real consolidation opportunity if your team is willing to move conversations out of Slack or Teams.
**Wrike** keeps collaboration on the work itself: comments, @mentions, attachments, activity streams and formal approvals with named approvers. It integrates with Slack and Microsoft Teams rather than replacing them, and Wrike Whiteboard is available as an add-on. The result is a cleaner record of decisions on each task, which matters when many departments touch the same work.

### Requests, Proofing and Approvals
Both tools turn requests into tasks through forms with conditional logic, and both let people outside the tool submit requests.
**Wrike** goes further on structured intake and review. Each form answer maps to a field, rules assign and route the work, and built-in proofing lets reviewers mark up images, videos and documents before formal approval. For marketing, creative and agency teams with many stakeholders, this is one of Wrike's strongest areas.
**ClickUp** Forms are unlimited from the Unlimited plan (one on Free Forever) and include proofing on files, with unlimited proofing on Business. They cover most request workflows well at a lower price.
Our free [work request template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/work-request-template/) shows what a good intake form should capture.

### Automation and AI

#### Automation
**Wrike** automates assignment, status changes, notifications and request routing with rule-based triggers and actions, with advanced automation, AI agents and cross-tool automation through Wrike Integrate on higher tiers or add-ons. **ClickUp** offers more than 100 automation templates and an AI builder, but executions are metered: 100 on Free Forever, 1,000 on Unlimited, 5,000 per month on Business and 250,000 per month on Enterprise.

#### AI
**Wrike AI** is included in the plans. AI Essentials (writing and editing, comment summaries, natural-language form and rule creation, AI highlights) comes with Team, and AI Elite (Copilot, AI dashboard widgets, configurable AI agents and the Whiteboard assistant) starts with a pooled allowance on Business that grows on Pinnacle and Apex.
**ClickUp Brain** is mostly an add-on. Free Forever has limited trial access; **Brain AI** ($9 per user/month) adds the assistant, AI writing, enterprise search and AI chat with a choice of models; **Everything AI** ($28 per user/month) adds the AI Notetaker, AI Fields, AI automations and more Super Agent usage. ClickUp's Super Agents can create tasks, draft documents and run multi-step workflows.
Both vendors' AI is capable; the main difference for buyers is cost.

### Reporting and Dashboards
**Wrike** includes shareable dashboards from the Team plan, with widgets for status, overdue work, workload and progress across projects, and advanced reporting and BI on Pinnacle and Apex. In Capterra's topic summaries, around 96% of Wrike reviews that mention project visibility and dashboards are positive.
**ClickUp** dashboards are actionable (you can change statuses or reassign tasks from them) and can be shared with clients, but they are a trial on Free Forever and Unlimited; unlimited dashboards with advanced cards start on Business.
For a weekly [project status report](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-status-report/), both work well. For executive and PMO-level reporting across a large portfolio, Wrike's top tiers go further.

### Integrations
**ClickUp** claims more than 1,000 integrations, including those through Zapier and Make. Native options include Slack, Microsoft Teams, Zoom, GitHub, GitLab, Google Drive, HubSpot, Figma and Tableau, plus a public API, webhooks and an MCP server. It also has importers for Wrike, Asana, Trello, Jira and others.
**Wrike** lists around 60 integrations, including Microsoft Teams, Slack, Salesforce, Google Sheets, Power BI, Tableau and Miro, plus an open API. **Wrike Integrate** automates workflows across other systems, and **Wrike Sync** offers two-way sync with 22 tools such as Jira, GitHub and HubSpot; both are included in Apex and available as add-ons on other plans.

### Security and Administration
Wrike scores 10/10 and ClickUp 8/10 for scalability and enterprise readiness in our review.
- **Wrike:** granular permissions, customisable user types (full, collaborator and read-only), locked spaces, admin controls and SSO on higher tiers. **Wrike Lock** (add-on) lets customers control the encryption keys that protect their data. Wrike's site displays AICPA, BSI and CSA STAR compliance badges.
- **ClickUp:** its security page lists SOC 1, SOC 2 and SOC 3 reports and several ISO certifications, including ISO 27001 and ISO 42001, with AES-256 encryption at rest. Two-factor authentication is on every plan, Google SSO on Business, and SAML SSO, SCIM, audit logs and data residency on Enterprise.
Both are credible for business use. Wrike's governance features and customer-managed encryption make it the stronger choice for large, regulated organisations; confirm current certifications in each vendor's trust documentation during procurement.

The gap narrows if everyone needs ClickUp's AI, and closes if you choose Everything AI ($12 + $28 = $40 per user/month on Business). Wrike's higher price buys AI Essentials from Team, an AI Elite allowance from Business, and a path to advanced resource planning, budgeting and BI without changing platforms.
Tip
Model three years of cost at your expected headcount, including AI and any add-ons, rather than comparing the cheapest plan of each tool.

### Wrike vs ClickUp by Team Type

#### Agencies and professional services
Both suit agencies. Wrike is stronger when you need client request intake, proofing, resource planning and budgets; ClickUp is attractive for agencies with many staff and simpler delivery processes.

#### Marketing and creative teams
Wrike's request forms, custom workflows, proofing and approvals make it the stronger fit for high-volume creative work.

#### Software and product teams
ClickUp's native sprints, Git integrations and Docs suit small and mid-sized product teams. Wrike is a good choice when product and business teams share one platform, with Wrike Sync connecting to Jira or GitHub.

#### PMOs and enterprises
Wrike is the better fit, with advanced resource planning, budgeting, BI and enterprise governance on its top tiers.

#### Small businesses and start-ups
ClickUp is one of the best fits: a usable free plan and low prices. Wrike's Free and Team plans are good options if you expect to grow into structured workflows.

### How to Switch Between Wrike and ClickUp
1. **Choose a pilot project** that reflects your normal work, and agree who owns the migration.
2. **Design the target structure first.** Wrike spaces, folders and projects map roughly to ClickUp Spaces, Folders and Lists; agree statuses and custom fields before importing.
3. **Import the data.** ClickUp has a built-in importer for Wrike. To move into Wrike, export your data to a spreadsheet and use Wrike's Excel import (Team plans and above, up to 5,000 tasks per import), mapping the "Assigned to" column to users.
4. **Rebuild automations, forms and dashboards**, which rarely transfer cleanly between tools.
5. **Train the team** on the new structure and notification settings, then run both tools in parallel for one reporting cycle.
6. **Switch over and archive** the old workspace once the pilot project is running smoothly.
Plan the move with a clear owner and timeline, and check our [Kanban board template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/kanban-board-template/) if you want a simple holding board during the transition.

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: Which is better, Wrike or ClickUp?**
In our review, Wrike scores 9.4/10 and ClickUp 8.9/10. Wrike wins on planning and resource management, collaboration and scalability; ClickUp wins on value for money and Agile support. Wrike is better for structured, multi-team work at scale; ClickUp is better for budget-conscious teams that want many tools in one.

**Q: Is ClickUp cheaper than Wrike?**
Yes, on base price. ClickUp Unlimited is $7 and Business $12 per user/month billed annually, against Wrike's Team at $10 and Business at $25 (checked 7 October 2026). ClickUp's full AI costs $9 to $28 per user/month extra, while Wrike includes AI Essentials from Team, so compare totals with AI included.

**Q: Do Wrike and ClickUp have free plans?**
Yes. Wrike's Free plan includes basic task management with board and table views. ClickUp's Free Forever plan includes unlimited members and tasks, Docs, boards and sprints, but only 60MB of storage and trial access to Gantt charts, dashboards and time tracking.

**Q: Which is easier to use, Wrike or ClickUp?**
Both score 7/10 for ease of use in our review. Wrike's learning curve comes from its depth of configuration; ClickUp's comes from the number of features and views. ClickUp reviewers also report more lag in large Workspaces, so test both with realistic data.

**Q: Is Wrike or ClickUp better for small teams?**
ClickUp usually suits small teams on a tight budget, thanks to its free plan and low prices. Wrike's Team plan (2 to 15 users) is a strong option for small teams that need Gantt charts, dashboards and structured workflows and expect to grow.

**Q: Which is better for agencies?**
Wrike is stronger for agencies that need client request intake, proofing and approvals, and resource and budget planning across clients. ClickUp is a good low-cost option for agencies with simpler delivery processes and many staff.

**Q: Which is better for resource management?**
Wrike. It offers workload and capacity views on paid plans and advanced resource planning, budgeting and financial tracking on Pinnacle. ClickUp has a Workload view and portfolio workload on Business, which suit smaller teams.

**Q: Which is better for Agile and Scrum teams?**
ClickUp, in our scoring (9/10 vs 8/10). It has native sprints, sprint points, burndown, burnup and velocity reporting, and Git integrations. Wrike supports Agile teams through boards, workflows, AI agents and Wrike Sync with Jira and GitHub.

**Q: How do Wrike AI and ClickUp Brain compare?**
Both offer AI writing, summaries, assistants and agents. The main difference is packaging: Wrike includes AI Essentials from Team and an AI Elite allowance (Copilot and agents) from Business, while ClickUp's full AI requires the Brain AI ($9) or Everything AI ($28) add-on per user per month.

**Q: Is ClickUp slow compared with Wrike?**
Lag is the most common complaint in ClickUp reviews, especially in large boards and busy Workspaces, while Wrike's most common complaints are its learning curve and dense interface. Performance depends on your data, so test both with a realistic volume of tasks.

**Q: Does Wrike have docs and chat like ClickUp?**
Not to the same extent. ClickUp has built-in Docs, wikis and ClickUp Chat. Wrike keeps collaboration in task comments, @mentions and approvals, integrates with Slack and Microsoft Teams, and offers Wrike Whiteboard as an add-on.

**Q: Can I migrate from Wrike to ClickUp, or the reverse?**
Yes. ClickUp has a built-in Wrike importer. To move into Wrike, export your ClickUp data to a spreadsheet and use Wrike's Excel import, available on Team plans and above. Automations, forms and dashboards usually need rebuilding.

**Q: Which is better for large enterprises?**
Wrike, in our scoring (10/10 vs 8/10 for scalability). It offers advanced resource planning, BI, Wrike Integrate and Sync on its top tiers, granular governance and customer-managed encryption through Wrike Lock. ClickUp Enterprise adds SAML SSO, SCIM, audit logs and data residency.
How we review.
Rankings and scores are the editorial opinion of the Neural Project Institute, based on features, pricing, ease of use, scalability and published user ratings. Prices were checked on vendors' pricing pages and ratings on G2 and Capterra on 5 October 2026; both change often, so confirm on the vendor's site before buying. ## Wrike vs Jira (2026): Which Is Better?
Wrike is best all-in-one work management platform; Jira is best for software and agile teams. We compare pricing, features, ease of use and G2 and Capterra ratings to help you choose.
- Published 16 September 2026
- Prices and ratings checked 5 October 2026

### Key takeaways
- **Overall winner:** Wrike (9.4/10 vs 8.6/10), winning 5 of 7 categories.
- **Choose Wrike** for growing teams and enterprises that want one platform for projects, resources, portfolios, approvals and reporting.
- **Choose Jira** for software development and IT teams running Scrum or Kanban.
- **Price:** Wrike Free; paid from $10/user/month; Jira Free for up to 10 users; Standard roughly $7.91/user/month.

### Quick verdict
Wrike is the most complete all-in-one choice in this list. If you need projects, resources, portfolios, approvals and reporting in one place, and can invest a little time in setup, it is our top recommendation.
Jira is the strongest choice for software teams. For organisations that need one platform across engineering, marketing and operations, Wrike or monday.com are easier to roll out widely.

Jira is stronger for Agile and software teams in our scoring.

**Q: Wrike vs Jira: which has better resource and portfolio management?**
Wrike scores higher for planning and resource management (Wrike 10/10, Jira 7/10).

**Q: Wrike vs Jira: which is better for large enterprises?**
Wrike scores higher for scalability and enterprise readiness.

# Wrike vs Microsoft Planner: Which Should You Choose in 2026?

URL: https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/wrike-vs-microsoft-planner/
Section: Tool comparisons
Summary: Wrike vs Microsoft Planner compared: pricing, Gantt scheduling, resources, reporting, AI and Microsoft 365 fit, plus which tool to choose in 2026.

vs

## Wrike vs Microsoft Planner: Which Should You Choose in 2026?
Wrike vs Microsoft Planner is really a choice between a dedicated work management platform and the task and project app that already comes with Microsoft 365. Planner is the convenient, low-cost default for teams that live in Teams and Outlook; Wrike adds much deeper scheduling, resource management, request intake, approvals and reporting for organisations running many projects. In our review Wrike scores 9.4/10 and Planner 8.1/10, but Planner wins on ease of use and value, so the right answer depends on how complex your work is.
- Published 17 September 2026
- Last updated 9 October 2026
- Prices and ratings checked 5 October 2026

### Key takeaways
- **Overall:** Wrike scores 9.4/10 (ranked #1) and Microsoft Planner 8.1/10 (ranked #7); Wrike wins 5 of our 7 categories.
- **Choose Planner** if you are standardised on Microsoft 365 and need simple boards, or affordable Gantt scheduling inside Teams.
- **Choose Wrike** if you manage many projects across departments and need workload views, request forms, approvals and ready-made dashboards.
- **Same entry price:** Wrike Team and Planner Plan 1 both cost $10 per user/month billed annually, but basic Planner is already included in most Microsoft 365 business plans.
- **AI costs differ:** Wrike includes AI Essentials from its Team plan; Planner's AI needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence at $30 per user/month.

### Quick verdict
**Microsoft Planner** is the sensible starting point for organisations already paying for Microsoft 365. Basic Planner costs nothing extra, it runs inside Teams and Outlook, and anyone can use it within minutes. Since Microsoft folded Project for the web into it in 2025, the premium plans also offer real scheduling: timelines, dependencies, sprints and goals on Plan 1, plus baselines and critical path on Plan 3. If your projects are mostly internal, moderately sized and run by teams that already work in Microsoft 365, Planner may be all you need.
**Wrike** is the better choice once work spans many projects, teams or clients. It gives you structured request intake, custom workflows, proofing and approvals, workload and capacity views, cross-project dashboards and a more capable automation and AI layer, all in one platform. It takes longer to set up and learn, and it is another vendor to manage, but for PMOs, marketing and creative teams, agencies and professional services firms the extra depth usually pays for itself. That is why Wrike ranks first in our [top 10 project management tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/).
Tip
A quick test: if your team mainly asks "what is on my list today?", Planner is likely enough. If managers keep asking "who is overloaded, which projects are late, and where did this request come from?", look seriously at Wrike.

### What is Wrike?
Wrike is a cloud-based work and project management platform used by teams from a handful of people up to large enterprises. Work is organised into spaces, folders, projects and tasks, and every item can carry custom statuses and custom fields. The same work can be viewed as a list, board, table, Gantt chart, calendar or dashboard.
Beyond tasks, Wrike covers the operational side of project delivery: request forms that create and route work, custom workflows per team, proofing and approvals for creative assets, workload and capacity planning, cross-project portfolio views and reporting. It is owned by Symphony Technology Group and says it is used by more than 20,000 organisations.

### What is Microsoft Planner?
Microsoft Planner is the task and project management app inside Microsoft 365. It runs in the browser, as an app in Microsoft Teams and on iOS and Android. Today it has two kinds of plan:
- **Basic plans** are the original Planner: Kanban boards of tasks grouped into buckets, with assignees, dates, labels and checklists. They are included with Microsoft 365 business, enterprise and education subscriptions.
- **Premium plans** are what used to be Microsoft Project for the web: scheduled projects with a timeline (Gantt) view, dependencies, milestones, sprints, goals and custom fields. They need a Planner Plan 1 or Planner and Project Plan 3 licence.
Microsoft began retiring Project for the web in August 2025 and moving its users to Planner, and its pricing pages state that Project Online was being retired on 30 September 2026. Planner is therefore now Microsoft's main cloud project tool, with the Project desktop app included in Plan 3 for heavy scheduling. Our [Microsoft Planner review](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/microsoft-planner/) explains the basic and premium plans in detail.

### Key differences between Wrike and Microsoft Planner
|  | Wrike | Microsoft Planner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Approach | Stand-alone, highly configurable work management platform | Task and project app built into Microsoft 365 |
| Best fit | Multi-project, cross-department and client work | Internal teams standardised on Microsoft 365 |
| Entry price | Free plan; Team $10/user/month (annual) | Basic plans included in Microsoft 365; Plan 1 $10/user/month (annual) |
| Gantt scheduling | Interactive Gantt from the Team plan, with dependencies, critical path and baselines | Timeline on Plan 1; baselines, critical path, lead and lag on Plan 3 |
| Resource management | Workload views; advanced capacity planning and budgeting on Pinnacle | People view (premium) and Assignments view (Plan 3) |
| Request intake and approvals | Request forms with conditional logic; proofing and approvals | No built-in request forms or proofing |
| Automation | Built-in rules engine, plus AI agents from Business | Through Power Automate |
| Reporting | Dashboards on paid plans; advanced reporting and BI on Pinnacle and Apex | Charts view; Power BI for anything more |
| AI | AI Essentials from Team; AI Elite (Copilot, agents) from Business | Requires Microsoft 365 Copilot ($30/user/month) |
| External users | Collaborator and read-only user types, external request forms | Guests must be added to your Microsoft 365 tenant |
In short, Planner wins on convenience and price for Microsoft 365 customers, while Wrike wins on depth, flexibility and visibility across many projects.

### Ease of use and setup
**Planner is the easier tool to adopt.** For a team already on Microsoft 365, there is nothing to buy or install: open Planner in Teams, create a plan, add buckets and assign tasks. Identities, groups and permissions come from Microsoft 365. Capterra reviewers rate Planner's ease of use 4.5/5, and on G2's comparison page Planner scores higher than Wrike for ease of use, ease of setup and ease of administration. The main source of confusion is licensing: basic and premium plans look similar but support different features, and recurring tasks and the Schedule view exist only in basic plans.
**Wrike asks for more up front.** Simple task management is quick to pick up, but getting full value means designing spaces, workflows, custom fields, request forms, dashboards and permissions. A small team can be running in a day; a department-wide rollout is a project in itself. The learning curve is the most consistent complaint in Wrike reviews, and its interface is denser because it puts more information within reach.
Our scores reflect this: Planner gets 8/10 for ease of use and Wrike 7/10. If your team has little time for configuration or training, that gap matters. If you have an owner who can set Wrike up properly, the extra effort buys a system that fits your process instead of the other way round.

### Views, planning and scheduling
Both tools offer board, list and calendar-style views, and both now offer Gantt scheduling on paid plans. The difference is in depth and in how the features are packaged.

#### Gantt charts and dependencies
Wrike's interactive [Gantt charts](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/gantt-chart/) start on the Team plan. They support all four dependency types with lead and lag, automatic rescheduling, milestones, the [critical path](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/critical-path-method/), float and baselines for planned-versus-actual tracking. A table view works like a live spreadsheet for editing hundreds of items at once.
Planner Plan 1 adds a Timeline (Gantt) view, all four [task dependency](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/task-dependencies/) types, milestones, summary tasks and custom calendars. [Project baselines](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-baseline/), critical path and advanced dependencies with lead and lag need Planner and Project Plan 3 at $30 per user/month, which also includes the Project desktop app. Premium plans allow up to ten custom fields and 3,000 tasks per plan (basic plans allow 9,000 tasks), so large programmes should be split across several plans.
For a moderately complex internal project, Planner Plan 1 is a capable and affordable scheduler. For portfolios of date-driven projects, or when you need critical path and baselines without buying a separate higher licence for each scheduler, Wrike is the stronger and more consistent option.

#### Agile, sprints and Kanban
Both tools cover Kanban boards on every plan. Planner premium plans add a backlog and time-boxed sprints, which suits teams running light Agile alongside other work; Microsoft does not describe story points, velocity or burndown reports. Wrike supports Agile boards, sprints and custom workflows, and its AI agents can handle routine sprint operations such as rolling over unfinished work. Neither is a specialist software development tool, but Wrike scores higher in our Agile category (8/10 vs 6/10). Our guide to [sprint planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/scrum/sprint-planning/) covers what any tool needs to support.

### Resource and portfolio management
This is where the gap is widest. Wrike shows team workload and capacity across projects: who is assigned to what, how much effort is allocated and who is overloaded, with working hours, holidays and time tracking taken into account. Pinnacle adds advanced resource and capacity planning, role-based planning, budgeting and financial tracking. Portfolio views and dashboards let a [PMO](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-management-office-pmo/) see status, risk and workload across every project with consistent fields.
Planner's premium plans include a People view that shows how work is spread across the team, and Plan 3 adds an Assignments view for effort per person by day, week or month. Plan 1 users can view portfolios and Plan 3 users can create them. These support basic [resource allocation](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/resource-allocation/), but they are not a substitute for dedicated resource management.
We score Wrike 10/10 and Planner 7/10 for planning and resource management. If [capacity planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/capacity-planning/) across many projects is a real need, this category alone often decides the comparison.

### Collaboration, request intake and approvals
**Planner's collaboration happens through Microsoft 365.** Plans sit as tabs in Teams channels, tasks can be created from Teams messages and meetings, notifications arrive in Teams and Outlook, and plans can be embedded in Loop. Premium plans add threaded task chat with @mentions and task history. For internal teams this is very convenient: there are no extra accounts, and work stays next to the conversations that created it.
**Wrike's collaboration is built around the work item.** Comments, @mentions, files, approvals with named approvers and proofing of images, videos and documents all live on the task. Request forms with conditional logic collect complete briefs from stakeholders and route them to the right team automatically; external forms let clients and non-users submit requests through a link. If your team is buried in requests arriving by email or chat, our free [work request template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/work-request-template/) shows the information a good intake form should capture.
Working with people outside your organisation is noticeably easier in Wrike, which has collaborator and read-only user types. In Planner, external people need to be added as guests in your Microsoft 365 tenant, and there is no built-in proofing or approval of creative assets. Notification volume is a common complaint in Wrike reviews, so agree notification settings early.

### Automation and AI

#### Automation
Wrike has a built-in rules engine: when a status changes, a form is submitted or a date passes, Wrike can assign people, change statuses, create subtasks or notify the team. Planner has no rules engine of its own; automation is built in Power Automate, which can connect Planner with hundreds of services but adds complexity, and some connectors need separate licensing.

#### AI
Wrike includes **AI Essentials** from the Team plan: content creation and editing, comment summaries, natural-language creation of forms and automation rules, AI highlights and mobile inbox prioritisation. From Business, accounts get a pooled monthly allowance of **AI Elite** actions for Wrike Copilot, AI dashboard widgets, AI agents and the Whiteboard assistant, with larger allowances on Pinnacle and Apex. Agents can validate requests, triage and route tasks, run risk checks and produce portfolio reports.
In Planner, Microsoft states that access to AI capabilities requires a **Microsoft 365 Copilot** licence, which costs $30 per user/month paid yearly. With it, Copilot can create buckets and tasks from your goals, draft status reports and highlight risks, and the Planner agent (renamed from the Project Manager agent in 2026) can work on tasks assigned to it and produce an editable outline. Organisations already buying Copilot for Word, Excel and Outlook get this as part of that licence; for everyone else it can triple the cost of a Plan 1 seat.

### Reporting and dashboards
Planner's built-in reporting is the Charts view, which shows tasks by status, bucket, priority and person. Premium plans add the timeline, People view, goals and, on Plan 3, baselines. Plans can be exported to Excel, and Microsoft points customers to Power BI for cross-plan reporting; premium plans are stored in Dataverse, so the data is available to the Power Platform. That works well if you have Power BI skills, but it means building reports rather than using them out of the box, and basic reporting is one of the most common complaints in Planner reviews.
Wrike includes shareable dashboards from the Team plan, with widgets for tasks by status, overdue work, workload and project progress, and reports across projects. Pinnacle and Apex add advanced reporting and BI for portfolio, financial and resource analysis. For managers who need a weekly [project status report](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-status-report/) across many projects, Wrike gets you there with far less building.

### Integrations and the Microsoft 365 question
Planner's strength is its native place in Microsoft 365: Teams, Outlook, To Do, Loop, SharePoint (basic plans), Power Automate, Power Apps, Power BI, the Microsoft Graph API and, with Plan 3, Project desktop. If Microsoft 365 is where your organisation works all day, nothing else is quite as seamless. Organisations that rely on Slack, Google Workspace, Jira or Salesforce will find Planner much less connected.
Wrike is not a Microsoft product, but it is designed to sit alongside one. Its directory lists around 60 integrations, including **Microsoft Teams**, **Power BI** and a connector for **Microsoft Copilot**, as well as Slack, Salesforce, Google Sheets, Tableau and Miro. **Wrike Sync** (powered by Unito) offers two-way sync with 22 systems, including Excel, Jira and GitHub, and **Wrike Integrate** automates workflows across cloud and on-premises systems. Both are included in Apex and are add-ons on other plans.
Many organisations keep Microsoft 365 for email, documents, chat and identity and add Wrike for project delivery. That is a common, workable pattern, which we cover below.

### Security and administration
Planner uses the same Microsoft Entra ID identities, sign-in policies and admin controls as the rest of Microsoft 365, which is a significant advantage for IT teams. It is available in commercial, education and US government clouds (GCC, GCC High and DoD), although some features are not available in every government cloud.
Wrike offers granular permissions, customisable user types, locked spaces, admin controls and single sign-on on higher tiers, so you can still sign in with your Microsoft identity. Wrike Lock, an add-on, lets you control the encryption keys that protect your data in Wrike. Wrike's website displays AICPA, BSI and CSA STAR compliance badges. For both vendors, confirm the current certifications and their scope during procurement.
