### Which should you choose?

##### Choose Wrike if…
- PMOs and professional services firms managing many projects and resources
- Marketing and creative teams that need proofing and request intake
- Organisations replacing several point tools with one platform
- One of the most complete feature sets in the category matters to you

##### Choose Microsoft Planner if…
- Organisations already on Microsoft 365 and Teams
- Teams needing simple, integrated task management
- Included or low-cost for Microsoft 365 customers matters to you
Wrike review
Microsoft Planner review
Some common situations:
- **A Microsoft 365 business with a few internal projects:** start with basic Planner and add Plan 1 for the people who need timelines.
- **An IT or operations team running rollouts and checklists in Teams:** Planner fits naturally; see [IT project management](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/industries/it-project-management/).
- **A team moving off Project for the web or Project Online:** Planner premium plans and Plan 3 give the most familiar path; consider Wrike if you also need intake, workload and dashboards.
- **A marketing, creative or agency team handling many requests and approvals:** Wrike, for its request forms, proofing, approvals and custom workflows.
- **A PMO or professional services firm managing resources across many projects:** Wrike, for workload, capacity planning, portfolio dashboards and reporting.
- **A growing company that works with clients and freelancers:** Wrike, because external collaboration is simpler.
If you are still unsure, our guide on [how to choose project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/how-to-choose-project-management-software/) walks through the decision step by step.

### Can you use Wrike and Planner together?
Yes, and many organisations effectively do. A common pattern is to keep Microsoft 365 for email, files, chat and identity, and personal or small-team task lists in Planner and To Do, while running cross-functional projects, request intake and portfolio reporting in Wrike. Wrike's Microsoft Teams integration keeps project updates visible where people chat, and single sign-on on higher Wrike tiers lets people use their Microsoft identity.
The risk is duplication. Decide clearly which work lives where, for example "anything with a deadline, a requester or more than one team goes in Wrike", so nobody has to check two systems for the same project.

### How to switch from Microsoft Planner to Wrike
1. **List what you need that Planner does not do**, such as request forms, workload views, approvals or dashboards. This becomes your success criteria.
2. **Export your plans.** Planner can export plans to Excel, which gives you tasks, buckets, assignees and dates to bring across.
3. **Design the Wrike structure first.** Create spaces, a project template, statuses and the custom fields you actually need; resist recreating every Planner bucket.
4. **Import or rebuild one live project** and run it in Wrike for two to four weeks using the 14-day trial and, if needed, a paid Team plan. Our [project tracker template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/project-tracker-template/) is a useful checklist of fields.
5. **Connect Teams and set notification rules** so people are not overwhelmed in the first week.
6. **Train by role.** Requesters need forms, team members need their work view, and managers need dashboards.
7. **Move remaining projects in waves**, then archive the old plans so there is one source of truth.
Going the other way, from Wrike to Planner, follows the same steps in reverse: export Wrike data to a spreadsheet, decide which projects need premium plans, and rebuild them in Planner.

### Alternatives to consider
If neither tool feels right, a few other options are worth comparing. Asana offers rules, forms and goals with simpler adoption, monday.com is very visual and customisable, and Smartsheet suits spreadsheet-minded enterprise teams.
For broader shortlists, see [Wrike alternatives](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/wrike-alternatives/) and [Microsoft Planner alternatives](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/microsoft-planner/microsoft-planner-alternatives/).

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: Is Wrike better than Microsoft Planner?**
For complex, multi-project work, yes: Wrike scores 9.4/10 in our review against Planner's 8.1/10 and wins on feature depth, resource management, collaboration, Agile and scalability. Planner wins on ease of use and value, and it is the better choice for Microsoft 365 teams with simple or moderately complex projects.

**Q: Is Microsoft Planner free with Microsoft 365?**
Basic Planner has no separate price because it is included with Microsoft 365 business, enterprise and education subscriptions. There is no stand-alone free plan for people without Microsoft 365, and premium features need Planner Plan 1 ($10/user/month) or Planner and Project Plan 3 ($30/user/month), paid yearly.

**Q: Which is cheaper, Wrike or Microsoft Planner?**
For Microsoft 365 organisations, Planner is usually cheaper: basic plans cost nothing extra and Plan 1 is $10 per user/month. Wrike has a Free plan, then Team at $10 and Business at $25 per user/month billed annually. AI changes the maths, because Planner's AI needs a $30 Copilot licence while Wrike includes AI Essentials from Team (checked 7 October 2026).

**Q: Does Microsoft Planner have Gantt charts like Wrike?**
Yes, on premium plans. Planner Plan 1 includes a Timeline (Gantt) view with dependencies and milestones, and Plan 3 adds baselines, critical path and lead and lag. Wrike's interactive Gantt charts start on its Team plan and support dependencies, critical path and baselines.

**Q: Does Wrike integrate with Microsoft Teams?**
Yes. Wrike integrates with Microsoft Teams and Power BI and offers a connector for Microsoft Copilot, among around 60 integrations. Wrike Sync can also keep data in sync with tools such as Excel, Jira and GitHub.

**Q: Can Microsoft Planner replace Microsoft Project?**
Partly. Microsoft retired Project for the web from August 2025 and moved its features into Planner premium plans, and announced Project Online's retirement for 30 September 2026. The Project desktop app remains and is included with Planner and Project Plan 3.

**Q: Which is easier to use, Wrike or Microsoft Planner?**
Microsoft Planner. It scores 8/10 for ease of use in our review against Wrike's 7/10, and G2 users rate it higher for ease of setup and administration. Wrike is straightforward for basic tasks but takes more time to configure and learn for advanced workflows.

**Q: Which is better for resource management?**
Wrike. It offers workload and capacity views across projects, time tracking and, on Pinnacle, advanced resource planning and budgeting. Planner has a People view on premium plans and an Assignments view on Plan 3, which cover basic allocation only.

**Q: Do Wrike and Microsoft Planner have AI?**
Yes. Wrike includes AI Essentials from the Team plan and adds Copilot and AI agents through AI Elite allowances from Business. Planner's AI, including Copilot in Planner and the Planner agent, requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence at $30 per user/month.

**Q: Which is better for small businesses?**
If the business already uses Microsoft 365, Planner is the obvious place to start because it is included. Wrike's Team plan (2 to 15 users) is a strong option for small teams that need Gantt charts, dashboards, request intake or client work.

**Q: Which is better for working with clients and external users?**
Wrike. It has collaborator and read-only user types and external request forms. In Planner, external people must be added as guests in your Microsoft 365 tenant, and there is no built-in proofing or approval workflow.

**Q: Can I use Wrike and Microsoft Planner together?**
Yes. Many organisations keep Microsoft 365 for email, files and chat, use Planner or To Do for simple team lists, and run cross-functional projects in Wrike. Agree clear rules about which work lives where to avoid duplication.

**Q: How do I migrate from Microsoft Planner to Wrike?**
Export your plans from Planner to Excel, design your Wrike spaces, statuses and fields, then import or rebuild one live project and pilot it during Wrike's 14-day free trial. Move the remaining projects in waves and archive the old plans.
How we review.
Rankings and scores are the editorial opinion of the Neural Project Institute, based on features, pricing, ease of use, scalability and published user ratings. Prices were checked on vendors' pricing pages and ratings on G2 and Capterra on 5 October 2026; both change often, so confirm on the vendor's site before buying. We are independent and do not receive payment for rankings.

# Wrike vs monday.com: Which Work Management Tool Wins in 2026?

URL: https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/wrike-vs-monday/
Section: Tool comparisons
Summary: Wrike vs monday.com compared: pricing and seat rules, Gantt, resource management, automation, AI, ratings and which platform fits your team in 2026.

vs

## Wrike vs monday.com: Which Work Management Tool Wins in 2026?
Wrike vs monday.com is a choice between depth and ease of adoption. Wrike is the better fit for organisations that need detailed scheduling, resource and portfolio management, approvals and reporting in one platform; monday.com is the better fit for teams that want colourful, flexible boards that non-technical colleagues pick up in minutes. This comparison covers ease of use, planning, resources, automation, AI, pricing at real team sizes, user ratings and how to decide.
- Published 14 September 2026
- Last updated 9 October 2026
- Prices and ratings checked 5 October 2026

### Key takeaways
- Wrike scores 9.4/10 (our #1) and monday.com 9.1/10 (#2); Wrike wins four of seven categories, monday.com wins ease of use, and two are tied.
- Wrike goes deeper on Gantt scheduling (critical path and baselines), resource and capacity planning, proofing and approvals, and portfolio-level reporting.
- monday.com is easier to adopt, more visual, and rated higher by users on G2 (4.7 vs 4.2) and Capterra (4.6 vs 4.4).
- Paid plans start at $10 per user/month for Wrike Team and $9 per seat/month for monday.com Basic (annual billing, checked 7 October 2026), but monday.com sells seats in buckets with a 3-seat minimum.
- monday.com caps automation and integration actions by plan (250 a month each on Standard); serious automation starts on Pro.
- Both offer a 14-day free trial without a credit card, so test one real workflow in each before deciding.

### Quick verdict
**Choose Wrike** if you run many projects at once and need interactive Gantt charts with critical path and baselines, workload and resource planning, request intake with approvals, and reporting across a whole portfolio. **Choose monday.com** if fast adoption matters most and you want visual boards that every department can shape into its own workflow with little help.
In our scoring, Wrike (9.4/10, ranked #1 in our [top 10 project management tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/)) wins on feature depth, planning and resource management, Agile and software teams, and enterprise readiness. monday.com (9.1/10, #2) wins clearly on ease of use, and the two tie on collaboration and value for money. The gap is small: both are excellent platforms, and the right one depends on how complex your work is.
Put simply, monday.com is the easier platform to roll out, and Wrike is the more complete platform once work gets complex.

### The core difference: depth vs ease of adoption
Both tools manage tasks, projects, requests and processes, and both offer list, board, table, calendar and Gantt views, dashboards, forms, automation and AI. The difference is in design philosophy.
**Wrike** is built around a structured hierarchy of spaces, folders, projects and tasks, with custom item types, fields and workflows. It is designed to be the single system of record for complex work, so it puts scheduling, resource management, proofing and reporting in the same platform. That depth takes longer to set up and learn.
**monday.com** is built around boards: flexible, spreadsheet-like tables where each row is a piece of work and each column holds information about it. Anyone can create a board and add columns in seconds, which is why non-technical teams adopt it quickly. Advanced capabilities, such as time tracking, workload, portfolio and resource management, arrive on the Pro and Enterprise plans.
|  | Wrike | monday.com |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Building block | Spaces, folders, projects, tasks | Workspaces, boards, groups, items |
| Biggest strength | Depth: scheduling, resources, approvals, reporting | Ease of adoption and visual flexibility |
| Learning curve | Higher for advanced setups | Low to start, higher for advanced setups |
| Pricing model | Per user; Team plan for 2 to 15 users | Per seat, sold in buckets with a 3-seat minimum |
| Best known for | PMO, marketing operations and professional services | Marketing, operations and cross-department workflows |

### What are Wrike and monday.com?

#### Wrike
Wrike was founded in 2006 by Andrew Filev and has been owned by private equity firm Symphony Technology Group since 2023. It says it is used by more than 20,000 organisations. It covers tasks and projects, request forms, custom workflows, interactive Gantt charts, dashboards, workload and resource planning, proofing and approvals, AI agents and, on top tiers, advanced reporting and BI.

#### monday.com
monday.com Ltd. was founded in Tel Aviv in 2012 and has been listed on Nasdaq since 2021. It sells several products on one platform, including work management, CRM, service and monday dev for software teams. This comparison focuses on monday work management, which covers boards and views, dashboards, WorkForms, automations, docs, AI and, on Enterprise, portfolio and resource management.

### Ease of use and onboarding
Ease of adoption is monday.com's best-known advantage, and it earns its 9/10 in our scoring. A new user understands a board in minutes, colour-coded statuses make progress obvious, and more than 200 templates give a working start. Small teams can run real work on day one. The learning curve rises for connected boards, cross-board dashboards, complex automations and permissions, and G2 reviewers mention it for advanced setups.
Wrike scores 7/10. Creating, assigning and updating tasks is straightforward, but designing spaces, workflows, custom fields, request forms, dashboards and permissions for a whole department takes planning. Capterra reviewers consistently praise Wrike's flexibility and visibility while mentioning setup complexity, onboarding effort and a dense interface. Wrike provides training through Wrike Discover, templates and professional services for larger rollouts.
Tip
Whichever tool you choose, appoint one administrator to own standards: statuses, fields, templates and naming. In monday.com this prevents board sprawl; in Wrike it keeps the configuration manageable as more teams join.

### Project planning and Gantt charts
Both tools offer [Gantt charts](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/gantt-chart/), but Wrike's scheduling is deeper and available on a lower plan.
| Scheduling feature | Wrike | monday.com |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gantt / timeline view | Interactive Gantt from Team | Timeline and Gantt from Standard |
| Dependencies | All four dependency types with lead and lag time | Dependency column with drag-and-drop rescheduling |
| Rescheduling | Automatic when a predecessor moves, plus drag and drop | Drag bars to reschedule |
| Milestones | Yes | On Pro, per monday.com's plan documentation |
| Critical path | Yes, with float | On Pro, per monday.com's plan documentation |
| Baselines | Yes, planned versus actual | Listed on monday.com's Gantt feature page |
For most marketing, operations and client projects, monday.com's Gantt view on Standard or Pro is enough. For complex, date-driven work such as launches, events or construction-style schedules, Wrike's support for lead and lag, float and the [critical path](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/critical-path-method/) helps you see what a delay will affect before it happens. If you are still planning in spreadsheets, our free [Gantt chart template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/gantt-chart-template/) is a good starting point.
Wrike also scores higher for Agile and software teams in our review (8/10 vs 7/10). monday.com sells a separate product, monday dev, for sprints and bug tracking, so software teams comparing the two should evaluate monday dev rather than work management boards.

### Resource, workload and portfolio management
This is where Wrike pulls ahead, and it drives most of its lead in our planning and resource score (10/10 vs 8/10).
**Wrike** shows team workload and allocated effort, accounts for working hours, non-working days and holidays, and supports time tracking with approved timesheets. Pinnacle adds advanced resource and capacity planning with job roles, budgeting and financial tracking, and advanced reporting and BI. Because projects share the same structure and fields, PMOs can roll many projects into portfolio views and dashboards.
**monday.com** adds a workload view and time tracking on Pro, which is often enough for basic [capacity planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/capacity-planning/) in small and mid-sized teams. Its pricing page lists portfolio management and resource management as Enterprise features, along with multi-level permissions.
For a [PMO](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-management-office-pmo/) or professional services firm that needs formal [resource allocation](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/resource-allocation/) across many projects, both answers involve a quote-based plan (Wrike Pinnacle or monday.com Enterprise). Ask each vendor for a demo of exactly the resource and portfolio views you need.

### Request intake, approvals and proofing
Both tools turn form submissions into work. Wrike's **request forms** map answers to task fields, use conditional logic and can be shared externally, and rules route each request to the right person. monday.com's **WorkForms** support conditional questions, branding and an AI form builder, and each submission creates an item on a board. Our [work request template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/work-request-template/) lists the fields worth collecting in either tool.
The difference is what happens next. Wrike has built-in **proofing and approvals**: reviewers mark up images, videos and documents and approve with named approvers, which is a long-standing strength for creative and [marketing teams](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/industries/marketing-project-management/). monday.com handles approvals through statuses and automations, which works for simple sign-offs; that is why our feature table marks its proofing as Partial.

### Automation and workflows
Both tools use "when this happens, do that" rules: when a status changes, assign someone; when a form is submitted, create a task; when a date approaches, send a reminder. monday.com's automation recipes are among the easiest to set up in the category. Wrike's rules work with its custom statuses and request forms to route work through multi-step processes, and AI Essentials (from Team) can create forms and automation rules from plain-language descriptions.
The practical difference is metering. monday.com counts **automation actions and integration actions** each month: 250 of each on Standard, 25,000 of each on Pro, and up to 250,000 combined on Enterprise (checked 7 October 2026). A busy team can use 250 actions quickly, so serious automation on monday.com starts on Pro. In Wrike, the more advanced automation, AI agents and cross-tool automation through Wrike Integrate sit on higher tiers or add-ons, so check which plan your workflows need.

### AI features
Both vendors have made AI central to their platforms, with usage-based allowances (checked 7 October 2026).
- **Wrike** splits AI into two tiers. **AI Essentials**, from Team, covers content creation and editing, comment summaries, natural-language creation of forms and rules, AI highlights and mobile inbox prioritisation. **AI Elite**, with a pooled monthly allowance of actions from Business, adds **Wrike Copilot** (questions about your work data), AI dashboard widgets and configurable **AI agents** for request validation, triage, risk checks, auto-assignment and portfolio reporting. Allowances grow on Pinnacle and Apex.
- **monday.com** uses a shared monthly pool of **AI credits**: at least 1,000 on Basic, 2,000 on Standard and 3,000 on Pro, with custom amounts on Enterprise. Credits power **monday sidekick** (an assistant that summarises, drafts and updates work), prebuilt and custom **AI agents** for intake, planning, status reporting and risk analysis, AI blocks on boards, and the Notetaker (from Standard).
Both treat agents as configurable automation with permissions, logs and admin controls, not as autonomous staff. Wrike's agents are tightly connected to its request and portfolio workflows; monday.com's sidekick is the more accessible everyday assistant. Heavy AI users should model costs on either platform.

### Reporting and dashboards
Wrike's **dashboards**, shareable from Team, pull tasks, statuses, workload and metrics from across projects onto one screen. Pinnacle and Apex add advanced reporting and BI for portfolio, financial and resource analysis. Capterra reviewers rate Wrike's project visibility very highly, though some mention a learning curve in configuring reports.
monday.com's dashboards are visually excellent, with charts, battery widgets, Gantt and workload widgets, scheduled reports and AI summaries. The key limit is how many boards one dashboard can combine: 1 on Free and Basic, 5 on Standard, 20 on Pro and 50 on Enterprise. A team running a dozen projects on separate boards will need Pro for one cross-project dashboard, and some Capterra reviewers mention workarounds for reporting across many boards.

### Collaboration and guest access
Both tools score 9/10 for collaboration in our review. Each task or item has its own conversation with comments, @mentions and files, so decisions stay with the work. Wrike adds formal approvals and shared dashboards; monday.com adds collaborative docs and unlimited free read-only viewers on paid plans, which is useful for executives and clients who only need to look. monday.com guests (external editors) start on Standard.
Users of both mention notification overload in busy accounts. Agree notification settings and @mention habits early, and use automations to notify the right person rather than everyone.

### Integrations
monday.com advertises more than 850 integrations and apps, counting its marketplace, including Slack, Microsoft Teams, Gmail, Outlook, Zoom, Jira, GitHub, Salesforce, HubSpot, Zapier and Make, plus an API and an MCP server for AI assistants. Remember that integration actions count against the monthly limit on your plan, and some marketplace apps carry their own cost.
Wrike's directory lists around 60 integrations, including Microsoft Teams, Slack, Salesforce, Google Sheets, Power BI, Tableau, Miro, ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot, plus an open API. Two add-ons go further: **Wrike Integrate** automates workflows across cloud and on-premises systems, and **Wrike Sync** keeps work aligned through two-way sync with 22 systems, including Jira, GitHub, Salesforce and HubSpot. Both are included in Apex and sold as add-ons on other plans.
If you need a long list of ready-made connectors, monday.com has the edge. If you need deep two-way sync between business teams and engineering tools, Wrike Sync is a strong option.

### Security and administration
Both are mature enterprise platforms. monday.com's trust centre lists SOC 1, SOC 2 and SOC 3 reports, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018, 27032 and 27701, CSA STAR and TX-RAMP, with a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement on Enterprise. SAML single sign-on, SCIM, audit logs and IP restrictions are Enterprise features.
Wrike offers granular permissions, customisable user types, locked spaces and single sign-on on higher tiers, and its website displays AICPA, BSI and CSA STAR compliance badges. **Wrike Lock**, an add-on, lets organisations control the encryption keys protecting their data, which is valued in regulated industries. On either platform, confirm current certifications and their scope in the vendor's trust documentation during procurement.

Headline prices look similar, but the two vendors charge in different ways (checked 7 October 2026):
- **Wrike** charges per user, billed annually. **Team** ($10) is for 2 to 15 users and includes Gantt charts, shareable dashboards and AI Essentials. **Business** ($25) is for 5 to 200 users and adds templatised workspaces, standard integrations and an AI Elite allowance. Business and higher plans are annual only. Pinnacle and Apex are quote-based.
- **monday.com** charges per seat, billed annually, with a **minimum of 3 seats**, and sells seats in buckets that rise in multiples of 5 after that. **Standard** ($12) is the entry point for timeline, Gantt and automations, and **Pro** ($19) adds time tracking, workload and 25,000 actions a month. monday.com asks teams of more than 40 users to request a quote. Free viewers do not use a seat.

Two conclusions stand out. For small teams of up to 15, **Wrike Team** is often the cheaper way to get Gantt charts and dashboards, especially at headcounts that fall awkwardly between monday.com's seat buckets. For larger teams, **monday.com Standard and Pro** usually cost less per month than Wrike Business, but compare what each plan includes: Wrike Business adds AI Elite and more workflow customisation, while monday.com Pro adds time tracking and higher automation limits.

#### Free plans and trials
Wrike's Free plan includes board and table views and basic task management; monday.com's Free plan covers up to 2 seats, 3 boards and 3 docs. Neither free plan includes Gantt charts or automation. Wrike offers a 14-day free trial and monday.com a 14-day trial of its Pro plan; both say no credit card is required. Wrike's extras include the Whiteboard add-on at $15 per user/month and Integrate, Sync, Lock and extra AI actions on request.

### How to switch between Wrike and monday.com
Switching platforms is mostly a design and adoption exercise, not a data one.
1. **Inventory active work.** List live projects, recurring processes, forms and dashboards. Archive finished work in the old tool or export it.
2. **Map structures.** monday.com boards, groups and items roughly map to Wrike projects or folders, sections and tasks. Decide how columns become Wrike custom fields (or the reverse) before importing.
3. **Import a sample.** Both tools import spreadsheets, so export a board or project to Excel or CSV and test field mapping for owners, dates and statuses on one project.
4. **Rebuild forms and automations.** These do not transfer. Recreate the essential ones first, and check monday.com's monthly action limits or Wrike's plan features for what you need.
5. **Pilot with one team** for two to four weeks, using the trial, then adjust the structure.
6. **Set a cut-over date** and keep the old tool read-only for reference for a few months.
Tip
If you are moving to Wrike from monday.com, use the change as a chance to standardise: agree one set of statuses and custom fields per type of work, rather than recreating every board's columns one for one.

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: Is Wrike better than monday.com?**
Wrike is better for complex, multi-project work that needs detailed scheduling, resource planning, approvals and portfolio reporting; monday.com is better for fast adoption and visual, flexible workflows. In our review Wrike scores 9.4/10 and monday.com 9.1/10, while monday.com has higher user ratings on G2 and Capterra.

**Q: Which is cheaper, Wrike or monday.com?**
It depends on team size. Wrike Team costs $10 per user/month for 2 to 15 users, which is often cheaper for small teams. monday.com Standard ($12) and Pro ($19) per seat are usually cheaper than Wrike Business ($25) for larger teams, but seats are sold in buckets with a 3-seat minimum (annual prices, checked 7 October 2026).

**Q: Why does monday.com charge for seats I do not use?**
monday.com sells paid plans in seat buckets that start at 3 seats and then rise in multiples of 5, so a team of 6 pays for 10 seats. Free viewers do not use a seat, but everyone who edits does. Wrike charges per user, with a 2 to 15 user range on Team and 5 to 200 on Business.

**Q: Which is easier to use, Wrike or monday.com?**
monday.com. Its visual boards and templates let non-technical teams start in minutes, and we score it 9/10 for ease of use against Wrike's 7/10. Wrike is straightforward for basic tasks but takes more setup and training for custom workflows, dashboards and reporting.

**Q: Which has better Gantt charts, Wrike or monday.com?**
Wrike. Its interactive Gantt charts, from the Team plan, support all four dependency types with lead and lag, automatic rescheduling, critical path, float and baselines. monday.com's timeline and Gantt views start on Standard, with milestones and critical path on Pro according to its plan documentation.

**Q: Which is better for resource management?**
Wrike. It includes workload views and time tracking with timesheets, and Pinnacle adds advanced resource and capacity planning, budgeting and BI. monday.com offers a workload view and time tracking on Pro, with full resource and portfolio management on Enterprise.

**Q: Which is better for marketing and creative teams?**
Both are strong. Wrike suits teams that need request forms, built-in proofing and named approvers on creative assets. monday.com suits teams that want colourful campaign boards and content calendars that everyone adopts quickly.

**Q: Which is better for agencies?**
Wrike suits agencies that need resource visibility across clients, time tracking and approvals in one platform. monday.com suits agencies that want simple client boards with free viewers. Time tracking needs Pro on monday.com, and resource management across clients needs Enterprise.

**Q: Which is better for large enterprises?**
Both serve large enterprises. Wrike scores higher for scalability in our review, thanks to portfolio and resource management, advanced reporting and BI, Wrike Integrate and Sync, and Wrike Lock. monday.com Enterprise offers portfolio and resource management, strong security certifications and a 99.9% uptime SLA.

**Q: Which has better AI, Wrike or monday.com?**
Both are capable. Wrike includes AI Essentials from Team and adds Copilot and configurable AI agents through AI Elite from Business. monday.com includes sidekick, AI agents and AI blocks on paid plans, powered by a monthly pool of AI credits. Choose based on the workflows you want AI to support and model usage costs.

**Q: Do Wrike and monday.com have free plans and trials?**
Yes. Wrike's Free plan includes board and table views and basic task management; monday.com's Free plan covers up to 2 seats, 3 boards and 3 docs. Wrike offers a 14-day free trial and monday.com a 14-day Pro trial, and both say no credit card is required.

**Q: Which has more integrations?**
monday.com advertises more than 850 integrations and apps, including its marketplace. Wrike lists around 60 integrations, plus Wrike Integrate for cross-system automation and Wrike Sync for two-way sync with 22 systems such as Jira, GitHub and Salesforce.

**Q: Can I switch from monday.com to Wrike?**
Yes. Export boards to Excel or CSV, map columns to Wrike custom fields, import a sample project to check owners, dates and statuses, then rebuild forms and automations and pilot with one team during Wrike's 14-day trial.

**Q: What are the best alternatives to Wrike and monday.com?**
Asana for cross-team task management linked to goals, ClickUp for many features at lower prices, and Smartsheet for spreadsheet-style enterprise planning. See our [Wrike alternatives](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/wrike-alternatives/) and [monday.com alternatives](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/monday-alternatives/).
How we review.
Rankings and scores are the editorial opinion of the Neural Project Institute, based on features, pricing, ease of use, scalability and published user ratings. Prices were checked on vendors' pricing pages and ratings on G2 and Capterra on 5 October 2026; both change often, so confirm on the vendor's site before buying. # Wrike vs Notion: Which Is Better for Project Management?

URL: https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/wrike-vs-notion/
Section: Tool comparisons
Summary: Wrike vs Notion compared: project features, docs, AI, pricing, ease of use and ratings, plus which to choose for your team in 2026.

vs

## Wrike vs Notion: Which Is Better for Project Management?
Wrike vs Notion compares a dedicated work management platform with a flexible, docs-first workspace. Notion is excellent for wikis, specs and lightweight project tracking that you design yourself; Wrike gives you ready-made project management with Gantt scheduling, workload views, request intake, approvals and cross-project reporting. In our review Wrike scores 9.4/10 and Notion 8.0/10: choose Notion when knowledge and flexibility matter most, and Wrike when structured delivery across many projects does.
- Published 17 September 2026
- Last updated 9 October 2026
- Prices and ratings checked 5 October 2026

### Key takeaways
- **Overall:** Wrike scores 9.4/10 (ranked #1) and Notion 8.0/10 (ranked #8); Wrike wins 4 of our 7 categories, Notion wins value and two are tied.
- **Choose Notion** for docs, wikis and connected lightweight project tracking, especially in start-ups, product and content teams.
- **Choose Wrike** for structured project delivery: Gantt charts with critical path, workload and capacity planning, request forms, approvals and dashboards.
- **Pricing starts at the same point:** Wrike Team and Notion Plus both cost $10 per user/month billed annually, but Notion AI needs Business ($20) while Wrike includes AI Essentials from Team.
- **Many teams use both:** Notion as the knowledge base and Wrike as the system for delivering projects.

### Quick verdict
**Notion** is the better choice when your work is mostly written: product specs, meeting notes, wikis, editorial calendars and light project boards that connect to them. It is flexible, pleasant to use and strong value, and it suits small and medium teams that are happy to design their own system. Its limits show when projects multiply: there is no native time tracking or resource management, its timeline has no critical path or baselines, and reporting has to be built by hand.
**Wrike** is the better choice when delivery itself is the challenge: many projects at once, several departments or clients, incoming requests, approvals, and managers who need to see workload and status without asking. It takes longer to set up and learn, and it is not a wiki, but it provides the project controls that Notion leaves you to build. That depth is why Wrike ranks first in our [top 10 project management tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/).
Tip
If your team spends more time writing about the work than scheduling it, start with Notion. If people keep asking who is overloaded, which projects are late and where a request came from, Wrike is the better fit.

### What is Wrike?
Wrike is a cloud-based work and project management platform for teams from a handful of people to large enterprises. Work is organised into spaces, folders, projects and tasks with custom statuses and fields, and the same items can be viewed as a list, board, table, Gantt chart, calendar or dashboard.
Its strength is the operational side of project delivery: request forms that create and route work, custom workflows for each team, proofing and approvals, workload and capacity planning, portfolio views and reporting, with AI and automation on top.

### What is Notion?
Notion is a connected workspace built from pages and databases. Every page is made of blocks, and any page can hold a database whose items have properties such as status, owner and dates. Project management in Notion is built on those databases, shown as tables, boards, timelines, calendars or charts, and linked to each other with relations and rollups.
Teams use Notion for wikis, specs, meeting notes, roadmaps, sprint boards and request forms, with Notion AI, Notion Agent and Custom Agents adding AI assistance. It is neither a to-do app nor a classic project suite: it is a set of building blocks that can become a project system. Our [Notion review](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/notion/) covers it in depth.

### Key differences between Wrike and Notion
|  | Wrike | Notion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Approach | Dedicated work management platform, configured to your process | Docs-first workspace; you build the project system from databases |
| Best fit | Multi-project, cross-department and client delivery | Knowledge-heavy teams with lightweight to moderate projects |
| Entry price | Free plan; Team $10/user/month (annual) | Free plan; Plus $10/member/month (annual) |
| Scheduling | Interactive Gantt with dependencies, critical path and baselines | Timeline view with dependencies; no critical path or baselines |
| Resources and time | Workload views and time tracking; advanced capacity planning on Pinnacle | No native time tracking or workload view |
| Docs and wikis | Task and project descriptions and files; whiteboards as an add-on | Core strength: nested pages, wikis, verified pages |
| Intake and approvals | Request forms with conditional logic; proofing and approvals | Forms into databases (conditional logic on Business); no proofing |
| Reporting | Ready-made dashboards; advanced reporting and BI on top tiers | Charts and filtered views you assemble yourself |
| AI | AI Essentials from Team; AI Elite (Copilot, agents) from Business | Notion AI from Business; Custom Agents on paid credits |
Put simply, Notion is where teams think and document, and Wrike is where teams plan, assign and track delivery.

### Project planning and scheduling

#### Gantt charts and timelines
Wrike's interactive [Gantt charts](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/gantt-chart/) start on the Team plan. They support all four dependency types with lead and lag, automatic rescheduling, milestones, the [critical path](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/critical-path-method/), float and [baselines](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-baseline/) for comparing plan with actual. This is what date-driven work such as launches, events and client programmes needs.
Notion's timeline view plots database items with date ranges on a Gantt-style chart. You can drag items to change dates, and Notion highlights dependencies so teams can spot blocked work. It works well for roadmaps and high-level plans, but Notion's documentation does not describe critical path, baselines or lead and lag, so complex schedules are harder to manage.

#### Sprints and Kanban
Both tools offer Kanban-style boards on every plan, including Free. Notion can add sprints to a task database, with a sprint board, sprint planning and backlog views, sprints of one to eight weeks and automatic rollover of unfinished work. Wrike supports Agile boards, sprints and custom workflows, and its AI agents can handle routine sprint operations. Neither replaces a specialist engineering tracker, but both cover the basics of [sprint planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/scrum/sprint-planning/); Wrike scores higher in our Agile category (8/10 vs 6/10).

### Docs, wikis and knowledge management
This is Notion's home ground. Pages are fast to write, easy to nest and can embed databases, files, designs and code; wikis gather them into a searchable knowledge base, and Business adds verified pages. Because each database item is itself a page, a task can contain its full brief, decisions and discussion, so the reasoning behind the work stays next to the work.
Wrike stores briefs in task and project descriptions, attached files and comments, and offers Wrike Whiteboard as an add-on at $15 per user/month. That is enough for project context, but Wrike is not designed as a company wiki, which is why our feature table marks its docs and wiki support as partial. If you use Wrike, keep a simple [project brief template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/project-brief-template/) for each project and link longer documentation from the project.

### Resource management, time tracking and portfolios
This is the clearest difference between the two tools. Wrike shows workload and capacity across projects: who is assigned to what, how much effort is allocated and who is overloaded, with working hours and holidays considered, plus time tracking with approved timesheets. Pinnacle adds advanced resource and capacity planning, budgeting and financial tracking, and portfolio views let a [PMO](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-management-office-pmo/) see status and risk across every project.
Notion has no native time tracking, workload view or resource scheduling. Teams approximate them with number properties for estimates, rollups and third-party time-tracking integrations, which works for small teams but becomes fragile at scale.
We score Wrike 10/10 and Notion 5/10 for planning and resource management. For agencies billing hours, professional services firms and anyone doing [capacity planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/capacity-planning/) or [resource allocation](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/resource-allocation/), this usually decides the comparison.

### Collaboration, request intake and approvals
We score both tools 9/10 for collaboration, but they collaborate differently. **Notion** is built for real-time co-editing: several people can work on a page at once, comment on any block, @mention colleagues and pages, and invite guests to specific pages (10 on Free, unlimited from Plus). On Capterra, its collaborative workspace is one of the most positively reviewed themes.
**Wrike** focuses collaboration on the work item: comments, @mentions, files, activity streams, approvals with named approvers and proofing of images, videos and documents. Request forms with conditional logic create complete, routed tasks, and external forms let clients submit work through a link. Notion forms also send responses straight into a database, but conditional logic needs Business, and there is no built-in proofing.
For marketing, creative and [agency teams](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/industries/agency-project-management/) that live on briefs, reviews and sign-offs, Wrike's approvals and intake are a practical advantage. Our free [work request template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/work-request-template/) shows what a good intake form should collect, whichever tool you choose.

### Automation and AI

#### Automation
Wrike's rules engine reacts to status changes, form submissions and dates by assigning people, changing statuses, creating subtasks or notifying teams; Wrike Integrate (an add-on, included in Apex) extends automation across other systems. Notion's database automations run when a page is added, a property changes or a schedule fires, and can edit pages, send notifications, post to Slack, send Gmail emails and call webhooks. They need a paid plan and are simpler than Wrike's for multi-step logic.

#### AI
Wrike includes **AI Essentials** from the Team plan: content creation and editing, comment summaries, natural-language creation of forms and rules, AI highlights and mobile inbox prioritisation. From Business, a pooled monthly allowance of **AI Elite** actions unlocks Wrike Copilot, AI dashboard widgets, AI agents and the Whiteboard assistant, with larger allowances on Pinnacle and Apex.
Notion AI, including Notion Agent, AI Meeting Notes and Enterprise Search, is included on Business and Enterprise; Free and Plus get a limited trial. Since 4 May 2026, Custom Agents run on Notion credits, a paid add-on for Business and Enterprise. Notion's AI is particularly good at writing, meeting notes and searching across connected apps; Wrike's is more focused on project operations such as triaging requests, checking risks and reporting on portfolios.
Whichever you choose, AI agents in both tools consume usage allowances on every run, so budget for them before rolling them out widely. Our guide to [AI project management tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/ai-project-management-tools/) compares how vendors package AI.

### Reporting and dashboards
Wrike includes shareable dashboards from the Team plan, with widgets for tasks by status, overdue work, workload and project progress, and reports across projects. Pinnacle and Apex add advanced reporting and BI across portfolios, resources and financials.
Notion builds reporting from database views, formulas, rollups and charts (one chart on Free, unlimited from Plus), and Business adds page analytics. A well-built dashboard page can show projects by status and overdue tasks by owner, but there are no packaged portfolio, workload or burndown reports, so someone has to build and maintain them. If leadership needs consistent reporting across many projects, see our guide to [managing multiple projects](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/managing-multiple-projects/) for what that reporting should show.

### Ease of use and setup
We score both tools 7/10 for ease of use, for opposite reasons. **Notion** is easy to start: writing pages and ticking off tasks takes minutes. The learning curve arrives when you build a project system with relations, rollups, formulas and automations, and G2 users list a steep learning curve for advanced setups among its main drawbacks. A blank workspace is liberating for some teams and paralysing for others, and workspaces can sprawl without clear owners. Performance is the most consistent Capterra complaint, especially with very large databases.
**Wrike** gives you project management features ready to use, so you configure rather than build. Basic task management is quick to learn, but designing spaces, workflows, custom fields, request forms and dashboards takes time, and the interface is denser. Its learning curve is the most common complaint in Wrike reviews, so plan for an administrator and some onboarding.

### Integrations
Wrike's directory lists around 60 integrations, including Microsoft Teams, Slack, Salesforce, Google Sheets, Power BI, Tableau and Miro, with connectors for ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot and an open API. Wrike Sync (powered by Unito) provides two-way sync with 22 systems, including Jira, GitHub, HubSpot and Airtable, and Wrike Integrate automates workflows across cloud and on-premises systems; both are add-ons outside Apex.
Notion's integrations are strong at bringing context into pages: Slack and Google Drive connections from Plus; premium connections such as GitHub and Asana on Business; and Jira issues, Figma designs and GitHub pull requests embedded in pages. A public API supports custom integrations. Deep two-way project syncing is more limited than in Wrike.

### Security and administration
Notion's security page states that it holds a SOC 2 Type 2 attestation and ISO 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701 certifications, and offers a HIPAA Business Associate Agreement. SAML SSO, private teamspaces and granular database permissions start on Business; SCIM, the audit log, advanced security controls and zero data retention with AI providers are Enterprise features. Notion states that it does not train AI models on customer content.
Wrike offers granular permissions, customisable user types (full, collaborator and read-only), locked spaces, admin controls and single sign-on on higher tiers. Its website displays AICPA, BSI and CSA STAR compliance badges, and Wrike Lock, an add-on, lets you control the encryption keys that protect your data. For both vendors, confirm current certifications and their scope during procurement.

- One of the most complete feature sets in the category matters to you

##### Choose Notion if…
- Start-ups and small teams wanting docs and tasks together
- Product teams managing specs and roadmaps
- Excellent docs and knowledge base matters to you
Wrike review
Notion review
Some common situations:
- **A start-up that needs a wiki, roadmap and task board in one place:** Notion, on Plus or Business.
- **A product or engineering team writing specs and running light sprints:** Notion for planning and documentation; see [software project management](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/industries/software-project-management/).
- **A marketing or creative team handling many requests, reviews and sign-offs:** Wrike, for request forms, proofing and approvals; see [creative project management](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/industries/creative-project-management/).
- **An agency or professional services firm tracking time and capacity across clients:** Wrike.
- **A PMO standardising delivery across many projects:** Wrike, for portfolio dashboards, baselines and resource planning.
- **A small team on a tight budget with simple projects:** Notion, or Wrike's Free plan if you expect to grow into structured project management.
Still undecided? Our guide on [how to choose project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/how-to-choose-project-management-software/) sets out the questions to ask.

### Has your team outgrown Notion?
Many teams start in Notion and stay happily. These signs suggest your project work needs a dedicated platform such as Wrike:
- Managers cannot see who is overloaded without asking people individually.
- You need time tracking for billing or for estimating future work.
- Delays on one task need to show their knock-on effect on the end date.
- Requests arrive in chat and email and nobody owns triage.
- Status reporting across projects takes hours of manual work each week.
- Several half-maintained project databases exist and nobody trusts them.
- Clients or other departments need a controlled way to review and approve work.
If two or three of these apply, run a pilot of Wrike on one real project while keeping Notion for documentation.

### Using Wrike and Notion together
Wrike and Notion are often complementary rather than direct substitutes. A practical split is to keep **Notion as the knowledge base**, for handbooks, specs, meeting notes and decision logs, and run **project delivery in Wrike**, for tasks, schedules, requests, approvals, workload and reporting. Link each Wrike project to its Notion spec, and link from the spec back to the Wrike project.
Agree a simple rule so nobody has to check two places for the same thing, for example "if it has an owner and a due date, it lives in Wrike". You will pay for two tools, so check that each one has a clear job.

### How to switch from Notion to Wrike
1. **Write down what Notion is not doing for you**, such as workload, time tracking, intake or reporting. These become your success criteria.
2. **Export your project databases from Notion as CSV.** Keep the documentation in Notion or export pages separately if you are moving everything.
3. **Design your Wrike structure first:** spaces, a project template, statuses, and only the custom fields you will really use. Our [project tracker template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/project-tracker-template/) is a useful checklist.
4. **Import or rebuild one live project** and run it during Wrike's 14-day free trial with the people who will use it every day.
5. **Set up request forms and dashboards** so requesters and managers see the benefit straight away.
6. **Move remaining projects in waves**, link each one to its Notion documentation, and archive the old Notion databases so there is one source of truth for delivery.
Moving from Wrike to Notion works the same way in reverse: export Wrike data to a spreadsheet, design your Notion databases and relations, then import and test with one project.

### Alternatives to consider
If neither tool feels right, ClickUp combines docs with richer built-in project management, Asana offers dedicated task, goal and portfolio management with less setup, and monday.com is visual and highly customisable.
For broader shortlists, see [Wrike alternatives](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/wrike-alternatives/) and [Notion alternatives](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/notion/notion-alternatives/).

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: Is Wrike better than Notion?**
For structured project management, yes: Wrike scores 9.4/10 in our review against Notion's 8.0/10 and wins on feature depth, planning and resource management, Agile and scalability. Notion wins on value and is the better choice for docs, wikis and lightweight project tracking.

**Q: Can Notion replace Wrike?**
For small teams with simple projects, often yes. For teams that need time tracking, workload and capacity planning, critical path scheduling, request intake with approvals or packaged cross-project reporting, Notion usually cannot replace Wrike without significant custom building and third-party tools.

**Q: Is Notion good for project management?**
Yes, for lightweight to moderately complex projects. Notion offers task databases, boards, timelines, sprints, forms and automations connected to your docs, but it lacks native time tracking, resource management, baselines and packaged portfolio reporting.

**Q: Which is cheaper, Wrike or Notion?**
Notion is usually cheaper. Both start at $10 per user/month billed annually (Wrike Team, Notion Plus), but Notion Business is $20 against Wrike Business at $25. Notion AI needs Business, while Wrike includes AI Essentials from Team (checked 7 October 2026).

**Q: Do Wrike and Notion have free plans?**
Yes. Wrike's Free plan includes task management with board and table views. Notion's Free plan is aimed at individuals and limits blocks once a workspace has two or more members. Wrike also offers a 14-day free trial of paid plans.

**Q: Does Notion have Gantt charts like Wrike?**
Notion has a timeline view that works like a simple Gantt chart, with date ranges and dependencies. It does not offer critical path or baselines, which Wrike's interactive Gantt charts include.

**Q: Does Notion have time tracking or resource management?**
No. Notion has no native time tracking, workload view or resource scheduling; teams use number properties, rollups or third-party integrations instead. Wrike includes workload views and time tracking, with advanced capacity planning on Pinnacle.

**Q: Which is easier to learn, Wrike or Notion?**
We score both 7/10. Notion is easier to start with but harder when you build complex databases; Wrike gives you ready-made project features but takes longer to configure and has a denser interface.

**Q: Which has better AI, Wrike or Notion?**
They focus on different things. Notion AI is strong for writing, meeting notes and searching across connected apps, and is included from Business. Wrike AI focuses on project operations, such as summaries, request triage, risk checks and portfolio reporting, with AI Essentials from Team and Copilot and agents from Business.

**Q: Which is better for start-ups?**
Notion is usually the better first tool for start-ups that want a wiki, roadmap and task board in one place. Wrike's Free or Team plan suits start-ups that already run many client or cross-team projects.

**Q: Which is better for agencies and marketing teams?**
Wrike, in most cases. Its request forms, proofing and approvals, time tracking and workload views fit agency and marketing workflows. Notion works well for editorial calendars and briefs but has basic approvals and no time tracking.

**Q: Can I use Wrike and Notion together?**
Yes. A common pattern is Notion for documentation and knowledge, and Wrike for project delivery, with each project linked to its spec. Agree which work lives where so nothing is tracked twice.

**Q: How do I move from Notion to Wrike?**
Export your Notion project databases as CSV, design your Wrike spaces, statuses and fields, then import or rebuild one live project and pilot it during Wrike's 14-day free trial. Move remaining projects in waves and keep documentation linked.
How we review.
Rankings and scores are the editorial opinion of the Neural Project Institute, based on features, pricing, ease of use, scalability and published user ratings. Prices were checked on vendors' pricing pages and ratings on G2 and Capterra on 5 October 2026; both change often, so confirm on the vendor's site before buying. We are independent and do not receive payment for rankings.

## Wrike vs Smartsheet: Which Is Better in 2026?
Wrike vs Smartsheet comes down to how your team likes to work. Wrike is a broad, all-in-one work management platform with request intake, proofing, resource planning and portfolio reporting, and it is our #1 tool overall (9.4/10). Smartsheet turns a familiar spreadsheet grid into connected project plans with strong Gantt charts and enterprise portfolio controls (8.6/10). Below we compare them on features, pricing, AI, ease of use and user ratings so you can pick the right one.
- Published 16 September 2026
- Last updated 9 October 2026
- Prices and ratings checked 5 October 2026

### Key takeaways
- **Overall:** Wrike scores 9.4/10 and Smartsheet 8.6/10 in our review; Wrike wins four of seven categories and the other three are ties.
- **Choose Wrike** for cross-team workflows, structured request intake, proofing and approvals, and resource and portfolio planning in one platform.
- **Choose Smartsheet** if your organisation thinks in spreadsheets and wants grid-based plans, roll-up reports and standardised portfolios through Control Center.
- **Price:** Wrike has a free plan and paid plans from $10 per user/month; Smartsheet has no free plan and starts at $9 per member/month (both billed annually).
- **Ease of use is a tie (7/10 each):** Smartsheet feels instantly familiar to Excel users, while Wrike's breadth takes longer to configure but pays off for multi-team work.

### Wrike vs Smartsheet: Quick Verdict
**Wrike is the better choice for most growing teams and enterprises** that want projects, requests, approvals, resources and reporting in one place. It wins on feature depth, planning and resource management, collaboration and Agile support in our scoring, and it is the more natural fit for marketing, creative, professional services and cross-functional teams.
**Smartsheet is the better choice for spreadsheet-minded organisations**, such as operations, finance, construction and many PMOs, that want to turn scattered Excel trackers into governed, connected plans. Its grid, Gantt view and cross-sheet reports are excellent, and Control Center is one of the strongest tools on the market for provisioning standardised projects at scale.
Both are mature, enterprise-ready platforms, and both tie on ease of use, value for money and scalability in our review. The deciding question is usually the working style you want: a configurable work platform with many views (Wrike) or a powerful spreadsheet-style planner (Smartsheet).

### What Is Wrike?
Wrike is a cloud-based work and project management platform founded in 2006 and owned by Symphony Technology Group since 2023. It organises work into spaces, folders, projects and tasks, and lets each team see the same work as a list, board, table, Gantt chart, calendar or dashboard.
Its strength is breadth: interactive Gantt charts with the critical path and baselines, request forms with conditional logic, custom workflows and item types, proofing and approvals, workload and resource planning, cross-project dashboards and, on higher tiers, budgeting, advanced reporting and BI. Wrike AI adds summaries, writing help, Copilot and configurable AI agents.
Wrike suits teams that want one system of record for all their work, rather than a task tool, a proofing tool and a resource tool stitched together.

### What Is Smartsheet?
Smartsheet is a cloud-based work management platform launched in 2006 and taken private by Blackstone and Vista Equity Partners in January 2025. Work lives in **sheets**: grids of rows and columns where each row can be a task with an owner, dates, dependencies, a status and a discussion thread.
On top of sheets, Smartsheet adds Gantt, board, calendar, timeline and table views, forms, no-code automation, cross-sheet reports and dashboards. Enterprise customers get Portfolios and Scenario Planning, and Advanced Work Management adds Control Center, Dynamic View and Data Shuttle for running standardised portfolios.
Smartsheet suits organisations that already run projects and processes in spreadsheets and want them shared, automated and governed.

### Key Differences Between Wrike and Smartsheet
The two tools overlap heavily, but they are built on different ideas. The table summarises the differences that matter most when choosing.
|  | Wrike | Smartsheet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Core model | Tasks and projects with custom workflows, viewed many ways | Sheets of rows and columns that behave like project plans |
| Free plan | Yes (basic task management, board and table views) | No; free Contributors can view and comment |
| Free trial | 14 days, no credit card | 30 days on the Business plan, no credit card |
| Entry paid plan | Team: $10/user/month, 2–15 users | Pro: $9/member/month, 1–10 members |
| Main team plan | Business: $25/user/month, 5–200 users | Business: $19/member/month, 3+ members |
| Gantt charts | From Team, with critical path and baselines | All plans, with dependencies and critical path |
| Resource planning | Workload charts; advanced planning on Pinnacle | Workload on Business; Resource Management is an add-on |
| Portfolio management | Portfolio views and dashboards; BI on Pinnacle and Apex | Portfolios on Enterprise; Control Center on Advanced Work Management |
| Proofing | Built-in proofing and approvals | Proofing on Business and above |
| AI | AI Essentials from Team; Copilot and agents from Business | Smart Assist and other core AI on all plans; MCP from Business |
| Integrations | About 60 listed, plus Wrike Integrate and Wrike Sync | Over 175 listed, plus Bridge and Data Shuttle |
Prices are per user or member per month, billed annually, checked 7 October 2026.

### Ease of Use and Learning Curve
Both tools score 7/10 for ease of use in our review, but for different reasons.
**Smartsheet** is quick to start for anyone who knows Excel. A sheet looks like a spreadsheet, you can import an existing file, and basic editing needs almost no training. The learning curve arrives later: cross-sheet formulas, report logic, automation and permission design all take time, and the grid is less visual than board-first tools, which can slow adoption among non-spreadsheet users.
**Wrike** is straightforward for creating, assigning and updating tasks, but its breadth means more decisions up front: spaces, workflows, custom fields, request forms, dashboards and permissions. Reviewers consistently praise its flexibility and visibility while mentioning onboarding effort and a dense interface. Once configured, though, most users only see the views and fields that matter to them.
Tip
In a trial, rebuild one real process in each tool with the people who will use it. Spreadsheet-heavy teams usually feel at home in Smartsheet within a day; cross-functional teams usually get more from Wrike once workflows and request forms are set up.
If you are still writing your requirements, our guide on [how to choose project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/how-to-choose-project-management-software/) sets out the questions to ask.

### Views, Planning and Gantt Charts
Both tools are strong for date-driven work, which is one reason PMOs shortlist them together.

#### Wrike
Wrike's interactive [Gantt charts](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/gantt-chart/) are included from the Team plan. They support all four dependency types with lead and lag, automatic rescheduling, milestones, the critical path, float and baselines for planned-versus-actual tracking. Board and table views are available on every plan, including Free, and dashboards pull work together across projects.

#### Smartsheet
Smartsheet's Gantt view is available on all plans and sits on the same rows as the grid, so editing a date in either place updates both. It supports dependencies, milestones and critical path highlighting, and row hierarchy turns a flat list into phases and subtasks. Board and calendar views are on every plan, and timeline view starts on Business.
**Verdict:** a close call. Smartsheet's grid-plus-Gantt is excellent for people who plan in rows; Wrike adds baselines and more ways to view the same work, which suits mixed teams. Our free [Gantt chart template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/gantt-chart-template/) is a useful way to sketch a plan before you choose.

### Resource and Portfolio Management
This is the biggest functional difference between the two, and Wrike scores 10/10 against Smartsheet's 9/10 for planning and resource management in our review.

#### Resource and capacity planning
**Wrike** shows workload and capacity across the team, accounts for working hours, non-working days and holidays, and supports time tracking with approved timesheets. Advanced resource and capacity planning, role-based planning and budgeting are part of the Pinnacle plan, so organisations that need them get them inside the same platform.
**Smartsheet** offers workload tracking from the Business plan and Scenario Planning on Enterprise. Fuller resource management (capacity planning, time tracking, demand management, skill-based assignments and project budgets) is a separate **Resource Management** add-on with its own set-up.

#### Portfolio management
**Smartsheet** is very strong here. Portfolios on Enterprise give a standard view of related projects, and **Control Center** (in Advanced Work Management or as an add-on) provisions new projects from blueprints, pushes changes across existing projects and rolls up portfolio reporting.
**Wrike** handles portfolios through shared spaces, custom item types and fields, cross-project dashboards and, on Pinnacle and Apex, advanced reporting and BI. Its advantage is that portfolio data, resource data and the day-to-day work all live in the same system.
For background on the techniques, see [capacity planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/capacity-planning/), [resource allocation](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/resource-allocation/) and [program vs project vs portfolio management](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/program-vs-project-vs-portfolio-management/).

### Collaboration, Requests and Approvals
Wrike scores 9/10 and Smartsheet 8/10 for collaboration in our review.
**Wrike** keeps conversations on the work itself: comments, @mentions, attachments, activity streams and formal approvals with named approvers. Request forms with conditional logic create and route tasks automatically, and external forms let clients submit work without a Wrike account. Built-in proofing lets reviewers mark up images, videos and documents, a long-standing strength for creative and marketing teams.
**Smartsheet** handles collaboration at row and sheet level: conversations, @mentions, attachments and notifications. Forms with conditional logic feed rows straight into sheets, and proofing is available on Business and above. Its user model is cost-friendly for stakeholders: Contributors are free and can view and comment, and Guests are free on Business and above.
If your work starts as a request from another team or a client, Wrike's intake-to-approval flow is the more complete experience. Our free [work request template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/work-request-template/) shows the information a good intake form should capture.

### Automation and AI

#### Automation
Both tools offer no-code, trigger-and-action automation. **Wrike** automates assignment, status changes, notifications and request routing, with more advanced automation, AI agents and cross-tool automation through Wrike Integrate on higher tiers or as add-ons. **Smartsheet** automates reminders, approval requests, row updates and moves, and document generation; Pro is limited to 250 automations per month, while Business and above are unlimited.

#### AI
**Wrike AI** comes in two tiers. AI Essentials (content creation and editing, comment summaries, natural-language form and rule creation, AI highlights) is included from Team. AI Elite (Wrike Copilot, AI dashboard widgets, configurable AI agents and the Whiteboard assistant) starts with an allowance on Business that grows on Pinnacle and Apex.
**Smartsheet AI** includes Smart Assist (summaries, project health checks and actions), Smart Columns that apply AI to every row, an AI dashboard builder, formula generation and data analysis on all plans, plus an MCP server that connects sheets to external assistants from the Business plan.
Smartsheet's AI is especially handy for querying and summarising structured sheet data; Wrike's agents go further in automating workflow steps such as validating requests and routing work.

### Reporting and Dashboards
**Smartsheet** reporting is built on roll-ups: reports pull matching rows from many sheets, dashboards present them to stakeholders, and Portfolios and Control Center add portfolio-level reporting. Pro dashboards are limited to 10 widgets. Data can also be pushed to Power BI or Tableau.
**Wrike** includes shareable dashboards from the Team plan, with widgets for status, overdue work, workload and progress across projects, and advanced reporting and BI on Pinnacle and Apex. In Capterra's topic summaries, around 96% of Wrike reviews that mention project visibility and dashboards are positive.
Both can produce a reliable weekly [project status report](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-status-report/) without manual copying, as long as projects use consistent fields.

### Integrations
**Smartsheet** says it has over 175 integrations, including Microsoft Teams, Outlook, Slack, Google Workspace, Salesforce, Jira, DocuSign, Power BI and Tableau. Bridge offers low-code cross-system workflows, the API is available on Business and above, and Data Shuttle automates imports and exports.
**Wrike** lists around 60 integrations, including Microsoft Teams, Slack, Salesforce, Google Sheets, Power BI, Tableau and Miro, plus an open API. **Wrike Integrate** automates workflows across other systems, and **Wrike Sync** offers two-way sync with 22 tools such as Jira, GitHub, HubSpot and Excel; both are included in Apex and available as add-ons on other plans.
If you depend on a long list of enterprise connectors, Smartsheet's catalogue is larger. If you need engineering and business teams to share live work across tools, Wrike Sync is a strong option.

### Security and Administration
Both platforms are built for enterprise governance and score 10/10 for scalability in our review.
- **Wrike:** granular permissions, customisable user types (full, collaborator and read-only), locked spaces, admin controls and SSO on higher tiers. **Wrike Lock** (add-on) lets customers control the encryption keys that protect their data. Wrike's site displays AICPA, BSI and CSA STAR compliance badges.
- **Smartsheet:** its Trust Center lists SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, FedRAMP and HIPAA (with a BAA), with AES-256 encryption at rest, SAML SSO on Enterprise, SCIM and admin-enforced MFA. Enterprise customers can add customer-managed keys, data regions and Safeguard policies.
Smartsheet's FedRAMP listing is particularly relevant for US public-sector buyers. For any regulated use, confirm current certifications and plan availability in each vendor's trust documentation, and set up sound governance whichever tool you choose.

### Wrike vs Smartsheet by Team Type

#### PMOs and enterprise portfolios
Both are excellent. Choose Smartsheet if standardisation through blueprints and spreadsheet-style reporting is the priority; choose Wrike if you also want resource, budget and request management in the same system.

#### Marketing, creative and agency teams
Wrike is usually the better fit, thanks to request forms, custom workflows, proofing and approvals.

#### Operations and finance teams
Smartsheet is usually the more natural step up from spreadsheets: the data model barely changes, but you gain automation, forms and dashboards. Our [project tracker template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/project-tracker-template/) shows a typical starting structure.

#### Professional services and IT
Wrike's resource planning, timesheets and budgeting on Pinnacle suit firms that plan staff across many client projects; see [professional services project management](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/industries/professional-services-project-management/). IT teams use both, often alongside Jira.

#### Construction and engineering
Smartsheet's grid-based schedules, mobile forms for field data and roll-up reporting make it a common choice.

#### Small businesses
Wrike's Free and Team plans give small teams an easier start, while Smartsheet's lack of a free plan and 10-member Pro cap make it better suited to small teams that already think in spreadsheets.

### How to Switch Between Wrike and Smartsheet
1. **Pick one pilot project** that represents your typical work, rather than migrating everything at once.
2. **Map the structure.** Smartsheet sheets, rows and columns map roughly to Wrike projects, tasks and custom fields; parent rows become tasks with subtasks.
3. **Export and clean the data.** Export the sheet to a spreadsheet file, remove formulas and keep one row per task with owner, dates and status.
4. **Import.** Wrike can import Excel files on Team plans and above (up to 5,000 tasks per import) and map names in the "Assigned to" column to users. Smartsheet can create new sheets from imported Excel files.
5. **Rebuild what does not migrate:** dependencies, automations, request forms, reports and dashboards usually need to be set up again.
6. **Run both tools in parallel** for one reporting cycle, then switch the team over and archive the old workspace.
Plan the move like any small project, with an owner, a timeline and a short training session.

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: Which is better, Wrike or Smartsheet?**
In our review, Wrike scores 9.4/10 and Smartsheet 8.6/10. Wrike wins on feature depth, planning and resource management, collaboration and Agile support, and the two tie on ease of use, value and scalability. Wrike is better for cross-functional work in one platform; Smartsheet is better for spreadsheet-minded teams and standardised portfolios.

**Q: Is Wrike similar to Smartsheet?**
They overlap a lot: both offer Gantt charts, boards, forms, automation, dashboards, AI and enterprise security. The difference is the model. Smartsheet is built around spreadsheet-style sheets, while Wrike is built around tasks, projects and custom workflows that you can view in many ways.

**Q: Is Wrike cheaper than Smartsheet?**
Smartsheet is slightly cheaper per seat on list price: Pro is $9 and Business $19 per member/month, against Wrike's Team at $10 and Business at $25 per user/month (billed annually, checked 7 October 2026). Wrike has a free plan, Smartsheet's Contributors are free, and add-ons can change the total for either tool.

**Q: Does Smartsheet have a free plan like Wrike?**
No. Smartsheet does not list a free plan; it offers a 30-day free trial of the Business plan. Wrike has a Free plan with basic task management and board and table views, plus a 14-day trial of paid features.

**Q: Which is easier to learn, Wrike or Smartsheet?**
Both score 7/10 for ease of use in our review. Smartsheet is quicker to start for Excel users because the grid is familiar. Wrike needs more set-up because of its many options, but once workflows and views are configured, everyday use is straightforward.

**Q: Which is better for resource management?**
Wrike. It includes workload and capacity views on paid plans and advanced resource planning and budgeting on Pinnacle. Smartsheet offers workload tracking on Business and Scenario Planning on Enterprise, but full resource management is a separate add-on.

**Q: Which is better for portfolio management and PMOs?**
Both are strong. Smartsheet's Control Center is excellent for provisioning standardised projects from blueprints. Wrike combines portfolio dashboards, custom item types, resource planning and BI on its top tiers in the same system as the day-to-day work.

**Q: Which has better Gantt charts?**
Both have capable Gantt charts with dependencies and the critical path. Smartsheet includes Gantt on every plan, tied to its grid. Wrike includes it from the Team plan and adds baselines for planned-versus-actual tracking.

**Q: Which has better AI features?**
They focus on different things. Wrike's AI Elite tier adds Copilot and configurable AI agents that automate workflow steps, from the Business plan. Smartsheet includes Smart Assist, Smart Columns, formula generation and an AI dashboard builder on all plans, which is especially useful for structured sheet data.

**Q: Is Wrike or Smartsheet better for marketing teams?**
Wrike is usually the better fit for marketing and creative teams, thanks to request forms, custom workflows, proofing and approvals. Smartsheet works well for marketing calendars and plans, especially with Brandfolder for digital assets.

**Q: What are the limitations of Smartsheet compared with Wrike?**
Smartsheet has no free plan, is less visual than board-first tools, charges extra for full resource management and some portfolio apps, and reviewers report slower performance on very large sheets. In return it offers a familiar grid and excellent roll-up reporting.

**Q: Can I move from Smartsheet to Wrike?**
Yes. Export your sheets to Excel, clean the data and import it into Wrike, which accepts Excel files on Team plans and above. Dependencies, automations, forms and dashboards usually need rebuilding, so pilot one project first.

**Q: Which is closer to Excel, Wrike or Smartsheet?**
Smartsheet. Its sheets look and behave much like spreadsheets, with formulas and cell links. Wrike's table view also feels familiar to spreadsheet users, but Wrike is organised around tasks and workflows rather than cells.

## Wrike vs Trello (2026): Which Is Better?
Wrike is best all-in-one work management platform; Trello is best for simple kanban boards. We compare pricing, features, ease of use and G2 and Capterra ratings to help you choose.
- Published 18 September 2026
