### Key takeaways
- **Overall winner:** Wrike (9.4/10 vs 7.8/10), winning 5 of 7 categories.
- **Choose Wrike** for growing teams and enterprises that want one platform for projects, resources, portfolios, approvals and reporting.
- **Choose Trello** for individuals and small teams that want simple, visual Kanban boards.
- **Price:** Wrike Free; paid from $10/user/month; Trello Free; paid from $5/user/month.

### Quick verdict

**Q: What is a cheaper alternative to Asana?**

Most tools offer CSV import and many provide direct importers from popular competitors. Plan a pilot project, map fields and statuses, and migrate active work first.

URL: https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/basecamp/basecamp-alternatives/

## Best Basecamp Alternatives in 2026
The best Basecamp alternatives are Wrike for teams that need Gantt charts, workload planning and reporting, monday.com and Asana for easier structured project management, and Trello or ClickUp for tight budgets. Basecamp itself is excellent for calm, communication-centred projects with clients, so the right replacement depends on what you are missing. Below we compare nine alternatives on features, pricing, free plans and user ratings, show how flat and per-user pricing compare at different team sizes, and explain how to move your projects across.
- Published 14 September 2026
- Last updated 9 October 2026
- Prices and ratings checked 5 October 2026

### Key takeaways
- Wrike (9.4/10) is the strongest all-round alternative for teams that have outgrown Basecamp and need Gantt dependencies, workload views, proofing and dashboards.
- monday.com and Asana add structure, timelines and automation while staying easy to learn, which matters if clients and non-technical staff use the tool.
- Trello (from $5/user/month) and ClickUp (from $7/user/month) are the cheapest per-user options, but Basecamp's flat price can still be cheaper for larger teams.
- Count both people and active projects before you switch: Basecamp charges per account, most alternatives charge per user.
- Jira suits software teams running sprints, Microsoft Planner suits Microsoft 365 organisations, and Notion suits teams that want docs and wikis alongside projects.

### Why teams look for Basecamp alternatives
Basecamp, made by 37signals, does a few things very well. Each project gets one page with a message board, to-do lists, a Kanban-style Card Table, a schedule, group chat (Campfire), automatic check-ins, and docs and files. Clients can be invited with controlled visibility, and paid plans charge a flat monthly price rather than per user. It is one of the easiest project tools to learn, and it rates 4.4/5 on Capterra.
That simplicity is deliberate, and it is also why teams eventually look elsewhere. The most common reasons are:
- **No Gantt dependencies.** Basecamp's schedules and Lineup show dates, but you cannot link tasks so that one slipping moves the next. Projects with [task dependencies](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/task-dependencies/) and fixed deadlines need a tool that models them.
- **No resource or workload planning.** There is no view of who is over- or under-loaded across projects, which makes [capacity planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/capacity-planning/) a spreadsheet exercise.
- **Limited reporting.** Basecamp offers activity views and Hill Charts, but no custom dashboards, budget tracking or portfolio roll-ups.
- **Little custom structure.** There are no custom fields or priorities, and only one level of subtasks, so standardising processes across many projects is harder.
- **Active-project caps.** Every plan except Unlimited limits the number of active projects, so a small team running many projects can end up on the $299/month plan.
- **No built-in AI (as of October 2026).** Basecamp has opened its API and command-line interface to AI agents you run yourself, but it has no built-in AI summaries or writing help.
- **No native Slack or Microsoft Teams integration.** 37signals positions Campfire and pings as the alternative; third-party connectors exist.
- **Not designed for Agile.** There are no backlogs, sprints or story points.

#### When staying with Basecamp makes sense
If your main problem is scattered email and chat, most of your projects are client-facing, and you rarely need dependencies or formal reporting, Basecamp may still be the best fit. Its flat pricing also becomes more attractive as headcount grows. In that case, consider adding a lightweight Gantt or time-tracking integration rather than switching.

### How we chose these alternatives
We compared the other nine tools in our [top 10 project management tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/) ranking. Each one is scored from 1 to 10 on seven categories: ease of use, feature depth, planning and resource management, collaboration, Agile and software teams, value for money, and scalability and enterprise readiness. We also considered published G2 and Capterra ratings and prices on each vendor's pricing page.
Many of the pages that rank for this topic are written by software vendors that place their own product first. We do not sell software or accept payment for rankings, and we only include tools we have reviewed in depth. Prices and ratings change often, so confirm them on the vendor's site before you buy.

### Basecamp alternatives reviewed
Here is how each alternative compares with Basecamp specifically: what it adds, what you give up and who should consider it.

#### 1. Wrike: best all-round Basecamp alternative
Wrike is our highest-rated tool (9.4/10) and the natural next step for teams that have outgrown Basecamp's simplicity. It adds interactive Gantt charts with dependencies on paid plans, workload views, dashboards, request forms with conditional logic, automation, and built-in proofing and approvals for creative work. Guest access lets you bring clients into projects, which matters if client collaboration is why you chose Basecamp in the first place.
The trade-off is that Wrike takes longer to set up and learn, and it charges per user: a free plan, then Team at $10/user/month for 2 to 15 users and Business at $25/user/month (billed annually). It suits agencies, marketing teams and PMOs that now need scheduling, resources and reporting.

#### 2. monday.com: best for easy, visual workflows
monday.com keeps much of Basecamp's approachability but adds far more structure. Boards can be switched between table, Kanban, timeline, Gantt and calendar views, and dashboards combine data from several boards. Recipe-style automations handle routine updates. It is one of the easiest tools for non-technical teams to adopt.
Plans are sold in seat bundles with a three-seat minimum: Basic is $9, Standard (with timeline and Gantt) $12 and Pro $19 per seat/month, billed annually, and the free plan covers two seats. Automation and integration actions are capped by plan. See our [monday.com review](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/) and [monday.com vs Basecamp](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/monday-vs-basecamp/).

#### 3. Asana: best for structured task management
Asana gives you what Basecamp's to-do lists lack: custom fields, multiple views (list, board, calendar, timeline and Gantt), dependencies, forms, rules and dashboards from the Starter plan, with portfolios, goals, workload and approvals on Advanced. Paid plans include unlimited free guests, which helps agencies working with clients.
Starter costs $10.99/user/month and Advanced $24.99/user/month (billed annually), and the free Personal plan is for individuals and very small teams. Asana is more task-centred than Basecamp, so long-form discussion and announcements need a little more thought.

#### 4. Notion: best for docs, wikis and projects together
If Basecamp's Docs and Files and message boards are what your team values most, Notion goes much further on documentation. Pages, wikis and databases live in one workspace, and project trackers can be built from databases with board, timeline and calendar views. Notion AI adds writing and summarising help.
Project management in Notion requires design effort, and it has no native time tracking or resource management. Plus starts at $10/member/month and Business at $20 (yearly rate), with a free plan.

#### 5. Trello: best for simple Kanban at a low price
Trello is the closest match to Basecamp's Card Table, with intuitive boards, lists and cards, Butler automation and a large library of Power-Ups. It is very easy to learn and the free plan supports up to 10 collaborators per workspace. Premium adds calendar, timeline, table and dashboard views.
Trello lacks Basecamp's message boards, check-ins and docs, so many teams pair it with a chat tool. Standard is $5 and Premium $10 per user/month (billed annually).

#### 6. ClickUp: best value for feature-rich teams
ClickUp packs tasks, docs, whiteboards, chat, goals, time tracking, Gantt charts and sprints into one low-priced workspace. For a team leaving Basecamp because it needs more features without a big price rise, it is hard to beat on value: Unlimited is $7/user/month and Business $12/user/month (billed annually), with a Free Forever plan.
The trade-off is complexity: ClickUp is the opposite of Basecamp's calm, focused design, and its most capable AI features are paid add-ons.

#### 7. Smartsheet: best for spreadsheet-style planning
Smartsheet suits operations, finance and PMO teams that think in rows and columns. Its sheets support dependencies, Gantt charts with critical path, forms, automation, cross-sheet reports and dashboards, with strong enterprise governance on higher plans.
There is no free plan (Pro is $9/member/month billed yearly, with a 30-day trial), and its grid-first interface is less inviting for clients than Basecamp. Free Contributors can view and comment on shared work.

#### 8. Jira: best for software and Agile teams
If you are a software team using Basecamp for development work, Jira is the specialist tool. It provides backlogs, sprints, story points, velocity and burndown reports, configurable workflows and deep developer integrations. The free plan covers up to 10 users.
Jira is complex to administer and not designed for clients or non-technical teams, so agencies often keep a separate tool for client communication.

#### 9. Microsoft Planner: best for Microsoft 365 organisations
Basic Planner is included in many Microsoft 365 business plans and works inside Teams and Outlook, which fills one of Basecamp's gaps: native Teams integration. Planner Plan 1 ($10/user/month, paid yearly) adds timeline (Gantt) views, dependencies, milestones, sprints and custom fields, and Planner and Project Plan 3 ($30/user/month) adds baselines, critical path and resource management.
Planner is lighter than specialist platforms and is designed for internal teams rather than client collaboration.

### Flat pricing vs per-user pricing: what will you really pay?
Basecamp is the only tool in our top 10 with flat, per-account pricing. Its plans differ mainly by the number of active projects and storage (checked on Basecamp's pricing page on 7 October 2026):
| Basecamp plan | Price | Active projects | Users |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 | 1 | Up to 5 |
| Freelancer | $25/month | Up to 3 | Up to 20 |
| Studio | $59/month | Up to 10 | Unlimited |
| Pro | $99/month | Up to 25 | Unlimited |
| Unlimited | $299/month, billed annually | Unlimited | Unlimited |
Most alternatives charge per user, so the comparison depends on your headcount. This illustration assumes about eight active projects (Basecamp Studio) and each tool's entry-level paid plan at list prices billed annually:
| Monthly cost | 5 people | 15 people | 40 people |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Basecamp Studio (flat) | $59 | $59 | $59 |
| Trello Standard ($5/user) | $25 | $75 | $200 |
| ClickUp Unlimited ($7/user) | $35 | $105 | $280 |
| monday.com Basic ($9/seat) | $45 | $135 | $360 |
| Wrike Team ($10/user, max 15) | $50 | $150 | $1,000 on Business ($25/user) |
| Notion Plus ($10/member) | $50 | $150 | $400 |
| Asana Starter ($10.99/user) | $54.95 | $164.85 | $439.60 |
Two lessons follow. First, small teams can often switch to a per-user tool for the same or less money, especially if they need features Basecamp lacks. Second, larger teams pay much more per month after switching, so the move needs to be justified by the time saved on scheduling, reporting and resource planning. Remember to price guest or client access too: Asana includes unlimited free guests on paid plans, Smartsheet's Contributors are free, and monday.com includes free viewers from Basic, but rules differ by tool.
Tip
Count your active projects as well as your people. A three-person team with 30 active projects needs Basecamp Unlimited at $299 a month, which is more than most per-user tools would cost for three people.

### Best Basecamp alternatives by use case

#### Best free Basecamp alternative
Basecamp's Free plan is limited to one project. For a small team that needs more on a free plan, **Trello** (up to 10 collaborators per workspace), **ClickUp** (Free Forever) and **Wrike** (free plan with board and table views) are the most practical. **Jira** is free for up to 10 users if you are a software team. Asana's Personal plan and monday.com's two-seat free plan are better for trying the tools than for running a team.

#### Cheapest Basecamp alternative
Per user, Trello Standard ($5) and ClickUp Unlimited ($7) are the lowest-priced paid plans in our review. For teams of more than about 10 people, Basecamp's flat pricing often remains the cheapest option overall.

#### Best Basecamp alternative for agencies and client work
**Wrike** is the strongest choice when agency work involves approvals, proofing, resource planning and reporting, with guest access for clients. **Asana** and **monday.com** are easier to roll out and handle client collaboration well. Our guide to [agency project management](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/industries/agency-project-management/) covers the processes these tools support, and a [communication plan template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/communication-plan-template/) helps you agree what clients see.

#### Best Basecamp alternative with Gantt charts
Wrike, Smartsheet, monday.com (Standard and above), Asana (Starter and above) and ClickUp (Unlimited and above) all offer Gantt or timeline views with dependencies. Our [Gantt chart software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/gantt-chart-software/) guide compares the approaches, and our [project plan template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/project-plan-template/) is a quick way to sketch a schedule before you migrate.

#### Best Basecamp alternative for small businesses
Small businesses usually want quick setup and predictable costs. **Trello**, **ClickUp** and **monday.com** are good fits, and **Wrike's** Team plan (2 to 15 users) is worth considering if you need Gantt charts and dashboards.

#### Best Basecamp alternative for enterprises
**Wrike** and **Smartsheet** score highest for scalability and enterprise readiness in our review, with portfolio views, governance and advanced security on higher plans.

#### Best Basecamp alternative for remote and asynchronous teams
Basecamp's check-ins and message boards are built for asynchronous work. **Notion** is strong for written, document-led collaboration, and **Asana** and **Wrike** support status updates, comments and dashboards that reduce meetings.

#### Best Basecamp alternative for Agile and software teams
**Jira** is the standard for Scrum and Kanban in software teams; **ClickUp** offers sprints and sprint points with broader business use. Teams that mainly want a visual workflow can start with Trello and a simple [Kanban board](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/kanban/kanban-boards/).

#### Best Basecamp alternative for Microsoft 365
**Microsoft Planner** works inside Teams and Outlook and is included in many Microsoft 365 plans. Wrike also integrates with Microsoft tools if you need more depth.

### How to choose the right Basecamp alternative
A short, structured evaluation avoids swapping one compromise for another:
1. **List what you use in Basecamp today.** Note which tools on the project page your team relies on: message boards, to-dos, Card Tables, schedules, check-ins, Campfire, docs and client access.
2. **Name the gap.** Write down the specific problems that triggered the search, such as dependencies, workload, reporting or AI. If the only issue is cost, compare plans before switching tools.
3. **Separate must-haves from nice-to-haves.** Our guide to [project management software features](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-management-software-features/) explains what each feature does and when you need it.
4. **Check the client and guest model.** If clients work in your projects, confirm how each tool licenses and restricts external users.
5. **Work out the 12-month cost** using your expected headcount and the plan you will actually need, including add-ons such as AI.
6. **Trial two tools on a real project**, ideally one with a client, for two weeks. Judge notifications, permissions and reporting with real data.
For a full walkthrough, read [how to choose project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/how-to-choose-project-management-software/).

### How to migrate from Basecamp
Basecamp organises everything around the project page, so most of the work in a migration is deciding where each kind of information will live in the new tool:
| In Basecamp | Typical equivalent in other tools |
| --- | --- |
| Project | Project, folder, board or space |
| To-do lists and to-dos | Task lists or sections with tasks and subtasks |
| Card Table | Kanban or board view |
| Schedule and Lineup | Calendar, timeline or Gantt view |
| Message Board | Project updates, comments or a docs page |
| Campfire chat and pings | Built-in chat, or Slack or Microsoft Teams |
| Automatic Check-ins | Status updates, recurring forms or stand-up integrations |
| Hill Charts | Progress fields, status reports or dashboards |
| Docs and Files | Docs, wiki pages or connected cloud storage |
| Client access | Guest, client or viewer permissions |
1. **Take an inventory.** List active projects, owners, clients with access and any integrations. Archive projects that are finished; they do not need to move.
2. **Decide what to migrate.** Move open to-dos, upcoming dates and current documents. Keep historical discussions in Basecamp's archive or export them for reference rather than recreating them.
3. **Build the structure first.** Set up project templates, statuses, custom fields and views in the new tool before importing anything. Most tools import tasks from CSV or spreadsheet files; check each vendor's help centre for current importers.
4. **Set permissions and guest access** for clients and contractors, and test what an external user can see.
5. **Pilot with one or two live projects** for a few weeks, then migrate the rest in waves.
6. **Agree new working norms**: where announcements go, how status is reported and which notifications people should switch on. Our guide to [managing multiple projects](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/managing-multiple-projects/) helps when you start running a portfolio in one place.
7. **Close Basecamp deliberately.** Keep it read-only for a short overlap period, export anything you must retain, then cancel. Basecamp has no contract, but you cannot downgrade a paid account to the Free plan.
Tip
Do not try to copy Basecamp exactly. The point of switching is to use what the new tool does better, such as dependencies, workload views or dashboards, so redesign your process around those.

### Our verdict on Basecamp alternatives
Basecamp remains a good tool for calm, communication-centred projects with clients, and its flat pricing is unusual value for larger teams. When projects need dependencies, workload planning, structured fields or reporting, it is time to look elsewhere. For most teams in that position, **Wrike** is our first recommendation because it covers scheduling, resources, approvals and reporting in one platform while still supporting client collaboration. If ease of adoption matters most, shortlist **monday.com** and **Asana**; if budget matters most, **ClickUp** and **Trello**.
See all head-to-head matchups on our [compare project management tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/compare/) page, or read about [AI project management tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/ai-project-management-tools/) if built-in AI is part of your reason for switching.

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: What is the best alternative to Basecamp?**
For most teams that have outgrown Basecamp, Wrike is the best alternative because it adds Gantt charts with dependencies, workload views, proofing, dashboards and guest access in one platform. monday.com and Asana are easier to learn, and ClickUp and Trello are the cheapest options.

**Q: Is there a free alternative to Basecamp?**
Yes. Trello (up to 10 collaborators per workspace), ClickUp (Free Forever), Wrike, Notion and Jira (up to 10 users) all have free plans that support more than Basecamp's one-project Free plan. Asana's Personal plan and monday.com's two-seat free plan are better for trials than for teams.

**Q: What is cheaper than Basecamp?**
For small teams, Trello Standard ($5/user/month) and ClickUp Unlimited ($7/user/month), both billed annually, are usually cheaper than Basecamp Studio at $59/month. For teams of more than about 10 people, Basecamp's flat pricing is often cheaper than any per-user tool.

**Q: Which Basecamp alternative is best for agencies?**
Wrike is the strongest choice for agencies that need approvals, proofing, resource planning and client reporting. Asana and monday.com are easier to roll out and handle client collaboration well. Check how each tool licenses guest users before you switch.

**Q: Which Basecamp alternative has Gantt charts?**
Wrike, Smartsheet, monday.com (Standard and above), Asana (Starter and above), ClickUp (Unlimited and above) and Microsoft Planner's paid plans all offer Gantt or timeline views with task dependencies. Basecamp has schedules but no dependencies.

**Q: What is the easiest alternative to Basecamp?**
Trello and monday.com are the easiest tools to learn in our review, followed by Asana. All three are suitable for clients and non-technical staff.

**Q: Is Asana better than Basecamp?**
Asana is better for structured task management, timelines, goals and portfolios; Basecamp is better for simple, communication-centred projects and flat pricing. See our [Asana vs Basecamp comparison](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/asana-vs-basecamp/).

**Q: Is Trello better than Basecamp?**
Trello is better if you mainly need simple, low-cost Kanban boards. Basecamp is better if you want message boards, check-ins, docs and client access in one place with flat pricing. See [Trello vs Basecamp](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/trello/trello-vs-basecamp/).

**Q: Which Basecamp alternative is best for enterprises?**
Wrike and Smartsheet score highest for scalability and enterprise readiness in our review, with portfolio management, governance and advanced security on their higher plans.

**Q: Does Basecamp have AI, and which alternatives do?**
As of October 2026, Basecamp has no built-in AI features, but its API, CLI and connectors let AI agents work in Basecamp. Wrike, monday.com, Asana, Smartsheet, Notion, Trello and Jira include AI features on some plans; ClickUp and Microsoft Planner sell AI as add-ons.

**Q: Can I move my Basecamp projects to another tool?**
Yes. Most tools import tasks from CSV or spreadsheet files, and some offer direct importers. Migrate active work first, archive finished projects, set up structure and permissions before importing, and pilot with one or two projects.

**Q: Why do people leave Basecamp?**
The most common reasons are the lack of Gantt dependencies and resource management, limited reporting, little custom structure, active-project caps on most plans and the absence of built-in AI. Many teams stay because of its simplicity and flat pricing.

**Q: Is Basecamp still worth using in 2026?**
Yes, for agencies, small businesses and remote teams whose main need is organised communication with clients and colleagues. Teams that need structured planning and reporting will be better served by an alternative. Read our [Basecamp review](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/basecamp/).
How we review.
Rankings and scores are the editorial opinion of the Neural Project Institute, based on features, pricing, ease of use, scalability and published user ratings. Prices were checked on vendors' pricing pages and ratings on G2 and Capterra on 5 October 2026; both change often, so confirm on the vendor's site before buying. We are independent and do not receive payment for rankings.

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: What is the best alternative to ClickUp?**
It depends on why you are switching. Choose Wrike if you want more mature enterprise resource and portfolio management. Choose monday.com if you want a simpler, more polished interface.

**Q: Why do teams look for ClickUp alternatives?**
The most common reasons are: can feel overwhelming; setup takes effort; some users report performance lags; best ai features cost extra.

**Q: Is there a free alternative to ClickUp?**
Yes: Wrike, monday.com, Asana, Jira, Notion, Trello, Basecamp have free plans.

**Q: What is a cheaper alternative to ClickUp?**
Trello (from $5/user/month) and ClickUp (from $7/user/month, annual) are among the lowest-priced paid options; Basecamp's flat pricing can be cheaper for large teams.

**Q: What is an easier alternative to ClickUp?**
Trello and monday.com are the easiest tools to learn, followed by Asana and Basecamp.

**Q: What is the best ClickUp alternative for enterprises?**
Wrike, Smartsheet and monday.com offer the strongest enterprise features in our review.

**Q: What is the best ClickUp alternative for software teams?**
Jira is the standard for software teams; ClickUp is a flexible, lower-cost option.

**Q: Which ClickUp alternative has the best user ratings?**
On G2, monday.com (4.7), ClickUp (4.6) and Notion (4.6) have some of the highest ratings among the tools we reviewed (checked 5 October 2026).

**Q: Can I migrate from ClickUp to another tool?**
Most tools offer CSV import and many provide direct importers from popular competitors. Plan a pilot project, map fields and statuses, and migrate active work first.

**Q: How did you choose these ClickUp alternatives?**
We compared the other nine tools in our top 10 on features, pricing, ease of use, scalability and published G2 and Capterra ratings, and ordered them by how well they address common reasons for switching.
How we review.
Rankings and scores are the editorial opinion of the Neural Project Institute, based on features, pricing, ease of use, scalability and published user ratings. Prices were checked on vendors' pricing pages and ratings on G2 and Capterra on 5 October 2026; both change often, so confirm on the vendor's site before buying. We are independent and do not receive payment for rankings.

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: What is the best alternative to Microsoft Planner?**
It depends on why you are switching. Choose Wrike if you want far deeper project, resource and approval features. Choose monday.com if you want more customisable workflows.

**Q: Why do teams look for Microsoft Planner alternatives?**
The most common reasons are: lighter feature set than specialist platforms; product changes and retirements can confuse buyers; limited customisation and reporting without power bi.

**Q: Is there a free alternative to Microsoft Planner?**
Yes: Wrike, monday.com, Asana, Trello, ClickUp, Jira, Notion, Basecamp have free plans.

**Q: What is a cheaper alternative to Microsoft Planner?**
Trello (from $5/user/month) and ClickUp (from $7/user/month, annual) are among the lowest-priced paid options; Basecamp's flat pricing can be cheaper for large teams.

**Q: What is an easier alternative to Microsoft Planner?**
Trello and monday.com are the easiest tools to learn, followed by Asana and Basecamp.

**Q: What is the best Microsoft Planner alternative for enterprises?**
Wrike, Smartsheet and monday.com offer the strongest enterprise features in our review.

**Q: What is the best Microsoft Planner alternative for software teams?**
Jira is the standard for software teams; ClickUp is a flexible, lower-cost option.

**Q: Which Microsoft Planner alternative has the best user ratings?**
On G2, monday.com (4.7), ClickUp (4.6) and Notion (4.6) have some of the highest ratings among the tools we reviewed (checked 5 October 2026).

**Q: Can I migrate from Microsoft Planner to another tool?**
Most tools offer CSV import and many provide direct importers from popular competitors. Plan a pilot project, map fields and statuses, and migrate active work first.

**Q: How did you choose these Microsoft Planner alternatives?**
We compared the other nine tools in our top 10 on features, pricing, ease of use, scalability and published G2 and Capterra ratings, and ordered them by how well they address common reasons for switching.

# Best Notion Alternatives for Project Management in 2026

URL: https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/notion/notion-alternatives/
Section: Tool alternatives
Summary: Compare the best Notion alternatives for project management: Wrike, Asana, ClickUp, monday.com and more, with scores, pricing, free plans and migration tips.


## Best Notion Alternatives for Project Management in 2026
The best Notion alternatives for project management are Wrike for full project and resource management, ClickUp for docs plus richer project features at a low price, Asana for structured task management and Trello for simple boards. Notion remains one of the best docs-first workspaces, so many teams keep it as their wiki and move only their project tracking. Below we compare nine alternatives on scores, pricing, free plans and the features Notion does not include.
- Published 13 September 2026
- Last updated 9 October 2026
- Prices and ratings checked 5 October 2026

### Key takeaways
- Wrike (9.4/10) is the strongest Notion alternative when you need time tracking, workload views, Gantt charts and portfolio reporting in one platform.
- ClickUp (8.9/10) is the closest like-for-like swap: docs, wikis and tasks in one workspace, with time tracking and Gantt charts from $7 per user/month (annual).
- Asana (9.0/10) and monday.com (9.1/10) give you ready-made project management without designing databases yourself.
- Trello, Basecamp, ClickUp, Asana, Wrike, monday.com and Jira all have free plans; Smartsheet has a 30-day trial instead.
- You do not have to leave Notion completely: keeping it for documentation and adding a dedicated project tool is often the best answer.

### Quick answer: the best Notion alternatives at a glance
If you only have a minute, this table matches each alternative to the main reason teams leave Notion for project work. Scores are from our [top 10 project management tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/) review; prices are entry-level paid plans (checked 7 October 2026).
| Alternative | Score | Best Notion alternative for | Paid plans from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Wrike](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/) | 9.4 | Full project, resource and portfolio management | $10/user/month (annual) |
| [monday.com](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/) | 9.1 | Easy, visual workflows with dashboards | $9/seat/month (annual, 3-seat minimum) |
| [Asana](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/) | 9.0 | Dedicated task and goal management | $10.99/user/month (annual) |
| [ClickUp](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/clickup/) | 8.9 | Docs plus richer project management at low cost | $7/user/month (annual) |
| [Smartsheet](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/smartsheet/) | 8.6 | Spreadsheet-style enterprise planning | $9/member/month (annual) |
| [Jira](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/jira/) | 8.6 | Software teams running Scrum or Kanban | About $7.91/user/month |
| [Microsoft Planner](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/microsoft-planner/) | 8.1 | Organisations on Microsoft 365 | Basic included; Plan 1 $10/user/month |
| [Trello](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/trello/) | 7.8 | Simple Kanban boards | $5/user/month (annual) |
| [Basecamp](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/basecamp/) | 7.6 | Calm, communication-centred projects | $25/month flat |
For context, [Notion](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/notion/) scores 8.0/10 in the same review, with top marks among the ten tools for collaboration (9/10) and value (9/10) but 5/10 for planning and resource management. That gap is the main reason people search for alternatives.

### Why teams look for Notion alternatives
Notion is an excellent workspace. It is rated 4.7/5 from 2,834 reviews on Capterra (checked 7 October 2026), and teams love it for documentation, wikis, meeting notes and flexible databases. The reasons people look elsewhere are almost always about project management, not about Notion being a poor product:
- **You build the project system yourself.** Projects in Notion are databases with properties, relations and views that someone has to design and maintain. That is flexible, but dedicated tools give you tasks, dependencies, workload and reports ready to use.
- **No native time tracking or resource management.** Notion has no timesheets, workload view or capacity planning. Agencies billing hours and teams doing [resource allocation](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/resource-allocation/) usually need these out of the box.
- **Scheduling is light.** Notion's timeline view shows dates and dependencies, but not baselines or critical path analysis, which date-driven projects rely on.
- **Reporting is assembled by hand.** Charts and filtered views can make a good dashboard, but there are no packaged portfolio, workload or burndown reports.
- **Performance with large databases.** Capterra reviewers who discuss large amounts of content often describe Notion as sluggish, which becomes noticeable as project databases grow.
- **AI and plan costs.** Notion AI is included only on the Business plan ($20 per member/month, annual) and Enterprise, and Custom Agents run on paid credits (checked 7 October 2026).

#### Do you need to leave Notion at all?
Often, no. Many teams get the best result by keeping Notion as the knowledge base (specs, handbooks, meeting notes) and running delivery in a dedicated project tool. Notion's Business plan includes connections to tools such as GitHub and Asana, and most project tools integrate with Slack, Google Drive and each other. Replace Notion completely only if you want a single tool and your alternative's docs are good enough for your team.

### How we chose these Notion alternatives
We compared the nine other tools in our top 10 ranking. Each tool is scored from 1 to 10 on seven categories: ease of use, feature depth, planning and resource management, collaboration, Agile and software support, value for money, and scalability and enterprise readiness. We also checked vendors' pricing pages (7 October 2026) and published G2 and Capterra ratings.
The list below is ordered by how well each tool fixes the most common reasons teams leave Notion for project work, then by overall score. That is why Trello and Basecamp, which rank lower overall, appear higher here than Smartsheet or Jira: they solve specific Notion frustrations very simply. Scores are our editorial opinion and we do not accept payment for rankings.

### Each Notion alternative in brief

#### 1. Wrike: best for full project and resource management
[Wrike](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/) is our top-ranked tool and the most direct answer to Notion's project management gaps. It includes interactive Gantt charts with dependencies, critical path and baselines on paid plans, workload charts, time tracking, cross-project portfolio views, request forms, proofing and approvals, and dashboards. Notion is easier to start with and better for long-form documentation; Wrike is far stronger once you manage many projects and people. Wrike has a free plan, and paid plans start with Team at $10 per user/month (annual, 2 to 15 users) and Business at $25 (checked 7 October 2026).

#### 2. Asana: best for dedicated task management
[Asana](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/) gives you clean, ready-made task and project management: list, board, calendar, timeline and Gantt views, rules, forms and dashboards from Starter, with portfolios, goals, workload and time tracking on Advanced. You do not need to design databases, which is the main relief for teams coming from Notion. Notion still wins for wikis and documents. The free Personal plan is limited to two seats; Starter costs $10.99 per user/month annually (checked 7 October 2026).

#### 3. ClickUp: best for docs plus richer project management
[ClickUp](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/clickup/) is the closest like-for-like replacement because it combines docs, wikis, whiteboards and chat with full project features: Gantt charts with dependencies and baselines, native time tracking, workload views, goals and sprints. It also has a Notion importer. The trade-off is complexity: ClickUp has a lot of settings, and its full AI features are paid add-ons. Unlimited costs $7 per user/month annually and Business $12 (checked 7 October 2026).

#### 4. Trello: best for simple boards
If your Notion setup has become a maze of databases and you mainly need a board, [Trello](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/trello/) is the easiest tool in our review (10/10 for ease of use). Boards, lists and cards work immediately, with built-in automation and Power-Ups. It is lighter than Notion for documentation and has no dependencies or resource management, and timeline, table and dashboard views need Premium. Standard costs $5 per user/month annually, and the Free plan allows 10 collaborators per Workspace (checked 7 October 2026).

#### 5. Basecamp: best for simple, communication-centred projects
[Basecamp](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/basecamp/) suits teams who used Notion mainly to keep project conversations, to-dos, documents and client updates together. Each project has message boards, to-dos, a Kanban-style Card Table, schedules, docs and chat, with client access built in. It deliberately avoids complex planning features. Pricing is flat rather than per user, from $25/month for Freelancer up to $299/month (annual) for Unlimited, plus a free plan for one project (checked 7 October 2026).

#### 6. monday.com: best for easy, visual workflows
[monday.com](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/) offers the flexibility people like in Notion, with far less building. Colourful boards switch between table, Kanban, timeline, Gantt and calendar views, and dashboards, automations and monday docs are built in. Time tracking needs Pro and portfolio and resource management are on Enterprise. Basic starts at $9 per seat/month annually with a three-seat minimum (checked 7 October 2026).

#### 7. Smartsheet: best for spreadsheet-style planning
[Smartsheet](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/smartsheet/) is the right Notion alternative if your team thinks in grids and needs structured plans: sheets with dependencies, Gantt and critical path, roll-up reports, dashboards and enterprise portfolio tools. It has no docs or wiki equivalent and no free plan, but offers a 30-day trial of Business. Pro costs $9 per member/month annually (checked 7 October 2026).

#### 8. Jira: best for software teams
Product and engineering teams often use Notion for specs and roadmaps, then find they need real issue tracking. [Jira](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/jira/) is our top tool for Agile software teams, with backlogs, sprints, story points, velocity and burndown reports, configurable workflows and developer integrations. Docs live in Confluence rather than Jira. The free plan covers up to 10 users.

#### 9. Microsoft Planner: best for Microsoft 365 organisations
If your organisation runs on Microsoft 365, [Microsoft Planner](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/microsoft-planner/) may already be included. Basic Planner offers boards and task lists inside Teams and Outlook; Plan 1 ($10 per user/month, annual) adds timelines and dependencies, and Plan 3 ($30) adds resource management and portfolios (checked 7 October 2026). It is lighter than specialist tools but easy to adopt where everyone already uses Teams.

### Notion alternatives by use case

#### Best free Notion alternative
ClickUp's Free Forever plan has the broadest feature set, including docs, though Gantt is limited to a trial. Trello's Free plan is the simplest and allows 10 collaborators per Workspace. Jira is free for up to 10 users, Wrike's free plan covers basic task management on board and table views, Basecamp's free plan covers one project, and monday.com's covers up to two seats.

#### Cheapest Notion alternative
Trello Standard ($5 per user/month annual) and ClickUp Unlimited ($7) are the lowest per-user prices. For larger teams with few projects, Basecamp's flat pricing can cost less overall. All are cheaper than Notion Business ($20), although Notion Plus at $10 compares closely.

#### Best for start-ups and small teams
ClickUp suits small teams that want docs and projects together; Trello and Basecamp suit teams that want something simpler.

#### Best for agencies and client work
Wrike combines time tracking, workload, proofing and client-facing request forms. Basecamp is the simpler choice for client communication, with flat pricing and controlled client access.

#### Best for enterprises and PMOs
Wrike and Smartsheet score 10/10 for scalability in our review, with portfolio management, governance and advanced reporting. A [project management office](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-management-office-pmo/) running many projects at once will find either far more structured than a Notion workspace.

#### Best for Agile and software teams
Jira is the standard for software teams. ClickUp is the alternative for teams who want sprints, docs and lower complexity in one tool.

#### Best for docs-first teams
ClickUp and monday.com have the strongest built-in docs among the alternatives, and Basecamp keeps docs and files inside each project. If documentation matters most, test the editor with your real content before you switch.

### If you use Notion mainly for notes and wikis
Our list compares project management tools, because that is what we review. If you use Notion mostly as a personal notebook or company wiki, the right alternative may be a dedicated knowledge tool instead. Examples include Confluence (Atlassian's wiki, often paired with Jira), Microsoft Loop and OneNote for Microsoft 365 organisations, and local-first note apps for personal knowledge management. These sit outside our scored top 10, so check their current plans and features directly.
If you use Notion for both notes and projects, the docs features in ClickUp, monday.com and Basecamp may be enough to replace both. If they are not, keeping Notion for knowledge and moving projects is usually less disruptive.

### How to choose the right Notion alternative
1. **Write down what Notion is not doing for you.** Time tracking, workload, Gantt depth, reporting, performance or price: the answer points to different tools.
2. **Decide whether you are replacing Notion or adding to it.** If your wiki works well, look for a project tool that integrates with Notion rather than one with strong docs.
3. **Shortlist two or three tools.** Use the use-case section above and our [head-to-head comparisons](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/compare/).
4. **Check the plan you would actually need.** Many of the features that make an alternative attractive sit on mid or upper tiers.
5. **Run one real project in each trial.** Rebuild a live project with its tasks, dates, owners and a status report, using the people who will work in it.
6. **Compare total cost.** Include seat minimums, AI add-ons or credits, guests and any integrations you need.
Our guide on [how to choose project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/how-to-choose-project-management-software/) covers requirements, stakeholder input and trials in more depth.

### How to migrate from Notion
Moving out of Notion is straightforward for simple databases and more work for complex, interlinked workspaces. According to Notion's help centre, you can export pages and databases as **Markdown and CSV** (pages as Markdown, databases as CSV), **HTML** or **PDF**, and export a whole workspace from Settings on desktop or web; the download link expires after seven days.
ClickUp offers a direct Notion importer on all plans. Its help centre says databases become folders and lists, Notion properties become text custom fields, and pages go into a ClickUp Doc. Some content does not transfer, including inline database comments and attachments and page history, and toggles and callouts arrive as plain text. Most other alternatives import CSV files, so export each Notion database to CSV and map its columns.
1. Audit your workspace and archive anything no longer used.
2. Agree how Notion properties map to the new tool's fields, statuses and owners.
3. Export active project databases to CSV (or use a direct importer) and run a test import.
4. Rebuild views, automations and dashboards in the new tool rather than copying old workarounds.
5. Move one team or project first, then the rest once the pilot works.
6. Keep Notion read-only for reference, or keep it as your wiki, until you are confident nothing is missing.
Tip
Notion relations and rollups do not survive a CSV export as live links. Plan to recreate them as task dependencies, subtasks or project links in your new tool.
A simple starting structure, such as our free [project tracker template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/project-tracker-template/), can help you decide which fields you actually need before you import.

### Our verdict
Notion is a superb place for documents and lightweight project tracking, and it earns its place in our top 10. When project work outgrows it, the right move depends on why. Choose **Wrike** if you need resource management, time tracking, portfolios and proofing in one platform. Choose **ClickUp** if you want docs and projects together at a low price. Choose **Asana** or **monday.com** for ready-made, easy-to-adopt project management. Choose **Trello** or **Basecamp** if you want something simpler than Notion, not more powerful.
Whichever you pick, try it on a real project before you commit, and consider keeping Notion as your wiki.

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: What is the best alternative to Notion?**
For project management, Wrike is our top pick because it adds time tracking, workload views, Gantt charts and portfolio reporting that Notion lacks. ClickUp is the closest like-for-like option, combining docs and projects at a lower price, and Asana is best for dedicated task management.

**Q: What is the best Notion alternative for project management?**
Wrike (9.4/10) is the most complete. monday.com (9.1) and Asana (9.0) are easier to roll out, and ClickUp (8.9) gives the most features per dollar. All four include project features that Notion requires you to build yourself.

**Q: Is there a free alternative to Notion?**
Yes. ClickUp, Trello, Wrike, Asana, monday.com, Jira and Basecamp all have free plans, with limits. ClickUp's Free Forever plan is the closest to Notion because it includes docs; Trello's Free plan is the simplest.

**Q: What is cheaper than Notion?**
Trello Standard ($5 per user/month, annual) and ClickUp Unlimited ($7) are cheaper than Notion Plus ($10) and Business ($20). Basecamp's flat pricing, from $25/month, can be cheaper for larger teams (prices checked 7 October 2026).

**Q: Is ClickUp better than Notion?**
For project management, ClickUp offers more built-in features, including time tracking, workload views and Gantt charts with baselines. Notion is stronger and simpler for documents and knowledge management. See our [ClickUp vs Notion comparison](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/clickup/clickup-vs-notion/).

**Q: Is Asana better than Notion?**
Asana is better for structured task, goal and portfolio management with little setup; Notion is better for docs and flexible, custom systems. See [Asana vs Notion](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/asana-vs-notion/).

**Q: Which Notion alternative has time tracking?**
Wrike, ClickUp, Asana (Advanced plan), monday.com (Pro plan) and Basecamp include native time tracking. Notion has none, so teams rely on integrations or manual number fields.

**Q: Which Notion alternative is easiest to use?**
Trello is the easiest tool in our review, followed by monday.com, Asana and Basecamp. All are quicker to set up for projects than a custom Notion database.

**Q: What is the best Notion alternative for enterprises?**
Wrike and Smartsheet score highest for scalability and enterprise readiness, with portfolio management, governance and advanced reporting. monday.com and Asana also offer strong enterprise plans.

**Q: What is the best Notion alternative for software teams?**
Jira is the standard for Agile software teams, with backlogs, sprints and developer integrations. ClickUp is a flexible, lower-cost option that also includes docs.

**Q: Can I import my Notion data into another tool?**
Yes. Notion exports pages as Markdown, databases as CSV, and whole workspaces as HTML or Markdown and CSV. ClickUp has a direct Notion importer on all plans, and most other tools can import CSV files.

**Q: Should I replace Notion or use it alongside a project management tool?**
If Notion works well as your wiki, keeping it and adding a dedicated project tool is often the least disruptive option. Replace it fully only if the new tool's docs meet your needs.

**Q: Is there a Notion alternative for Microsoft 365 users?**
Microsoft Planner is the natural project management choice for Microsoft 365 organisations, with basic Planner included in many business plans. For notes and wikis, Microsoft's own apps such as Loop and OneNote are the usual alternatives.

**Q: How did you choose these Notion alternatives?**
We compared the nine other tools in our top 10 on seven scored categories, current pricing and published G2 and Capterra ratings, then ordered them by how well they address the most common reasons teams leave Notion for project work.
How we review.
Rankings and scores are the editorial opinion of the Neural Project Institute, based on features, pricing, ease of use, scalability and published user ratings. Prices were checked on vendors' pricing pages and ratings on G2 and Capterra on 5 October 2026; both change often, so confirm on the vendor's site before buying. We are independent and do not receive payment for rankings.

# Best Smartsheet Alternatives in 2026

URL: https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/smartsheet/smartsheet-alternatives/
Section: Tool alternatives

## Best Smartsheet Alternatives in 2026
The best Smartsheet alternatives are Wrike for an all-in-one platform with stronger collaboration, proofing and resource management, monday.com for a more visual table-based workspace, Asana for simpler cross-team coordination and ClickUp for lower prices. Smartsheet remains one of the strongest tools for spreadsheet-style planning at enterprise scale, so the right replacement depends on why you are leaving. Below we compare nine alternatives on features, pricing, free plans and user ratings, show which ones feel most like a spreadsheet, and explain how to move your sheets across.
- Published 11 September 2026
- Last updated 9 October 2026
- Prices and ratings checked 5 October 2026

### Key takeaways
- Wrike (9.4/10) is our top Smartsheet alternative: it matches Smartsheet on Gantt charts and enterprise scale and adds a free plan, built-in proofing and deeper workload management.
- monday.com, Wrike, ClickUp and Notion all offer table views, so spreadsheet-minded teams do not have to give up rows and columns.
- Smartsheet has had no free plan since 2025; Wrike, ClickUp, Trello, Asana, monday.com, Notion, Jira and Basecamp all offer one.
- ClickUp (from $7/user/month) and Trello (from $5/user/month) are the cheapest paid alternatives, but count Smartsheet's free Contributors before comparing costs.
- Plan your migration around formulas, cross-sheet references, reports and automations: they do not transfer between tools and must be rebuilt.

### Why teams look for Smartsheet alternatives
Smartsheet has real strengths. Its sheets look like Excel but behave like project plans, with dependencies, Gantt charts with critical path on every plan, forms, automation, cross-sheet reports and dashboards. Enterprise features such as Portfolios, Control Center and strong security controls make it a long-standing choice for PMOs, and it rates 4.5/5 on Capterra and 4.4/5 on G2.
Teams still look elsewhere, usually for one or more of these reasons:
- **No free plan.** Smartsheet removed its free plan in 2025. The cheapest option is Pro at $9 per member/month billed yearly, with a 30-day trial of the Business plan.
- **Plan limits and the step up to Business.** Pro is capped at 10 members and 250 automations per month and excludes timeline view, workload tracking, proofing and free Guests. Business costs $19 per member/month billed yearly, with a three-member minimum (checked 7 October 2026).
- **Add-on costs.** Resource Management, Dynamic View, Data Shuttle, Brandfolder and Premium Support are sold separately, and Enterprise and Advanced Work Management are quote-based.
- **A grid-first interface.** Board and calendar views exist, but the experience is less visual than board-first tools, which can slow adoption among creative and non-spreadsheet users.
- **A learning curve for advanced use.** Basic sheets are quick to learn; cross-sheet references, complex formulas, report logic and permission design take training.
- **Performance on very large sheets.** Users report that large, formula-heavy solutions can feel slow.
- **Limited Agile tooling.** There are no native backlogs, story points or velocity reporting for software teams.

#### When staying with Smartsheet makes sense
If your organisation plans in rows and columns, relies on Gantt charts with [critical path](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/critical-path-method/), and reports across many projects through cross-sheet roll-ups, Smartsheet may still be the best fit. Its security credentials (its Trust Center lists SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP and HIPAA with a BAA) also matter in regulated industries. Free Contributors keep costs down when many stakeholders only need to view and comment.

### How we chose these alternatives
We compared the other nine tools in our [top 10 project management tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/) ranking. Each one is scored from 1 to 10 on seven categories: ease of use, feature depth, planning and resource management, collaboration, Agile and software teams, value for money, and scalability and enterprise readiness. We also considered published G2 and Capterra ratings and prices on each vendor's pricing page.
Many pages that rank for this topic are written by vendors that place their own product first, and some list spreadsheet-database tools we have not reviewed. We only include tools we have reviewed in depth, and we do not accept payment for rankings. Prices and ratings change often, so confirm them on the vendor's site before you buy.

### Smartsheet alternatives reviewed
Here is how each alternative compares with Smartsheet specifically: what it does better, what you give up and who should consider it.

#### 1. Wrike: best overall Smartsheet alternative
Wrike is our highest-rated tool (9.4/10) and the closest match to Smartsheet's enterprise depth, with a more collaborative, all-in-one design. Paid plans include interactive Gantt charts with dependencies, critical path and baselines, plus table, board and calendar views. Workload charts show who is over- or under-allocated, and higher tiers add effort allocation, job roles and capacity planning. Built-in proofing and approvals, request forms with conditional logic, dashboards and cross-project portfolio views cover what many Smartsheet customers buy as separate add-ons.
Wrike has a free plan with board and table views; Team costs $10/user/month for 2 to 15 users and Business $25/user/month (billed annually), with Pinnacle and Apex on quote. Like Smartsheet, it takes time to configure well.

#### 2. monday.com: best for a more visual interface
monday.com is the natural choice for teams that like Smartsheet's rows and columns but want something friendlier. Every board is a table with many column types, and it can be switched to Kanban, timeline, Gantt and calendar views. Dashboards combine data from several boards, and recipe-style automations handle routine updates.
Plans are sold in seat bundles with a three-seat minimum: Basic is $9, Standard (with timeline and Gantt) $12 and Pro $19 per seat/month, billed annually, and the free plan covers two seats. Advanced resource and portfolio features are on Enterprise. See our [monday.com review](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/) and [monday.com vs Smartsheet](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/monday-vs-smartsheet/).

#### 3. Asana: best for simpler task coordination
Asana suits teams that use Smartsheet mainly to track who is doing what by when across departments. It offers list, board, calendar, timeline and Gantt views, dependencies, custom fields, forms, rules and dashboards from the Starter plan, with portfolios, goals, workload and approvals on Advanced. Paid plans include unlimited free guests.
Starter costs $10.99/user/month and Advanced $24.99/user/month (billed annually). Asana is less suited than Smartsheet to formula-heavy trackers and detailed financial tracking.

#### 4. ClickUp: best for lower prices
ClickUp gives you table, list, board, Gantt, calendar, timeline and workload views, docs, whiteboards, goals, time tracking and sprints in one workspace, at prices well below Smartsheet's Business plan: Unlimited is $7/user/month and Business $12/user/month (billed annually), with a Free Forever plan.
The trade-off is complexity and less mature enterprise portfolio and governance controls than Smartsheet, and its best AI features are paid add-ons.

#### 5. Microsoft Planner: best for Microsoft 365 organisations
Many organisations use Smartsheet alongside Excel and Teams. Microsoft Planner keeps everything inside Microsoft 365: basic Planner is included in many business plans, Planner Plan 1 ($10/user/month, paid yearly) adds timeline (Gantt) views, dependencies, milestones and custom fields, and Planner and Project Plan 3 ($30/user/month) adds baselines, critical path and resource management. Microsoft retired Project for the web in 2025 and moved its capabilities into Planner.
Planner is lighter than Smartsheet for reporting and customisation, and richer reporting usually means Power BI.

#### 6. Jira: best for software teams
If software or IT teams are tracking work in Smartsheet, Jira is the specialist alternative, with backlogs, sprints, story points, velocity and burndown reports, configurable workflows and deep developer integrations. Its free plan covers up to 10 users, and timeline view is available on all plans.
Jira is not designed for business teams or spreadsheet-style trackers, so many organisations keep a separate tool for non-technical work.

#### 7. Notion: best for docs and database-style trackers
Notion's databases can be viewed as tables, boards, timelines and calendars, so they feel familiar to spreadsheet users, and they sit next to the documents, wikis and meeting notes that Smartsheet does not handle. It is excellent value, with a free plan, Plus from $10/member/month and Business from $20.
Notion has no native time tracking or resource management, and complex project setups take effort to build.

#### 8. Trello: best for simple boards
If Smartsheet is more than your team needs, Trello is the simplest step down: intuitive Kanban boards, Butler automation and Power-Ups, with a free plan for up to 10 collaborators per workspace. Premium adds calendar, timeline, table and dashboard views.
Trello is not built for dependencies, resource planning or portfolios. Standard costs $5 and Premium $10 per user/month (billed annually).

#### 9. Basecamp: best for flat pricing and client communication
Basecamp takes the opposite approach to Smartsheet: message boards, to-dos, a Kanban-style Card Table, schedules, chat and docs on one page per project, with flat monthly pricing from $25 and unlimited users from the $59 Studio plan.
It has no Gantt dependencies, resource management or advanced reporting, so it suits teams whose priority is communication rather than detailed planning.

### Smartsheet pricing vs the alternatives
Smartsheet charges per member (paid users who create and manage work); Contributors who view and comment are free, and Guests are free from Business. Published plans, checked on Smartsheet's pricing page on 7 October 2026:
| Smartsheet plan | Price | Members | Notable limits and inclusions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pro | $9/member/month billed yearly ($12 monthly) | 1–10 | Gantt, table, board and calendar views; 250 automations/month |
| Business | $19/member/month billed yearly ($24 monthly) | 3 or more | Timeline, workload tracking, unlimited automations, proofing, free Guests |
| Enterprise | Contact sales | 10 or more | Portfolios, scenario planning, SAML SSO |
| Advanced Work Management | Contact sales | — | Control Center, Dynamic View, Data Shuttle, Premium Support |
This illustration compares the monthly list price, billed annually, for 10 and 25 people who create and manage work, using each tool's plan with Gantt or timeline views:
| Monthly cost | 10 editors | 25 editors |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Smartsheet Pro ($9) / Business ($19) | $90 (Pro) or $190 (Business) | $475 (Business; Pro is capped at 10) |
| Wrike Team ($10, max 15) / Business ($25) | $100 | $625 (Business) |
| monday.com Standard ($12/seat) | $120 | $300 |
| Asana Starter ($10.99) | $109.90 | $274.75 |
| ClickUp Unlimited ($7) | $70 | $175 |
| Microsoft Planner Plan 1 ($10) | $100 | $250 |
| Basecamp Studio or Pro (flat) | $59 | $59 (up to 10 projects) or $99 (up to 25) |
Smartsheet is competitive for small teams on Pro, but the move to Business for timeline, workload and unlimited automation roughly doubles the per-member cost. Add-ons such as Resource Management can change the picture again. When you compare, count only the people who need to edit: Smartsheet's Contributors are free, and most alternatives also offer free or low-cost viewers or guests, with rules that differ by tool.
Tip
Price the plan you will need in 12 months, not the cheapest one. Seat minimums, member caps, automation limits and add-ons are where costs usually change.

### Which alternatives feel most like a spreadsheet?
If your team lives in rows and columns, you do not have to give that up:
- **monday.com:** every board is a table with typed columns (status, people, dates, numbers, formulas), which makes it the most natural move for Smartsheet users who want a more visual tool.
- **Wrike:** table view on every plan, including Free, plus custom fields and custom item types for structured data across projects.
- **ClickUp:** table view with custom fields, plus Gantt and workload views on paid plans.
- **Notion:** database tables with properties and formulas, linked to documents.
- **Microsoft Planner:** works alongside Excel and the rest of Microsoft 365 for organisations standardised on it.
None of these reproduces Smartsheet's cross-sheet formulas exactly, so expect to rebuild complex calculations. Our free [project tracker template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/project-tracker-template/) and [Gantt chart template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/gantt-chart-template/) are a useful bridge while you decide.

**Wrike** has the most capable free plan for teams that expect to grow into Gantt charts and resource management. **ClickUp** (Free Forever) and **Trello** (up to 10 collaborators per workspace) are strong for small teams, and **Jira** is free for up to 10 users for software teams. Basic **Microsoft Planner** is included in many Microsoft 365 plans.

#### Cheapest Smartsheet alternative
Trello Standard ($5) and ClickUp Unlimited ($7) are the lowest-priced paid plans in our review. Basecamp's flat price is cheapest for large teams with relatively few active projects.

#### Best Smartsheet alternative for small teams
**ClickUp**, **monday.com** and **Wrike's** Team plan (2 to 15 users) give small teams Gantt charts and dashboards without Smartsheet's Pro limits.

#### Best Smartsheet alternative for enterprises and PMOs
**Wrike** is our first recommendation: it shares Smartsheet's top score for scalability and enterprise readiness and adds stronger collaboration, proofing and resource management in one platform. **monday.com** and **Asana** also offer enterprise plans. Our guides to the [project management office (PMO)](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-management-office-pmo/) and [enterprise project management](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/industries/enterprise-project-management/) cover what to look for.

#### Best Smartsheet alternative for resource management
**Wrike** includes workload charts on paid plans and adds capacity planning on higher tiers, while **Asana** includes workload on Advanced. Smartsheet's own Resource Management is a separate add-on. Our guides to [capacity planning](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/capacity-planning/) and [resource allocation](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/resource-allocation/) explain the techniques.

#### Best Smartsheet alternative for Microsoft 365
**Microsoft Planner**, with Plan 3 for baselines, critical path and resource management. Wrike also integrates with Microsoft tools if you need more depth.

#### Best Smartsheet alternative for Agile and software teams
**Jira** for dedicated software teams; **ClickUp** for sprints alongside broader business work.

#### Best Smartsheet alternative for visual and creative teams
**monday.com** for colourful, flexible boards, and **Wrike** for creative teams that need proofing and approval workflows.

### How to choose the right Smartsheet alternative
1. **Audit how you use Smartsheet today.** List your key sheets, reports, dashboards, forms, automations and integrations, and which ones people actually rely on.
2. **Name the reason for leaving.** Cost, usability, collaboration, resource management and Agile support each point to a different alternative.
3. **Decide whether you need a grid.** If yes, prioritise monday.com, Wrike, ClickUp or Notion; if not, the field opens up.
4. **List must-have planning features**, such as Gantt with dependencies, baselines, workload and portfolio views. Our guides to [project management software features](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-management-software-features/) and [Gantt chart software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/gantt-chart-software/) explain the options.
5. **Compare 12-month costs** for editors and viewers, including seat minimums and add-ons.
6. **Rebuild one real plan and its status report** in two shortlisted tools during their trials, and ask the people who use it daily to judge.
For a fuller process, read [how to choose project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/how-to-choose-project-management-software/).

### How to migrate from Smartsheet
Moving rows of data is the easy part. Most of the effort goes into rebuilding the logic around them. This table shows where common Smartsheet elements usually go:
| In Smartsheet | Typical equivalent in other tools |
| --- | --- |
| Sheet | Project, board, list or database |
| Row and parent/child rows | Task with subtasks |
| Columns (dropdown, contact, date) | Custom fields, assignee and date fields |
| Predecessors column | Task dependencies (usually re-created after import) |
| Gantt view | Gantt or timeline view |
| Formulas and cross-sheet references | Formula fields, rollups or reports (rebuilt by hand) |
| Reports and dashboards | Cross-project reports, saved views and dashboards |
| Forms | Request or intake forms |
| Automations | Automation rules (rebuilt) |
| Contributors and Guests | Viewers, guests or collaborators (check licensing) |
| Control Center blueprints | Project templates and blueprints |
1. **Inventory and clean up.** Archive finished sheets, remove unused columns and standardise status values before exporting.
2. **Export active sheets to Excel.** Most alternatives import tasks from Excel or CSV files, and some offer direct importers, so check your new vendor's help centre for current options.
3. **Build structure first.** Create templates, custom fields, statuses and views in the new tool, then import into them.
4. **Re-create dependencies, formulas and automations**, and test them on a copy of a live project.
5. **Rebuild reports and dashboards** so that stakeholders get the same [project status reports](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/project-status-report/) they rely on today.
6. **Pilot, then migrate in waves.** Move one team or programme first, keep Smartsheet available read-only for an overlap period, then plan the rest around your renewal date.
Tip
Attachments, comment history and integrations rarely transfer cleanly. Decide early what must be kept for audit purposes and store an export of it.

### Our verdict on Smartsheet alternatives
Smartsheet remains an excellent tool for spreadsheet-minded organisations that need structured plans, roll-up reporting and governance at scale. If you are leaving because of cost, the lack of a free plan, add-ons or a grid-first interface, there are strong options. **Wrike** is our first recommendation for most teams: it matches Smartsheet on planning depth and enterprise readiness and adds a free plan, built-in proofing and deeper workload management. **monday.com** is the best choice if you want a more visual table-based tool, **Asana** for simpler coordination, and **ClickUp** for the lowest cost per feature.
Browse every head-to-head on our [compare project management tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/compare/) page, and if AI features matter to your decision, see our guide to [AI project management tools](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/ai-project-management-tools/).

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: What is the best alternative to Smartsheet?**
Wrike is the best overall Smartsheet alternative in our review. It matches Smartsheet's Gantt charts and enterprise scale and adds a free plan, built-in proofing and deeper workload management. monday.com is best for a more visual interface, Asana for simpler coordination and ClickUp for lower prices.

**Q: Is there a free alternative to Smartsheet?**
Yes. Wrike, ClickUp, Trello, Asana (Personal), monday.com (two seats), Notion, Jira (up to 10 users) and Basecamp (one project) all have free plans, and basic Microsoft Planner is included in many Microsoft 365 plans. Smartsheet itself has no free plan.

**Q: Does Smartsheet still have a free plan?**
No. Smartsheet discontinued its free plan in 2025. The cheapest plan is Pro at $9 per member/month billed yearly, and there is a 30-day free trial of the Business plan. Free Contributors can view and comment on shared work.

**Q: What is cheaper than Smartsheet?**
Trello Standard ($5/user/month) and ClickUp Unlimited ($7/user/month), both billed annually, are cheaper per user than Smartsheet Pro ($9) and much cheaper than Business ($19). Basecamp's flat pricing can be cheaper still for larger teams.

**Q: Which Smartsheet alternative is most like a spreadsheet?**
monday.com is the closest in feel, because every board is a table with typed columns. Wrike and ClickUp offer table views with custom fields, and Notion's databases work like linked tables. None reproduces Smartsheet's cross-sheet formulas exactly.

**Q: Which Smartsheet alternative is best for enterprises?**
Wrike shares Smartsheet's top score for scalability and enterprise readiness in our review and adds stronger collaboration, proofing and resource management. monday.com and Asana also offer enterprise plans with advanced security and administration.

**Q: Is Wrike better than Smartsheet?**
For most teams that want an all-in-one platform, yes: Wrike scores 9.4/10 to Smartsheet's 8.6 in our review, with stronger collaboration, proofing and resource management. Smartsheet is better for teams that want a pure spreadsheet-style grid. See [Wrike vs Smartsheet](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/wrike-vs-smartsheet/).

**Q: Is monday.com better than Smartsheet?**
monday.com is easier to adopt and more visual, and it scores 9.1/10 in our review. Smartsheet is stronger for Gantt-heavy scheduling and enterprise roll-up reporting. See [monday.com vs Smartsheet](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/monday-vs-smartsheet/).

**Q: Is Microsoft Planner a good alternative to Smartsheet?**
Yes, for Microsoft 365 organisations. Planner Plan 1 adds timeline views and dependencies, and Plan 3 adds baselines, critical path and resource management. It is lighter than Smartsheet for reporting and customisation.

**Q: Which Smartsheet alternative has the best Gantt charts?**
Wrike offers interactive Gantt charts with dependencies, critical path and baselines on paid plans. monday.com (Standard and above), Asana (Starter and above), ClickUp (Unlimited and above) and Microsoft Planner's paid plans also include Gantt or timeline views.

**Q: Which Smartsheet alternative is best for resource management?**
Wrike, which scores 10/10 for planning and resource management in our review. It includes workload charts on paid plans and capacity planning on higher tiers, whereas Smartsheet sells Resource Management as an add-on.

**Q: Can I move my Smartsheet data to another tool?**
Yes. Export active sheets to Excel and import them into the new tool, then re-create dependencies, formulas, reports, dashboards and automations, which do not transfer automatically. Pilot with one team before migrating everything.

**Q: Why do businesses switch from Smartsheet?**
The most common reasons are the lack of a free plan, per-member costs and add-ons, the Pro plan's 10-member and automation limits, a less visual grid-first interface, the learning curve for advanced formulas and performance on very large sheets.
How we review.
Rankings and scores are the editorial opinion of the Neural Project Institute, based on features, pricing, ease of use, scalability and published user ratings. Prices were checked on vendors' pricing pages and ratings on G2 and Capterra on 5 October 2026; both change often, so confirm on the vendor's site before buying. We are independent and do not receive payment for rankings.

### Why teams look for Trello alternatives
Trello is popular for good reasons. It is rated 4.5/5 from 23,628 reviews on Capterra (checked 7 October 2026), anyone can understand a board within minutes, and its Free plan is genuinely useful. Teams usually start looking elsewhere when their work changes shape:
- **The Free plan cap.** Free Workspaces are limited to 10 collaborators and 10 boards, so a growing team soon has to pay or move.
- **Advanced views need Premium.** Timeline, table, calendar, dashboard and map views, plus Workspace-wide views across boards, require Premium ($10 per user/month, annual).
- **No task dependencies.** Trello cannot link cards so that one waits for another, and its timeline has no critical path or baselines. Projects where [task dependencies](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/task-dependencies/) drive the schedule outgrow it quickly.
- **No resource or portfolio management.** There is no workload view, capacity planning or portfolio reporting across many projects.
- **Power-Up sprawl.** Gaps are filled with Power-Ups, some with their own fees and admin, so a "simple" setup becomes complex.
- **Boards get cluttered at scale.** Hundreds of cards and dozens of boards make it hard to see how work connects.

#### Could upgrading Trello be enough?
Before switching, check whether a higher Trello plan solves your problem. Standard ($5 per user/month, annual) removes the board limit and adds custom fields, advanced checklists and AI features. Premium ($10) adds timeline, table, calendar and dashboard views, Workspace views across boards and unlimited automation runs. If your work still fits on boards, an upgrade is cheaper and less disruptive than a migration. If you need dependencies, workload or portfolio reporting, an alternative is the better route.

### How we chose these Trello alternatives
We compared the nine other tools in our top 10 ranking. Each is scored from 1 to 10 on seven categories: ease of use, feature depth, planning and resource management, collaboration, Agile and software support, value for money, and scalability and enterprise readiness. We checked pricing on vendors' pages on 7 October 2026 and considered published G2 and Capterra ratings.
The list is ordered by how well each tool addresses the most common reasons teams outgrow Trello, then by overall score. That is why Notion appears above Smartsheet and Jira here: for many small teams, adding docs to boards is the first thing they miss. Scores are our editorial opinion, and we do not accept payment for rankings.
