### Each Trello alternative in brief

#### 1. Wrike: best for full project and resource management
[Wrike](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/wrike/) is our top-ranked tool and the biggest step up from Trello. It keeps board views but adds interactive Gantt charts with dependencies, critical path and baselines on paid plans, workload charts, time tracking, portfolio views, request forms, proofing and approvals, and dashboards. It takes longer to learn than Trello, but it is built for teams running many projects with shared people. Wrike has a free plan; Team costs $10 per user/month (annual, 2 to 15 users) and Business $25 (checked 7 October 2026).

#### 2. monday.com: best for more views and automation
[monday.com](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/) is the easiest move for teams who love Trello's visual style. Boards switch between table, Kanban, timeline, Gantt and calendar views, with dashboards across boards, recipe-style automations and monday docs. It has a built-in Trello importer. The Free plan covers two seats, and paid plans start at $9 per seat/month annually with a three-seat minimum; time tracking needs Pro (checked 7 October 2026).

#### 3. Asana: best for more structured project management
[Asana](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/) adds the structure Trello lacks while staying easy to use: list, board, calendar, timeline and Gantt views with dependencies and milestones, rules, forms and dashboards from Starter, and portfolios, goals, workload and time tracking on Advanced. It suits teams coordinating work across several departments. The free Personal plan is limited to two seats; Starter costs $10.99 per user/month annually (checked 7 October 2026).

#### 4. ClickUp: best for far more features at low cost
[ClickUp](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/clickup/) gives Trello users boards plus almost everything else: list, Gantt, calendar, table, timeline, workload and mind map views, native time tracking, docs, whiteboards, goals and sprints. It imports directly from Trello. The trade-off is complexity, and its full AI features are paid add-ons. Unlimited costs $7 per user/month annually and Business $12 (checked 7 October 2026).

#### 5. Notion: best for docs and boards together
If your Trello cards are full of links to documents stored elsewhere, [Notion](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/notion/) brings docs, wikis and boards into one workspace. Any database can be shown as a board, timeline, calendar or table, and the board view is free on every plan. It lacks native time tracking and resource management, and you design the project structure yourself. Plus costs $10 per member/month annually and Business, which includes Notion AI, $20 (checked 7 October 2026).

#### 6. Smartsheet: best for spreadsheet-style planning
[Smartsheet](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/smartsheet/) suits teams that have outgrown Trello because they need real schedules and reports. Sheets look like spreadsheets but include dependencies, Gantt charts, critical path, card (board) views, forms, automation and roll-up dashboards, with strong enterprise governance. There is no free plan, but there is a 30-day trial of Business; Pro costs $9 per member/month annually (checked 7 October 2026).

#### 7. Jira: best for software and Agile teams
[Jira](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/jira/), also from Atlassian, is the natural next step for development teams that started on Trello. It adds backlogs, sprints, story points, velocity and burndown reports, configurable workflows and deep developer integrations, and Jira Cloud has a Trello importer. It is more complex and less suited to non-technical teams. The free plan covers up to 10 users.

#### 8. Microsoft Planner: best for Microsoft 365 organisations
[Microsoft Planner](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/microsoft-planner/) offers Trello-style boards inside Teams and Outlook, and basic Planner is included in many Microsoft 365 business plans. Plan 1 ($10 per user/month, annual) adds timelines and dependencies, and Plan 3 ($30) adds resource management and portfolios (checked 7 October 2026). It is a convenient choice if everyone already works in Teams.

#### 9. Basecamp: best for client communication with flat pricing
[Basecamp](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/basecamp/) is a good fit for agencies and small businesses whose Trello boards have become a substitute for project communication. Each project has message boards, to-dos, a Kanban-style Card Table, schedules, docs and chat, with client access built in. Pricing is flat rather than per user, from $25/month up to $299/month (annual) for unlimited projects and users, and there is a free plan for one project (checked 7 October 2026).

### Trello alternatives by use case

#### Best free Trello alternative
ClickUp's Free Forever plan has the most features. Jira is free for up to 10 users, which suits small software teams. Wrike's free plan covers basic task management with board and table views. Asana's and monday.com's free plans are limited to two seats, and Basecamp's to one project.

#### Cheapest Trello alternative
Trello itself is one of the cheapest tools, at $5 per user/month on Standard. ClickUp Unlimited ($7) is the cheapest alternative per user, and Basecamp's flat pricing can be cheaper for larger teams. For Microsoft 365 customers, basic Planner may cost nothing extra.

#### Best Trello alternative with Gantt charts
Wrike, Smartsheet and ClickUp offer full Gantt scheduling with dependencies, critical path and baselines. monday.com and Asana include Gantt and timeline views with dependencies on their mid-tier plans.

#### Best Kanban-first alternative
monday.com and Jira keep the board at the centre while adding more. Jira supports WIP limits on its boards, which plain Trello boards do not. Our guide to [Kanban boards](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/kanban/kanban-boards/) explains which board features matter.

#### Best for small teams
ClickUp, Asana and Basecamp suit small teams that have outgrown Trello. Wrike's Team plan (2 to 15 users) is a good choice if the team needs Gantt charts and dashboards from day one.

#### Best for enterprises and PMOs
Wrike and Smartsheet score 10/10 for scalability in our review, with portfolio management, governance and advanced reporting. monday.com and Asana also offer strong enterprise plans.

#### Best for software and Agile teams
Jira is the standard for software teams, and ClickUp is a lower-complexity option that also includes docs and sprints.

#### Open-source and self-hosted options
Some teams want a self-hosted Kanban board instead of a cloud service. Open-source projects such as Taiga, Wekan and Kanboard are often suggested. They are outside our scored top 10, so check their current features, maintenance and support before you commit.

### How to choose the right Trello alternative
1. **Name the limit you have hit.** Collaborator cap, views, dependencies, workload, reporting or Power-Up costs each point to different tools.
2. **Check whether a Trello upgrade solves it.** If Premium's views and Workspace views would do the job, compare that cost with switching.
3. **Shortlist two or three alternatives.** Use the use-case section above and our [head-to-head comparisons](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/compare/).
4. **Check the plan you would need.** Dependencies, time tracking, workload and portfolios often sit on mid or upper tiers.
5. **Pilot one real project.** Import or rebuild a live board, add dates and owners, and ask the team to work in it for a week or two.
6. **Compare total cost.** Include seat minimums, guests, AI add-ons and any integrations you would still need.
Our guide on [how to choose project management software](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management/how-to-choose-project-management-software/) covers requirements gathering and trials in more depth.

### How to migrate from Trello
Several alternatives have direct Trello importers, which makes moving boards much quicker than rebuilding them:
- **monday.com:** a built-in importer connects to your Trello account. Its help centre says it imports task names, labels and dates, but not descriptions, checklists, activity or attachments, and handles up to 10,000 rows at a time.
- **ClickUp:** a direct Trello importer is included alongside importers for Asana, Jira, monday.com, Wrike and others.
- **Jira:** Jira Cloud can import data directly from Trello; Atlassian says only organisation, site or Jira administrators can run it.
- **Asana:** Asana's app directory lists a third-party integration, Migrator.xyz, for importing Trello boards.
- **Other tools:** most accept CSV imports. Trello Premium includes simple data export.
Whichever tool you choose, follow the same steps:
1. Archive finished cards and boards you no longer need.
2. Decide how Trello lists, labels and custom fields map to statuses, tags and fields in the new tool.
3. Import one board as a test and check what came across, especially descriptions, checklists and attachments.
4. Rebuild automations and Power-Up functions with the new tool's own features.
5. Move one team first, then the rest once the pilot works.
6. Keep Trello boards read-only for reference until you are sure nothing is missing.
Tip
Importers vary in what they bring across. Check checklists, comments and attachments on a test board before you migrate everything, and keep the originals until the team signs off.
If you want to rethink your board before moving it, our free [Kanban board template](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/templates/kanban-board-template/) is a useful way to agree columns and fields first.

### Our verdict
Trello is still the quickest way to make work visible, and for many individuals and small teams it is all they need. When projects outgrow boards, choose **Wrike** for full project, resource and portfolio management, **monday.com** to keep the visual simplicity with more views and automation, **Asana** for structured cross-team work, or **ClickUp** for the most features at a low price. Software teams should look at **Jira**, Microsoft 365 organisations at **Planner**, and agencies that mainly need client communication at **Basecamp**.
Try your shortlist on a real project before you commit.

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: What is the best alternative to Trello?**
Wrike is our top pick when you need Gantt charts with dependencies, workload views, time tracking and portfolio reporting. monday.com is best if you want Trello's ease of use with more views and automation, and ClickUp offers the most features for the money.

**Q: Is there a free alternative to Trello?**
Yes. ClickUp, Wrike, Asana, monday.com, Notion, Jira and Basecamp all have free plans with limits. ClickUp's is the most feature-rich, and Jira's covers up to 10 users. Basic Microsoft Planner is included in many Microsoft 365 plans.

**Q: What is cheaper than Trello?**
Few tools are cheaper per user than Trello Standard at $5 per user/month (annual). ClickUp Unlimited at $7 is the closest, and Basecamp's flat pricing, from $25/month, can be cheaper for larger teams (checked 7 October 2026).

**Q: Is there a Trello alternative with Gantt charts?**
Yes. Wrike, Smartsheet and ClickUp offer full Gantt charts with dependencies, critical path and baselines. monday.com, Asana and Microsoft Planner's paid plans also include Gantt or timeline views with dependencies.

**Q: Is Asana better than Trello?**
Asana is better for structured, multi-team projects with dependencies, goals and portfolios. Trello is simpler and cheaper for board-based work. See [Trello vs Asana](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/asana/asana-vs-trello/).

**Q: Is monday.com better than Trello?**
monday.com offers more views, dashboards and automation while staying easy to learn. Trello is simpler and costs less. See [Trello vs monday.com](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/monday/monday-vs-trello/).

**Q: Is Jira or Trello better?**
Both are from Atlassian. Jira is better for software teams that need backlogs, sprints and reports; Trello is better for simple, visual boards for any kind of team. See [Trello vs Jira](https://neuralprojectinstitute.com/project-management-tools/jira/jira-vs-trello/).

**Q: Does Microsoft 365 have a Trello equivalent?**
Yes. Microsoft Planner provides Trello-style boards inside Teams and Outlook, and basic Planner is included in many Microsoft 365 business plans. Paid Planner plans add timelines, dependencies and resource management.

**Q: Is there an open-source Trello alternative?**
Yes. Open-source Kanban tools such as Taiga, Wekan and Kanboard can be self-hosted. They are not part of our scored review, so check their current features and support before choosing one.

**Q: Why do teams outgrow Trello?**
The most common reasons are the Free plan's 10-collaborator limit, advanced views needing Premium, no task dependencies, no resource or portfolio management, reliance on Power-Ups and boards becoming cluttered as work grows.

**Q: What is the best Trello alternative for small teams?**
ClickUp offers the most features at a low price, Asana adds structure without much complexity, and Basecamp suits small businesses that mainly need communication and client access. Wrike's Team plan suits small teams needing Gantt charts and dashboards.

**Q: Can I import my Trello boards into another tool?**
Yes. monday.com, ClickUp and Jira Cloud have direct Trello importers, Asana's app directory lists a third-party migration tool, and most other tools accept CSV files. Always test with one board first, because importers differ in what they bring across.

**Q: How did you choose these Trello alternatives?**
We compared the nine other tools in our top 10 on seven scored categories, current pricing and published G2 and Capterra ratings, then ordered them by how well they address the most common reasons teams outgrow Trello.
How we review.
Rankings and scores are the editorial opinion of the Neural Project Institute, based on features, pricing, ease of use, scalability and published user ratings. Prices were checked on vendors' pricing pages and ratings on G2 and Capterra on 5 October 2026; both change often, so confirm on the vendor's site before buying. We are independent and do not receive payment for rankings.

### Frequently asked questions

**Q: What is the best alternative to Wrike?**
It depends on why you are switching. Choose monday.com if you want an easier, more visual interface. Choose Asana if you want simpler cross-team task and goal tracking.

**Q: Why do teams look for Wrike alternatives?**
The most common reasons are: steeper learning curve than simpler tools; interface can feel dense for new users; advanced resource, budgeting and bi features sit on higher, quote-based tiers.

**Q: Is there a free alternative to Wrike?**
Yes: monday.com, Asana, ClickUp, Jira, Notion, Trello, Basecamp have free plans.

**Q: What is a cheaper alternative to Wrike?**
Trello (from $5/user/month) and ClickUp (from $7/user/month, annual) are among the lowest-priced paid options; Basecamp's flat pricing can be cheaper for large teams.

**Q: What is an easier alternative to Wrike?**
Trello and monday.com are the easiest tools to learn, followed by Asana and Basecamp.

**Q: What is the best Wrike alternative for enterprises?**
Smartsheet, monday.com and Asana offer strong enterprise plans.

**Q: What is the best Wrike alternative for software teams?**
Jira is the standard for software teams; ClickUp is a flexible, lower-cost option.

**Q: Which Wrike alternative has the best user ratings?**
On G2, monday.com (4.7), ClickUp (4.6) and Notion (4.6) have some of the highest ratings among the tools we reviewed (checked 5 October 2026).

**Q: Can I migrate from Wrike to another tool?**
Most tools offer CSV import and many provide direct importers from popular competitors. Plan a pilot project, map fields and statuses, and migrate active work first.

**Q: How did you choose these Wrike alternatives?**
We compared the other nine tools in our top 10 on features, pricing, ease of use, scalability and published G2 and Capterra ratings, and ordered them by how well they address common reasons for switching.
How we review.
Rankings and scores are the editorial opinion of the Neural Project Institute, based on features, pricing, ease of use, scalability and published user ratings. Prices were checked on vendors' pricing pages and ratings on G2 and Capterra on 5 October 2026; both change often, so confirm on the vendor's site before buying. We are independent and do not receive payment for rankings.

## About the Neural Project Institute
The Neural Project Institute is an online institute dedicated to project delivery. We write the free Project Management, Agile, Scrum and Kanban guides on this site and award the PMAI certification.

### How we write our guides
Every guide is written and reviewed by the Neural Project Institute editorial team. We base our content on widely recognised sources such as the Agile Manifesto, the Scrum Guide and established project management practice, and we explain them in plain, practical language. Some content is prepared with the help of AI tools; all of it is checked before publication, and we correct errors reported to us.

### Independence
We are independent and not affiliated with PMI, PeopleCert, Scrum.org, Scrum Alliance, Scaled Agile, Inc. or any software vendor. Product and framework names belong to their owners.

### Contact
Corrections and questions: support@neuralprojectinstitute.com. The Institute is operated by Flaunt Weekly LLC, 30 N Gould St, Suite 38589, Sheridan, WY 82801, USA.
